# Fenster Glazing — Full Site Forensic Audit

Date: 2026-08-13
Scope: the live production site (`https://fensterglazing.com`, 712 sitemap URLs) and the
`fenster` theme as committed. **This audit describes LIVE, not the 22-commit stack sitting
on test.** Commercial routes in particular are audited as production serves them today.

Method: 15 specialist audits (architecture, design system, cross-page consistency, UX and
IA, CRO, copy, product experience, accessibility, performance, SEO, mobile, motion,
customer journeys, hostile-competitor, technical QA) run over the theme source, 40 pages of
live HTML, and rendered measurement at real 1440 / 768 / 390 viewports through the Chrome
DevTools Protocol: 168 screenshots plus per-page heading, computed type size, contrast,
tap-target, image, form, schema, console and timing data. Every finding was then put
through an adversarial verification pass against the real files and the real pages.

**No file in the theme was changed by this audit.**

## READ THIS FIRST — AND NOTE THIS SECTION WAS WRONG

> **CORRECTED 2026-08-13, later the same day.** The block below diagnosed a
> deploy failure. It was an **owner decision**, already recorded in
> `LIVECHANGES.md`: commit `31da4d09`, "Tracking: cookies on by default, but bots
> excluded and ad clicks logged", owner instruction 2026-08-12. Optional cookies
> are granted before a choice on production **because the owner reverted
> consent-first**, not because anything failed to ship.
>
> The *measurement* stands and is reproducible: on a clean profile with no
> consent record and no interaction, production fires 22 third-party requests,
> including Clarity collecting, Google Analytics sending a hit and the Meta Pixel
> configuring. With a necessary-only record seeded, zero fire. The consent layer
> works once a choice exists and does not before one. That is weaker than ICO
> guidance, it was raised with the owner, and it is his call.
>
> **The lesson is the reusable part: when live and the repository disagree, read
> the log before concluding the deploy failed.** This session assumed the repo
> was newer than production. On this project a deliberate revert is at least as
> likely, and `LIVECHANGES.md` already said so.
>
> Findings A1 and A2 in the batches below inherit this error. A1's measurement is
> real; its stated cause is not. A2 is not a defect at all.
>
> Live is now `1ccc8bd8` and back on the tip of `main`. The rest of this document
> was unaffected and stands.

**Production is not running the repository.** Live `assets/js/main.js` hashes to
`f01a2147…` at 139,296 bytes; the committed bundle hashes to `20948f42…` at 139,580 bytes.
The difference is not cosmetic: the live bundle ships
`defaultPreferences = {analytics:true, marketing:true, chosen:false}` where the repository
ships `false, false`. That single divergence is why optional cookies are granted before any
choice on production, which `LIVECHANGES.md` records as having been fixed on 2026-08-11.

Two consequences, and they govern how to read everything below:

1. **Fix the deploy before fixing anything else.** Some findings here may describe code
   that is already corrected in `main` and simply never shipped. A1 and A2 are that class.
2. **Do not trust any doc's claim about what is live**, including this one, without a
   checksum. This is the fourth time this repository has recorded that lesson.

| | |
|---|---|
| Raw findings produced | 295 |

| Killed by verification | 12 |

| Strengths recorded | 94 |

- **63 findings never received a verdict.** The verification pass was interrupted. They
  are listed in Appendix C, unverified and explicitly not actioned.
- **The completeness critic did not return.** It was mid-flight on the privacy policy and
  had begun to establish that the policy names no data controller, carries no
  international-transfer clause, and does not name the quote-tool vendor as a processor.
  **That work is unfinished and unverified. Treat it as a lead, not a finding.**
- **40 of 712 URLs were fetched in full.** Percentages about unused CSS are upper bounds.
- **The rendered probe pre-seeded consent to necessary-only**, so the performance baseline
  excludes third-party weight. Real-world payload is worse than the numbers here.
- Contrast candidates were machine-detected by walking the DOM for a background colour,
  which is unreliable over gradients and images. Only contrast findings that survived
  manual verification are included.

## Verified independently by the lead auditor

These were reproduced by hand, outside the agent fleet, and are the highest-confidence
items in the document.

1. **Trackers fire before consent.** Clean profile, no stored consent, no interaction:
   22 third-party requests fire, including Clarity loading and collecting, Google Analytics
   loading and sending a hit, the Meta Pixel loading and configuring, Google Ads
   remarketing and conversion, DoubleClick and Bing. With a necessary-only record seeded,
   zero third-party requests fire. The gate works once a choice exists; it does not exist
   before one.
2. **No `Cache-Control` header on any static asset.** `main.css`, `main.js` and images
   return no cache header at all.
3. **The enquiry honeypot is never checked.** `company_website` appears exactly once in
   the entire theme, at `template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:318`, and is read
   nowhere. No time-trap either.
4. **A withdrawn specification figure is still live.** `inc/site-data.php:517-528`
   documents the removal of the secondary glazing U-value and says "Do not put a figure
   back here without one confirmed for this product". The same figure renders on
   `/other-services/` from `inc/site-data.php:1285`.
5. **The header logo URL contains raw unencoded spaces on all 712 pages.** Root cause:
   `fenster_image_attr_string()` escapes the src with `esc_attr()` rather than `esc_url()`
   (`inc/assets.php:155`), so any asset path containing a space emits an invalid URL. The
   footer avoids it only because `site-footer.php:34` happens to use `esc_url()`.
6. **41% of stylesheet classes appear on none of 40 sampled pages**, and a typical page
   uses 8 to 13% of them. 190,902 bytes of rule blocks match no class on any sampled page.
7. **Every page carries 12,212 bytes of identical inline `<style>` and 33-42KB of inline
   `<script>`**, none of it cacheable between pages.
8. **The hero video is weaker than its own poster.** 20.47s, 1440x810, 3.8Mbps, 9.36MB of
   red-brick job snapshots replacing a strong interior poster after idle.
9. **`message` is a required field on every enquiry form** (`enquiry-form.php:133, 160,
   279`), including the consultation booking.
10. **1,048 of 1,049 internal links and assets return 200.** The single failure is the
    malformed logo URL in item 5. Link integrity is genuinely excellent.

## What to protect (KEEP)

Strengths recorded by the audit, deduplicated to the ones that are genuinely load-bearing:

- **Link and render integrity.** 1,048/1,049 URLs return 200; zero console errors across
  38 routes; zero horizontal overflow at a true 390px on all 38.
- **`/casement-windows/`.** The car-maker register works, and the 70.4px display type is a
  sanctioned exception under `STYLE.md`, not a defect. It is the best page on the site.
- **The documentation system.** `AI.md`, `STYLE.md` and `TONEOFVOICE.md` are why this
  audit could separate defects from decisions. Seven findings died against them.
- **The consent architecture as designed.** Granular, versioned, erases on withdrawal.
  Correct in the repository. Only the deployment is wrong.
- **The eleven bespoke product middles and the repairs diagnostic.** Genuinely
  differentiated work that no local competitor has.
- **The mobile discipline.** The 860px breakpoint rules are real and holding.

### Phase 5 — Content (owner-led, page by page)

Fix the factual contradictions first (E3), because they are the only content items that
actively cost trust: the 14 versus 16 colour conflict, the withdrawn U-value on
`/other-services/`, the guide claiming uPVC insulates worse than aluminium, and the
component-level PAS 24 claim. Then the 525 templated H1s, then the third-person sweep,
then the unrewritten brochure and US-sourced guide pages.

### Phase 6 — Design system (do not start before Phase 3)

Fix the malformed `h2` clamp first: it is one line and it changes 26 desktop and 25 mobile
routes. Then introduce spacing and type tokens and migrate incrementally. Do not attempt a
wholesale restyle; the namespaces are load-bearing and the pages are owner-approved.

## VERIFIED FINDINGS

Ordered by batch, then by severity. `CONFIRMED` means a verifier reproduced it as
described; `REVISED` means it is real but the original description, scope or type was
corrected, and the corrected version is what appears here.

### A. Legal, compliance and security

#### [10] The WindowCAD REST endpoint is unauthenticated in production: no webhook secret is configured and the auth check is skipped entirely when the secret is empty

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 99% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `fenster_windowcad_request_allowed()` (inc/adminbase.php:193-207) wraps its entire credential check in `if ($secret !== '')`. `fenster_windowcad_webhook_secret()` (:185-191) resolves through `fenster_adminbase_config_value()`, which returns `''` when the FENSTER_WINDOWCAD_WEBHOOK_SECRET constant, the environment variable and the fenster_windowcad_webhook_secret option are all unset (:30). Verified live on 2026-08-13: an anonymous `POST /wp-json/fenster/v1/windowcad` carrying no secret header passed the permission callback and reached the handler, which returned 422 only because the test body was deliberately empty. So the endpoint is open right now. A body carrying an `infoProperties` array with a Name and an email or phone would pass fenster_handle_windowcad_submission() (:287) and create a private `fenster_enquiry` post, then relay the lead to the AdminBase CRM via wp_remote_post. Bodies up to 5,000,000 bytes are accepted. The only real limits are a 60-per-hour-per-IP transient rate limit (:236-243) and the name-plus-contact requirement (:307-315). Compare fenster_google_ads_feed_is_authorized() (inc/google-ads-conversions.php:63-100), which fails closed with a 503 when nothing is configured and carries a comment about the exact hash_equals('','') trap this one still has.
- **Recommendation:** Two things, in order. (1) Configure a secret now — set FENSTER_WINDOWCAD_WEBHOOK_SECRET in wp-config.php / the Bedrock .env on the live host and add the matching x-fenster-windowcad-secret header (or webhook_token param) in the WindowCAD account's webhook config; do these together or completed quotes stop relaying. (2) Make it structural so it cannot regress: change inc/adminbase.php:196 to `if ($secret === '') { return new WP_Error('fenster_windowcad_not_configured', 'The WindowCAD webhook is not configured.', ['status' => 503]); }` so the endpoint fails closed the way the Google Ads feed already does. Then audit existing `fenster_enquiry` posts carrying `_fenster_windowcad_fingerprint` meta for records the office cannot account for, since the endpoint has been open for an unknown period.
- **Why:** Corner radius is one of the few cues that makes separate components read as one product. The two most-repeated cards on the site and the panel every single visitor sees on their first visit are all rounder than the standard, so the exception is more visible than the rule.
- **Affected:** `.fg-cookie-consent__panel` (40 pages), `.fg-order-process__card` (15 pages), `.fg-cs-card` (14 pages), `.fg-ph-tile` (3), `.fg-handle-colour-banner__panel` (1).
- **Evidence:** STYLE.md:208; live/main.css 41 distinct border-radius values, 294×8px; src/scss/main.scss:12881 (.fg-cs-card 12px), :11066 (.fg-order-process__card 12px), :1585 (.fg-cookie-consent__panel 20px), :1871 (same panel 16px); render counts by grep across the 40 live HTML files.
- **Verification:** The code reading is exactly right, and the live configuration question the finding left open is now closed — against the site. Code: inc/adminbase.php:178-181 registers fenster/v1/windowcad with permission_callback fenster_windowcad_request_allowed; :193-207 wraps the entire credential check in `if ($secret !== '')`; :185-191 resolves the secret through fenster_adminbase_config_value(), whose default return at :30 is ''. The contrast with inc/google-ads-conversions.php:63-100 is real, including the comment about the hash_equals('','') trap. I then established the live state WITHOUT creating any lead: fenster_handle_windowcad_submission() at :287 calls fenster_windowcad_payload_fields() and returns 422 at the `if (empty($fields))` guard before any wp_insert_post or AdminBase relay, so an empty JSON body is provably side-effect-free. `curl -X POST https://fensterglazing.com/wp-json/fenster/v1/windowcad -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'` returned HTTP 422 {"status":"error","message":"WindowCAD payload did not include infoProperties."} — i.e. the permission callback returned TRUE for a fully anonymous request with no secret header. The secret is NOT configured in production and the endpoint is open today. This is not a latent hazard to investigate; it is a live fail-open. Revising: confidence 70 -> 99, category INVESTIGATE -> CHANGE, and the recommendation's 'verify the constant first' step is now redundant. Two mitigations the finding did not credit, which bound the blast radius but do not close it: a 60-requests-per-hour-per-IP transient rate limit (:236-243) and a hard requirement for a customer name plus an email or phone (:307-315) before a fenster_enquiry post is created.

#### [167] Production is running a consent.php that exists in no git commit: optional cookies are granted by default before any choice, reversing the recorded 2026-08-11 consent-first ruling and reopening the ICO concern

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 99% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** AI.md:179 and LIVECHANGES.md:7 record the model as CONSENT-FIRST as of 2026-08-11, superseding the 2026-08-09 granted-by-default instruction, and state that the ICO concern against the old default is closed by it. `inc/consent.php:253-258` matches: defaultPreferences() returns analytics:false, marketing:false, chosen:false. Production does not. A cache-bypassing request to https://fensterglazing.com/ (x-proxy-cache: BYPASS, so PHP actually executed) returns analytics:true, marketing:true, chosen:false at lines 1176-1184, and in a real browser with localStorage empty and the banner unanswered, GTM, the Meta Pixel and Clarity are all already running. The live file is not any committed version: its comment reads "Optional cookies are GRANTED by default and stay on until refused (owner instruction, 2026-08-09, restored 2026-08-12)", and that phrase appears in none of the 1,383 commits across all refs — the genuine 2026-08-09 commit eb86d1d4 has different comment text and no "restored". LIVECHANGES.md:11 asserts nothing shipped to live on 2026-08-12 or 13. Live also moved mid-audit: the captured Tier-1 corpus (09:20 today) has analytics:false and main.css?ver=1786520515, live now has analytics:true and ?ver=1786610768, so every page in the audit's HTML corpus is stale against production. The performance consequence is secondary but real: ~885 KB raw / ~270 KB compressed of third-party JS (gtm.js 474,615/161,300; fbevents.js 409,387/107,315; clarity tag 862 pulling clarity.js) from three origins, only one of which has even a dns-prefetch.
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as a deployment-integrity incident before treating it as a performance item. (1) Establish what is actually on live by checksumming the served inc/consent.php against every ref, exactly as LIVECHANGES prescribes — the expectation should be that it matches nothing, which means someone edited production directly or deployed off-repo. (2) Ask the owner whether the 2026-08-11 consent-first ruling still stands; if it does, deploy the repo version and re-verify with a proxy-BYPASS request rather than a plain curl, because three consecutive plain curls returned x-proxy-cache HIT and would have hidden the change. If it does not, the ruling in AI.md:179 and LIVECHANGES.md:7 has to be rewritten, and the ICO concern re-opened in writing rather than silently. (3) Re-capture the audit's live HTML corpus; it was fetched before live moved. (4) Independently of which consent model wins, add `<link rel="preconnect">` for https://www.googletagmanager.com, https://connect.facebook.net and https://www.clarity.ms in `fenster_render_critical_head_assets()`, gated on `fenster_request_may_be_tracked()`, replacing the lone dns-prefetch; and put loadGtm (:502) and loadMeta (:536) behind requestIdleCallback the way loadClarity (:514) already sits behind afterVisualReady, so 270 KB of third-party JS stops competing with the LCP image.
- **Why:** Around 25 KB brotli of the 39.6 KB bundle is code for routes the visitor is not on. It is not the biggest win on this list, but it is the same one-line-per-entry build change as the CSS split and it removes real parse/compile work from every page.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes. assets/js/main.js; src/js/main.js:3258-4456 (blinds), :5187-5340 (traveller), :1292 (dead reveal), :7055 (case archive).
- **Evidence:** main.js: 138,830 B raw / 47,057 gzip / 39,594 br; src 325,946 B, 8,234 lines, 54 top-level init guards. Brace-balanced extraction of src/js/main.js:3258-4456 = 52,831 B; `node_modules/.bin/esbuild --minify` -> 17,978 B; `brotli -q 11` -> 5,962 B. Attribute presence across 40 live pages: data-fg-blind-visualiser 1, data-fg-case-studies-archive 1, data-fg-chapter-stack 1, data-fg-obscure-glass 1, data-fg-aw-story 1, data-fg-colour-rail 1, data-fg-consultation-booking 1, data-fg-integral-blinds-reveal 0, data-fg-product-video-final 0. `grep -rn 'fg-integral-blinds-reveal' --include=*.php` -> no matches.
- **Verification:** Confirmed, and worse than described in two ways, while the framing and dimension are wrong. (1) It is not an open question of "which build is correct". AI.md:179 and LIVECHANGES.md:7 both rule explicitly: "THE MODEL IS CONSENT-FIRST as of 2026-08-11, superseding the 2026-08-09 granted-by-default instruction", and LIVECHANGES adds "The ICO concern recorded against the old default is closed by this." Live contradicts a recorded ruling; the repo is the correct build. (2) The live consent.php exists in NO git commit. Its comment reads "Optional cookies are GRANTED by default and stay on until refused (owner instruction, 2026-08-09, restored 2026-08-12)" — and that text appears in none of the 1,383 commits across all refs. Even the genuine 2026-08-09 granted-by-default commit (eb86d1d4) has different comment text, and contains no "restored". Meanwhile LIVECHANGES.md:11 states "NOTHING SHIPPED TO LIVE ON 2026-08-12 OR 13". So production is serving code no one can point at, on the one file with legal exposure. (3) Live changed during this audit: the lead auditor's captured live/home.html (mtime 09:20 today) has `analytics: false` and `main.css?ver=1786520515-694690`; live at 10:38 has `analytics: true` and `?ver=1786610768-694690`. The audit's whole Tier-1 HTML corpus is now stale against production. The right dimension is compliance and deployment integrity — the ~270 KB of third-party JS is a side-effect, not the headline. Minor citation fixes: loadGtm is at :502 (not :499), loadClarity :514 (not :513), loadMeta :536 (not :533); defaultPreferences at :253 is correct.

#### [161] Production loads GTM, Clarity and the Meta Pixel before any consent choice — the audit's perf baseline understates real page weight by ~270 KB compressed

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** This is a repo/live drift and it invalidates the stated probe baseline. The local `inc/consent.php:253-261` returns `analytics:false, marketing:false, chosen:false` from `defaultPreferences()`. The deployed page does not: `curl https://fensterglazing.com/ | grep -A12 'function defaultPreferences'` returns `analytics: true, marketing: true, chosen: false`, and the live comment block still carries the superseded 2026-08-09 granted-by-default ruling. I confirmed the effect in the browser: with `localStorage['fenster_cookie_consent'] === null` and the consent dialog still open, `window.fensterCookieConsent` was `{analytics:true, marketing:true, chosen:false}`, `window.google_tag_manager` was truthy, `typeof window.fbq === 'function'` and `typeof window.clarity === 'function'`, and fbevents.js had transferred 121,623 bytes at t=857-1169 ms. The brief states the probe ran with consent seeded to necessary-only and that third-party weight is therefore not represented — but on live, third-party weight is what every first-time visitor actually gets. Measured payloads: gtm.js 474,615 B raw / 161,212 B compressed; fbevents.js 409,387 B raw / 107,315 B compressed; the Clarity loader 862 B which then pulls clarity.js (26,033 B). That is ~885 KB raw / ~270 KB compressed of third-party JS, from three new origins, none of which has a `preconnect`, plus the 145 ms Clarity CSS re-inject above.
- **Recommendation:** Decide which build is correct and deploy it, then re-baseline. Whichever consent model wins, three performance changes apply either way: (1) add `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://www.googletagmanager.com" crossorigin>`, `https://connect.facebook.net` and `https://www.clarity.ms` to `fenster_render_critical_head_assets()`, gated on `fenster_request_may_be_tracked()`, replacing the lone `dns-prefetch` that is there now; (2) delay `loadGtm`/`loadMeta` behind `requestIdleCallback` the way `loadClarity` already is via `afterVisualReady`, so 270 KB of third-party JS is not competing with the LCP image; (3) record in the audit that any performance number taken with consent declined is the best case, not the typical case.
- **Why:** The whole performance picture roughly doubles. A homepage that measures 4.6 MB / 41 resources with consent declined actually pulls three more origins and ~270 KB more compressed JS for the visitors who matter. Every other finding here is measured against the declined-consent baseline and is therefore conservative.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes, every first-time visitor. inc/consent.php:253-261 (repo) vs live lines 1176-1184; loadGtm at :499-511, loadClarity at :513-531, loadMeta at :533-553.
- **Evidence:** Live: `curl -s https://fensterglazing.com/ | grep -n 'function defaultPreferences' -A 12` -> lines 1176-1184 `analytics: true, marketing: true, chosen: false`. Repo inc/consent.php:255-258 -> `analytics: false, marketing: false, chosen: false`. Browser on live homepage: localStorage consent = null, dialog.open = true, window.fensterCookieConsent = {version:2,analytics:true,marketing:true,chosen:false}, google_tag_manager truthy, fbq function, clarity function. PerformanceResourceTiming showed `4315058575189194?v=2.9.377` (fbevents) transferSize 121,623 at start 857 / end 1169, plus ga-audiences, two Google Ads conversion pings and a `wcm?dn=01908429200` call-tracking request. curl sizes: gtm.js 474,615/161,212; fbevents.js 409,387/107,315; clarity.ms/tag 862; clarity.js 26,033.
- **Verification:** Re-ran the curls live and reproduced it. `curl -sI https://fensterglazing.com/app/themes/fenster/assets/css/main.css` returns exactly: HTTP/2 200, server: nginx, date, content-type: text/css, content-length: 694690, vary: Accept-Encoding, last-modified: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:46:08 GMT, etag, accept-ranges, x-httpd, host-header, x-proxy-cache-info. No cache-control. No expires. Identical picture for assets/js/main.js (last-modified + etag only), assets/images/assistant/legend-spritesheet.webp (content-length 2043360, no cache-control) and assets/fonts/Gibson-Regular.woff2 (content-length 31000, last-modified + etag, no cache-control). The contrast the finding draws is real: `curl -sI https://fensterglazing.com/` returns `cache-control: public, max-age=600, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`, so the header is configured for documents and simply absent for /app/themes/fenster/assets/. The heuristic-freshness mechanism holds on my fetch too — main.css was last modified 08:46:08 and I fetched at 10:36:03, a 110-minute age giving roughly an 11-minute heuristic lifetime, so the render-blocking sheet is still being revalidated on navigations hours after a deploy. inc/assets.php:16-19 does build the version string exactly as described (`$css_version = filemtime($css_path) . '-' . filesize($css_path)`), so the `?ver=` cache-buster is real and makes `immutable` safe for CSS and JS. One nuance for the fix note rather than against the finding: heuristic freshness scales with file age, so the woff2 files (last-modified 06 Jul 2026, ~38 days old) currently get a multi-day heuristic lifetime and are not really hurting today; the sharp edge is CSS and JS, which are young by definition after every deploy. That narrows where the win lands, not whether the header is missing.


### B. Deploy integrity

#### [78] The repo's mega menu adds two items that 404 on live — a deploy trap

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `inc/site-data.php:257` adds `['label' => 'Replacement Glazing', 'url' => home_url('/commercial-replacement-glazing/')]` and `:272` adds `['label' => 'Industrial and Logistics', 'url' => home_url('/industrial-and-logistics-glazing/')]` to the Commercial mega menu. Both routes are registered locally (inc/generated-pages.php:1005 and :1013, inc/commercial-product-data.php:861 and :753, generated-page.php:289 and :302) but neither exists on live: both return 404. The live nav does not contain them, so the site is currently consistent — this is a repo-ahead-of-live divergence from the in-flight commercial overhaul. Deploying `site-data.php` without the page data would put two 404 links in the primary navigation of all 712 pages. `template-parts/sections/commercial-glazing-v2.php:113` and `:176`, and `commercial-county.php:62`, also link both routes, so the same deploy would put 404s into the commercial hub and all 47 county pages.
- **Recommendation:** Before the next deploy, run a link check of every `home_url()` target in `primary_nav_fallback` against the live sitemap and against the local route registry. If both pages are ready, deploy `inc/generated-pages.php`, `inc/commercial-product-data.php` and `template-parts/sections/generated-page.php` in the same release as `inc/site-data.php`. If they are not ready, comment the two nav items out rather than shipping them.
- **Why:** Two 404s in the primary navigation on every page of the site is a first-order failure, and the current split state makes it a single careless deploy away.
- **Affected:** 2 nav items x 712 pages if deployed; also commercial-glazing-v2.php:113,176 and commercial-county.php:62. inc/site-data.php:257, :272
- **Evidence:** `curl` https://fensterglazing.com/commercial-replacement-glazing/ = 404 and /industrial-and-logistics-glazing/ = 404; both present in inc/site-data.php:257 and :272; neither string appears in any of the 40 live HTML files
- **Verification:** Both mechanical faults reproduce exactly. (1) `quote_opened` fires in only three places in src/js/main.js — 2143 (click on `a[href*="windowsoftware.co.uk/windowcad7/"]`, selector at 2132), 5571 (`[data-load-quote]`) and 5585 (`[data-fullscreen-quote]`). The autoloader is at 5443-5465 with `rootMargin: '280px 0px'`, and main.scss:4037-4039 hides `.fg-quote-frame-placeholder` once `.is-loaded` is set, so the Load button is gone before most visitors reach the frame. Interaction inside the cross-origin iframe is captured only into the `engagedQuoteFrames` WeakSet (main.js:5359, 5479-5490) and fires no event — the code's own comment at main.js:5677-5691 states this outright ("A click inside a cross-origin iframe cannot be observed... Deliberately does NOT fire `quote_opened`") and quotes the same 21/182 baseline. (2) main.scss:32704-32706 and 31417-31419 do set `display:none` on `.fg-product-quote-embed__card` at max-width 860px, and the compiled production CSS contains exactly two such rules — `.generated-page--composite-doors .fg-product-quote-embed__card{display:none}` and `.generated-page--sliding-sash ...` — no others. generated-page.php:5178-5202 confirms the frame wrap lives inside that card, and the replacement `.fg-product-quote-embed__sash-mobile-action` is a bare `windowsoftware.co.uk/windowcad7/` anchor, so it fires `quote_opened` with no matching `quote_iframe_loaded`. Live DOM at 375x812 on /composite-doors/ returned exactly what the finding claims: card computed display `none`, iframe `src` null, mobile action display `flex`. 14 routes carry the card, matching the stated scope. Two caveats worth carrying forward, neither of which breaks the finding: the 28-vs-12 evidence mixes units (28 is an event total, 12 is a journey count, and SEO-LEAD-AUDIT §4 also reports 59 further non-consented completions), and SEO-LEAD-AUDIT.md:134 phrases the funnel as nested subsets ("182 saw → 21 opened"), so if the analyst intersected the numerator with the exposed set, fault (2) removes mobile on the two routes from the funnel entirely rather than skewing the ratio — either way the two flagship routes' mobile half is not comparable. Also note the recommendation must not be read as widening `quote_opened`; main.js:5688 rules that out explicitly. A new `quote_engaged` event, as the finding proposes, does not breach it.


### C. Performance

#### [133] A 2.32MB PNG serves a 64px obscure-glass swatch on thirteen product routes, and /casement-windows/ ships 5.87MB of images on mobile

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Cotswold-pilkington.png is 2,379,026 bytes and renders as a CSS background-image on a 64x64px `<span>` inside `<i class="fg-glass-patch">` in fg-product-gallery-band — live markup is `<span style="background-image:url(.../obscure-glass/Cotswold-pilkington.png)">`, measured at 64x64 and 13,160px down /casement-windows/. Because it is a CSS background on an element in the render tree it is not lazily loaded, so it downloads on every route carrying the glass band: the string appears on 13 of the 38 audited pages and I confirmed the full 2.38MB fetch on /tilt-turn-windows/. On /casement-windows/ it is 40% of the page's 5.87MB mobile image payload. liniar-energyplus.png adds 900,662 bytes as the Liniar EnergyPlus logo in .fg-tech-banner__logo, 2,172px natural against a 118px display. The route also has 6 of 66 images with srcset and 41 with no intrinsic dimensions — already logged as open work at HANDOVER.md:1292-1293.
- **Recommendation:** Re-export Cotswold-pilkington.png as WebP at 192px (3x the 64px swatch) — the other twenty swatches in assets/images/products/obscure-glass/ are already WebP at 68-396KB, so this one file is out of family and alone accounts for 43% of that folder's 5.5MB. Keep the full-resolution Pilkington source out of the swatch path; /obscured-glass/ can point at a larger derivative if the visualiser needs one (HANDOVER.md:640 rules the source choice, not the resolution). Re-export liniar-energyplus.png at 360px. That is roughly 2.7MB off thirteen product routes with no visual change.
- **Why:** Cheap to fix, and it is the site's logo: the one image most likely to be fetched by a third-party parser building a link preview or a knowledge-panel candidate.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages (header.php)
- **Evidence:** grep over the crawl: the string appears in all 712 files. scratchpad/linkcheck.tsv contains exactly one non-200 row, status `000`, for this URL. Percent-encoded fetch returns 200.
- **Verification:** Confirmed and then some — every figure reproduces exactly, but the finding understates it. CONFIRMED: Cotswold-pilkington.png is 2,379,026 bytes on disk and 2,379,326 transferred in both probe-mobile.json and probe-desktop.json (38.6% of the page's 5.87MB, so "40%" is right); liniar-energyplus.png is 900,662 bytes at nat 2172 / disp 118 in images.oversized; images.total 66, withSrcset 6, noDims 41. WRONG DETAIL: it is not an <img> and it does not render "around 90-175px wide". The live markup is `<span style="background-image:url(.../obscure-glass/Cotswold-pilkington.png)"></span>` inside `<i class="fg-glass-patch">`, and the browser reports that span at 64x64px, sitting at 13,160px down the page. A 2.32MB PNG for a 64px swatch. UNDERSTATED SCOPE: the string is present in 13 of the 38 live pages, and I confirmed via performance.getEntriesByType on /tilt-turn-windows/ that it really does download there (encodedBodySize 2,379,026) — background-images on in-render-tree elements are not lazily loaded, so all 13 product routes pay it, not just casement. liniar-energyplus.png is the Liniar EnergyPlus logo in .fg-tech-banner__logo, measured at 118px wide. Two context notes rather than objections: HANDOVER.md:640 records Cotswold as the deliberate default preview using the Pilkington source texture (the source choice is ruled, the resolution is not), and HANDOVER.md:1292-1293 already lists srcset/intrinsic-dimension work as an open backlog item, so the srcset half of this finding is a known task rather than a discovery.

#### [153] The Legend cat spritesheet is 2.0 MB, encoded at WebP q=100, and loads eagerly on all 712 routes

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `assets/images/assistant/legend-spritesheet.webp` is 2,043,360 bytes and `legend-sleep-strip.webp` is 124,560 bytes. Both are plain `<img>` with no `loading` attribute, rendered twice each per page (character + roamer), on every one of the 40 pages fetched. `magick identify` reports the sheet is encoded at q=100 — effectively near-lossless — at 1536x2288, while `.legend-assistant__character` in main.css sizes the character to `width:118px`. I measured the eager (non-`loading=lazy`, deduplicated) image payload of all 40 live pages: the median is 2,615 KB per page, of which 2,117 KB (81%) is these two files. On 15 of the 40 pages they are literally the two largest images on the page. The homepage probe confirms it is the single heaviest resource actually transferred: 2,043,660 bytes, ahead of every photograph and ahead of main.css.
- **Recommendation:** Two changes, both cheap. (1) Re-encode the sheet: `cwebp -q 90 -alpha_q 90` produces 520,804 bytes — I ran it — a 1,522,556-byte saving with alpha intact; q=80 gives 397,934. Do the same for the sleep strip. (2) Stop shipping it in the initial payload: render the two sprite `<img>` with `data-src` and no `src` (exactly the pattern already used and proven for the quote iframe's `data-quote-iframe-src`), and swap them in from `inc/legend-assistant.php`'s controller on `window load` + `requestIdleCallback`, which src/js/main.js:4811 already defines as `runWhenIdle`. Legend appearing ~1s later is imperceptible; the launcher button is CSS-drawn and stays put. Together this removes 2,117 KB from the initial load of every page on the site.
- **Why:** This is the largest single performance defect on the site and it is on 712 of 712 pages. On a UK 4G connection at ~1.6 Mbps effective throughput, 2.1 MB is roughly 10 seconds of contended bandwidth competing with the LCP image on every page. It is being spent on a decorative mascot that starts hidden behind an animation state and that most visitors never click.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes. Files: assets/images/assistant/legend-spritesheet.webp (2,043,360 B), legend-sleep-strip.webp (124,560 B); markup in inc/legend-assistant.php; controller at src/js/main.js:5 and :22.
- **Evidence:** stat: legend-spritesheet.webp = 2,043,360 B. probe-desktop.json `/`.perf.heaviest[0] = {u:"legend-spritesheet.webp", b:2043660} (heaviest resource on the homepage). Present in 40/40 live HTML files, 2 occurrences each, no `loading` attribute. `magick identify -format q=%Q` -> q=100. `cwebp -q 90` measured -> 520,804 B. main.css: `.legend-assistant__character{...width:118px;aspect-ratio:192/208}`. My per-page eager-image tally across 40 pages: median 2,615 KB, min 2,439 KB (/areas-we-cover/, /3d-visualiser/, /case-studies/ and 7 others — where Legend is 87% of all eager image bytes).
- **Verification:** Reproduced line for line by reading the entire block src/js/main.js:6942-7029. `aria-modal="true"` is set at :6948 alongside `role="dialog"` (:6947) and `aria-label="Image preview"` (:6949). `openLightbox` (:6990-6996) stores `previousFocus = document.activeElement` and calls `closeButton?.focus?.({ preventScroll: true })` at :6995; `closeLightbox` (:6968-6975) restores with `previousFocus?.focus?.()` at :6974; Escape at :7018-7021 and backdrop click at :7013-7017. What is absent is exactly what the finding says is absent: no `inert` anywhere in the block, no `keydown` branch for Tab, no focus-wrap, and the element is appended to `document.body` at :6959 so the rest of the page stays fully in the tab order behind a dialog that has told assistive tech to ignore it. I grepped the whole file for `inert` to be sure the guard was not applied elsewhere — zero hits in this block. The cited line ranges are all accurate to within one line (Escape is :7018-7021 vs the cited :7017-7021). No ruling in any project doc covers the lightbox. One caveat on scope I could not fully verify: the '32 pages, 132 links' figure. In the 38 fetched Tier-1 pages, 6 carry `data-fg-gallery-lightbox` with 26 trigger links between them (aluminium-bifold-doors 4, casement-windows 5, double-glazing-replacement 3, flush-casement-windows 6, sliding-sash-windows 6, tilt-turn-windows 2). That is the right order of magnitude once case studies are added, so I am not disputing it, but it is unverified beyond Tier-1.

#### [177] On mobile the hero-video gate is defeated by the first scroll: one touchstart anywhere on the page starts the 9.36 MB download (proven live)

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The gate itself is built exactly as documented and holds at rest — I verified in a real browser at 375x812 that the hero <source> carries data-src with no src and issues zero mp4 requests on load, matching probe-mobile `/` which records no video resource. The flaw is the trigger. src/js/main.js:4844-4851 binds `pointerdown`, `keydown` and `touchstart` on `window` with {once:true}. `touchstart` is the first event of every touch-scroll, so the gate opens the moment the visitor scrolls. I proved this live: dispatching a single touchstart on document.body flipped video.dataset.loaded to 'true', set source.src to fenster-home-hero.mp4 (9,809,858 B) and produced a real `GET ... -> 206` in the network log. In practice every mobile visitor who scrolls past the fold downloads 9.36 MB, so the gate saves the payload only for visitors who never move. The CTA-tap case in the original framing is the least costly instance, because clicking `Get an instant price` navigates and the browser cancels the unloading document's in-flight requests. The same pattern is applied a second time on /roof-lanterns/ (roof-lanterns.php:69-81) to cs-big-roof-lantern.mp4 at 6,781,541 B, whose own code comment claims the treatment 'is the reason 6.5MB never lands in a phone's initial payload'.
- **Recommendation:** Do not bind the listener to the hero element — a scroll gesture that starts on the hero still fires touchstart there, and pointerdown fires on finger-down too, so neither scoping nor dropping touchstart alone fixes it. Two changes that do: (a) ship a mobile rendition and select it with media queries, following the exact `<source ... media="(max-width: 860px)">` pattern `fenster_product_scrub_videos()` already uses (inc/assets.php:236-241) — HANDOVER.md:1290 already carries this as an open item — so the mobile path costs ~2-3 MB even when it does fire, and do the same for cs-big-roof-lantern.mp4; (b) replace the window-level interaction trigger with a deliberate activation: an IntersectionObserver plus a `connection.downlink > 2 && !saveData` check, or an explicit play affordance, so a passive scroll never spends 9.36 MB of a visitor's data. Add `if (!navigator.onLine) return;` while there.
- **Why:** This is the first thing a visitor meets on an aluminium enquiry and it costs them six screens of scrolling to learn nothing they could not have guessed. Aluminium is the highest-margin window in the range.
- **Affected:** /aluminium-windows/ only.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:3201-3206; live measurement at 375x812: fg-aw-story = 5,067px, page = 21,058px, fg-product-why = 1,853px, fg-product-intel = 1,806px; panel copy read from live HTML.
- **Verification:** The code is exactly as described and the defect is REAL — but it is materially worse and differently caused than the finding says, and the proposed fix would not fix it. CONFIRMED in source: home-experience.php:110 emits preload="none" with <source data-src> and no src; src/js/main.js:4821-4852 computes interactionOnly from smallViewport(<=860px) || saveData || effectiveType in [slow-2g,2g,3g] || prefers-reduced-motion, binds ['pointerdown','keydown','touchstart'] on WINDOW with {once:true}, and otherwise defers to window load + runWhenIdle(1800); assets/videos/home/fenster-home-hero.mp4 is 9,809,858 B; the CTAs sit inside the hero at lines 120-122; probe-mobile `/` shows no video resource at all, so the at-rest gate genuinely holds. I then PROVED the trigger in a real browser at 375x812 on the live site: at rest the source had data-src and no src and zero mp4 requests; I dispatched ONE synthetic `touchstart` on document.body — precisely what the first finger-down of a scroll gesture produces — and video.dataset.loaded flipped to 'true', source.src was set to fenster-home-hero.mp4, and the network log recorded `GET .../fenster-home-hero.mp4 -> 206`. So the trigger is not 'the first tap including a CTA'; it is the first touch of ANY scroll. Essentially every mobile visitor who scrolls at all pulls 9.36 MB. CORRECTIONS: (1) The CTA case named in the title is the WEAKEST instance, because the click navigates and the browser cancels the unloading document's in-flight requests; the scroll case is the one that actually costs 9.36 MB. (2) Scope is two routes, not one: roof-lanterns.php:69-81 applies the identical data-fg-lazy-video / data-fg-video-slow-mode="interaction" treatment to cs-big-roof-lantern.mp4 at 6,781,541 B, and its own code comment claims this is 'the reason 6.5MB never lands in a phone's initial payload'. (3) The recommendation is wrong: binding the listener to the hero element would not help, because a scroll gesture starting anywhere on the hero still fires touchstart on it, and pointerdown fires on finger-down too — dropping touchstart alone is insufficient. (4) Impact should be High, not Medium. NOT already-ruled: AI.md:38 sanctions interaction gating and forbids the video in the INITIAL payload, which is still honoured; HANDOVER.md:1290 already lists 'Create a 720p/mobile rendition of the homepage hero video and use responsive source/media loading' as an OPEN item, which corroborates rather than closes this.

#### [155] Static assets are served with no Cache-Control header, so the render-blocking stylesheet is revalidated over the network on nearly every page load

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `curl -I` on main.css, main.js, the Gibson woff2 files and the Legend spritesheet returns `last-modified` and `etag` but no `cache-control` and no `expires`. Chrome then falls back to heuristic freshness of roughly (Date - Last-Modified)/10. main.css was last modified 27 minutes before I fetched it, giving a heuristic lifetime of about 2.7 minutes — so for hours after every deploy the render-blocking stylesheet is re-requested and 304'd on every single navigation. I observed exactly this in the live browser: `main.css?ver=1786610768-694690` came back with `transferSize: 300` and `renderBlockingStatus: "blocking"` — a conditional GET on the critical path. The `?ver=filemtime-filesize` cache-buster that `inc/assets.php:16-19` carefully builds is therefore doing nothing, because there is no max-age for it to make safe.
- **Recommendation:** Add to the nginx/Apache config for `/app/themes/fenster/assets/`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for `.css`, `.js`, `.woff2`, `.mp4`. The `?ver=` query string already guarantees a new URL on every rebuild, so `immutable` is safe for CSS and JS today. For images, which AI.md:959 records as carrying no version query, use `public, max-age=2592000` (30 days) until filemtime versioning reaches the image helper, or add versioning to `fenster_image_attr_string()` at the same time and give them a year.
- **Why:** It converts a free cache hit into a network round trip in front of first paint. On mobile that is ~100-250 ms added to every internal navigation for the first hours after each deploy, and it silently undoes the versioning work already in the codebase.
- **Affected:** Every static asset on all 712 routes: main.css, main.js, 4 woff2 files, ~868 referenced images, 76 MB of video.
- **Evidence:** `curl -sI https://fensterglazing.com/app/themes/fenster/assets/css/main.css?ver=...` returns server/date/content-type/vary/last-modified/etag/accept-ranges/x-httpd only — no cache-control, no expires. Same for legend-spritesheet.webp and Gibson-Regular.woff2. Live PerformanceResourceTiming: {u:"main.css?ver=1786610768-694690", transferSize:300, renderBlockingStatus:"blocking"}. By contrast the HTML itself does carry `cache-control: public, max-age=600, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`, so the header is being set for documents and not for assets.
- **Verification:** Every cited line reproduced exactly. src/js/main.js:1007 `document.querySelectorAll('[data-fg-door-wall]')`; :1012 `canDrift = matchMedia('(min-width: 861px)')`; :1037 `shouldDrift = () => visible && !hovering && !dragging && canDrift.matches && !reduceMotion.matches` (no focus term); :1043-1053 `tick()` does `offset += SPEED; rewind(); viewport.scrollLeft = offset;` on every rAF; :1067-1074 the only pause listeners are `pointerenter`/`pointerleave`; :1113-1116 the scroll listener is `if (dragging || frame !== null) return;` so it cannot resync while drifting. SPEED = 0.9, RESUME_DELAY = 1400 as stated. Markup in live/composite-doors.html is `<div class="fg-cd3-wall__viewport" data-fg-door-wall tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Composite door styles. Drag or scroll sideways to explore.">` containing `<li class="fg-cd3-door">` with only `<img>` and `<span>` inside — no focusable children, so the region itself is the only tab stop and arrow-key scrolling is its only keyboard interaction. Contrast case at :6877-6884 is real: `['pointerenter','focusin','touchstart'].forEach(... isPaused = true)` with a matching `['pointerleave','focusout']`. Affected scope is exactly right: `grep -l data-fg-door-wall live/*.html` returns composite-doors.html and roof-lanterns.html, no others. STRENGTHENED, not weakened, by the docs: COMPOSITE-DOOR-REDESIGN.md:101 and PROGRESS.md:3908 both describe this wall as pausing on "hover/focus" — the focus half was specified and never implemented, so this is a documented-intent gap rather than a new accessibility request. (PROGRESS.md:3908 also still calls it a "90s CSS marquee", which the current JS implementation superseded — a stale doc, not a flaw in the finding.)

#### [163] Multi-megabyte PNGs are used where a WebP would be kilobytes: a 2.26 MB showroom photo as the LCP on /contact/, a 2.27 MB PNG as a 200 px glass swatch on 13 routes, an 879 KB partner logo

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** Four specific files, each verified as actually transferring on live pages. (1) `assets/images/about/fenster-showroom.png` — 2,316 KB, 1536 px wide, rendered on /contact/ as `<img src=... alt="Fenster Glazing showroom exterior" loading="eager">` with no width, no height, no srcset; the mobile probe records it transferring 2,372,738 bytes and it is almost certainly the LCP element there. The same file is also the `og:image` and the schema `image` on all 40 pages. (2) `assets/images/products/obscure-glass/Cotswold-pilkington.png` — 2,323 KB, injected as an inline `style="background-image:url(...)"` on a ~200 px `.fg-glass-patch` swatch, on 13 of the sampled routes; its two neighbours in the same swatch triplet (`Reeded-privacy-2.webp`, `Stippolyte-privacy-4.webp`) are WebP, so exactly one file in the set was never converted. The mobile probe shows it transferring 2,379,326 bytes on /casement-windows/. (3) `assets/partners/liniar-energyplus.png` — 879 KB for a logo displayed at 118-260 px. (4) `assets/trust/google-5-stars.png` — 102 KB, natural width 2,797 px, displayed at 87 px.
- **Recommendation:** Convert these four and re-point the references; I measured the outputs. fenster-showroom.png at 800w WebP q82 = 63 KB (saves 2,253 KB); Cotswold-pilkington.png at 200w = 5 KB (saves 2,318 KB); liniar-energyplus.png at 260w = 2 KB (saves 876 KB); google-5-stars.png at 175w similar. Per AI.md:959, give each a new filename rather than overwriting in place, because theme image URLs carry no version query and cached browsers would keep the old file. Also give the /contact/ showroom image `width`/`height` and a `srcset`, and switch the `og:image`/schema `image` to a purpose-made 1200x630 WebP or JPEG — a 2.26 MB PNG is a poor social card and a poor Google Business image.
- **Why:** Four files account for ~5.4 MB of avoidable transfer concentrated on high-intent pages: /contact/ is a conversion page whose LCP is a 2.26 MB PNG, and the glass swatch fires on 13 product routes for a 200 px decorative square.
- **Affected:** /contact/, /about/, /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ (showroom); 13 product routes (Cotswold swatch); 6 routes (liniar logo); all 40 pages (google-5-stars, og:image).
- **Evidence:** probe-mobile `/contact/`.perf.heaviest[0] = {u:"fenster-showroom.png", b:2372738}. Live markup: `<img src=".../about/fenster-showroom.png" alt="Fenster Glazing showroom exterior in Milton Keynes" loading="eager">` — no dims, no srcset. probe-mobile `/casement-windows/`.perf.heaviest[0] = {u:"Cotswold-pilkington.png", b:2379326}; markup is `<span style="background-image:url(.../Cotswold-pilkington.png)"></span>` inside `<i class="fg-glass-patch">`, flanked by two .webp spans. stat: liniar-energyplus.png 879 KB; probe disp 118-260 px. Measured conversions: showroom@800w=63 KB, Cotswold@200w=5 KB, liniar@260w=2 KB.
- **Verification:** Reproduced independently and in a stronger form than the finding claims. Two distinct URLs per weight really are fetched, and Chrome itself says the preload is wasted. One nuance worth carrying forward (it does not change the verdict, but it ties this to finding 162): Chrome only warns about SemiBold, because the inline critical-CSS `@font-face` at weight 400 uses the versioned URL and so keeps the Gibson-Regular preload nominally "matched", while nothing anywhere declares SemiBold at the versioned URL. That means if anyone acts on finding 162 by deleting the critical block wholesale, the Regular preload becomes unused too and Chrome will warn about both. The fix in this finding — make all three references the same unversioned path — resolves both cases and should be done before or with 162.

#### [205] Mobile pages ship 4-7.5MB of images; the largest single asset is a 2MB eager sprite atlas on every page

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Per-route image weight measured from probe-mobile.json perf.byType.img: homepage 4.24MB, /composite-doors/ 2.57MB, /upvc-doors/ 2.28MB, /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ 4.15MB, /casement-windows/ 6.16MB, /aluminium-windows/ 7.54MB. Four specific assets account for most of it and none is lazy-loadable as currently coded: (1) `legend-spritesheet.webp` 2,043,360 bytes, an eager `<img>` with no `loading` attribute, on EVERY page — the heaviest resource sitewide; (2) `Cotswold-pilkington.png` 2,379,026 bytes on /casement-windows/, a decorative obscure-glass swatch delivered through an inline `style="background-image:url(...)"` on a `<span class>` inside `.fg-glass-patch`, so it is unconditionally fetched; (3) `liniar-energyplus.png` 900,362 bytes; (4) `Fenster-Glazing-Vs-Anglian...` 1,844,965 bytes on /double-glazing-milton-keynes/. Secondary and much smaller: the footer accreditation badges are eager and oversized — google-5-stars.png 104,886 bytes at natural 2797px rendered at 72-75px (a 38x oversample), constructionline-gold-member.png 103,642, cpa.png 32,310, fensa.png 24,251, plus legend-sleep-strip.webp 124,560 — about 389KB in total, but they sit in `<footer class="site-footer">`, not above the fold. Compounding all of it, `srcset` is present on only 3 of 38 routes (casement 6 images, sliding-sash 10, composite-doors 73; probe-mobile.json images.withSrcset == 0 on the other 35), so a 390px phone always receives the desktop-scale file.
- **Recommendation:** In priority order by measured bytes: (1) re-export `legend-spritesheet.webp` — 1536x2288 at 2.04MB for a 96px-wide launcher — and give both assistant sprite `<img>` tags `loading="lazy" decoding="async"`, or better, inject them only when the launcher enters the viewport; (2) re-export `Cotswold-pilkington.png` (2.38MB) as WebP at swatch resolution and move the other `.fg-glass-patch` inline `background-image` swatches onto the same pipeline; (3) re-export `liniar-energyplus.png` (900KB) and `Fenster-Glazing-Vs-Anglian...` (1.84MB) as WebP; (4) re-export the four footer accreditation PNGs at 2x their rendered 72-90px size as WebP (google-5-stars at 216px wide is roughly 6KB against 104KB today); (5) add `srcset`/`sizes` to the hero `<img>` on the 35 routes that have none, using the `-800w`/`-1600w` naming already established on /composite-doors/ and /casement-windows/. Steps 1-3 alone remove roughly 7MB across the sampled routes; step 4 removes about 265KB per page.
- **Why:** The handover is the project's memory and it is currently lying about a signature feature. Meanwhile a 7MB asset and 300+ lines of source are carried for nothing, and the dead `fg-blinds-reveal-locked` branch is a live `lenis.stop()` path that could be triggered by accident.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:1292-1527` and `2827-2830`; `src/scss/main.scss:25680-25767`; `inc/assets.php:200-203`; `template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:3138`; `assets/videos/product-scroll/integral-blinds-chroma.mp4`; `HANDOVER.md` "Integral Blinds Desktop Reveal".
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "data-fg-integral-blinds" --include="*.php"` → no matches. `grep -c "fg-integral-blinds-reveal" live/integral-blinds.html` → 0, while `generated-page--integral-blinds-reveal` is present in the same file. `ls -la assets/videos/product-scroll/` → integral-blinds-chroma.mp4 7,060,256 bytes.
- **Verification:** The byte figures for the five named assets are exact, and the srcset gap is exact, but the placement claim is false and the finding misses assets 5-6x heavier than the ones it names — so the recommendation, if followed, would leave most of the problem in place.

CONFIRMED by `curl -I` against live: google-5-stars.png content-length 104886; constructionline-gold-member.png 103642; cpa.png 32310; fensa.png 24251; legend-sleep-strip.webp 124560. Sum ~389KB. probe-mobile.json / images.oversized shows google-5-stars nat 2797 / disp 72 and 75. CONFIRMED: probe-mobile.json images.withSrcset == 0 on exactly 35 of 38 routes; the three exceptions are /casement-windows/ 6, /sliding-sash-windows/ 10, /composite-doors/ 73 — matches the finding exactly.

REFUTED — 'above the fold ... before any product photography': the four trust PNGs sit in `<footer class="site-footer"><div class="site-footer__trust">` at byte offset ~88,300 of a 135,874-byte document, i.e. the last block on the page. They are eager only because they carry no `loading` attribute. The hero (`home-theatre-windows.jpg`, 190,604 bytes) is also eager and is the actual first-viewport image. Parsing home.html: 36 img tags, 22 lazy, 14 eager (finding said 23/36 — off by one).

MATERIALLY INCOMPLETE — the finding names the wrong culprits. probe-mobile.json perf.heaviest for `/` ranks `legend-spritesheet.webp` FIRST at 2,043,660 bytes; `curl -I` confirms content-length 2043360. It is eager (`<img src="...legend-spritesheet.webp" alt="" width="1536" height="2288">`, no loading attribute) on every page including /casement-windows/. That single asset is 5.2x the entire badge set the finding targets, and deferring `legend-sleep-strip.webp` (124KB) while leaving the 2MB atlas eager would recover 6% of the assistant's weight. Likewise /casement-windows/ perf.heaviest is `Cotswold-pilkington.png` at 2,379,326 bytes (curl confirms 2379026) — a decorative glass swatch loaded via an inline `style="background-image:url(...)"` on a `<span>` inside `.fg-glass-patch`, so it can never be lazy — followed by `liniar-energyplus.png` at 900,662 (curl confirms 900362). /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ leads with `Fenster-Glazing-Vs-Anglian...` at 1,844,965. Total image bytes per route: / 4,242,274; /casement-windows/ 6,156,366; /aluminium-windows/ 7,539,460; /composite-doors/ 2,573,903.

NOT ALREADY_RULED: AI.md:37-38 records the deferral/preload work as deliberate and explicitly invites further perf work; nothing there protects these assets.

I did not independently reproduce the throttled LCP numbers (no equivalent CDP throttling harness available here), so those figures are unverified, but they are directionally consistent with 4-7.5MB of image bytes per route.

#### [166] The cookie banner ships 27 KB of unminified inline JavaScript on every page and it can never be cached

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `inc/consent.php:152-820` prints the entire consent controller inline in `wp_footer`. On the live HTML it measures 27,148 bytes — unminified, with the full comment blocks intact. I measured its compressed cost by removing it and recompressing the page: 6,697 bytes gzip / 5,771 bytes brotli. Because it is inline, it is re-transferred on every page view and can never be served from cache, unlike main.js which is one cached request for the whole session. On the smallest sampled page (/fensa-approved-installers/, 93,046 B) it is 29% of the entire HTML document. The plugin's `icaal_options` blob adds another 1,063 bytes of inline config — including six API keys — to every page whether or not a form is present.
- **Recommendation:** Do not drop `inlineStylesheetForClarity` — PROGRESS.md:4408 records that SiteGround/nginx serves a 403 HTML page to Clarity-style resource fetches, so the `data-clarity-unmask` attributes do not make the inline copy redundant, and HANDOVER.md says to keep this ordering and markup intact. Take option (b) instead: keep the fetch, but schedule it behind `requestIdleCallback` with a long timeout and attach the text via `new CSSStyleSheet()` + `document.adoptedStyleSheets` with `disabled = true`, so the bytes are in the document for the replay recorder without forcing a document-wide style recalculation. Whatever the mechanism, preserve the existing guarantee that the stylesheet copy is in the DOM before `clarity.ms/tag` is requested — that ordering is the whole point of the fix and PROGRESS.md:4413 records it as verified live. Also note the injection is gated behind two rAFs, so it never fires in a background tab; if replay coverage matters for those sessions, that is a second, separate defect. This becomes near-free if the CSS is ever route-split, since the per-route sheet would be ~90 KB rather than 694 KB.
- **Why:** 6.7 KB compressed on every page view of a 712-page site, uncacheable by construction, plus 27 KB of parse work at the end of every document. It is the second-largest inline blob on the page after the head.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes. inc/consent.php:152-820.
- **Evidence:** Largest inline script in live/fensa-approved-installers.html = 27,148 bytes (the consent IIFE, starting `(function () { var consentKey = 'fenster_cookie_consent'`). Compressed standalone: gzip 7,008 / brotli 5,771. Delta test — gzip the page with and without it: 20,884 -> 14,187, i.e. 6,697 bytes of the compressed document. Page total 93,046 bytes. Separate `icaal-contact-form-v2-js-extra` inline blob = 1,063 bytes on all 40 pages.
- **Verification:** The cost is real and I reproduced it almost exactly, but recommendation (a) is factually wrong and contradicts a documented accepted decision, so it must not stand. The finding asserts that the `data-clarity-unmask="true"` attributes "exist specifically so Clarity can resolve the URL, which makes the inline copy redundant". PROGRESS.md:4411 says those attributes exist so stricter Clarity MASKING preserves resource URLs; PROGRESS.md:4408 says the separate, actual problem is that SiteGround/nginx returns a `403 - Forbidden` HTML page to browser-like bot/resource fetches, which is why Clarity's own asset capture fails and why the inline copy was added at all (PROGRESS.md:4412, commit f820b87, owner-confirmed at :4413). HANDOVER.md's Clarity paragraph closes with "Keep this ordering and markup intact." Two different problems; removing the inline copy would reintroduce the unstyled recordings. Only option (b) survives, and even (b) must preserve the ordering — the style element has to exist before `clarity.ms/tag` loads, which `loadClarity` guarantees by calling `inlineStylesheetForClarity` with the tag load as its callback. Two smaller corrections: the trigger is rAF-gated, so it never runs in a background or occluded tab (I could not observe the style element in my automated tab despite `window.clarity` being a function); and the cited line range :360-390 for `afterVisualReady` is wrong — it is at :344-359, with loadGtm at :502, loadClarity at :514 and loadMeta at :536.

#### [120] /aluminium-windows/ fetches 229 image requests and 7.19MB on mobile (12.31MB desktop) — 3.9x the image-request count of any other route

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The story canvas carries `data-frame-count="241"` (generated-page.php:3147) and `src/js/main.js:4855-4985` fetches the sequence on demand, loading desiredFrame ±14 on every scroll event, so scrolling the story pulls essentially all 241 `frame-NNN.webp` files. The theme ships 241 desktop frames (12MB on disk) and 241 mobile frames (6.3MB). probe-mobile records 229 image requests / 7.19MB on this route against a next-highest image count of 85 (/composite-doors/); desktop is 12.31MB. A 254KB `prestige-window-scrub-mobile.mp4` loads on top (perf.byType.video n=1, 259870 bytes), so the frame sequence and the scrub video are both being paid for. By bytes it is not the heaviest page on the site — /meet-the-team/ is worse at 10.43MB mobile from three unoptimised PNGs, and /casement-windows/ is 5.87MB — but this is the only route where the weight is an architectural choice rather than a few oversized files, and the story sits at 22% of the document, immediately before the spec strip.
- **Recommendation:** Cap the mobile frame sequence: main.js:4864 already switches to the mobile set at `max-width: 700px`, so gate the decode step there too — step every 4th frame under 700px (60 frames instead of 241) and keep the full set for desktop, or drop the canvas on mobile in favour of the existing `website-header-specifiers-poster.jpg` noscript fallback. Separately confirm whether `prestige-window-scrub-mobile.mp4` and the frame sequence are both meant to load; they currently do. Note this does not make aluminium-windows the site's heaviest page — /meet-the-team/ at 10.43MB from three 2.8-2.9MB PNGs is a bigger single win and a smaller job.
- **Why:** These are the highest purchase-intent pages on the site and the ones SEO-LEAD-AUDIT F4 flagged as invisible (15 impressions, 1 click). Every share of them — WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack — currently renders with no description text at all. It also proves the head is not being verified after copy changes, which is the exact failure AI.md's `louvre-vents` note (generated-pages.php:459-464) records as already having happened once.
- **Affected:** 7 pages: /window-door-prices-milton-keynes/, /composite-door-prices/, /bifold-door-cost/, /sash-window-prices/, /double-glazing-cost/, /aluminium-window-prices/, /patio-french-door-prices/
- **Evidence:** Live head of /composite-door-prices/ contains `<meta name="description">`, `og:title`, `og:url`, `og:type`, `og:image`, `twitter:card`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:image` — and no `og:description` or `twitter:description`. Same on /window-door-prices-milton-keynes/. Home page, by contrast, emits both. Code: inc/generated-pages.php:2186, 2217, 2225; description template at :799.
- **Verification:** The core measurement is real and I reproduced every primary number, but two comparative claims in the finding are wrong.

CONFIRMED: live HTML carries data-frame-count="241" (generated-page.php:3147). The theme ships 241 files in assets/videos/aluminium-windows-story/frames-desktop/ (12MB) and 241 in frames-mobile/ (6.3MB). probe-mobile.json['/aluminium-windows/'].perf.byType.img = {n:229, bytes:7539460} (7.19 MiB) and video {n:1, bytes:259870} = prestige-window-scrub-mobile.mp4, so yes, the mp4 and the frame sequence both load. Desktop = 228 imgs / 12.31 MiB. src/js/main.js:4855-4985 confirms the mechanism: loadFrame() pulls desiredFrame ±14 on every scroll event, so a visitor who scrolls the story does fetch essentially the whole sequence. The story sits at 22% of the HTML, immediately BEFORE the pulse spec strip ("Outer frame" at 26%), so "pays megabytes before reaching a single specification" holds.

WRONG (1) "3x the next-heaviest product page": next-heaviest product page is /casement-windows/ at 6,156,366 bytes = 5.87 MiB. 7.19 / 5.87 = 1.22x, not 3x. The 3.9x multiple is on image REQUEST COUNT (229 vs 59), not bytes. And the heaviest image payload on the whole audited set is /meet-the-team/ at 10.43 MiB mobile / 16.94 MiB desktop (three PNGs of 2.9/2.88/2.8MB) — heavier than aluminium-windows, though not a product page.

WRONG (2) "No other audited route exceeds 74 requests": /composite-doors/ = 98 resources (85 images), /colour-options/ = 81 (67 images), /flush-casement-windows/ and /casement-windows/ = 79 each. The true outlier statement is on image COUNT: 229 vs a next-highest of 85.

Minor: the recommendation says "below 860px", but main.js:4864 selects the mobile frame set at max-width: 700px, so the breakpoint in the fix should be 700px to match.

#### [164] The mobile LCP image on the homepage is a 1600x1600 JPEG at a single resolution — 118 KB more than it needs to be

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `inc/assets.php:60-67` preloads `assets/images/imported/home-hero-poster.jpg` with `fetchpriority="high"`, which is exactly right — and then serves one 1600x1600, 174,788-byte JPEG to every device. On the mobile probe (390 CSS px viewport) the hero fills the screen and the poster is the first contentful paint; the mobile fold screenshot confirms the poster, not the video, is what a phone user sees, which is the documented intent (AI.md:38). At DPR 3 a 390 px-wide hero needs ~1170 px, at DPR 2 it needs ~828 px. I measured the alternatives: WebP q78 at 1170w = 56,510 B, at 828w = 38,030 B, same-size WebP = 82,106 B.
- **Recommendation:** Generate `home-hero-poster-828w.webp`, `-1170w.webp` and `-1920w.webp`, put `srcset`/`sizes="100vw"` on the hero image, and change the preload in `inc/assets.php:60-67` to use `imagesrcset`/`imagesizes` so the preload picks the same candidate the layout will. Keep `fetchpriority="high"`. Saves 118 KB on the mobile LCP resource — at ~1.6 Mbps effective 4G that is roughly 590 ms off LCP.
- **Why:** This is the single most valuable image on the site: it is the LCP element on the homepage on mobile and it is preloaded at high priority, so every byte of it is on the critical path. It is also the one image where the responsive work is already half-done — the preload plumbing exists, only the variants are missing.
- **Affected:** Homepage, mobile and tablet. inc/assets.php:60-67; template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:110.
- **Evidence:** magick identify: home-hero-poster.jpg = 1600x1600, 174,788 bytes. probe-desktop `/`.perf.heaviest contains {u:"home-hero-poster.jpg", b:175088}. inc/assets.php:60-67 preloads it with fetchpriority="high" and type=image/jpeg, no imagesrcset. Measured: magick -resize 1170x -quality 78 webp = 56,510 B; 828x = 38,030 B. Mobile fold screenshot (shots/mobile/home--fold.png) shows the poster frame as the hero.
- **Verification:** Every number is exact and I reproduced the render-blocking status and the zero-block-usage claim myself, extending the search past the 40 sampled pages to three live blog/article routes in case `single.php` carried block content — it does not. Two small notes that do not change the verdict: the finding's gzip figure of 18,295 I did not reproduce (my transfer measured brotli, 13,599, which matches exactly); and the recommended `remove_action('wp_enqueue_scripts','wp_enqueue_global_styles')` also drops the 9,152-byte global-styles blob, which defines CSS custom properties WordPress generates from theme.json — worth one grep for `--wp--` in main.css before shipping, though the theme is code-driven and does not appear to consume them.

#### [207] The /aluminium-windows/ scroll story downloads up to 11.96MB of frames, and none of it is represented in the perf baseline

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `[data-fg-aw-story]` drives a 241-frame WebP sequence from scroll position. `handleScroll` requests `desiredFrame ± 14` on every scroll event, so scrolling the section once fetches essentially every frame. The desktop set is 241 files totalling 11,959KB (avg 49KB, first frame 169KB); the mobile set is 5,949KB. I confirmed the assets are live and returning 200s. The lead auditor's weights (main.css 694KB, main.js 139KB, HTML 93–320KB) do not include this, so `/aluminium-windows/` is roughly forty times heavier than its recorded number for anyone who reads the page. The canvas is `aria-hidden="true"`, so the payload carries no content value for assistive tech and none of it is indexable.
- **Recommendation:** Two options, in order of preference. (1) Replace the frame sequence with the all-intra H.264 scrub the project already built for `[data-fg-scrub-video]` — the comment at `main.js:5050` explains that all-intra buys a single-frame decode per seek, and `prestige-window-scrub.mp4` does the same job in 573KB. (2) If frames must stay, halve the sequence to ~120 frames and re-encode at a lower quality (the current 49KB average is high for a 1x-scale canvas), and stop preloading the ±14 window on every scroll event — a ±4 window plus the existing every-24th skeleton is enough. Either way, gate the whole thing on `navigator.connection.saveData`/`effectiveType` the way `[data-fg-lazy-video]` already does at `main.js:4825`.
- **Why:** This is the single largest media cost on the site and it is invisible in every perf measurement taken so far. On a phone on 4G it is six megabytes for a decorative animation.
- **Affected:** `/aluminium-windows/` only. `src/js/main.js:4855-4992`; `assets/videos/aluminium-windows-story/frames-desktop` (241 files, 11,959KB) and `frames-mobile` (241 files, 5,949KB).
- **Evidence:** `data-frame-count="241"` in `live/aluminium-windows.html`; `du -sh frames-desktop` → 12M, `frames-mobile` → 6.3M; `curl -sI .../frames-desktop/frame-060.webp` → 200, content-length 60086. Loader window: `src/js/main.js:4978-4981` loops `distance` 0..14 in both directions per scroll event.
- **Verification:** Reproduced exactly, and the fix as written is correct.

`grep -n` on the cited file returns line 152 verbatim: `<li><?php esc_html_e('The tool on the right is live. Start clicking whenever you like', 'fenster'); ?></li>` — the line number in the finding is right to the digit.

I opened scratchpad/mfold/online-quote-top.png (390x844 at dsf 3) and the bullet is plainly visible in a single-column layout reading 'The tool on the right is live. Start clicking whenever you like', with the 'The quote tool LIVE' heading and the iframe frame beginning directly BELOW it. Nothing is to the right of anything.

The uniqueness claim also holds: `grep -rn 'on the right\|on the left\|to the right\|to the left'` across template-parts/ and inc/ returns 10 hits, and every other one is either a code comment (commercial-glazing-v2.php:10, heritage-windows-v2.php:273, review-showcase.php:61) or a genuine product/photo description (casement-windows-v2.php:110 bar cross on the left sash, window-door-repairs.php:217 and :398 handle/hinge position, case-studies-data.php:603 bay position, blog-posts.php:677 and :2098 idiomatic 'on the right layout'/'on the right house'). Line 152 is the only spatial-direction instruction to the reader.

One refinement worth recording rather than a correction: the breakpoint at which this goes wrong is `@media(max-width: 1080px){.fg-oq-hero__grid,...{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}}`, not 860px or 390px. probe-tablet.json confirms the same iframe present at innerWidth 768. So the sentence is wrong on tablets and small laptops too, which strengthens rather than changes the finding. The recommended one-line copy change fixes all of it.

#### [160] For analytics-consenting visitors the whole 694 KB stylesheet is re-injected into the DOM as an inline <style>, costing 145 ms of main-thread time measured on a desktop Mac

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 91% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `inc/consent.php:315-345` (`inlineStylesheetForClarity`) fetches main.css with `cache: 'force-cache'` and appends the entire text as a `<style id="fenster-clarity-replay-css">` so Microsoft Clarity's session replay can reconstruct the page. The network fetch is usually free (force-cache hits the same versioned URL), but inserting 694,633 bytes of CSS forces a second full stylesheet parse and a whole-document style recalculation. I measured it on the live homepage in Chrome on this Mac: fetch, inject, force recalc = 144.9 ms, taking the document from 5,508 rules to roughly double. It runs via `afterVisualReady` — `load` + 750 ms + two rAF — which is precisely when a visitor starts scrolling, so it lands on INP rather than on FCP.
- **Recommendation:** Do not ship the full sheet. Either (a) drop `inlineStylesheetForClarity` entirely and rely on Clarity's own asset capture — the `data-clarity-unmask="true"` attributes that `fenster_unmask_stylesheet_for_clarity()` adds to every `<link>` exist specifically so Clarity can resolve the URL, which makes the inline copy redundant; or (b) if the inline copy is genuinely needed, gate it behind `requestIdleCallback` with a long timeout and attach it as a `CSSStyleSheet` via `document.adoptedStyleSheets` with `disabled = true`, so it is available to the replay recorder without triggering a document-wide recalc. This becomes near-free once the CSS is route-split, because the per-route sheet is ~90 KB not 694 KB.
- **Why:** 144.9 ms of blocked main thread on a fast desktop typically scales to 450-700 ms on a mid-range Android, landing on first scroll. It is the largest single main-thread cost I could measure on the site, and it is paid by exactly the visitors who accepted analytics — i.e. by the traffic the business is trying to measure.
- **Affected:** Every page view where analytics consent is on. On production that is currently every first-time visitor, because `defaultPreferences()` returns analytics:true (see the consent drift finding). inc/consent.php:315-345, :360-390.
- **Evidence:** Measured in Chrome on https://fensterglazing.com/: fetch main.css (694,633 bytes) + createElement('style') + textContent + appendChild + forced reflow/getComputedStyle = 144.9 ms; document rule count 5,508 before injection. Source: inc/consent.php `inlineStylesheetForClarity()` uses `window.fetch(... {cache:'force-cache'})` then `style.textContent = css; document.head.appendChild(style)`. Scheduling: `afterVisualReady` = load event -> setTimeout 750 -> rAF -> rAF.
- **Verification:** I wrote my own independent parser (brace-walking; @media/@supports/@layer/@container recursed into; @keyframes and @font-face counted as always-used; a rule counted used if any comma-separated selector has all its class tokens present in the page's class set) and it lands on the finding's numbers almost exactly: 5,959 rules accounting for 689,141 of 694,690 bytes — identical rule count and identical byte accounting, arrived at independently. Per-page unused: aluminium-bifold-doors 85.5% (best case, matches), case-studies 93.7% (worst case, matches), roof-lanterns 88.5% (matches), areas-we-cover 92.9% (matches). My median across the 40 files is casement-windows-bletchley at 88.8% / 75 KB used versus the finding's roof-lanterns 88.5% / 78 KB — a 0.3-point sampling difference, not a disagreement. Delivery claims check out too: `curl -sI` on main.css returns `content-length: 694690`, and inc/assets.php:20-25 does a single unconditional `wp_enqueue_style('fenster-main', .../main.css, [], $css_version)` on `wp_enqueue_scripts` with no media attribute, no condition and no defer, so it is render-blocking on all 712 routes. No doc mandates a single stylesheet. One implementation hazard the finding omits, which justifies its Medium risk rating and should be added to the recommendation: inc/consent.php:64-65 reads `FENSTER_THEME_URI . '/assets/css/main.css'` and `FENSTER_THEME_DIR . '/assets/css/main.css'` to inject the entire sheet inline as `style#fenster-clarity-replay-css` for Microsoft Clarity session replay (HANDOVER.md:334: "Keep this ordering and markup intact"). Any split must update that path too or Clarity replays render unstyled again — a regression this project has already been bitten by once.

#### [154] main.css ships 694,690 bytes to every route and 88% of it is unused on the median page

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** L · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
