- **Problem:** I parsed main.css into 5,959 rules accounting for 689,141 of 694,634 bytes (99.2%), then matched every rule's class tokens against the class set of each of the 40 live pages. A rule counts as used if any one of its comma-separated selectors has all its classes present. Result: the median page (/roof-lanterns/) uses 78 KB and does not use 595 KB — 88.5%. The range is 85.5% (/aluminium-bifold-doors/) to 93.7% (/case-studies/). I checked the obvious objection: allowing every `is-*`/`has-*`/`js-*` runtime state class to count as present moves the figure only from 88.5% to 88.0%, i.e. JS-added classes explain 2.9 KB of the 595 KB. Grouped by namespace: only 40.1 KB across 19 namespaces is used on all 38 sampled routes (legend-assistant 13.4 KB, fg-cookie-consent 6.1 KB, site-footer 5.5 KB, site-nav 4.9 KB, site-mobile-nav 4.3 KB, site-header 1.5 KB); 307.3 KB across 236 namespaces is used on exactly one sampled route. Biggest single-route blocks: fg-home-product-theatre 16.9 KB, fg-contact-hero 11.2 KB, fg-obscure-stage 9.7 KB, fg-consultation-page 9.5 KB, fg-areas-page 9.4 KB, fg-contact-page 6.6 KB.
- **Recommendation:** Split the SCSS at the entry point, not the partials. Keep `src/scss/main.scss` importing only the ~40 KB of global chrome (tokens, type, buttons, site-header, site-nav, site-mobile-nav, site-footer, fg-cookie-consent, legend-assistant) plus the generic `generated-page` shell, and add per-template entries built by the same sass script already in package.json: `home.scss`, `product.scss`, `location.scss`, `commercial.scss`, `contact.scss`, `areas.scss`, `case-study.scss`, `article.scss`. Enqueue the second sheet in `inc/assets.php` off `get_query_var('fenster_generated_page')['slug']`, which the file already reads in `fenster_preload_product_scroll_video()`. A product page would then load ~40 KB global + ~50 KB route CSS instead of 694 KB — roughly 20 KB brotli instead of 97.4 KB.
- **Why:** Every visitor downloads, decompresses and parses 694 KB of CSS to use ~78 KB of it, and it is render-blocking, so it sits directly on the critical path to first paint on every page of the site.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes. assets/css/main.css (694,690 B raw / 151,429 B gzip / 97,413 B brotli), built from src/scss/main.scss.
- **Evidence:** Parsed 5,959 rules covering 689,141/694,634 bytes. Per-page unused: case-studies 93.7%, areas-we-cover 92.9%, roof-lanterns 88.5% (median), aluminium-bifold-doors 85.6%. Namespace-by-page-count buckets: used on all 38 pages = 40.1 KB; used on exactly 1 page = 307.3 KB across 236 namespaces; used on 0 sampled pages = 204.4 KB (commercial/county/blog/case-detail routes not in the 38-route sample, so this bucket is partly legitimate). Runtime-state-class sensitivity test on /roof-lanterns/: 88.5% -> 88.0%.
- **Verification:** All seven source lines are correct verbatim, and I verified the rendered output rather than trusting the templates. `grep -rn '<main' --include='*.php'` over the theme returns exactly the eight hits claimed: header.php:26 `<main id="main-content" class="site-main">`; flat-rooflights.php:21 and roof-lanterns.php:37 and heritage-aluminium-doors.php:83 each re-declaring `id="main-content"`; generated-page.php:2344 `<main class="fg-window-handle-page">`; generated-page.php:2734 `<main class="fg-colour-hub-page">`; customer-portal.php:8 `<main class="fg-customer-portal-page">`. The eighth hit is a comment at blog-post.php:100 reading 'header.php already opens <main id="main-content">; older dedicated…' — i.e. this exact bug was already found and fixed once in the blog template, which corroborates the diagnosis rather than contradicting it. Live verification: /roof-lanterns/, /colour-options/ and /handle-options/ in the fetched Tier-1 set all return two `<main` tags (roof-lanterns with `id="main-content"` twice, the other two once). I curled the two routes not in the Tier-1 set — https://fensterglazing.com/flat-rooflights/ and /heritage-aluminium-doors/ — both HTTP 200, both `<main`×2 with `id="main-content"`×2. Exactly the 5 routes claimed, and exactly 3 of them with the duplicate id. I also checked the risk that the whole heritage location estate inherits it: /heritage-aluminium-doors-bletchley/ returns `<main`×1, so the 26 heritage location variants route through location-service.php and are clean — the scope really is 5 routes, not 31. One footnote: /customer-portal/ is live (HTTP 200, `<main`×2) but absent from page-sitemap.xml, which is why it does not appear in the 712, exactly as the finding states.

#### [226] ~380KB of oversized PNG trust badges and mascot art load above the fold on every mobile page

- **Severity:** HIGH · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Eight controllers in `src/js/main.js` query markup that exists nowhere. Corrected greps (`grep -rl --include='*.php'` across the theme, plus all 38 fetched live pages, plus the whole `app/public` tree) return zero for `[data-fg-home-product-story]` (~102 lines, 6365-6466), `.fg-home-case-wall`/`.fg-home-case-card` (~56 lines, 6735-6790, plus 31 SCSS rules), `[data-scroll-video]` (~56 lines, 4810 + 4994-5048), `[data-fg-cd-range]`/`[data-fg-cd-config]` (~30 lines, 966-995), `[data-fg-product-intel]` (~41 lines, 6900-6940), the `[data-fg-enquiry-step*]` stepped-form scaffolding (~80 lines scattered through 2416-2590 inside the otherwise-live enquiry controller), `[data-fg-choice-mode]` (~8 lines at 1197/1249-1254 inside the live door selector), and `[data-fg-product-counter]` (6476). Total is roughly 370-410 lines, about 5% of the 8,234-line file — not a tenth. Two of the eight are already on the record: `HOMEPAGE.md:244` declares the product-story controller inactive legacy, `HANDOVER.md:1118` and `PROGRESS.md:4871` declare the stepped-form selectors inactive, and `AUDIT.md:396` already recommends deleting both. The six others are undocumented. Separately, `[data-fg-product-theatre]` is rendered with `data-fg-product-theatre-mode="static"` hardcoded at `template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:157`, so `syncScroll` (main.js:6582) returns immediately, `readTheatreProgress` (6539) and `updateFromScroll` (6545) never run, and `jumpToScene` never reaches its `window.scrollTo` branch (6598-6605). Note that `renderTheatre` itself DOES run — the static branch calls `requestRender()` at 6594 — so only the scroll inputs are dead, not the render loop.
- **Recommendation:** Delete the six undocumented controllers and their CSS, and act on the two the docs already declare dead (AUDIT.md:396 asks for exactly that). For the theatre, delete `readTheatreProgress` (6539-6543), `updateFromScroll` (6545-6559), the body of `syncScroll` (6582-6587) and the non-static branch of `jumpToScene` (6598-6605), keeping `renderTheatre`/`requestRender` which the static path uses. Then record in HANDOVER.md that the homepage runs the static theatre variant, because the audit brief still describes it as 'sticky, scroll-driven, 5 scenes', which is not what ships.
- **Why:** A Milton Keynes homeowner searching on a phone on mobile data waits 5–9 seconds for the main image. The bytes being spent are on accreditation logos rendered at 72–90px, not on the windows the page is selling. This is the highest-ratio mobile fix on the site: one re-export pass, no layout change, no design decision.
- **Affected:** All 38 Tier-1 routes for the badge set. srcset missing on 35 of 38 routes. Measured LCP over 5s on 5 of 8 sampled routes at 390px.
- **Evidence:** CDP run at 390x844 dsf=3, Network.emulateNetworkConditions 1.6Mbps/150ms, cache cleared per route, no forced-eager and no scroll: /casement-windows/ initKB=1265 img=706 LCP={t:9280,url:'casement-stone-cottage-1600w.webp'}; / initKB=1457 img=729 LCP=6288; /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ initKB=1639 img=1309. Top images identical on every route: legend-sleep-strip.webp 122KB, google-5-stars.png 103KB, constructionline-gold-member.png 102KB, cpa.png 32KB. `curl -I` on google-5-stars.png: content-length 104886, content-type image/png. probe-mobile.json images.oversized on /: `{src:'google-5-stars.png', nat:2797, disp:72}`. probe-mobile.json images.withSrcset = 0 on 35 of 38 routes.
- **Verification:** The core claim is real and every token checks out, but two supporting claims are wrong. VERIFIED: with a corrected grep (the original zsh run silently failed on `--include=*.php` and returned php_files=0 for everything — I re-ran it properly), all eight tokens return zero hits across every `*.php` in the theme AND zero hits in all 38 `scratchpad/live/*.html` (the earlier non-zero 'live_files' counts were `live/main.js`, the compiled bundle itself). I also swept the whole `app/public` tree for five of them: nothing. Every cited line number is accurate — 6365 `[data-fg-home-product-story]`, 6735 `.fg-home-case-wall`, 4810 `[data-scroll-video]` + 4994 the forEach, 966 `[data-fg-cd-range]`, 6900 `[data-fg-product-intel]`, 2414 `[data-fg-enquiry-step]`, 1197 `[data-fg-choice-mode]`, and `[data-fg-product-counter]` is 0 in both PHP and home.html. Theatre static mode confirmed hardcoded at `template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:157` `data-fg-product-theatre-mode="static"`, read by `main.js:6479`, and `syncScroll` (6582) returns immediately when static, so `readTheatreProgress` (6539) and `updateFromScroll` (6545) never execute in production, and `jumpToScene` takes the static branch (6590-6596) so the `window.scrollTo` path is dead. WRONG #1: 'roughly a tenth of it never runs' is overstated by ~2x. Summing the cited spans gives 102 + 56 + 55 + 30 + 41 + ~8 + 1 = ~293 contiguous dead lines, plus ~80 scattered stepped-form lines (2416-2590, interleaved inside a live controller, not a deletable block) and ~40 theatre scroll lines — about 370-410 lines, or 4.5-5% of 8,234, not 10%. WRONG #2: 'the rest are not recorded anywhere' is fine for the six, but the framing that only stepped-form is documented undersells it — `HOMEPAGE.md:244` explicitly rules `[data-fg-home-product-story]` inactive legacy ('Do not document or rebuild new homepage work around it'), and `AUDIT.md:396` already recommends deleting both the product-story controller and the stepped-form logic. So two of the eight are a restatement of an existing recommendation. IMPRECISE: `renderTheatre` is NOT dead — the static branch of `jumpToScene` calls `requestRender()` at 6594, so the rAF/progress-bar loop runs in production; only its scroll-fed inputs are dead.

Live curl of /commercial-glazing-manchester/ returns title AND h1 both exactly "Commercial Glazing Manchester: 5 Powerful Refurbishment Strategies for Lower Energy Costs" — Python len() = 89 chars, and a sweep of all 712 crawled titles confirms it is the longest on the site (next: what-is-a-door-lintel at 84). #### [191] /casement-windows/ ships a 2.32MB PNG for a privacy-glass thumbnail and 5.87MB of images on mobile

#### [156] Nine pages autoplay looping video with no pause control, and on the seven case-study pages reduced motion is not honoured at all

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Nine live pages autoplay a looping muted video and not one carries `controls` or a pause button. They split into two cases. (1) The homepage and /roof-lanterns/ heroes (template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:110, roof-lanterns.php:69-79) are `autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="none" data-fg-lazy-video data-fg-video-slow-mode="interaction"`. The lazy controller (src/js/main.js:4821-4853) folds `prefers-reduced-motion` into `interactionOnly` alongside small viewport and constrained connection (:4829-4830), which only defers loading until the first `pointerdown`/`keydown`/`touchstart` anywhere on `window` (:4844-4851) and then calls `loadVideo()`, ending in `video.play()` (:4842). A reduced-motion visitor presses Tab once and a full-bleed video starts looping behind the H1 with no way to stop it. (2) Worse, the seven case-study pages carrying a hero video (template-parts/sections/case-studies-residential.php:222 and :234) emit `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="metadata">` with a direct `src` and no `data-fg-lazy-video` at all — no reduced-motion branch, no mobile branch, no connection branch, so they autoplay unconditionally for every visitor on every device. Verified by curl on all 14 /case-studies/* URLs: 7 autoplay (flush-casement-windows-and-composite-door-little-horwood, integral-blinds-leagrave-luton, upvc-casement-windows-bolbeck-park-milton-keynes, sheerline-roof-lantern, roof-lantern-and-heritage-doors, white-charisma-rose-sash-windows-wolverton, flush-casement-windows-and-composite-door-wolverton), 0 carry controls. The only reduced-motion CSS anywhere near this is `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .fg-home-hero__video { transform: scale(1.03) } }` (main.scss:26584-26587), which adjusts framing, not motion. This is not desktop-only: the case-study heroes autoplay on phones too.
- **Recommendation:** Two fixes, and the case-study one is the urgent half. (1) In template-parts/sections/case-studies-residential.php:222 and :234, move the `src` onto `data-src` and add `data-fg-lazy-video data-fg-video-slow-mode="interaction"` so those seven heroes at least enter the same gate the homepage already uses. (2) In src/js/main.js:4821-4853, split the two concerns that are currently conflated: keep `interactionOnly` as the bandwidth/small-viewport deferral it was designed to be (HOMEPAGE.md:41 records that as deliberate — do not undo it), and add a separate hard branch so that under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` `loadVideo()` is never called and the poster stays, which is what AI.md:981 asks for. Independently, add a `<button>` toggling `video.paused` to each video hero, positioned above the shade layer, so SC 2.2.2 has a real mechanism for everyone else.
- **Why:** Three separate handover documents describe an optimisation that does not exist, so the next person to audit performance will trust the docs and skip it. Meanwhile the site pays 2.2 KB per page for a critical-CSS block that cannot help, and pays 58 KB per cold visit for the font bug it causes.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes. inc/assets.php:12-32 (enqueue), :34-43 (the surviving filter), :45-79 (critical block). Docs: AI.md:38, HANDOVER.md:329, PROGRESS.md:4511.
- **Evidence:** inc/assets.php contains one `wp_enqueue_style` with no media/preload trick and no second `style_loader_tag` filter. Live head: `<link data-clarity-unmask="true" rel='stylesheet' id='fenster-main-css' href='.../main.css?ver=1786520515-694690' media='all' />`. Live Chrome PerformanceResourceTiming renderBlockingStatus for that URL = "blocking". Inline `<style id="fenster-critical-css">` measured at 2,189 bytes in live/home.html.
- **Verification:** The mechanism is confirmed exactly, but the finding materially understates the problem and looks in the wrong place for the worst case. Confirmed: home-experience.php:110 is `<video class="fg-home-hero__video" autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="none" ... data-fg-lazy-video data-fg-video-slow-mode="interaction">`; roof-lanterns.php:69-79 is the same pattern; src/js/main.js:4821-4853 computes `interactionOnly` at :4829-4830 from `prefersReducedMotion || smallViewport || constrainedConnection`, and the interaction branch at :4844-4851 registers `['pointerdown','keydown','touchstart']` on `window` with `{once:true}` calling `loadVideo()`, which ends `video.play?.().catch(()=>{})` at :4842. main.scss:26584-26587 is verbatim `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .fg-home-hero__video { transform: scale(1.03); } }`. The 9-page corpus count is exactly right — I curled all 14 case-study URLs and got autoplay on 7, plus home and roof-lanterns = 9, controls on 0. BUT those 7 case-study pages are a strictly worse instance the finding never examined: case-studies-residential.php:222 and :234 emit `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster=...><source src=...>` with a direct `src` and no `data-fg-lazy-video`, so the lazy controller never touches them. No reduced-motion branch, no viewport branch, no connection branch — they autoplay unconditionally for everyone, mobile included. Verified live: /case-studies/sheerline-roof-lantern/ serves `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="...cs-big-roof-lantern-poster.jpg" aria-label="...">`. So on 7 of the 9 pages the reduced-motion deferral the finding criticises does not even exist, and the claim that this is desktop-only is wrong. Not ALREADY_RULED: HOMEPAGE.md:41 and HANDOVER.md:1278 record the interaction gate as a bandwidth measure ("9.36 MB video source", "do not revert to unconditional eager loading"), which the recommendation tightens rather than reverses, while AI.md:981 ("Reduced-motion users should receive static or simplified content") and AI.md:898 ("Autoplay, scroll-controlled or cinematic desktop media needs reduced-motion and mobile fallbacks") both point the same way as the finding.

#### [172] Uncached PHP render is ~150-170 ms on every route and the HTML edge cache only holds for an hour, so most of the 712 long-tail routes serve cold to most visitors

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** HTML carries `cache-control: public, max-age=600, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`, which is sensible. But with 712 routes and an hour of shared-cache life, the 529 town/matrix routes and the commercial pages will be cold for a large share of their (by definition thin) traffic. I measured the cold path by cache-busting with a random query: TTFB is a very consistent 258-302 ms across /areas-we-cover/, /composite-doors/, the homepage and /patio-doors-aylesbury/, against 90-130 ms warm — so roughly 150-170 ms of PHP render per request, uniform across page shapes. The probe caught the tail: TTFB of 813 ms on /windows-milton-keynes/, 398 ms on /book-a-consultation/, 390 ms on /contact/, and my own sweep hit 1.58 s on /flush-casement-windows-brooklands/. Part of that render cost is self-inflicted: `inc/consent.php:31-54` runs an `ob_start` over every page and applies 8 `preg_replace` patterns with `.*?` and the `/is` modifier to the whole document — up to 320 KB on /areas-we-cover/ — to strip tracking tags that a plugin only emits in the first place.
- **Recommendation:** These pages are fully deterministic — hardcoded data in `inc/site-data.php` and `inc/generated-pages.php`, no CMS content, no per-visitor server output. Raise `s-maxage` to 86400 with `stale-while-revalidate=604800`; nothing on the page changes between deploys, and a deploy can purge. That converts a 270 ms cold TTFB into a ~90 ms edge hit for the long tail. Separately, replace the 8-pattern output-buffer strip with proper dequeuing: the tracking tags come from the `ihaf`/Clarity plugin options, which `inc/consent.php:16-20` is already blanking via `option_*` filters — finish that job so the regex pass can be deleted rather than run on 712 routes.
- **Why:** TTFB is the first term in LCP. 150-170 ms of avoidable server time on the pages with the least traffic (and therefore the coldest caches) is where the site's worst measured LCPs come from — the 813 ms and 1.58 s outliers are all cold renders.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes, disproportionately the 529 town/matrix routes. inc/consent.php:31-54.
- **Evidence:** Cache-busted curl (`?cb=$RANDOM`), repeated: /areas-we-cover/ time_starttransfer 0.272/0.276/0.275/0.269/0.282; /composite-doors/ 0.278/0.281/0.302; / 0.269/0.280/0.279; /patio-doors-aylesbury/ 0.258/0.273/0.259. Warm repeats of the same URLs: 0.090-0.155. Random sweep of 12 sitemap URLs, first hit: /flush-casement-windows-brooklands/ 1.579 s. probe-desktop ttfb: /windows-milton-keynes/ 813, /book-a-consultation/ 398, /contact/ 390, /doors-milton-keynes/ 356. Response header on all HTML: `cache-control: public, max-age=600, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`. inc/consent.php:41-52 lists 8 regex patterns applied to the full document buffer.
- **Verification:** Reproduced to within 40 bytes on every number. Extracting all <script> blocks from live/fensa-approved-installers.html: the largest is 27,160 bytes and begins `(function () { var consentKey = 'fenster_cookie_consent'` (finding said 27,148 — 12 bytes, presumably a trailing-newline convention). Page total 93,084 B (finding: 93,046), so the block is 29.2% of the document. gzip -9 standalone = 6,997 (finding: 7,008). Delta test — gzip -9 of the whole page with and without the block = 20,874 -> 14,175, a delta of 6,699 (finding: 6,697). The `icaal_options` blob is 1,063 bytes exactly. Source confirmed: inc/consent.php is 822 lines, `<script>` opens at line 152 and `</script>` closes at 821, rendered from wp_footer priority 45 (inc/consent.php:57), and the whole thing is unminified with comments intact. It really does need very little from PHP: only 6 `<?php` interpolations exist inside the 670-line block — trackingAllowed, the Clarity stylesheet URL, FENSTER_GTM_ID, FENSTER_CLARITY_ID and FENSTER_META_PIXEL_ID. So the proposed inline-config blob is genuinely small. CAVEAT WORTH CARRYING, not a refutation: AI.md:180 states 'Both inc/consent.php and src/js/main.js carry the default and the validator; change one and change the other, because main.js runs first and cannot wait to be told', and AI.md:194 documents inc/consent.php publishing the live choice on window.fensterCookieConsent as a fallback for unwritable storage. Merging the controller into main.js is therefore a change to load-bearing consent plumbing with several documented failure modes behind it — the Medium risk rating is correct and if anything generous.

#### [157] The Gibson font preloads never match the @font-face that actually wins, so Regular and SemiBold are downloaded twice on every cold visit

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 94% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `inc/assets.php:50-58` preloads `Gibson-Regular.woff2?ver=1783344686` and `Gibson-SemiBold.woff2?ver=1783344686`. The inline critical CSS declares `@font-face` for Gibson weight 400 pointing at that same versioned URL — so the preload matches it. But main.css declares the full family with unversioned URLs (`src:url("../fonts/Gibson-Regular.woff2")`), and because main.css is parsed after the inline block, its weight-400 and weight-700 faces win the cascade. I confirmed this in the live browser: the resource list contains `Gibson-Regular.woff2?ver=1783344686` and `Gibson-SemiBold.woff2?ver=1783344686` with `initiatorType: "link"` at t=570/571 ms, and separately `Gibson-Regular.woff2`, `Gibson-SemiBold.woff2` and `Gibson-Bold.woff2` with `initiatorType: "css"` at t=626 ms. Two distinct URLs, two distinct cache entries, two downloads. 31,000 + 27,432 = 58,432 bytes are thrown away per cold visit, and they are thrown away at preload priority, i.e. ahead of the LCP image. Gibson-Bold (29,908 B) is used but not preloaded at all.
- **Recommendation:** Make the two URLs identical. Simplest: drop `?ver=` from the two preload tags in `inc/assets.php:50-58` and from the critical-CSS `@font-face`, so all three references are `/assets/fonts/Gibson-Regular.woff2`. (The fonts have not changed since 2026-07-06 and are not part of the rebuild cycle, so they do not need a cache-buster; give them a long max-age instead per the Cache-Control finding.) Then add a third preload for `Gibson-Bold.woff2` — it is declared at weight 800 in main.css and is fetched on every page, so it is on the critical path already, just without priority.
- **Why:** 58 KB of wasted download at the highest resource priority on the very first paint, on every page, for every new visitor. Font bytes compete directly with the LCP image, so this is a measurable LCP regression that costs nothing to fix.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes. inc/assets.php:47-58; src/scss @font-face block compiled into assets/css/main.css.
- **Evidence:** Live Chrome: performance.getEntriesByType('resource') filtered to fonts returned [{u:"Gibson-Regular.woff2?ver=1783344686",init:"link",start:570},{u:"Gibson-SemiBold.woff2?ver=1783344686",init:"link",start:571},{u:"Gibson-Regular.woff2",init:"css",start:626},{u:"Gibson-SemiBold.woff2",init:"css",start:626},{u:"Gibson-Bold.woff2",init:"css",start:626}]. main.css @font-face src values are all `../fonts/Gibson-*.woff2` with no query. File sizes: Regular 31,000 B, SemiBold 27,432 B, Bold 29,908 B, Light 28,936 B.
- **Verification:** Reproduced exactly. src/scss/main.scss:23786-23800, inside the `@media (max-width: 860px)` block opened at :22586 (nearest preceding @media before 23786): `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button { width: 28px; height: 6px; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; ... }` and `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button[aria-pressed="true"] { width: 48px; }`, with the parent `.fg-sash-carousel__dots` at :23778-23783 carrying `display:flex; justify-content:center; gap:0.5rem`. `padding: 0` is explicit, so there is no hidden hit-area padding to rescue it. probe-mobile.json smallTargets for /sliding-sash-windows/ contains verbatim {tag:button, txt:"Show Ultimate Rose", w:48, h:6}, {"Show Heritage Rose", 28, 6}, {"Show Charisma Rose", 28, 6} — real entries, not a truncation artefact (that route's array is at the 30-item cap, but these three are present and specific). The SC 2.5.8 reasoning is sound and correctly stops short of claiming a conformance failure: gap 0.5rem = 8px, so centre-to-centre on the narrow dots is 36px > 24px and nothing sits above or below, so the undersized-target spacing exception is met. It is nevertheless a violation of the project's own written standard — AI.md:886 "Interactive targets should be at least `44px` high" and STYLE.md:280 identical — which makes the Objective classification safe. One citation correction only: the "Dots must be native buttons with accessible labels" rule is AI.md:905, not :906.

#### [159] jQuery 3.7.1 plus jquery-migrate (101 KB) are render-blocking in the head purely for a contact-form plugin whose own scripts run in the footer

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The live head contains `<script src=".../jquery.min.js?ver=3.7.1" id="jquery-core-js">` and `<script src=".../jquery-migrate.min.js?ver=3.4.1">`, both with no `defer` and no `async`; Chrome reports both as `renderBlockingStatus: "blocking"`. That is 87,553 + 13,577 = 101,130 bytes raw, 29,597 + 4,677 = 34,274 bytes brotli, parsed and executed before first paint. The theme does not need them: `assets/js/main.js` contains no reference to the `jQuery` symbol, and `inc/assets.php` enqueues `fenster-main` with an empty dependency array and `$in_footer = true`. The only consumer is the `contact-form-v2-master` plugin, whose two scripts (`icaal-contact-form-v2-public.js` 8,033 B, `icaal-contact-form-v2-addalert.js` 1,251 B) are already correctly in the footer — jQuery is in the head only because the plugin enqueues it without `$in_footer`.
- **Recommendation:** Two options, in order of preference. (1) Retire the dependency: the plugin's public script is ~10 jQuery call sites — a `submit` handler, `serializeArray`, a `fetch` to admin-ajax, and an `addAlert` helper. Rewriting it in vanilla JS inside `main.js` removes 101,130 bytes and two render-blocking requests outright. (2) If the plugin must stay as-is, add to `inc/assets.php` at a late `wp_enqueue_scripts` priority: `wp_scripts()->add_data('jquery-core','group',1)` and the same for `jquery-migrate` and `jquery`, to move jQuery to the footer. Also drop `jquery-migrate` entirely — it exists to support pre-1.9 jQuery code and this plugin uses none of it, saving 13,577 B on its own.
- **Why:** ~34 KB brotli and two extra requests on the critical path of every page, for a library the theme does not use. On a cold 4G load that is roughly 170 ms of blocking download before first paint, plus ~9 ms of eval measured on a fast desktop (so ~35 ms on a mid-range phone).
- **Affected:** All 712 routes. Head scripts on all 40 live pages. Plugin: app/plugins/contact-form-v2-master/.
- **Evidence:** Live head script positions verified by splitting live/home.html at `</head>`: jquery-core-js and jquery-migrate-js are both in HEAD with no defer/async; all other scripts are in BODY. Chrome renderBlockingStatus="blocking" for both. curl sizes: jquery.min.js raw 87,553 / br 29,597; jquery-migrate.min.js raw 13,577 / br 4,677. `grep -c 'jQuery' live/main.js` on the compiled theme bundle -> the symbol never appears. icaal-contact-form-v2-public.js contains 10 `$(` call sites total. Measured jQuery eval on this desktop: 8.7 ms.
- **Verification:** Every number reproduced. `ls -l` gives legend-spritesheet.webp = 2,043,360 bytes and legend-sleep-strip.webp = 124,560 bytes. `magick identify -format '%f %wx%h q=%Q'` gives `legend-spritesheet.webp 1536x2288 q=100` and `legend-sleep-strip.webp 1536x208 q=100` — the q=100 claim is exact. `grep -l legend-spritesheet live/*.html` = 40 of 40, 2 occurrences per page, and the tags are literally `<img src="...legend-spritesheet.webp" alt="" width="1536" height="2288">` with no `loading` attribute (same for the sleep strip). probe-desktop.json `/`.perf.heaviest[0] = {u:"legend-spritesheet.webp", b:2043660}, and the next four are 462,271 / 448,652 / 319,605 / 190,604 — heavier than the next four combined and 4.4x the largest photograph. I re-ran the re-encode myself: `cwebp -q 90 -alpha_q 90` produced exactly 520,804 bytes, matching to the byte (a 1,522,556-byte saving; the encoder reports a 176-colour palette, which is why a lossy q=90 pass collapses it so far — this is flat cel art stored at near-lossless quality). live/main.css confirms `.legend-assistant__character{...width:118px;aspect-ratio:192/208}` with a mobile override to 96px, against a 1536px-wide source. Nothing in the docs sanctions the size or the eager load — LIVECHAT.md:52 and :224 only name the atlas and its verified rows, no ruling on encoding or loading. Two small evidence corrections that do not touch the substance: (a) the markup lives in template-parts/components/legend-assistant.php:15-16 (`$legend_sprite = get_theme_file_uri('/assets/images/assistant/legend-spritesheet.webp')`), not inc/legend-assistant.php — that file exists but does not emit the img, so the recommendation should target the component; (b) the two `<img>` per page share one URL, so the network cost is one fetch, which is what the finding's own de-duplicated 2,117 KB tally already assumes.

#### [171] On mobile the hero-video gate turns the visitor's first tap — including a tap on a CTA — into a 9.36 MB download

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The gate itself works and is exactly as documented; I verified it in code rather than trusting the docs. `template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:110` emits `preload="none"` with `<source data-src>` and no `src`, so nothing downloads until JS acts. `src/js/main.js:4821-4852` then computes `interactionOnly` from `smallViewport (<=860px) || saveData || effectiveType in [slow-2g,2g,3g] || prefers-reduced-motion`, and on desktop defers to `window load` + `requestIdleCallback(1800)`. The flaw is the interaction trigger: it binds `pointerdown`, `keydown` and `touchstart` on `window` with `{once:true}`, so any first interaction starts the 9,809,858-byte download — including tapping "Get an instant price", which navigates away. A phone user who arrives and immediately taps the CTA begins a 9.36 MB fetch that competes with the next page's navigation.
- **Recommendation:** Scope the trigger. Bind the interaction listener to the hero element rather than `window`, or require the pointer event to land inside `[data-fg-home-hero]` and not inside `.button-row` before calling `loadVideo()`. Add `if (!navigator.onLine) return;` and, cheaply, gate on `connection.downlink > 2`. Also add a `<source>` variant: a 720p encode of the hero for the `(max-width: 860px)` case, following the exact pattern `fenster_product_scrub_videos()` already uses for the scrub pair, so the mobile path is ~2-3 MB rather than 9.36 MB even when it does fire.
- **Why:** The gate was built to keep 9.36 MB off mobile (AI.md:38 — "do not make the 9.36 MB homepage video part of the initial mobile payload again"), and a window-level first-tap listener partially defeats it: the most common first tap on a mobile hero is the CTA sitting inside it.
- **Affected:** Homepage on all viewports <=860px and on saveData/2G/3G connections. assets/videos/home/fenster-home-hero.mp4 (9,809,858 B); src/js/main.js:4821-4852.
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:4844-4851: `if (interactionOnly) { const loadOnInteraction = () => loadVideo(); ['pointerdown','keydown','touchstart'].forEach((eventName) => { window.addEventListener(eventName, loadOnInteraction, {once:true, passive:true}); }); return; }`. Markup: home-experience.php:110 `<video ... preload="none" poster="..." data-fg-lazy-video data-fg-video-slow-mode="interaction"><source data-src="..." type="video/mp4"></video>`. stat: assets/videos/home/fenster-home-hero.mp4 = 9,809,858 B. Homepage CTAs `Get an instant price` / `Explore our products` sit inside the hero at home-experience.php:120-122.
- **Verification:** Reproduced independently and it is unambiguous. `grep -c preconnect` across all 40 live HTML files returns zero matches on every file. `grep -rn 'preconnect|dns-prefetch'` across the entire theme (PHP, JS, SCSS, excluding node_modules) returns ZERO hits — so the only dns-prefetch on the page is WordPress core's `//www.googletagmanager.com`, exactly as claimed, and nothing in the theme adds a hint dynamically either. The deferral is real: template-parts/sections/casement-windows-v2.php:654,660, template-parts/sections/quote-tool.php:56,63 and template-parts/sections/location-service.php:1238 all emit `data-quote-iframe-src` with `data-quote-autoload="near"|"idle"` and no src. Handshake timing reproduces: cold curl to windowsoftware.co.uk gave namelookup 0.225 / connect 0.247 / appconnect 0.280; warm-DNS repeat gave 0.005 / 0.022 / 0.045, i.e. 40 ms of TCP+TLS even with DNS cached and 280 ms cold — the finding's 74 ms is a warm-DNS best case and the real cold number is worse. lh3.googleusercontent.com: 0.031 / 0.049 / 0.073. Scope is very slightly overstated: probe-desktop shows 19 of 38 routes carrying a windowsoftware iframe (not 20), though 21 of the 40 live HTML files contain the origin. 30/40 files contain lh3.googleusercontent.com at 5 occurrences each — exact. AI.md:181 explicitly rules that the WindowCAD embed is deliberately NOT consent-gated ('What is gated is the measurement, not the service'), which strengthens rather than blocks this: the origin is always going to be hit, so a preconnect is free of consent complications.

#### [176] /aluminium-windows/ downloads 12.9 MB across 228 image requests for a 241-frame canvas story, and separately loads a 574 KB scrub video for a second motion system on the same page

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The desktop probe records 250 resources on this route with `byType.img = {n:228, bytes:12,908,412}` and `byType.video = {n:1, bytes:573,629}` — by far the heaviest page on the site. The image bulk is `assets/videos/aluminium-windows-story/frames-desktop/`: 241 WebP frames at 1440x960, 12,246,326 bytes on disk, averaging 51 KB (mobile set: 241 frames, 6.3 MB). The loader in src/js/main.js:4960-4990 is well built — frame 0, then a skeleton of every 24th frame, then a +/-14 window around the current frame — so nothing is preloaded en masse, but a visitor who scrolls the story through downloads nearly all of it. Separately, `fenster_product_scrub_videos()` (inc/assets.php:244) also maps `aluminium-windows => prestige-window`, so the same page loads `prestige-window-scrub.mp4` (573,329 B) for the all-intra scrub treatment used on three OTHER routes. The two systems render in different sections — the canvas story is the hero (live HTML lines 108-119), the scrub sits in the product-intel figure (lines 359-360) — so this is not literal duplication, but the page pays for both motion techniques. The story renders on this one route only: `$is_aluminium_windows = $slug === 'aluminium-windows'` (generated-page.php:151), and /aluminium-windows-bletchley/ carries zero story markup. No ruling justifying the frame sequence over an mp4 appears in AI.md, HANDOVER.md or PROGRESS.md, though `fenster_preload_product_scroll_video()` special-cases the slug to preload frame-001.webp, so the choice was deliberate at some point.
- **Recommendation:** Ask the owner before changing anything, because this is the site's most elaborate scroll piece. Then measure the alternative: the project's own all-intra encoder (`scripts/encode-product-scroll-videos.cjs`) produces 573 KB for the prestige-window scrub, so a 241-frame 1440x960 all-intra mp4 should land around 1.5-2.5 MB against 12.2 MB of frames — a 5-8x reduction with the same seek-per-scroll-frame behaviour the comments in inc/assets.php explicitly designed for. Re-encoding the frames instead is not worth it: `cwebp -q 70` on frame-060 only goes 60,086 -> 53,092 bytes (12%). If the frames must stay, halve the count to 120 and interpolate (~6.1 MB). Note that any deletion sweep over `assets/` must exclude these frames — they are referenced only programmatically (see the correction to finding 179).
- **Why:** The main product pages are the highest-intent traffic on the site and they hand the office the least information. It also breaks the sales script: a caller who came from the heritage page gets asked which product they were looking at.
- **Affected:** 10 of 15 audited product routes; the same hidden field feeds the saved `fenster_enquiry` post and the email.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:5352; template-parts/sections/location-service.php:1471; live HTML: /heritage-windows/ `name="project_type" value="Residential windows and doors"` vs /casement-windows-bletchley/ `value="uPVC casement windows in Bletchley"`.
- **Verification:** The measurements reproduce almost exactly, but three details are wrong and the type classification is wrong. CONFIRMED: probe-desktop `/aluminium-windows/`.perf.byType is precisely {img:{n:228,bytes:12908412}, video:{n:1,bytes:573629}}, resources 250; frames-desktop holds 241 WebPs summing to 12,246,326 B (avg 50,814 B = 51 KB); frames-mobile 241 files; frame-060.webp is 60,086 B on disk; inc/assets.php:244 maps 'aluminium-windows' => $scrub('prestige-window'); fenster_preload_product_scroll_video() special-cases the slug at inc/assets.php:349 to preload frames-desktop/frame-001.webp; the loader at src/js/main.js:4960-4990 works exactly as described (loadFrame(0,true), every 24th frame skeleton, +/-14 window in handleScroll). Live HTML confirms BOTH systems render on the one page: the canvas story at live/aluminium-windows.html:108-119 and the scrub <source> pair at lines 359-360. I searched all *.md for a ruling on the frame sequence and found only AUDIT.md:87 (a deployment verification note), so the 'no ruling found' claim holds. CORRECTIONS: (1) '12,504 KB total' is the `du -sk` block-padded figure; the real byte sum is 12,246,326 B (11.68 MiB). (2) 'the all-intra scrub treatment used on four other routes' is wrong — fenster_product_scrub_videos() returns exactly four entries INCLUDING aluminium-windows, so three other routes. (3) 'and its town variants if the story renders there' resolves to no: $is_aluminium_windows = $slug === 'aluminium-windows' (generated-page.php:151), and I curled https://fensterglazing.com/aluminium-windows-bletchley/ — zero occurrences of 'aluminium-windows-story'. Scope is exactly one route. (4) Type should be Objective, not Creative: 12.9 MB with a named, project-owned encoder producing the same seek-per-scroll behaviour at ~1/6 the bytes is a measurable performance defect with a specific fix, not a preference. The 'ask the owner first' caution is correct process, but it does not make the defect a matter of taste.

#### [165] No preconnect to the quote tool's origin — the conversion iframe pays a full DNS+TCP+TLS handshake before it can start

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The instant-quote iframe on 20 of the 38 sampled routes points at `https://www.windowsoftware.co.uk/windowcad7/`. The deferral itself is well built — the iframe carries `data-quote-iframe-src` with no `src`, and the wrapper carries `data-quote-autoload="near"` (product pages) or `"idle"` (/online-quote/), so nothing loads until it is needed. But there is no resource hint for that origin anywhere on the site: I grepped all 40 live pages for `preconnect` and found zero, and the only hint present is `<link rel='dns-prefetch' href='//www.googletagmanager.com' />`. So at the moment the visitor scrolls the quote tool into view, the browser has to do DNS, TCP and TLS from cold before the first byte. From this machine that is 34 ms DNS + 16 ms TCP + 24 ms TLS = 74 ms; on a mobile network it is routinely 200-400 ms. The same applies to `lh3.googleusercontent.com`, which serves 5 hotlinked Google review avatars on 30 of the 40 pages.
- **Recommendation:** Add to `fenster_render_critical_head_assets()` in `inc/assets.php`, gated to routes that actually render the embed: `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://www.windowsoftware.co.uk" crossorigin>`. Add `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://lh3.googleusercontent.com" crossorigin>` on routes carrying the review showcase — or better, cache the 5 avatars locally as 88x88 WebP alongside the review text in `inc/google-reviews.php`, which removes the third-party origin entirely. Upgrade the googletagmanager `dns-prefetch` to a `preconnect` since it is always used when tracking is allowed.
- **Why:** The quote tool is the site's primary conversion mechanism and the handshake is unavoidable dead time in front of it. A preconnect is one line and removes 200-400 ms from the moment a mobile visitor decides to price a job.
- **Affected:** 20 of 38 sampled routes carry the quote iframe; 30 of 40 carry hotlinked Google avatars (5 each).
- **Evidence:** probe iframes: 20 routes with src `https://www.windowsoftware.co.uk/windowcad7/?interface=retail&username=fensterglazing...`, all `loading:"lazy"`. Live markup uses `data-quote-iframe-src` (no src) with `data-quote-autoload="near"|"idle"`. `grep -c preconnect live/*.html` -> no matches on any of 40 files; the only hint is dns-prefetch to googletagmanager. curl timing to windowsoftware.co.uk cold: time_namelookup 0.034, time_connect 0.050, time_appconnect 0.074. 30/40 live pages contain lh3.googleusercontent.com, 5 avatars each.
- **Verification:** Head placement, blocking status, byte sizes and the claim that nothing but the plugin consumes jQuery all reproduce exactly, and I found positive confirmation that jquery-migrate is genuinely executing (its startup banner is in the live console on every load). One practical caveat for whoever acts on it, which raises the effort rather than changing the verdict: `contact-form-v2-master` is NOT in this repo — the git tree is theme-only, and `find` across the whole project returns no `plugins` directory — so recommendation (1), rewriting the plugin's ~10 jQuery call sites in vanilla JS, is an off-repo change with no deploy guard and no checksum coverage, unlike everything else in this audit. Recommendation (2), moving jQuery to the footer from `inc/assets.php`, stays entirely inside the guarded theme and is the lower-risk first step; dropping jquery-migrate alone is 13,577 B / 4,677 B brotli for near-zero risk.

#### [168] Lenis smooth scroll runs a permanent rAF loop on every page including pages with no scroll animation

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `src/js/main.js:2810-2830` instantiates Lenis unconditionally for anyone not in `prefers-reduced-motion`, with `autoRaf: true`, `smoothWheel: true` and `lerp: 0.075`. I bundled the library on its own with the project's esbuild: 17,624 bytes minified, 4,545 brotli — about 11% of the compiled bundle. `autoRaf: true` means a `requestAnimationFrame` loop runs continuously for the lifetime of the page, so the browser never reaches an idle state and scrolling is driven from the main thread rather than natively. I confirmed it is active on routes with no scroll choreography at all: /meet-the-team/ reports `data-lenis-ready="true"`.
- **Recommendation:** Two options depending on how load-bearing the feel is. If smooth scroll is a design commitment, at least stop it running where nothing needs it: instantiate only when the document contains a scroll-driven component (`[data-fg-aw-story], [data-fg-scrub-video], [data-scroll-video], [data-fg-chapter-stack], [data-fg-product-theatre]`) or an in-page anchor target, and use `lenis.stop()`/`start()` on `visibilitychange`. If it is not a commitment, `scroll-behavior: smooth` plus `scroll-padding-top` (already set to 88px in the critical CSS) covers the anchor-offset case Lenis is configured for (`anchors:{offset:-88}`) natively, for zero bytes and zero main-thread cost. Check STYLE.md before removing, since scroll feel is a design decision.
- **Why:** A permanent rAF loop on 712 pages costs battery on mobile, keeps the main thread awake, and routes wheel input through JS, which is a known source of scroll jank and INP regressions. On pages like /meet-the-team/ or /fensa-approved-installers/ there is nothing for it to drive.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes for visitors without prefers-reduced-motion. src/js/main.js:1 (import), :2810-2830 (instantiation).
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:2811 `const lenis = new Lenis({anchors:{offset:-88}, autoRaf:true, lerp:0.075, smoothWheel:true, syncTouch:false, wheelMultiplier:0.95, prevent:...})`, guarded only by `if (!window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches)`. Bundled standalone with the project's esbuild: 17,624 B minified, 4,545 B brotli. Live check on https://fensterglazing.com/meet-the-team/: `document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-lenis-ready')` === "true". Bundle string `var eo="1.3.25"` at the head of the compiled main.js confirms Lenis 1.3.25 is inlined.
- **Verification:** The headline measurement reproduces to within 1 KB when recomputed from disk rather than from the finding's own script, the srcset counts are exactly right, and all four cited srcset precedents are real code at the exact lines given. Three precision corrections that do not change impact, scope or type. (a) The helper citation `inc/assets.php:120-146` is off — that range is `fenster_image_dimensions()`; `fenster_image_attr_string()` is at :136-158, and the description of it (emits src, decoding, width, height and nothing else) is correct. (b) "5-2.png and 7.png are 2,430x2,430 PNGs at 2.4 MB each" — 5-2.png is 2,505,871 B, but 7.png is 2,206,799 B, i.e. 2.1 MB. (c) "the 17 team/installer headshots … are 2.1-2.9 MB PNGs at 2025-2430 px square" overstates the batch: only 7 of them are PNGs in that range (17.2 MB combined); the other 10 are JPGs between 268 KB and 814 KB (5.6 MB). The ~22 MB saving still holds because the 7 PNGs carry most of it, and prioritising by measured saving — as the recommendation already says — puts those 7 first regardless.

#### [170] The mobile LCP on the homepage is a 1600x1600 JPEG video poster served at one resolution — but it is a <video poster> attribute, so it cannot take a srcset

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** High · **Confidence:** 80% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** L · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `inc/assets.php:60-66` preloads `assets/images/imported/home-hero-poster.jpg` with `fetchpriority="high"`, which is exactly right, and then serves one 1600x1600, 174,788-byte JPEG to every device. The mobile fold screenshot confirms the poster, not the video, is what a phone user sees, which is the documented intent (AI.md:38: 'Keep the poster as the mobile/slow-network first visual'). At DPR 3 a 390 px hero needs ~1170 px; WebP q78 at 1170w measures 56,510 B, so a phone is over-served by 118 KB on its LCP resource. The complication the finding must carry: `template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:110` emits this as `<video ... preload="none" poster="...">`, and `poster` accepts a single URL. There is no <img> in the hero, so a srcset has nowhere to live, and putting `imagesrcset` on the preload alone would fetch a variant the poster never uses on top of the poster itself. Note also that 1600x1600 is not oversized on desktop — the hero is object-fit:cover at full viewport width, so a 1920px display is already upscaling this source.
- **Recommendation:** The safe, no-risk change is a format swap, not a responsive one: encode `home-hero-poster.webp` at the same 1600x1600 (measured 82,106 B, saves 92,682 B on every device), point `$hero_poster` at it in template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:39, and change the preload in inc/assets.php:63 from `type="image/jpeg"` to `type="image/webp"`. Per AI.md:959 the new extension is already a new filename so cached browsers pick it up. If you want the further 26 KB on mobile, that needs a structural change, not an attribute: replace the `poster` attribute with a real `<img class="fg-home-hero__poster" srcset="...828w, ...1170w, ...1920w" sizes="100vw" fetchpriority="high">` layered under the video, hide it once the lazy video starts playing, and switch the preload to `imagesrcset`/`imagesizes` matching that exact srcset. Do NOT add `imagesrcset` to the preload while the `poster` attribute is still in place — the browser will download both the preloaded candidate and the poster.
- **Why:** 12.9 MB on a single product route is by far the heaviest page on the site, and the page is already carrying a second, cheaper motion system that does the same job elsewhere. Whichever survives, the page should not pay for both.
- **Affected:** /aluminium-windows/ (and its town variants if the story renders there). assets/videos/aluminium-windows-story/frames-desktop/ (12,504 KB), frames-mobile/ (6,448 KB), assets/videos/product-scroll/prestige-window-scrub.mp4 (573,329 B).
- **Evidence:** probe-desktop `/aluminium-windows/`.perf.byType = {img:{n:228,bytes:12908412}, video:{n:1,bytes:573629}}, resources:250. `ls | wc -l` on frames-desktop = 241 files, 12,504 KB (avg 51 KB); frames-mobile 241 files, 6,448 KB. magick identify frame-060.webp = 1440x960 q=92 60,086 B; cwebp -q 70 -> 53,092 B. inc/assets.php `fenster_product_scrub_videos()` returns 'aluminium-windows' => prestige-window scrub pair; `fenster_preload_product_scroll_video()` special-cases the slug to preload frames-desktop/frame-001.webp.
- **Verification:** Every number reproduces, but the recommended mechanism cannot be implemented as written and would cause a double download if attempted. CONFIRMED: `magick identify` gives home-hero-poster.jpg = JPEG 1600x1600, 174,788 B; probe-desktop and probe-mobile both list it in /.perf.heaviest at 175,088 B; inc/assets.php:60-66 is the preload, gated on is_front_page()||is_home(), with `as="image" type="image/jpeg" fetchpriority="high"` and no imagesrcset; my own magick re-runs reproduce 56,510 B at 1170w q78 and 82,106 B at full size q78; AI.md:38 says verbatim 'Keep the poster as the mobile/slow-network first visual', and shots/mobile/home--fold.png shows the poster frame filling the hero. WHAT IS WRONG: the poster is NOT an <img>. template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:110 emits `<video class="fg-home-hero__video" ... preload="none" poster="..." data-fg-lazy-video>`. The `poster` attribute takes a single URL — there is no srcset/sizes on it, and there is no fallback <img> anywhere in the hero. So 'put srcset/sizes on the hero image' has no element to attach to, and adding `imagesrcset`/`imagesizes` to the preload while the poster attribute still resolves to one fixed URL makes the browser fetch a preloaded variant the poster never uses and then fetch the poster too — a net regression, not a saving. SECOND CORRECTION: 1600x1600 is not oversized on desktop. The hero is `object-fit: cover` at full viewport width (critical CSS, inc/assets.php), so on a 1920px desktop a 1600px-wide source is already being upscaled. The '118 KB more than it needs' figure is mobile-only; the saving available without any responsive plumbing is 92,682 B (same-dimension WebP q78).

#### [173] 43.2 MB of images in the theme are referenced by nothing, inside a 347 MB assets directory

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `assets/` totals 347 MB, of which `assets/images/` is the bulk: 150 PNGs at 188.0 MB, 478 JPEGs at 105.6 MB, 1,160 WebPs at 74.3 MB. I cross-referenced every image filename on disk against every filename string appearing in any `.php`, `.json`, `.js` or `.scss` file in the theme. 920 files totalling 43.2 MB match no reference anywhere. Because the matcher is deliberately loose (bare filename, not full path), it over-counts references, so 43.2 MB is a floor, not an estimate. The unreferenced set is concentrated in `assets/images/imported/`, which also holds the largest files on the site — `Untitled-design-16.png` at 16.65 MB, `2-2-2.png` at 9.98 MB, `5-1.png` at 9.09 MB, three county map PNGs at 3.5-4.2 MB each.

Move `assets/images/imported/` behind an explicit allow-list: keep only the files that `inc/site-data.php`, `inc/case-studies-data.php`, `inc/commercial-product-data.php` and the templates actually name, and archive the rest outside the theme. Re-run the reference sweep with full paths rather than bare filenames before deleting anything — the registry-sprawl problem recorded in project memory (a name lives in 6-7 registries that never check each other) applies here, and `assets/images/imported/` is exactly the kind of directory where a stray reference hides.
- **Why:** Low direct performance impact, but 347 MB of theme assets slows every deploy and every backup, and the presence of 2-16 MB source PNGs in the same folder as the live team photographs is how those PNGs ended up shipping at 2.4-2.8 MB in the first place.
- **Affected:** assets/ (347 MB); assets/images/imported/ (356 files) is the main offender.
- **Evidence:** du by extension across assets/: png 150 files 188.0 MB, jpg 478 files 105.6 MB, webp 1,160 files 74.3 MB. Filename cross-reference against all theme .php/.json/.js/.scss: 868 referenced (324.7 MB), 920 unreferenced (43.2 MB). Largest files: Untitled-design-16.png 16.65 MB, 2-2-2.png 9.98 MB, 5-1.png 9.09 MB, 3-2-2.png 8.62 MB, 1-2-2.png 8.60 MB — of these, only 5-1.png appears in any of the 40 live pages.

Brace boundaries verified: `document.querySelectorAll('[data-fg-blind-visualiser]')` is at src/js/main.js:3258 and the next top-level controller `[data-fg-colour-carousel]` is at 4458, so 3258-4456 is the block; `awk 'NR>=3258 && NR<=4456' | wc -c` = 52,831 B exactly as claimed. Running the project's own node_modules/.bin/esbuild --minify on that extract gives 17,978 B and brotli -q 11 gives 5,962 B — both exact to the byte. I then did the check the finding did not do, minifying the whole source with and without those lines: brotli goes 32,215 -> 26,527, a real in-context saving of 5,688 B, so the standalone figure is not inflated by losing the shared dictionary. Attribute presence across the 40 live files is exact on all nine: blind-visualiser 1, case-studies-archive 1, chapter-stack 1, obscure-glass 1, aw-story 1, colour-rail 1, consultation-booking 1, integral-blinds-reveal 0, product-video-final 0. Both dead-code claims hold: `grep -rn 'fg-integral-blinds-reveal' --include=*.php` returns zero while src/js/main.js:1292 still queries it; and inc/assets.php:178-181 has `fenster_product_scroll_videos(): array { return []; }` under a docblock (inc/assets.php:160-176) that says verbatim 'This map is empty and the traveller therefore renders nowhere' and 'If it is still empty next time someone reads this, it is worth deleting properly' — the source itself invites the deletion. TWO NON-LOAD-BEARING CORRECTIONS. Raw bundle is 139,580 B not 138,830 (md5 of the live main.js matches the repo copy, so this is not a stale-file issue, just a mis-measure); the compressed figures however are RIGHT and better sourced than they look — curl with Accept-Encoding gzip/br against the live URL returns 47,211 and 39,739, matching the finding's 47,057/39,594 to within 0.3%, so those are real transfer sizes rather than local -9 output (my local gzip -9 gives 41,924, which would have understated the problem). And '~54 top-level querySelectorAll guards' is 39 at column zero (51 occurrences of document.querySelectorAll( anywhere in the file). Neither affects the conclusion.

#### [162] Four project docs describe an async/preload main stylesheet that was deliberately removed on 2026-07-09, leaving an orphaned 2,189-byte critical-CSS block that can no longer help

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** L · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** AI.md:38, HANDOVER.md:329, HANDOVER.md:1281 and PROGRESS.md:4511 all state that the main stylesheet is preloaded and activated asynchronously with a noscript fallback alongside inline critical CSS. That code was deleted on purpose in commit 76f5510d (2026-07-09, "Load main stylesheet normally for Clarity replay"), as part of the Microsoft Clarity replay fix recorded at PROGRESS.md:4405-4413. `inc/assets.php:20-25` is now a plain `wp_enqueue_style`, the only surviving `style_loader_tag` filter (`fenster_unmask_stylesheet_for_clarity`, :36-44) just adds a Clarity attribute, the live head emits `<link rel='stylesheet' id='fenster-main-css' … media='all'>`, and Chrome reports renderBlockingStatus "blocking" for it. The consequence is that the 2,189-byte inline critical CSS block in `fenster_render_critical_head_assets()` (:46-75) is dead weight on all 712 routes — nothing can paint before main.css arrives, so the critical rules never get a chance to apply. The defect is therefore twofold: four documents send the next reader looking for an optimisation that was deliberately dropped, and half of that optimisation was left behind.
- **Recommendation:** Fix the docs first, because they are the part that actively misleads: amend AI.md:38, HANDOVER.md:329, HANDOVER.md:1281 and PROGRESS.md:4511 to say the stylesheet loads normally, and record why (commit 76f5510d — Clarity replay needs a real `<link>` it can resolve). Then decide the critical block on its own merits. The cheap, safe move is to keep only the weight-400 `@font-face` (it is what makes the Gibson-Regular preload match anything before main.css parses — see finding 163) and delete the remaining ~1.9 KB of layout rules, which cannot run. Do NOT restore the preload/onload/noscript filter as a first move: it is exactly what was removed for Clarity, so any attempt to bring it back has to be re-tested against a live Clarity recording before it ships, and the critical block would have to be expanded to cover the first viewport of all four template shapes rather than just the home hero.
- **Why:** Mobile visitors on the worst pages download 10-19 MB of images to look at pictures rendered 88-381 px wide. It is the largest recoverable byte total on the site after the Legend sprite, and the helper and the srcset pattern both already exist — this is completing work that was started on three routes and never finished.
- **Affected:** 35 of 38 sampled routes have zero srcset; extrapolates to essentially all 712. Worst: /meet-the-team/, /window-and-door-repairs/, /double-glazing-milton-keynes/, /commercial-glazing/, /obscured-glass/, /about/, /contact/, /case-studies/.
- **Evidence:** probe images.withSrcset: 0 on 35/38 routes; 6 (casement), 10 (sliding-sash), 73 (composite-doors). Measured resize test (magick -resize {2*disp} -quality 82 webp) summed per page over resolvable oversized entries >40 KB: desktop /meet-the-team/ 23,341 KB -> 1,498 KB; mobile /meet-the-team/ 19,119 -> 584; desktop total across 38 pages 146.2 MB -> 23.7 MB. Individual: Untitled-design-36.png 2,828 KB (2025x2025) at disp 381 -> 25 KB webp; 2-4.png 2,813 KB (2430x2430) at disp 364 -> 22 KB; adam-butcher-scaled.jpg 483 KB (1829x2560) at disp 381 -> 12 KB. probe-mobile /window-and-door-repairs/ oversized: {nat:2430, disp:88} for both 7.png and 5-2.png.
- **Verification:** Every measurement reproduces, but the diagnosis is wrong on two counts. (1) It is not a regression. `git log --oneline -- inc/assets.php` shows commit 76f5510d, 2026-07-09, "Load main stylesheet normally for Clarity replay", which deletes exactly the `fenster_defer_main_stylesheet` filter the docs describe (`rel=preload as=style onload=this.rel='stylesheet'` + `<noscript>`). It was removed on purpose, on the same day as the Microsoft Clarity Replay Rendering Fix recorded at PROGRESS.md:4405-4413 and at HANDOVER.md ("Keep this ordering and markup intact"). So the recommendation to "restore async activation" is the one option that must NOT be taken by default — it would reopen the Clarity replay problem that motivated the deletion. (2) The claim that this is "the direct cause of the duplicate font downloads reported separately" is false: finding 163's duplication is a URL mismatch (`?ver=` vs no query) between the preload/critical `@font-face` and main.css's `@font-face`, and would occur identically under async CSS. What IS real and worth reporting is the documentation drift plus the orphaned critical block. Citation nits: the surviving filter is at inc/assets.php:36-44 (not 34-43) and the critical block at :46-75 (not 45-79); the enqueue at :20-25 is exact. Also add HANDOVER.md:1281 to the stale-doc list — it says "The main stylesheet is loaded through a preload/activate pattern", a fourth place the docs are wrong. Impact drops to Low: the recoverable cost is 2,189 bytes per page and reader-misdirection, not a render-path change.

#### [48] 407 of 525 town-matrix pages have exactly one internal in-link, because the related-links gate checks a scrape file the matrix is not in

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 98% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `$route_exists()` at template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:1946-1948 returns true only if the target slug is a key of `fenster_generated_pages_index()` (data/pages.json) or of `$virtual_page_titles` (4 static keys at :1503-1508 plus every commercial county slug added at :1509-1511). The town matrix is generated virtually by `fenster_location_matrix_page()`, and only 106 of its 525 routes survive in the legacy scrape file, so the related-links builder silently drops the other 419. Per town, data/pages.json holds ampthill 12, aylesbury 4, bedford 1, buckingham 1, dunstable 3, flitwick 11, hitchin 15, leighton-buzzard 1, letchworth 12, luton 4, northampton 14, stevenage 17, toddington 11 — and ZERO for all 12 Milton Keynes suburbs. Measured live: /double-glazing-hitchin/ links 14 of its own Hitchin product pages, /double-glazing-stevenage/ 15, /double-glazing-ampthill/ 11, while /double-glazing-bletchley/, /double-glazing-wolverton/ and /double-glazing-whitehouse/ link 0 of their own 20 (all six bands are capped at 24 anchors, and the MK ones burn several on duplicates — doors-milton-keynes, composite-doors and aluminium-bifold-doors each appear twice). A content-only in-link graph over all 712 crawled pages shows 407 of the 525 matrix routes have exactly ONE internal in-link site-wide, always /areas-we-cover/ — 240 of them MK-suburb product pages, 167 elsewhere. /areas-we-cover/ has one content in-link of its own (the homepage). This directly inverts the site's own plan: HIGH-INTENT-SEARCH-PLAN.md:202 puts the 12 MK suburbs in Tier 1 for 'full investment... internal links', and :204 puts Hitchin, Stevenage, Northampton, Luton, Letchworth and Toddington in Tier 3 with 'Do not add internal links' — yet the far ring is the only tier receiving them.

(a) `$virtual_page_titles` is not a 4-entry array: generated-page.php:1503-1508 has 4 static keys, then :1509-1511 loops every `$commercial_county_pages` slug into it (~51 total). TWO ADDITIONS THAT STRENGTHEN IT. #### [33] FAQPage schema missing from the entire 525-URL town matrix (74% of the sitemap), all 3 product hubs and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** 25 of the 40 Tier-1 pages render a visible FAQ accordion. 20 of them emit FAQPage JSON-LD; 5 do not — and those 5 are template-level, not one-off. `/windows-milton-keynes/`, `/doors-milton-keynes/` and `/other-services/` each render `fg-ph-faq` with 4 questions and emit only BreadcrumbList + HomeAndConstructionBusiness. `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` renders `fg-location-faq` with 5 questions and the same. `/casement-windows-bletchley/` renders `fg-location-faq` with 4 questions and the same — and that is the `location-service.php` template that serves the whole town matrix. The cause is structural: generated-page.php:339 excludes `$is_location_service` from `$use_product_journey`, and `$use_product_journey` is the gate on the only FAQPage builder in the file (:5015); :2124 hands location routes off to location-service.php and returns before ever reaching it. Confirmed live and not a probe artefact: curling https://fensterglazing.com/composite-doors-wolverton/ (200, 137KB) returns `class="fg-location-faq"` and zero occurrences of the string `FAQPage`, with only BreadcrumbList, HomeAndConstructionBusiness and a Service/Offer catalogue in the graph.
- **Recommendation:** Emit the same FAQPage graph the product template already builds at generated-page.php:5015-5030, in `template-parts/sections/location-service.php` (covers the town matrix and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/) and in `template-parts/sections/product-hub.php`, which renders `fg-ph-faq` (covers /windows-milton-keynes/, /doors-milton-keynes/, /other-services/). Extract the existing builder into a shared function rather than writing a second one, so the two cannot drift — and carry over the per-route question cap, which generated-page.php:4995-5012 records has already silently sliced correctly-written FAQs off three routes.
- **Why:** 525 of the site's 712 URLs are matrix routes. Their internal-link graph is currently a function of which scrape-era records happened to survive, not of which pages exist. Google discovers and weights these pages largely through internal links, and today a Bletchley page passes all its product equity to ten competing towns and none to its own. This is the single largest structural defect I found and the fix is two lines against helpers that already exist.
- **Affected:** template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:1512-1529 and :1946-1948; affects the related-links band on all 525 matrix routes (419 links suppressed, 12 of 25 towns mis-linked)
- **Evidence:** generated-page.php:1946 `return $target_slug === 'home' || isset($generated_pages[$target_slug]) || isset($virtual_page_titles[$target_slug]);`. Computed: 525 matrix routes in urls.txt, 106 present in data/pages.json, 419 absent. Live fetch of https://fensterglazing.com/casement-windows-luton/ fg-links-band = 20 links, 2 Luton-local; https://fensterglazing.com/casement-windows-bletchley/ fg-links-band = 26 links, 0 Bletchley-local, 10 to other towns.
- **Verification:** Every specific claim reproduces, and the scope claim is the only thing wrong — it is badly understated. Confirmed across scratchpad/live/*.html: 25 of the 40 pages render a visible FAQ block, 20 emit FAQPage JSON-LD, and the 5 that do not are exactly /windows-milton-keynes/, /doors-milton-keynes/, /other-services/ (all `fg-ph-faq`, 4 questions), /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ and /casement-windows-bletchley/ (both `fg-location-faq`). Confirmed live and not a probe artefact: my own curl of https://fensterglazing.com/composite-doors-wolverton/ returned 200/137,244 bytes, contains `fg-location-faq`, `fg-location-faq__grid` and `fg-location-faq__items`, and `grep -c FAQPage` = 0; its schema graph is BreadcrumbList + HomeAndConstructionBusiness + GeoCoordinates + OfferCatalog + 20 Service/Offer pairs. Confirmed the routing: generated-page.php:317-318 sets `$is_location_service`, :2124 hands off to location-service.php and returns, and :339 excludes `$is_location_service` from `$use_product_journey` — which is the gate on the only FAQPage builder in that file, at :5015. Where the finding is wrong: the town matrix is 25 towns (generated-pages.php:50-77) x 21 products (:81-105) = 525 combinations, and 526 slugs in urls.txt match that pattern — 74% of the 712-URL sitemap, not 'at least 238'. AI.md:43 is cited correctly and does name /windows-milton-keynes/, /doors-milton-keynes/ and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ as impression-holding pages to prioritise. No doc rules FAQ schema off location pages; AI.md:271 and HANDOVER.md:457 describe FAQPage as intended on FAQ-bearing pages, and AI.md:271's only prohibition is on aggregateRating/Review.

#### [181] 47 orphan pages — six of them produce 34% of all organic clicks, and /blog/ is one of them

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Across a full 712-page crawl, 75 URLs receive zero inbound internal links from any crawled page. 28 of those are false positives: /commercial-areas/ (HTTP 200, `noindex,follow`, deliberately absent from the sitemap per AI.md and therefore never crawled) links 47 commercial-glazing county pages, and Google follows links on noindex,follow pages. Live /blog/ has 2 linked headings against 12 total, so 10 cards are dead text — and /blog/ itself is orphaned, making the whole informational library invisible to internal crawl. SEO-AUDIT.md F2 fixed the /areas-we-cover/ orphan in July but never swept the class; /replacing-windows-doors-in-wolverton-mk/, which F2 itself named as an orphan proof-page, is still one.
- **Recommendation:** Three changes. (a) In generated-simple.php, give every imported card a `url` (the slug is already the card's identity) so /blog/ becomes a real hub, and raise the `array_slice($cards, 0, $is_archive ? 18 : 8)` cap at line 62 or paginate. (b) Link /blog/ from the footer alongside /case-studies/. (c) Add /3d-visualiser/ to the link-card set on /online-quote/, /composite-doors/, /upvc-doors/ and /windows-milton-keynes/, and make the guide-to-money-page links two-way (/what-is-a-door-lintel/ -> /doors-milton-keynes/ currently exists in one direction only). - **Why:** Half a documented fix is worse than none: the site now publishes one side of a misleading comparison and has removed the other, so nothing on the page corrects the impression.
- **Affected:** /aluminium-windows/ and its ~20 town matrix routes.
- **Evidence:** inc/site-data.php:308 vs the comment at inc/site-data.php:316-330; live pulse strip on /aluminium-windows/ reads "Outer frame 72mm".
- **Verification:** The mechanism and every high-value instance are CONFIRMED, but the headline count of 75 overstates the true orphan set by 60% because the crawl only covers sitemap URLs. I rebuilt the inbound graph independently from scratchpad/all/ (712 files, all 712 with a canonical, exact href="https://fensterglazing.com/..." matches, trailing-slash normalised) and got exactly 75 zero-source URLs — the same list, including all six named earners, /blog/, /3d-visualiser/ and /replacing-windows-doors-in-wolverton-mk/. I also verified there are ZERO relative internal hrefs anywhere in the crawl, so the absolute-URL matcher is sound. THE FLAW: 28 of the 75 are the commercial-glazing county pages, and they are linked. /commercial-areas/ returns 200 with `robots: noindex,follow`, is absent from page-sitemap.xml (hence never crawled, hence its outbound links invisible to the graph), and carries 47 unique href links to commercial-glazing-* county pages. I fetched it plus the other AI.md-documented non-sitemap utility pages (gallery, downloads, videos, customer-portal, refer-a-friend, brochures, fenster-partners) and matched them against the orphan list: 28 of the 75 are covered, all from /commercial-areas/. Google follows links on noindex,follow pages, so those 28 are not orphans in the sense that matters. True orphan count: 47. Also relevant: AI.md records '/commercial-areas/ removed from public navigation' as a deliberate launch SEO-hardening decision, so the county pages' thin link posture is partly by design, whereas the informational orphans are not. EVERYTHING ELSE CONFIRMED: /blog/ markup has 2 linked <h3><a> against 12 <h3> total, i.e. 10 unlinked cards; generated-simple.php builds imported cards with no 'url' key at lines 37-43, the scheduled-post branch adds 'url' at line 56, the comment 'Only these cards carry a URL, so only they render linked' is at lines 45-46, and the cap is `array_slice($cards, 0, $is_archive ? 18 : 8)` at line 62; grep -c '3d-visualiser' over all 712 crawl files returns exactly one file (itself, 5 self-references); click figures match SEO-LEAD-AUDIT §3 exactly (158+136+60+57+45+25 = 481) and the 1,397 total is confirmed at that document's lines 46 and 89, so 34.4% is right. AI.md's SEO directive independently names /3d-visualiser/ and /soundproof-windows/ as internal-link priorities and AI.md:349 treats orphaning as a bug ('leaves it orphaned, which is the same three-registry problem'), so this is not an owner ruling. Impact High stands.

- **Problem:** The 525-page matrix (25 towns x 21 products) is not a network, it is an island hanging off /areas-we-cover/.
