At the other end, double-glazing-<town> averages 21.7 sources because every one of the town's other 20 product pages links to it. The distribution by town is the damning part: all 12 Milton Keynes suburb pages — the routes the 22 July plan built with genuine local content, where proximity is a real advantage — average exactly 2.0 inbound links, against Stevenage 17.8, Hitchin 16.1 and Northampton 14.8. That is backwards. (Note the split is not simply MK-versus-out-of-area: Bedford, Buckingham and Leighton Buzzard are also at 2.0.) There is a suggestive but NOT exclusive correlation with rankings: double-glazing is the best-linked family and SEO-LEAD-AUDIT §2 records double glazing wolverton 7->1, northampton 100->17, bedford 100->29, stony stratford 100->34. But the same table also records `bifold doors newport pagnell 8 -> 2` and `bifold doors milton keynes 15 -> 5` in the aluminium-bifold-doors family, so link count is not the only variable moving.
- **Recommendation:** Do NOT prune or noindex the matrix yet — the 0.118% CTR at position 32.8 is confounded with the link starvation and you cannot tell them apart. Run a controlled test, but run it on a family that actually has the zero signal: use one of the four families measured at exactly 1.0 inbound (aluminium-flush-windows-*, slide-fold-doors-*, aluminium-sliding-doors-* or heritage-aluminium-doors-*), NOT aluminium-bifold-doors-* or composite-doors-*, which already average 7.2 and 8.6 sources and would confound the result. Add a same-town sibling block to every page in the chosen family listing the other 20 products in that town — the data already exists, since $area_groups is built per town at generated-page.php:1624-1656 but rendered only inside the `if ($slug === 'areas-we-cover')` guard at :1531/:1762 — and re-measure that family's average position at the October GSC export against double-glazing-* as control. If position does not move by 8+ places in a quarter, then prune. Also raise or remove the 24-link caps at generated-page.php:3449, location-service.php:1443 and commercial-county.php:268 that are doing the truncating.
- **Why:** Price is the first question and the top FAQ on the one page that answers it. Twelve of thirteen pages send an undecided visitor either to a configurator or to a form. The internal-link gap also strands a page the site built specifically to rank for price queries.
- **Affected:** 13 of 15 product routes; /window-door-prices-milton-keynes/ has zero product-page inbound links.
- **Evidence:** Currency sweep across all 15 live pages: only composite-doors (£2,000/£5,000) and window-and-door-repairs (£96) contain a figure; grep of the 38 live pages shows window-door-prices-milton-keynes linked only from about.html, other-services.html and composite-door-prices.html; the price page's own checked examples read £600 / £2,000 / £3,500 inc VAT, checked July 2026.
- **Verification:** The quantitative core reproduces EXACTLY — I rebuilt the histogram independently and got {1:407, 15:3, 16:4, 21:8, 22:43, 23:60}, digit for digit, with all 407 single-source pages having /areas-we-cover/ as that one source, zero of the 525 slugs missing from the crawl. Per-family averages confirm the four starved families at exactly 1.0 across all 25 towns (aluminium-flush-windows, slide-fold-doors, aluminium-sliding-doors, heritage-aluminium-doors = 100 pages) and double-glazing at 21.7. Per-town averages confirm all 12 MK suburbs at exactly 2.0 against Stevenage 17.8, Hitchin 16.1, Northampton 14.8. The matrix is 25 towns x 21 products = 525 (generated-pages.php:50-105). All three link caps are real at the cited lines: generated-page.php:3449, location-service.php:1443, commercial-county.php:268, each `array_slice(..., 0, 24)`. $area_groups is built at generated-page.php:1624-1656 and rendered at :1762 inside `if ($slug === 'areas-we-cover')` (guard at :1531) — so the claim that the per-town product grouping exists but is never rendered on the matrix pages themselves is exactly right. The 0.118% CTR at position 32.8 is verbatim at SEO-LEAD-AUDIT:172. TWO REAL ERRORS. (1) 'the one product family that is properly linked is the one producing every ranking win' / 'that is the only family in which the rank tracker records wins' is contradicted by the finding's own source. SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md:54-64 also lists `bifold doors newport pagnell 8 -> 2` and `bifold doors milton keynes 15 -> 5`, and the aluminium-bifold-doors family averages 7.2 inbound links, not 1. The link/ranking correlation is directionally suggestive but it is not the clean exclusive it is presented as, and that exclusivity is what carries the argument. (2) The recommended test families are misdescribed: it says to pick a family 'with real query volume and zero current links (aluminium-bifold-doors-* or composite-doors-*)' — those measure 7.2 and 8.6 average inbound respectively. The genuine zero-signal families are the four at 1.0, which the finding itself correctly identifies two sentences earlier. Running the test on a family that already has 7-9 links would confound the very thing it is meant to isolate. Minor: /areas-we-cover/ carries 587 unique internal links, not 592; and 'against 15-19 for out-of-area towns' is selective — Bedford, Buckingham and Leighton Buzzard are also at 2.0, so the split is not MK-suburb versus out-of-area. The 'do not prune yet, run a controlled test' conclusion is sound and I would keep it.

Click figures: SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md §3 table.

#### [124] 32 of the 51 commercial county pages are orphaned by a 24-link cap that truncates the cross-link block alphabetically

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `template-parts/sections/commercial-county.php:268` renders `array_slice(array_values($related_links), 0, 24)`. `$related_links` is built in slug order, so every county page shows the same 24 links: 6 commercial service routes then counties Bedfordshire → Greater London. #### [72] BreadcrumbList is a flat Home > Page on every residential and matrix route, and no breadcrumb is rendered visually anywhere on 712 pages

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `inc/generated-pages.php:2479-2496` builds `$breadcrumb_items` with 'Home' and then, as the only intermediate rule, `if (str_starts_with($slug, 'commercial-glazing-'))` inserts 'Commercial Glazing'. Every other route gets two levels. Verified on live: /casement-windows-bletchley/ emits `[Home, uPVC Casement Windows Bletchley]` while /commercial-glazing-kent/ correctly emits `[Home, Commercial Glazing, Commercial Glazing Kent]`. PROGRESS.md:4612 records the intended behaviour as "rolling commercial county pages up to /commercial-glazing/ and residential product/location pages up to /areas-we-cover/" — the residential half is not implemented and the doc has drifted. Separately, 39 of 40 Tier-1 pages carry BreadcrumbList JSON-LD and zero pages carry any visual breadcrumb: `grep -o 'class="[^"]*breadcrumb[^"]*"'` and `aria-label="[Bb]readcrumb"` both return 0 matches across all 40 live HTML files. On a 712-page site with 525 pages three levels deep, no visual breadcrumb and no site search, a visitor landing from Google on /roof-lanterns-shenley-church-end/ has no in-page indication of where they are.
- **Recommendation:** In `generated-pages.php` extend the intermediate rule: if `fenster_slug_matches_location_matrix($slug)` insert [Areas We Cover, /areas-we-cover/] then the town hub [Double Glazing <Town>, /double-glazing-<town>/]; if the slug is a key of any `product_hub_groups` products list, insert its hub ([Windows, /windows-milton-keynes/] etc.); if the slug starts with `case-studies/`, insert [Case Studies, /case-studies/]. Then render the same array as a visible `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` strip directly under the header on the matrix, product and case-study routes (not the homepage or hubs). One data source, two outputs.
- **Why:** Google renders breadcrumb trails in the SERP; a 2-level trail for a 3-level site wastes the slot and tells Google the IA is flat. For users, a visible trail is the cheapest possible fix for the orientation problem on the 525 deep pages, and it doubles as the missing 'up' link to /areas-we-cover/.
- **Affected:** All 712 routes for the visual gap; ~660 routes for the flat schema (everything except the 47 commercial county pages). inc/generated-pages.php:2479-2496
- **Evidence:** generated-pages.php:2488 `if (str_starts_with($slug, 'commercial-glazing-') && $slug !== 'commercial-glazing')` is the sole intermediate rule; live JSON-LD /casement-windows-bletchley/ = 2 items, /commercial-glazing-kent/ = 3 items; 0/40 live HTML files contain a `breadcrumb` class or `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`; PROGRESS.md:4612 claims otherwise
- **Verification:** Every number reproduces exactly. Case-sensitive `grep -lE 'instant price|Instant pricing' *.html` over the 38 Tier-1 live pages returns exactly 23 files (the case-insensitive variant returns 24 — the finding used the case-sensitive form, which is what it states). All 23 matches occur after `</header>`, so none is header/footer boilerplate. Exactly one file discloses the details wall: online-quote.html. I widened the disclosure grep to `before the (number|price|figure)|details first|we ask for your details|need your details|asks for your details` and got two hits — online-quote.html and double-glazing-milton-keynes.html, and I read the second one in context ('the layout matters before the price does', about bifolds vs sliders), which is not a disclosure. So the count of 1 stands under a deliberately generous test.

Source documents verified verbatim. online-quote.php:12-15 reads '**The price is shown after a required name, email, phone, address and postcode**, not during configuration' and states it was 'checked screen by screen on 2026-08-06 against the live retail interface'. GOOGLE-ADS-AUDIT-2026-08-11.md:225 (under §8, line 219) reads 'name, address, phone and email are required before any figure appears'. TONEOFVOICE.md:147 sanctions 'Get an instant price' as a button label, and the finding correctly does not propose changing it. I searched AI.md and the other docs for any owner ruling permitting or requiring the gate to go undisclosed and found none.

ONE CLARIFICATION, not a defect in the finding: /online-quote/ is not one of the 23 — it never uses the phrase 'instant price' in its body copy. So it is not '23 promise, 1 of them discloses'; it is '23 promise, none of them disclose, and the one page that discloses is a different page'. That makes the finding marginally stronger, not weaker. The disclosure wording the finding proposes to reuse is live at online-quote.php:153 ('Your details come before the number, and nothing is ordered') and I can see it rendered in shots/mobile/online-quote--fold.png.

#### [58] Four routes are deliberately excluded from the sitemap but left live, indexable and self-canonical — including /commercial-glazing-milton-keynes/, which is also linked from nowhere

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `inc/generated-pages.php:1969-1979` holds an explicit `$excluded_slugs` map that removes four real content routes from page-sitemap.xml: `commercial-glazing-milton-keynes`, `commercial-glazing-northamptonshire`, `double-glazing-buckinghamshire` and `double-glazing-northamptonshire`. All four still return 200 on live, all four emit a self-referencing canonical, and none of them carries a `<meta name="robots">`. The suppression therefore only hides them from the sitemap; they remain crawlable and indexable, and nothing tells Google they are not the preferred URL. /commercial-glazing-milton-keynes/ is the worst case because it is also linked from nowhere: it is not in the 40 live pages crawled, not on the commercial hub, and not on /commercial-glazing-buckinghamshire/. The router does try to add it (generated-page.php:2059-2062 appends `commercial-glazing-bedfordshire`, `commercial-glazing-milton-keynes`, `commercial-glazing-northamptonshire` after `$commercial_routes`, which is already 7 fixed routes plus 47 county keys built at generated-page.php:1899-1907), but `array_slice(array_values($related_links), 0, 24)` at commercial-county.php:269 truncates ~30 entries earlier. No project doc records why the four were excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Finish the decision the exclusion list started. For each of the four slugs, either (a) 301 to the canonical equivalent — /commercial-glazing-milton-keynes/ and /commercial-glazing-northamptonshire/ to /commercial-glazing/, /double-glazing-buckinghamshire/ and /double-glazing-northamptonshire/ to their kept counterparts — or (b) if the content is wanted, point the canonical at the kept page and add `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow">`. Do not leave a page 200 + self-canonical + sitemap-excluded, because that is the one combination that gives Google no signal at all. Separately, add a code comment at inc/generated-pages.php:1969 recording why each slug is on the list, since nothing in the .md docs explains it.
- **Why:** 62 opens a month of people typing questions is the largest pool of demonstrated interest on the site, and none of it can currently become a lead record.
- **Affected:** Site-wide chat widget; inc/legend-assistant.php prompt config plus one new chip in the drawer.
- **Evidence:** SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05 §4 event table (chat_opened 62, form_started 28, phone_click 9); inc/legend-assistant.php:73, :389; LIVECHAT.md:105, :180.
- **Verification:** The observations reproduce but the diagnosis is wrong in a way that changes the fix, and the scope is 4 routes not 1. Verified: curl = 200, <title>Commercial Glazing Milton Keynes</title>, self-canonical, no robots meta, H1 'Commercial Glazing Milton Keynes'; grep of urls.txt = 0; zero in-links across all 40 live HTML files; live /commercial-glazing/ and /commercial-glazing-buckinghamshire/ both return 0 matches for the slug. The truncation mechanism is real (generated-page.php:1899-1907 builds $commercial_routes as 7 fixed + array_keys of 47 county pages; the three-route add is at generated-page.php:2059-2062, NOT 1899-1903 as cited; commercial-county.php:269 array_slice(...,0,24) truncates long before them). BUT the sitemap absence is not an accident of the generator: inc/generated-pages.php:1969-1979 is an explicit $excluded_slugs map that names 'commercial-glazing-milton-keynes' => true alongside 'commercial-glazing-northamptonshire', 'double-glazing-buckinghamshire', 'double-glazing-northamptonshire' and test slugs. Someone deliberately suppressed it. I checked all four excluded content routes on live: every one returns 200, carries a self-referencing canonical and has NO robots meta. So the defect is not 'the sitemap forgot a page', it is 'four pages were deliberately pulled from the sitemap but left live, indexable and self-canonical'. That is a half-finished suppression, and the right fix is to complete it (noindex or 301) rather than to promote the page into the county set. No .md file documents the exclusion list.

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Four written comparison pieces — /what-is-the-difference-between-upvc-vs-composite-doors/, /difference-between-french-doors-and-sliding-patio-doors/, /different-types-of-window-frame-materials/, /why-choose-fenster-over-anglian/ — are live, indexable and in the 712-URL sitemap, yet an in-link graph built over all 712 crawled pages gives every one of them zero in-links, counting header and footer chrome as well as body content. Decide separately whether /why-choose-fenster-over-anglian/ should be linked from /why-trust-fenster/ or left out of the internal graph on purpose.

- **Verification:** Two halves, and they rule differently. The ORPHAN half is confirmed and stronger than claimed: I rebuilt the in-link graph over all 712 crawled pages (not 197), counting only <main> content, and all four comparison guides have ZERO in-links — in fact zero even counting header and footer chrome. PROGRESS.md:4362 records /different-types-of-window-frame-materials/ among pages with strong existing organic visibility, which makes the orphaning more costly. The positional measurements are also accurate: pageHeight is exactly 4499, the 9-card grid starts ~405px and the 'Both are A+ rated' heading sits ~1260px (finding said ~416 and ~1250), and DOM order confirms the grid precedes the panel. #### [132] Two 2,430px engineer portraits are 4.49MB of the 4.87MB /window-and-door-repairs/ mobile payload, shown at 88px — and the same files cost /meet-the-team/ far more

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** assets/images/imported/5-2.png (2,505,871 bytes) and 7.png (2,206,799 bytes) are 2430x2430 PNGs carrying width="2430" height="2430" in the markup, rendered at 88px on mobile in the "Two engineers, and the parts already on the van" section. This is not the site's worst image payload, though: /meet-the-team/ carries 10.43MB, /aluminium-windows/ 7.19MB and /casement-windows/ 5.87MB, and /meet-the-team/ serves these same two files plus five more 2430px PNGs at a 364px display.
- **Recommendation:** Do not export the portraits at 176px/264px — /meet-the-team/ renders the same two files at 364px CSS and would visibly degrade. Export one shared WebP per portrait at ~800px (covers 364px at 2x) and add a srcset with a ~264px entry so the 88px repairs slot takes the small one; that removes roughly 4.4MB from /window-and-door-repairs/ and far more from /meet-the-team/ if the same treatment is applied to all seven 2430px team PNGs. Regenerate fenster-van.jpg at 1170px in the same pass.
- **Why:** With every internal link identical, the internal graph tells Google exactly one phrase per page and nothing about the long tail. The site already has the right vocabulary in its body copy — it just is not hyperlinked.
- **Affected:** All money pages; the templated link-card component template-parts/components/link-cards.php
- **Evidence:** Anchor-text counter over `<main>` links across 712 pages: composite-doors → {'Composite Doors':805,'Compare composite doors':25,'composite door':2,'Composite doors':2}; aluminium-bifold-doors → {'Aluminium Bifold Doors':803,…}; contact → 15 body links vs 2,151 total.
- **Verification:** Every number reproduces within rounding, but two details are transposed, one superlative is false, and the fix as written would break another page. CONFIRMED on disk: 5-2.png is 2,505,871 bytes and 7.png is 2,206,799 bytes, both 2430x2430; live markup is `<img src=".../imported/7.png" alt="Andy McCullagh" width="2430" height="2430">` and the same for 5-2.png with alt="Steven Welch"; probe-mobile.json images.oversized lists both at nat 2430 / disp 88; perf.byType.img.bytes is 5,110,799 = 4.87MB; fenster-van.jpg is 555,150 bytes at 2200x943 for a 390px slot; the section heading "Two engineers, and the parts already on the van." is verbatim. TRANSPOSED: the problem text says 7.png is 2.45MB and 5-2.png 2.16MB — it is the other way round. OVERSTATED: the pair is 4,712,670 bytes = 4.49MB and 92% of the payload, not 4.6MB / 94%. SUPERLATIVE FALSE: "the single largest avoidable payload on any audited page" does not hold — ranking probe-mobile.json by perf.byType.img.bytes puts /meet-the-team/ at 10.43MB, /aluminium-windows/ at 7.19MB and /casement-windows/ at 5.87MB above /window-and-door-repairs/ at 4.87MB. FIX WOULD REGRESS: /meet-the-team/ serves the same two files (grep -l across live HTML confirms only those two pages use them) at a 364px display per probe images.oversized, so re-exporting them at 176px/264px would visibly degrade the team page. That page is also the bigger prize — it carries five more 2430px PNGs on the same pattern.

#### [125] Three content-free shells are indexable and in the sitemap, one of them promising a competitor comparison it does not contain

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** At ≤860px `main.scss:27908-27918` (inside the query opening at :27825) hides the desktop quote controls and shows a single `Open quote tool` link — but the iframe itself stays, scaled to 0.72 by :27926-27928 inside a 488px window (an effective 542x678 logical viewport for a full window configurator). `/composite-doors/` and `/sliding-sash-windows/` each add a route-scoped override (`main.scss:32704` and `:31417`) that sets `.fg-product-quote-embed__card { display: none }` and swaps in a full-width action button; probe-mobile confirms their iframes measure 0px tall against 488px on the other twelve. In the captured mobile render of /casement-windows/ the surviving frame is an empty bordered white rectangle 1,461 device px tall sitting directly under the green `Open quote tool` button. The iframe does carry a real src, so the emptiness may be partly a headless/consent-declined capture artefact rather than certain live behaviour — but the 488px of scaled, redundant configurator beside the button that replaces it is present either way.
- **Recommendation:** Promote the composite/sash override to the base mobile rule rather than repeating it per route: hide `.fg-product-quote-embed__card` under 860px site-wide and keep the `Open quote tool` action, which is already the owner's ruling for the mobile controls (AI.md:657). That removes ~490px from twelve pages and removes the risk of a blank rectangle in the middle of the conversion section. Before shipping, load one affected route on a real mobile browser with consent accepted to confirm whether the frame renders content or is genuinely blank — it changes nothing about the fix, but it changes how the change is described.
- **Why:** A page whose snippet promises a named-competitor comparison and delivers a generic 'call us' paragraph is the clearest possible helpful-content signal against the site, and a thank-you page with a broken headline in the index is straightforwardly embarrassing when it surfaces on a brand query.
- **Affected:** /why-choose-fenster-over-anglian/, /stable-doors-traditional-charm-meets-modern-efficiency-and-security/, /window-and-door-design/
- **Evidence:** `<main>` word counts from the 712-page crawl: 207 / 189 / 206 — the three thinnest indexable non-hub pages on the site (next is /careers/ at 304, which is legitimately a no-vacancies notice). All three carry the identical "We welcome our homeowners…" block. All three have 0 inbound internal links and all three appear in scratchpad/urls.txt.
- **Verification:** The mechanism, the CSS line numbers and the visual outcome all reproduce. Two corrections: the affected count is 12 not 11, and the "blank white box" needs a caveat.

CSS CONFIRMED: main.scss:27825 opens `@media (max-width: 860px)`. Inside it, :27908-27918 hides `[data-fullscreen-quote]` and `.button[target="_blank"]` and shows `.fg-product-quote-embed__mobile-open`; :27926-27928 sets `.fg-product-quote-embed__frame { --fg-quote-tool-scale: 0.72 }` and the card is never hidden. The two route overrides are exactly where cited: `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-product-quote-embed__card { display: none }` at main.scss:31417 (inside the 860px query opening at :31368) and `.generated-page--composite-doors ...` at :32704 (query at :32687), each paired with a full-width `__sash-mobile-action`. `grep -l fg-product-quote-embed__sash-mobile-action live/*.html` returns exactly composite-doors.html and sliding-sash-windows.html — no other route has the escape hatch.

PROBE CONFIRMED: probe-mobile iframes h = 0 on /composite-doors/ and /sliding-sash-windows/, 488 on every other product route. The 0.72/488 arithmetic checks: 390/0.72 = 542, 488/0.72 = 678.

SCREENSHOT CONFIRMED: I located the region by scanning shots/mobile/casement-windows.png (1170x65124, 3x DPR) for near-white row runs — there is a 1,461-device-px run at y=42309-43770 (= 487 CSS px). Cropping 41400-44600 and viewing it shows exactly what the finding describes: the "uPVC window quote tool" card, a green "Open quote tool" button, and directly beneath it a bordered, completely empty white rectangle running ~488 CSS px before the FAQ section starts.

CORRECTION 1 — SCOPE: the affected list omits /french-doors/. It has `fg-product-quote-embed__card` in its HTML, no override, and probe-mobile iframe h=488. That makes it 12 routes: casement, upvc-doors, patio-doors, tilt-turn, flush-casement, aluminium-windows, aluminium-doors, aluminium-bifold, heritage, secondary-glazing, double-glazing-replacement, french-doors.

CORRECTION 2 — CAVEAT ON "BLANK": the iframe did receive a real src (`...windowcad7/?...&tracking=rejected-cookies`), so the emptiness is not a missing src. But the probe ran headless with consent pre-seeded to necessary-only, so I cannot rule out that WindowCAD renders normally for a consenting real user and the white box is partly a capture artefact. The structural claim (a 488px iframe scaled to 0.72 retained beside the button that replaces it, on 12 routes, when two routes already delete it) stands regardless; the "blank rectangle" should be stated as observed-in-capture rather than as certain live behaviour. That is why I would hold confidence at 88 rather than raise it.

No contrary ruling: AI.md:32 and :657 rule on the CONTROLS ("hide the desktop quote controls and show one same-tab Open quote tool action"), not the card, and HANDOVER.md:558 describes the same. Nothing sanctions keeping the frame.

#### [89] /double-glazing-replacement/ links to /obscure-glass/, which 301s to /obscured-glass/

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** On a first visit at 375x812 the consent layer is a modal <dialog> — a centred card up to 680px wide (343px at this viewport), measured by GOOGLE-ADS-AUDIT-2026-08-11.md:234 at 501px of an 812px screen — over a dimmed, blurred ::backdrop, with page scroll locked (inc/consent.php:657 adds `fg-cookie-consent-open`; src/scss/main.scss:1556-1558 sets `overflow: hidden` on the root). It is not full-screen, but it is blocking and it is the first thing 76% of paid clicks meet. SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md:196 clears it with 'There is no evidence the modal is costing traffic: CTR rose 33% post-launch with the modal live throughout.' That reasoning cannot hold: CTR is a SERP metric produced before the visitor arrives, so it is structurally incapable of detecting an on-site loss caused by an overlay met after arrival. The same section at :194 correctly refuses to build a rate on banner_shown for exactly this reason. The modal may well be fine; nothing measured so far shows it either way.
- **Recommendation:** Find the `obscure-glass` string in the replacement-glazing source (`template-parts/sections/replacement-glazing-v2.php` or the section data feeding it) and change it to `obscured-glass`.
- **Why:** An avoidable redirect hop on a money page, and the kind of single-character route inconsistency the project's own 'registry sprawl' note is about.
- **Affected:** /double-glazing-replacement/ — 1 link
- **Evidence:** `grep -c 'href="[^"]*obscure-glass/"'` on live/double-glazing-replacement.html = 1; `curl -o /dev/null -w %{redirect_url}` on /obscure-glass/ returns https://fensterglazing.com/obscured-glass/
- **Verification:** The logical critique is sound and the citations are accurate; the physical description of the modal is overstated.

VERIFIED. SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md:196 reads exactly 'There is no evidence the modal is costing traffic: CTR rose 33% post-launch with the modal live throughout. It is costing measurement, not visitors.' The finding's objection holds: CTR is clicks over impressions on the search result, produced entirely before the visitor reaches the site, so it cannot register an on-site loss caused by an overlay met after arrival. The irony the finding points out is real — the same section, three paragraphs earlier (:194), correctly refuses to build a rate on banner_shown for precisely this class of reasoning, and AI.md:200 records that refusal as settled. The other numbers check out too: '35.5% of page views are attributable' is at SEO-LEAD-AUDIT:194; '76% of spend is mobile' and 'the cookie modal occupies 501px of an 812px screen on arrival' are both at GOOGLE-ADS-AUDIT-2026-08-11.md:234, which also carries the 'not a reason to weaken the consent layer' framing the finding challenges.

The scroll lock is real and I traced it in source rather than trusting the runtime observation: inc/consent.php:657 adds `fg-cookie-consent-open` to documentElement and :676 removes it, and src/scss/main.scss:1556-1558 defines `.fg-cookie-consent-open { overflow: hidden }`. The element is a <dialog> with a ::backdrop, so it is genuinely modal.

CORRECTION. 'renders full-screen over a dimmed page' is wrong. main.scss:1560-1564 sizes it `width: min(calc(100% - 2rem), 680px); max-height: calc(100dvh - 2rem); margin: auto` — a centred card, 343px wide on a 375px viewport, and the audit's own measurement puts it at 501px of 812, i.e. 62% of the height. Dimmed and scroll-locked, yes; full-screen, no. The finding's own cited source contradicts its wording.

NOT already-ruled. AI.md:179 makes consent-first an owner decision as of 2026-08-11 and :199 calls it 'the mandatory first-visit modal', but neither rules on modality or placement, and the finding explicitly declines to weaken the consent layer — it asks for measurement, which no doc forbids. GOOGLE-ADS-AUDIT:453 ('Keep the consent layer as it is') is an audit recommendation, not an owner ruling.

#### [69] The /blog/ index renders 10 of its 12 article cards with no link at all

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 98% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** fenster_render_nav_fallback() renders the full desktop menu and then calls fenster_render_mobile_nav_fallback($items) on the same data at inc/template-tags.php:173, so both renderings sit in the DOM at every viewport. Measured on the live homepage: 108 anchors inside <header class="site-header">, 15,180 bytes, split 60 desktop and 48 in the hidden drawer (6,506 bytes). The functional defect is the parity gap: the mobile renderer (inc/template-tags.php:176-270) contains no reference to $item['ctas'] — the only ctas references in the file are lines 134-136, inside the desktop function — so 'Send a commercial enquiry' and 'See our commercial projects' exist on desktop and not on mobile. /commercial-projects/ survives on mobile only because it appears once in the footer (it appears zero times in homepage main content). The weight argument is weak and should not carry the finding: the duplicated drawer costs 468 bytes gzipped, 1.76% of the transferred page, roughly 325KB gzip across all 712 pages.
- **Recommendation:** Primary fix, about 12 lines: add the ctas loop to fenster_render_mobile_nav_fallback(), mirroring inc/template-tags.php:134-153, so the mobile drawer offers the same four destinations as the desktop panel. This closes a real desktop/mobile parity gap and is aligned with HOMEPAGE.md:540 ('Do not reintroduce separate desktop/mobile navigation sources'), since both renderers already read one $items source. Treat consolidating the two renderers into one CSS-driven markup as an optional refactor for drift safety, not a performance fix, and check it against HOMEPAGE.md:540 before starting.
- **Why:** A visitor on the blog index clicks a headline and nothing happens, ten times out of twelve. It is the single most obviously broken interaction found anywhere on the site, and it sits on the page whose whole purpose is onward navigation.
- **Affected:** /blog/ — 10 of 12 cards. template-parts/sections/generated-simple.php:26-43 and :181-189
- **Evidence:** Parsed live /blog/: 12 `<article class="fg-simple-card">` blocks, only indices 1 and 2 contain an `<a href>`; generated-simple.php:184-188 `<?php if (! empty($card['url'])) : ?><h3><a href=…>…<?php else : ?><h3>…`; the in-code comment at generated-simple.php:45-46 states "Only these cards carry a URL, so only they render linked."
- **Verification:** Every measurement reproduces to the byte, and the functional half is a real defect — but the line numbers are all wrong and the performance rationale is substantially overstated. CONFIRMED EXACTLY: the live homepage <header class="site-header"> is 15,180 bytes with 108 anchors, splitting 60 desktop / 48 drawer at the <div class="site-mobile-nav" boundary, and the drawer carries a literal hidden attribute. The CTA parity gap is real and precisely as described: 'Send a commercial enquiry' and 'See our commercial projects' each appear once in the desktop portion and zero times in the drawer, and the only ctas references in inc/template-tags.php are lines 134-136, entirely inside the desktop function — the mobile renderer never reads $item['ctas']. The claim that /commercial-projects/ survives only via the footer also checks out: header desktop=1 (CSS-hidden on mobile), footer=1, main=0. WRONG LINE NUMBERS: fenster_render_nav_fallback spans 44-174 and its call to the mobile renderer is at line 173, not 160; fenster_render_mobile_nav_fallback spans 176-270, not 162-260; the ctas loop to mirror is 134-153, not 126-149. OVERSTATED: the 'why' argues '15KB x 712 pages of duplicated navigation is real weight on every request'. Only the 6,506-byte drawer is duplicated, and because it is highly repetitive markup it costs 468 bytes gzipped — 1.76% of the transferred page. Across 712 pages that is roughly 325KB gzip in total, not the multi-megabyte figure the framing implies. The impact rating of Low is correct, but the justification should rest on the CTA parity gap and the two-renderer drift risk, not on page weight. Worth noting for whoever fixes it: HOMEPAGE.md:540 says 'Do not reintroduce separate desktop/mobile navigation sources' — the two renderers already share one $items source, so the minimal ctas fix is aligned with that ruling, but a wholesale single-markup rewrite should be checked against it first.

#### [84] The postcode field rejects a leading or trailing space with a generic native error, and offers no format example

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The server trims and strips all whitespace before validating (inc/enquiries.php:504) and the JS validator trims before testing (main.js:2475, 2487). The HTML `pattern` attribute does neither: `^([Gg][Ii][Rr]\s?0[Aa]{2}|[A-Za-z]{1,2}[0-9][A-Za-z0-9]?\s?[0-9][A-Za-z]{2})$` (enquiry-form.php:51) is applied to the raw value, so a leading or trailing space from a paste or an address autofill fails `reportValidity()` with the browser's generic 'Please match the format requested.' — verified live: patternMismatch true, customError false. The JS never sees it because it trimmed first and cleared its own customValidity. An internal double space is handled correctly (both validators reject it and the visitor gets 'Enter a valid UK postcode.'), and each input does carry `title="Enter a valid UK postcode."`, which Chrome shows beneath the generic line — so the real gap is that there is no format example and no placeholder on any of the three postcode inputs, and that a whitespace-only difference produces a message naming no fix.
- **Recommendation:** Add `placeholder="MK9 1AB"` to the three postcode inputs in enquiry-form.php (:131, :156, :270), and normalise the value on `blur` (`field.value = field.value.trim().toUpperCase()`) inside the existing `validateContactField` handler at main.js:2473-2490 so the raw value can never disagree with the pattern.
- **Why:** The uPVC-versus-aluminium decision is the first fork a homeowner hits and the one that determines budget. The content to resolve it exists twice over — once as a well-built panel placed after the question, once as four articles nobody can find.
- **Affected:** /windows-milton-keynes/, /doors-milton-keynes/ (panel order); 4 orphaned comparison guides. inc/site-data.php product_hub_groups decision_* keys; template-parts/sections/product-hub.php
- **Evidence:** Full-page desktop screenshot of /windows-milton-keynes/ (pageHeight 4499px): 9-card grid begins ~416px, 'Both are A+ rated. The difference is the frame.' heading at ~1,250px; the four comparison slugs all appear in the zero-in-link set computed over 197 crawled pages
- **Verification:** I reproduced the core mechanism live on /contact/ by setting the postcode field and reading `validity`. 'MK9 1AB' passes clean. 'MK9 1AB ' (trailing space) and ' MK9 1AB' (leading space) both give patternMismatch true, customError false, validationMessage 'Please match the format requested.' — exactly the disagreement claimed: inc/enquiries.php:504 strips all whitespace, main.js:2475 trims before testing at :2487, and the HTML `pattern` at enquiry-form.php:51 sees the raw value. The form has no `novalidate` and main.js:2553/2574/2629 call `reportValidity()`, so that native bubble is what the visitor gets. No placeholder on any postcode input — confirmed. Three corrections. (a) The double-space case does NOT produce an unexplained error: 'MK9  1AB' returns customError true and validationMessage 'Enter a valid UK postcode.', because the JS regex at main.js:2388 allows at most one space and rejects it too. Only leading/trailing whitespace slips through the JS and hits the raw-value pattern. (b) 'no hint' is overstated — every postcode input carries `title="Enter a valid UK postcode."` (enquiry-form.php:131, :156, :270), which Chrome renders in the validation bubble beneath the generic line. The missing thing is a format *example*, not a hint. (c) There are three postcode inputs in the component, not four; line 51 is the shared pattern variable. Impact Low is right and the fix is right.

#### [118] Ten product pages send a generic project_type, which costs Meta conversion segmentation — but the office already gets the product name via the `source` field

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** generated-page.php:5352 sets project_type with a four-way ternary (commercial, repairs, sliding-sash, composite); /casement-windows/ sets its own at casement-windows-v2.php:724. Everything else falls through to 'Residential windows and doors', so /heritage-windows/, /aluminium-doors/, /tilt-turn-windows/, /patio-doors/, /upvc-doors/, /flush-casement-windows/, /aluminium-windows/, /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /integral-blinds/ and /secondary-glazing/ all submit the same value. The office is NOT blind to this: the same form posts `source` (the product name, e.g. "Aluminium Heritage Windows") and `page_url`, and inc/enquiries.php prints both in the notification email (:442, :456), stores both as meta (:670-671) and gives Source its own admin column (:125, :143). The real costs are narrower: Meta CAPI sends content_name from project_type (inc/website-tracking.php:418), so those ten routes cannot be segmented in Meta conversion reporting; the saved enquiry's post_title is "Name — Residential windows and doors" (:654); and the customer's confirmation email says "We have received your enquiry about Residential windows and doors" (:470) to someone who enquired about heritage windows. Note also that on these routes project_type is doing a deliberate second job — it is the homeowner/business discriminator flipped by the "Choose enquiry type" gate at enquiry-form.php:193-200.
- **Recommendation:** Do not lock project_type on these ten routes — that removes the homeowner/business enquiry-type gate from all of them. Instead send the product identity where it is actually missing: pass the product label into Meta CAPI's content_name at inc/website-tracking.php:418 by preferring _fenster_source and falling back to _fenster_project_type, so Meta conversion data segments by product. Separately, build the saved post_title at inc/enquiries.php:654 from source rather than project_type, and use source in the customer confirmation sentence at :470. All three are one-line changes against meta the system already stores.
- **Why:** The prior audits concluded "the matrix has produced nothing, hold" on CTR data alone. That conclusion is not safe while three quarters of the matrix has one internal link: no page can rank on copy alone with no internal PageRank. This is a cheap, reversible test that decides whether 525 pages get invested in or killed, and it is the only test that can decide it honestly.
- **Affected:** 525 matrix routes; 407 with a single inbound link. Link-cap code: generated-page.php:3449, commercial-county.php:268, location-service.php:1443.
- **Evidence:** Distinct-source histogram over all 525 matrix slugs: 1 source → 407 pages; 15 → 3; 16 → 4; 21 → 8; 22 → 43; 23 → 60. Verified individually: `casement-windows-wolverton` inbound = ['areas-we-cover']; `double-glazing-wolverton` inbound = 22 pages, 20 of them same-town products. Ranking moves from SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md §2.
- **Verification:** The observation is factually correct and the "why" is refuted. Confirmed: generated-page.php:5352 is exactly the four-way ternary described, and all ten named routes submit project_type="Residential windows and doors" live, while /casement-windows-bletchley/ submits "uPVC casement windows in Bletchley" from location-service.php:1471. But the claim that these leads "arrive at info@ indistinguishable from a generic homepage lead" is false. The same form carries a `source` hidden field (enquiry-form.php:322) set from the page title, and a `page_url` field (enquiry-form.php:323). Live values: /heritage-windows/ sends source="Aluminium Heritage Windows", /patio-doors/ "uPVC Sliding Doors", /tilt-turn-windows/ "uPVC Tilt & Turn Windows" — the homepage sends "Homepage". Both reach the office: inc/enquiries.php:442 prints a "Source" row in the notification email, :456 prints "Submitted from <page url>", :643-645 write both into the saved enquiry, :670-671 store them as meta, and inc/enquiries.php:125/:143 give the admin list its own Source column. So the office knows exactly which product page the lead came from, and the sales-script consequence does not occur. Two further corrections. First, project_type is not merely coarse — on unlocked routes it is deliberately the homeowner/business audience discriminator, flipped by the "Choose enquiry type" gate at enquiry-form.php:193-200; setting it to a product name requires lock_project_type, which REMOVES that gate from ten pages. That is a UX change, not "a one-line change against data the template already holds". Second, the finding's implicit claim that only four routes get a specific value is wrong: /casement-windows/ sends "Casement windows" from its bespoke template at casement-windows-v2.php:724, a fifth case outside the ternary. What genuinely remains is narrow: Meta CAPI reports content_name from project_type (inc/website-tracking.php:418), so those ten routes are unsegmentable in Meta conversion data; the saved post_title is "Name — Residential windows and doors" (enquiries.php:654); and the customer's own confirmation email reads "your enquiry about Residential windows and doors" (enquiries.php:470) after they enquired about heritage windows. The internal dashboard is unaffected — it already uses _fenster_source as the cta and the real page_path (website-tracking.php:648, :658-660).

#### [129] The generic "Specification choices" band costs 800px on mobile to announce the two sections directly beneath it, on eight routes

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** On eight routes fg-product-gallery-band reads "Finish the design with your colours, glass and hardware. Choose your colours, privacy glass and hardware; each guide helps narrow the detail before survey." and then contains one card, a link to /obscured-glass/ — because the colour grid and handle grid are rendered inline directly beneath it (HANDOVER.md:692 documents that suppression). Measured 800px at 375x812. The eight are /patio-doors/, /aluminium-doors/, /aluminium-windows/, /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /heritage-windows/, /tilt-turn-windows/, /flush-casement-windows/ and /french-doors/ — NOT /upvc-doors/, which already carries the fg-product-gallery-band--glass variant ("Privacy where the door needs it."), and /sliding-sash-windows/ has its own too ("Choose your glass and hardware."). /french-doors/ is the exception to the one-card claim: its band is 1,062px with two cards.
- **Recommendation:** Adopt the casement fg-product-gallery-band--glass variant as the default so the slot carries the obscure-glass decision the product actually has, and delete the "colours, glass and hardware" preamble. Be clear about the payoff: casement's rewritten band measures 713px against the generic 800px, so this buys roughly 87px per route plus a real decision in place of a table of contents. If the height is the goal rather than the copy, the band has to be deleted outright on the routes where the colour and handle grids already render inline — that is the full 800px.
- **Why:** 712 URLs, 73.7% of them a matrix that has not moved, and no way to tell Google which handful actually changed. Accurate lastmod is how you stop the crawler spending its budget re-reading 525 static town pages instead of this week's post.
- **Affected:** page-sitemap.xml (712 URLs) and sitemap_index.xml
- **Evidence:** Two fetches of https://fensterglazing.com/sitemap_index.xml return `<lastmod>2026-08-13T09:11:30+00:00</lastmod>` generated by `gmdate('c')` at inc/generated-pages.php:1962. page-sitemap.xml contains 712 `<loc>` and zero `<lastmod>`.

#### [88] The chat launcher sits on top of a primary CTA on mobile and takes the tap

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The prompt bubble is not on the fold — src/js/main.js:53 gates it behind 240px of scroll with a one-way latch, and live at 375x812 with scrollY 0 it computes visibility:hidden / opacity:0. The 279x116 measurement is the wrapper's bounding box, which is pointer-events:none by design (main.scss:1905-1912). The only thing on the first screen is the 96x104 launcher sprite in the bottom-right corner, and it does not cover the copy the finding named: at scrollY 0 the whole Step 1 sentence on /book-a-consultation/ and the hero caption on /composite-doors/ are legible. What is real is that the launcher is pointer-events:auto and is fixed at bottom-right with no awareness of what is under it. On /aluminium-windows/ at first view, elementsFromPoint(320,750) puts the launcher img directly above A.button.button--light, the full-width 'Instant pricing' CTA, so roughly the right-hand quarter of that button opens the chat instead of the quote tool.
- **Recommendation:** Add bottom padding or a safe zone to the hero button-row on mobile so a full-width primary CTA cannot come to rest under the fixed launcher, or inset the launcher above the CTA band. Verify by running elementsFromPoint at the launcher's centre on each product route at 375x812 and asserting no `.button` is in the stack beneath it. Do not change the prompt timing — it is already scroll-gated at 240px and is a deliberate design (LIVECHAT.md:322).
- **Why:** 15KB x 712 pages of duplicated navigation is real weight on every request, and two renderers over one dataset is exactly the drift risk the file's own comments warn about ('Change one of these two renderers and change the other'). The CTA omission is a live desktop/mobile parity gap.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages. inc/template-tags.php:44-160 (desktop) and :162-260 (mobile)
- **Evidence:** Live homepage header block = 15,180 bytes and 108 `<a href` matches, split 60 desktop / 48 drawer at the `<div class="site-mobile-nav"` boundary; inc/template-tags.php:162-260 contains no reference to `$item['ctas']`; probe-desktop.json linkCount ranges 148-214 across the 38 routes
- **Verification:** The central claim is refuted, and the screenshots that produced it are a harness artefact.

The prompt bubble is scroll-gated. src/js/main.js:53 sets promptRevealThreshold = 240 and :245-249 reveals it only when scroll exceeds that, behind a one-way `promptRevealed` latch that never re-hides it. Both survive minification in the production bundle (live/main.js: `Ie=240`, `qe=()=>{G||et()<Ie||(G=!0,oe.classList.add("is-prompt-visible"))}`). Because the latch is one-way, any harness that captures a full-page screenshot (which scrolls) before capturing the --fold shot will show the prompt at scrollY 0 even though a real first-view visitor never sees it. That is exactly what shots/mobile/book-a-consultation--fold.png and composite-doors--fold.png show.

I checked it live. At 375x812 on https://fensterglazing.com/book-a-consultation/ with scrollY 0: `.legend-assistant__prompt` computes to visibility:hidden, opacity:0. The .legend-assistant rect is indeed {x:96,y:696,w:279,h:116} exactly as the finding measured — but that is the transparent positioning wrapper, and its computed pointer-events is `none`, documented as such at main.scss:1905-1912 ('a transparent positioning box... It must never intercept taps'). The only visible element is `.legend-assistant__launcher` at {x:267,y:696,w:96,h:104} — 26% of viewport width, in the corner. So '279x116 across 74% of the viewport width' is a bounding box of nothing.

My own live screenshot of /book-a-consultation/ at scrollY 0 shows the entire Step 1 sentence legible and unobstructed: 'One of our experts comes to you, talks through the options for your property and prices the job before they leave. It is free, whether you go ahead or not.' The same free claim also appears unobstructed in the hero paragraph above it. On /composite-doors/ at scrollY 0 the 'DISTINCTION COMPOSITE DOOR' caption is fully legible; the sprite sits over the right side of the hero photo. Both named overlaps are false. LIVECHAT.md:322 and :325 independently record the prompt as scroll-triggered by design.

One genuine adjacent defect did survive, and it is narrower. The launcher itself IS pointer-events:auto, and on /aluminium-windows/ at scrollY 0 `document.elementsFromPoint(320,750)` returns the launcher img stacked directly on top of `A.button button--light` — the 'Instant pricing' CTA. A tap on the right-hand end of that primary CTA opens the chat instead.

CONFIRMED: /online-quote/ contains zero occurrences of 'guarantee', 'ten year', '10 year' or 'insurance-backed' (counted with `grep -o ... | wc -l`, not `grep -c`, which counts lines). WRONG: the finding states the single sash mention 'is inside a planning-permission FAQ... not a warranty statement.' /sliding-sash-windows/ has THREE 'guarantee' occurrences, and I extracted all three. Two are the planning FAQ (once in the FAQPage JSON-LD, once in the visible <details>) — i.e. one visible instance. The third is a genuine, prominent warranty statement in the key-specification strip: `<small>Guarantee</small> <strong>10 years</strong>`. #### [87] The submission success panel offers no next action, and the AJAX and non-JS success paths say different things

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 70% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** On AJAX success the form collapses in place and shows two lines and nothing else (src/js/main.js:2670-2673, strings from inc/enquiries.php:762-763). There is no onward action. The non-JS redirect path shows a different message — enquiry-form.php:57 adds 'We have your details and will come back to you as soon as we can' — so the two paths set different expectations for the same event, and the path almost every visitor takes is the one that sets none. A dedicated thank-you page is ruled out (AI.md:276), so any improvement has to happen in the panel.
- **Recommendation:** First, make the two paths agree: give the AJAX panel the same 'We have your details and will come back to you as soon as we can' second line the PHP notice already carries, which needs no new claim and no owner sign-off. Then, as a separate CRO experiment rather than a fix, consider adding a 'Book a free consultation' button to the panel. Do not add a response-time promise (AI.md:478). Also replace the JS fallback copy 'Your project details are safely with the Fenster team' — it is the third-person phrasing already removed from the PHP notice for that reason.
- **Why:** An indexable confirmation page saying 'Your Designed Door is close' is a poor SERP result for a brand query, and two competing visualiser URLs split whatever signal either would earn. Meanwhile a working interactive tool that would help exactly the undecided visitor the hubs are built for is invisible.
- **Affected:** /3d-visualiser/, /design-your-windows-and-doors/, /window-and-door-design/
- **Evidence:** All three return 200 with no `<meta name="robots">`; all three in scratchpad/urls.txt; all three have zero in-links across 197 crawled pages; titles and main-content text extracted from the live HTML as quoted
- **Verification:** Every code citation checks out. src/js/main.js:2670-2673 calls showFeedback('success', result.message || 'Thanks — your enquiry has been received.', result.copy || 'Your project details are safely with the Fenster team.') after form.classList.add('is-submitted'); the server sends those same two strings from inc/enquiries.php:762-763; fenster_enquiry_redirect() at inc/enquiries.php:289-300 does append 'fenster_enquiry' and '#fenster-enquiry'; the notice map is at template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:54-66 with 'success' on line 57. AI.md:276 is exactly the wcad-thank-you removal, and AI.md:478 is exactly the do-not-invent-response-times bullet. It is true that the success panel offers no onward action.

Two corrections. First, 'no expectation set' is true only of the JS path. The non-JS redirect notice at enquiry-form.php:57 reads 'We have your details and will come back to you as soon as we can' — a soft expectation the AJAX panel does not carry. That is itself a consistency defect worth naming: the two success paths say different things. Second, and more importantly, the type is wrong. Nothing here is broken or measurably deficient: the form submits, a panel confirms, a customer confirmation email is sent (inc/enquiries.php:715-720), and the conversion fires. Whether a post-submission consultation CTA belongs there is a CRO/design judgement reasonable people disagree about, and AI.md:276 shows the owner has already removed one post-submission surface. This is an opportunity, not a defect.

Worth flagging in passing: the JS fallback string 'Your project details are safely with the Fenster team' is third-person Fenster, and the comment directly above enquiry-form.php:57 records that this exact phrasing was removed from the PHP path for that reason — so the JS copy is an unswept instance of finding 91's fault.

#### [55] The headline 11.5% "open rate" measures click-outs, not commitment, and the mobile half of the two flagship routes is missing from the denominator entirely

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Main-content in-link counts over a full 712-page crawl: /other-services/ = 1 (the homepage tab widget), /areas-we-cover/ = 1 (the homepage location strip), /about/ = 1 (from /careers/, itself an orphan). All three sit in header/footer chrome on every page, so they are not orphans, but no page body treats them as a destination. None of the 8 products in the `other-services` group (inc/site-data.php:1263+) links back to its hub, and none of the 526 location-template pages links /areas-we-cover/. The cause is not the 24-link truncation the router's band applies — /double-glazing-luton/ and /roof-lanterns-whitehouse/ render only 16 band anchors, well under the cap, and still omit it. The cause is that 'areas-we-cover' exists in neither data/pages.json nor `$virtual_page_titles` (generated-page.php:1503-1508), so `$route_exists()` at :1946-1947 returns false and all three `$add_related_route('areas-we-cover', 'Areas We Cover')` call sites — :2016, :2030 and the under-six fallback at :2094 — are dead no-ops site-wide. The same registry gap silently drops /window-door-prices-milton-keynes/ and /flat-rooflights/ from every band.
- **Recommendation:** One-line fix first: add `'areas-we-cover' => 'Areas We Cover'` (and the other virtual routes registered at inc/generated-pages.php:2071, notably flat-rooflights and window-door-prices-milton-keynes) to `$virtual_page_titles` at generated-page.php:1503, which makes the three existing call sites start working on all 525 matrix pages at once. Because the band still slices at 24, additionally hard-pin `['text' => 'All areas we cover', 'url' => home_url('/areas-we-cover/')]` as the last element after the `array_slice` at location-service.php:1758 so it survives on the pages that do hit the cap. Separately, in template-parts/sections/product-hub.php and the bespoke product templates, add the parent hub as the first item of the links band ('All windows', 'All doors', 'All other services').
- **Why:** P1 in the project's own audit is aimed at a metric that cannot detect the behaviour it is meant to measure. Any change made now will be judged against a number that moves for reasons unrelated to the change.
- **Affected:** All 14 embed routes for fault (1); /composite-doors/ and /sliding-sash-windows/ on mobile for fault (2) — the two highest-value product pages, on the stronger half of the traffic.
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:2140-2146, 5442-5463, 5564-5575; src/scss/main.scss:32696-32711 and 31409-31424; live DOM at 375x812 on /composite-doors/: `.fg-product-quote-embed__card` computed display = "none", iframe src = null. SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05 §4 (quote_completed 28 vs 12 attributed).
- **Verification:** Every count reproduces exactly on my own 712-page crawl — /other-services/ 1 main-content in-link, /areas-we-cover/ 1, /about/ 1, against /commercial-glazing/ 64, /windows-milton-keynes/ 575 and /doors-milton-keynes/ 558 (the finding's 55 for windows-milton-keynes is a sampling artefact of its 10-matrix-page crawl, not an error in the claim). All three targets show 712 all-inlink counts, confirming they live in chrome only. None of the 8 products in the `other-services` group in inc/site-data.php:1263+ (roof-lanterns, flat-rooflights, integral-blinds, double-glazing-replacement, secondary-glazing, cat-and-dog-flaps, window-and-door-repairs, roofline) links back to the hub, and not one of the 526 location-template pages links /areas-we-cover/. The code citations are right: location-service.php:1062-1069 defines the six positional `$product_links` (finding said 1063-1070) and :1437 / :1758 merge and slice at 24. What is wrong is the stated cause. Truncation is not the mechanism: /double-glazing-luton/ and /roof-lanterns-whitehouse/ render bands of only 16 anchors, well under the 24 cap, and still contain no areas-we-cover. The real cause is upstream and is a one-line bug — 'areas-we-cover' is absent from data/pages.json (verified: 274 page records, no such slug) and absent from `$virtual_page_titles` (generated-page.php:1503-1508 holds only aluminium-flush-windows, aluminium-sliding-doors, commercial-areas, commercial-projects plus the commercial counties), so `$route_exists('areas-we-cover')` at :1946-1947 returns false and every `$add_related_route('areas-we-cover', 'Areas We Cover')` call — :2016, :2030 and the fallback at :2094 — is a silent no-op across all 712 pages. Same defect kills /window-door-prices-milton-keynes/ and /flat-rooflights/ in bands. One further detail: /about/'s single content in-link comes from /careers/, itself one of the 75 orphans, not from the homepage.

- **Verification:** The defect reproduces exactly: I re-fetched both URLs live on 2026-08-13. Stripped `<main>` text is 5277 chars on both, `a == b` is True, difflib quick_ratio 1.0, both H1s are 'Visualise your windows and doors with Fenster.'; the only byte differences in the whole `<main>` HTML are the self-referencing slug in two hrefs. Both self-canonical, neither carries a robots meta, both are in page-sitemap.xml and urls.txt. Sibling slugs behave as claimed: /instant-pricing/ and /door-designer/ 301 to /online-quote/, /pricing-gads/ and /instant-pricing-meta-ads/ serve `noindex,follow`. Inbound internal links from the 712-page crawl: 0. What is wrong is the causal story. This was not 'missed' — it is a documented, knowingly-deferred item: AUDIT.md:51 carries it as 'L12 — Quote-intent split remains', and SEO-AUDIT.md:193 records it as '⬜ Open decision: … Consolidate only after agreeing the intended search roles and preserving valuable visualiser/tool queries'. online-quote.php:5-10 also says explicitly that 'the others stay on the shared one until the visualiser gets its own treatment'. So the fix is one array entry but it sits behind an owner decision the docs already flagged, and the recommendation should say so rather than present it as an oversight. Note the counter-argument the docs raise does not survive contact with the data here: the two pages are byte-identical, so a 301 from /design-your-windows-and-doors/ to /3d-visualiser/ preserves every tool query — the open decision that genuinely needs owner input is /online-quote/ vs /3d-visualiser/, which this finding does not touch.

#### [184] Eight different button labels for the identical jump to #fenster-enquiry, up to five on one page

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** Across the fifteen pages the same anchor carries: "Start your project" (13 pages), "Start your design consultation" (12), "Start your enquiry" (11), "Start a product enquiry" (4), "Request a repair" (2), "Send us the sizes", "Send us a style name", "Ask about this product". `/aluminium-bifold-doors/` shows five of them on one page; `/patio-doors/` and `/integral-blinds/` show four. The two best pages show one each: composite "Send us a style name", repairs "Request a repair".
- **Recommendation:** Reduce to two per page: the hero CTA, which is route-specific and stays as-is, and one repeated mid-page label that matches it. Delete "Start your project", "Start your enquiry" and "Start a product enquiry" — the three generic ones — from `generated-page.php` and let each route's own verb repeat. TONEOFVOICE.md already requires buttons to "state the action in plain words" and bans "invented journey language".
- **Why:** Repeating one label teaches the visitor there is one thing to do. Four labels for one destination reads as four different offers and dilutes the one that matters.
- **Affected:** 13 of 15 pages carry three or more distinct labels for the same anchor.
- **Evidence:** probe-desktop.json ctas across all 15 routes: aluminium-bifold-doors has 5 distinct #fenster-enquiry labels, patio-doors and integral-blinds 4, ten routes 3; composite-doors 1.
- **Verification:** Reproduced end to end. Code path: `$social_description = (string) ($seo['meta_description'] ?? '')` at generated-pages.php:2173; `$is_bad_seo_content` at :2186 contains `WindowCAD` in its alternation; `<meta name="description">` is printed unguarded at :2202 while og:description (:2217) and twitter:description (:2225) are both wrapped in `if (! $is_bad_seo_content($social_description))`. The price-guide description template at :799 is verbatim 'Clear fitted ' . strtolower($guide['label']) . ' guidance from Fenster Glazing, with WindowCAD examples, …'. Live: all seven guides serve the WindowCAD description and zero occurrences of og:description or twitter:description. Scope is exactly right, not approximately — I swept all 712 crawled pages for a head missing og:description and got exactly 7 hits, all price guides. One point that strengthens the recommendation and should be carried into it: AI.md:67 rules that the customer-facing tool is 'always "the online quote tool" or "the quote tool" — never WindowCAD, which is an internal supplier name'. The meta description at :799 therefore already breaches an explicit owner rule and Google prints it, so option B (rewrite the copy) is the correct fix and option A (loosen the regex) would preserve a rule violation in SERP-visible text.

#### [54] Four residential product pages return early and lose their related-links band entirely, leaving casement windows and flat rooflights with almost no onward path

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Four routes take a `get_template_part(...); return;` exit before the shared tail of `generated-page.php` runs and so never reach the `fg-links-band` render: casement-windows (:3551-3561), roof-lanterns (:2250), heritage-aluminium-doors (:2260), flat-rooflights (:2274). De-duplicated, asset-excluded main-content out-degree is flat-rooflights 2, roof-lanterns 5, heritage-aluminium-doors 7, casement-windows 10, and none of the four links back to its hub, whereas 7 of 9 window products and 6 of 8 door products that keep the band do. /flat-rooflights/ is the worst case: 3 main-content in-links in the whole site and exactly two exits, /roof-lanterns/ and /privacy-policy/. Its isolation has a second cause the band fix will not touch — 'flat-rooflights' is absent from both data/pages.json and generated-page.php's `$virtual_page_titles` (:1503-1508), so `$route_exists()` is false and the route cannot be added to any related-links band site-wide. Two further routes, sliding-sash-windows and composite-doors, are excluded by the band condition at :5360, but SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md:171 records that removal as a deliberate template-level decision, so those two are a separate design question rather than part of this defect. The 'against 19-27 links on every page that keeps the band' comparison in the original finding does not hold: window-and-door-repairs (10), secondary-glazing (11), double-glazing-replacement (11), cat-and-dog-flaps (15) and roofline (16) keep the band and sit in the same range.
- **Recommendation:** Hoist the `fg-links-band` render out of the shared tail of generated-page.php into a partial (template-parts/components/links-band.php) and call it from casement-windows-v2.php, roof-lanterns.php, heritage-aluminium-doors.php and flat-rooflights.php just before each closing `</article>`, passing the `$related_links` the router already computed. Separately, add 'flat-rooflights' (and the other virtual routes registered at inc/generated-pages.php:2071) to `$virtual_page_titles` in generated-page.php:1503 so the route can be linked from bands elsewhere. Leave sliding-sash-windows and composite-doors alone unless the owner reopens the sash redesign decision; if he does, the reduced hub-plus-three-siblings variant is the right shape.
- **Why:** Risk-reversal has to be adjacent to the risk. Every proof asset the business owns is currently 8-12 screens away from every decision it is meant to support.
- **Affected:** /online-quote/, /book-a-consultation/, /contact/ and all 14 product pages.
- **Evidence:** Live-browser geometry at 375x812: online-quote reviews top=7727 vs frame top=711; book-a-consultation reviews top=3834 vs form top=629; composite-doors reviews top=9946 vs quote section top=9387. Guarantee-mention scan: online-quote.html contains 0 occurrences of "ten year|10 year|insurance-backed".
- **Verification:** The central defect is real and I reproduced it precisely, but the supporting comparison is wrong and one third of the scope is a recorded design decision. CONFIRMED parts: the early returns are exactly where cited (generated-page.php:2250 roof-lanterns, :2260 heritage-aluminium-doors, :2274 flat-rooflights, and :3551-3561 casement-windows ending `</article> <?php return; ?>` at :3559-3560), and the band condition at :5360 reads verbatim `if (! empty($related_links) && $slug !== 'sliding-sash-windows' && ! $is_composite_doors)`. `grep -c fg-links-band` on the freshly crawled live HTML is 0 for all six named routes and 1 for all 19 other residential product routes. Non-asset main-content out-degree reproduces the finding's numbers exactly once gallery lightbox hrefs are excluded: flat-rooflights 2, roof-lanterns 5, sliding-sash 6, composite-doors 7, heritage-aluminium-doors 7, casement-windows 10. /flat-rooflights/ has exactly 3 main-content in-links and exactly 2 exits, one of which is /privacy-policy/. REFUTED part: '19-27 for every product page that keeps the band' does not hold — window-and-door-repairs 10, secondary-glazing 11, double-glazing-replacement 11, cat-and-dog-flaps 15 and roofline 16 all keep the band and sit in the same range as the 'broken' pages, while flush-casement-windows and aluminium-doors reach 28. The band is therefore not the sole driver of out-degree. ALREADY-RULED part: SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md:171 records "redundant detail runs, generic benefits, generic buying-process content and repeated related-link sections were removed at template level. They were not merely hidden visually" — the sliding-sash suppression is a deliberate redesign decision, and composite-doors was built against the sash page as its quality reference (COMPOSITE-DOORS-CLAUDE-HANDOVER.md:17). Restoring a band on those two is a design argument, not a defect fix. I also found a mechanism the finding missed and which strengthens the flat-rooflights half: 'flat-rooflights' is absent from data/pages.json and from `$virtual_page_titles` (generated-page.php:1503-1508, only 4 hardcoded slugs plus commercial counties), so `$route_exists('flat-rooflights')` is false and the route can never enter any related-links band anywhere on the site — hoisting the band alone will not fix its 3 in-links.

Also a units problem worth flagging: the problem statement mixes percent-of-HTML-bytes with rendered pixels in the same sentence ('form at 27% of body (629px on mobile)'). 629px of a 6,210px document is 10%, not 27%; 27% is the byte offset. On integral-blinds.html the ghost button is `Book a consultation` → /book-a-consultation/, not `Instant pricing`, because $offers_instant_price is false for that route (the code comment at generated-page.php:928-935 explains why: a blind is a sealed-unit spec and the tool cannot price it). NOT ALREADY_RULED: generated-page.php:880-886 carries a developer comment reasoning about *which routes should override* the label ('the right label for somebody choosing windows and the wrong one for somebody whose door will not lock'), and repairs and replacement glazing were carved out on that basis. #### [83] A required free-text 'project details' box sits on every form, including the consultation booking where the visitor has already committed a date and time

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** inc/enquiries.php:591 makes `message` mandatory on every submission with no branch on `project_type` or `source`, and the template marks it Required in all three variants (enquiry-form.php:133, :159-160, :278-279). On /book-a-consultation/ the flow is genuinely three staged panels — date (Step 1 of 3), time (Step 2 of 3), details (Step 3 of 3) — and the required 'What would you like to discuss?' textarea sits in stage 3, after the visitor has already picked and committed a date and a time. probe-desktop.json shows that form as 7 visible controls with 6 required, `message` among them. Separately, the product variant's placeholder asks for 'Approximate sizes, number of items, access notes' — measurements demanded before anything has been given.
- **Recommendation:** Make `message` optional on the consultation-booking variant only (enquiry-form.php:133 and a `project_type`/`source`-keyed branch at inc/enquiries.php:591), so a visitor who has already chosen a date and time is not stopped by an open-text box. Soften the product placeholder at :279 and :160 to one easy question — 'Which rooms, and roughly how many?' — and drop the sizes request. Leave /contact/ alone: HANDOVER.md:301 records that the general enquiry form is on that page precisely so people can send a plain message, so the required box there is the page's purpose rather than an obstacle.
- **Why:** The homepage is where a first-time visitor forms their model of what the company sells. Being shown a category list on the homepage and a different one in the menu costs a re-orientation, and no product page being linked from the homepage body means the site's own strongest page passes no authority to any of the 26 products.
- **Affected:** Homepage. template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:49-53, :206-212, :243
- **Evidence:** home-experience.php:49-53 defines 5 routes; inc/site-data.php:158-201 defines 3 mega columns; homepage main-content links (chrome stripped) = 18 unique, of which the only product-level ones are /roof-lanterns/ and /integral-blinds/; desktop screenshot shows one panel expanded with a 5-item left rail
- **Verification:** The consultation half is exactly right and is the strong part of the finding. inc/enquiries.php:591 is verbatim the required-field check including `$data['message'] === ''`, applied to every submission with no `project_type`/`source` branch. enquiry-form.php:133 is the consultation variant's 'What would you like to discuss? Required' textarea; :159-160 the compact variant's 'Project details Required'; :278-279 the full variant's 'Tell us about your project Required' with the placeholder 'What would you like to change? Approximate sizes, number of items, access notes or anything else useful.' I read the consultation markup at lines 96-135: it is genuinely three stages — `data-fg-consultation-stage="date"` (Step 1 of 3), `"time"` (Step 2 of 3), then `"details"` (Step 3 of 3) — and the required free-text box sits in stage 3, after the date and time are committed. probe-desktop.json for /book-a-consultation/ confirms 7 visible controls with 6 required visible fields including `message`, plus two hidden required appointment fields. The /contact/ half is wrong, though, and should be dropped. HANDOVER.md:301 records that commit 931c7ef had turned /contact/ into a second booker and that this was reversed specifically because it left '/contact/ with no way to send a plain message'; the page carries the general enquiry form for the express purpose of sending a message. Making `message` optional there would work against the documented reason the form is on that page at all. Scope should narrow to the consultation booking, and to the product placeholder.

Stripping tags inside <main> and matching /roof ?light/i: /roof-lanterns-northampton/ = exactly 1 occurrence, 0 headings, and the context dump returns the finding's quote verbatim — "Modern aluminium profiles keep the rooflight crisp and elegant." Its H1 is "Roof lanterns in Northampton, designed around your home." while the title is "Roof Lights & Roof Lanterns Northampton | Fenster Glazing" and the meta description opens "Roof lights and roof lanterns in Northampton...", so the title/body mismatch is exactly as described. Comparators confirmed: /roof-lanterns/ = 4 occurrences with 1 heading ("Compare fixed and opening flat rooflights."), /flat-rooflights/ = 17 occurrences with 4 headings. The open item is real and still open at SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md:121 ("Verify 'roof lights' appears in on-page copy/H2s on the roof-lantern pages, not only titles") with the impression figures at lines 91-92. The dead-override claim holds: all five slugs return 301 live (roof-lanterns-milton-keynes → /roof-lanterns/, aluminium-bifold-doors-milton-keynes → /aluminium-bifold-doors/, upvc-doors-milton-keynes, composite-doors-milton-keynes, aluminium-doors-milton-keynes likewise), and their override entries sit at inc/generated-pages.php:380, 384, 388, 392 and 396 — inside the cited 252-440 range. I checked the three other -milton-keynes override keys are NOT dead: double-glazing-, windows- and doors-milton-keynes all return 200, so "five dead" is the correct count. Minor softness worth noting: SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md:92 itself cautions "Some is pre-Sept bot noise" about the MK query, so the 4,400-impression headline is slightly generous.

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED

- **Evidence:** generated-page.php:5166 vs online-quote.php:12-15; secondary-glazing.html FAQPage JSON-LD: "get a real figure without waiting for anybody to call you back".

The in-code comment at :45-46 documents the mechanism, not an intent to ship dead headlines.
