#### [196] The door-handle grid costs 1,499px of mobile scroll on four routes that already link to the handle hub

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `fg-handle-finishes--doors` renders eight handles at a measured 1,499px on mobile on /composite-doors/, /upvc-doors/, /aluminium-doors/ and (as the five-finish variant, 1,218px) /tilt-turn-windows/ and /patio-doors/. On composite it is the second-largest section on the page. `/handle-options/` exists as the site-wide handle hub and the section already ends with "See the full handle specification →".
- **Recommendation:** On mobile only, render the grid as a horizontally scrollable rail of the same eight cut-outs at 140px rather than a stacked grid — the pattern the colour rail already uses — and keep the full grid at 861px and above. That takes roughly 900px off four pages without removing a single finish or changing desktop.
- **Why:** Handle finish is a real decision but it is not the decision that closes the sale, and on mobile it currently outweighs the security section on three of the four pages that carry it.
- **Affected:** /composite-doors/, /upvc-doors/, /aluminium-doors/ (1,499px each); /tilt-turn-windows/, /patio-doors/ (1,218px, 1,098px).
- **Evidence:** Live measurement at 375x812: fg-handle-finishes--doors = 1,499px on composite-doors, upvc-doors and aluminium-doors; composite's largest sections are fg-cd3-colour 1,394 and handles 1,499.
- **Verification:** I rebuilt the anchor-text distribution independently over in-<main> internal links across all 712 pages and every headline number reproduced exactly: /composite-doors/ 837 inbound with 805 reading "Composite Doors" (96.2%, matching the claimed 96%) plus 'Compare composite doors':25, 'composite door':2, 'Composite doors':2 — the finding's dict verbatim; /aluminium-bifold-doors/ 803 of 836; /casement-windows/ 295 of 337 as "uPVC Casement Windows"; /windows-milton-keynes/ splitting 527 "Windows" and 296 "Double Glazed Windows Milton Keynes"; /contact/ 15 in-body against 2,151 total; /book-a-consultation/ 24 against 2,872 total. The cited component template-parts/components/link-cards.php exists (1,815 bytes). I also strengthened the structural claim the finding asserts qualitatively: counting links inside <p> elements, only 151 of 19,608 in-main internal links — 0.8% — sit in prose, so "essentially no contextual, in-sentence linking anywhere" is not just true but starker than stated, and the few that exist are mostly CTAs ("Compare colours across every material" x14, "instant quote tool" x10) rather than product mentions. Two small caveats that do not change the ruling: /composite-doors/ actually has 7 distinct anchors, not the 4 claimed, though the 3 extras are whole-card wrapper anchors (entire paragraph blobs) rather than genuine anchor variants, so the filtered count of 4 is defensible; and the finding is typed Objective while its own recommendation concedes this is "a relevance-breadth opportunity rather than a defect". I am keeping Objective because the deficiency is measurable and contextual internal linking is standard practice rather than design taste — but the honest framing in the recommendation should survive into any writeup, and the specific target of "15-20 contextual links" remains a judgement.

#### [66] The consent modal is the first experience of every mobile visitor, and the argument used to clear it cannot detect the harm it would cause

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** High · **Confidence:** 80% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** On a first visit at 375x812 the consent dialog renders full-screen over a dimmed page and locks scroll — I hit the lock myself: `window.scrollTo` and `scrollIntoView` had no effect until `.fg-cookie-consent__close` was clicked. GOOGLE-ADS-AUDIT-2026-08-11.md measures it at 501px of an 812px screen and notes 76% of ad spend is mobile. SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05 §F5 clears it with "There is no evidence the modal is costing traffic: CTR rose 33% post-launch with the modal live throughout." That reasoning does not hold: CTR is a SERP metric measured before the visitor arrives, so it is structurally incapable of detecting an on-site loss caused by an overlay the visitor meets after arriving. The modal may well be fine — but nothing measured so far shows it either way.
- **Recommendation:** Do not weaken the consent layer on this reasoning alone. Measure it: compare bounce/scroll-depth/lead rate for journeys where a choice was recorded within the first N seconds against those where it was not, using data already in the tracker. If the answer is that it costs leads, the change is a bottom-anchored banner that does not lock scroll rather than a centre modal — the choice quality is unaffected, the obstruction is.
- **Why:** 35.5% attributable traffic and a modal that every paid mobile click meets before the page. Whatever the truth, the current position rests on a metric that cannot answer the question, and the same audit correctly disqualified `banner_shown` as a denominator for exactly this kind of reasoning.
- **Affected:** Site-wide, first visit; heaviest on the 76% of ad spend that is mobile.
- **Evidence:** Live first-visit test at 375x812: dialog `.fg-cookie-consent` blocking, `document.documentElement` carrying `fg-cookie-consent-open`, scrollY pinned at 0 until close. GOOGLE-ADS-AUDIT-2026-08-11.md §8; SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05 §F5.
- **Verification:** Reproduced exactly, on both the template and the live site. The copy promises links the page does not have, and there is no other recovery surface. Only correction is cosmetic: the cited line numbers are off by one. The sentence is at 404.php:14 and the single button at 404.php:15 (the finding said 13 and 14). The template is 19 lines total and renders nothing between the sentence and the button. Live verification: GET https://fensterglazing.com/this-page-does-not-exist-xyz-abc/ returns HTTP 404 with a <main> block of 403 bytes containing exactly one anchor, href=https://fensterglazing.com/ labelled 'Back to home'. The no-search-box claim also holds: a strict grep for type="search", role="search" or searchform across all 40 live HTML files returns zero matches (an initial looser grep appeared to match many files, but that was the pattern 's=' matching unrelated markup — the strict pattern is the sound one). I found no ruling on the 404 page or on the absence of site search in AI.md, STYLE.md, HANDOVER.md or PROGRESS.md.

#### [75] The free consultation is offered only from the sticky header and footer — no product page or the homepage puts it in the page's own content

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 80% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Counting /book-a-consultation/ links in page content (between </header> and <footer) in the live HTML: homepage = 0, composite-doors = 0, casement-windows = 0, aluminium-bifold-doors = 0, patio-doors = 0, french-doors = 0, aluminium-windows = 0, heritage-windows = 0, flush-casement-windows = 0, double-glazing-replacement = 0; also 0 on /bow-bay-windows/ and /aluminium-sliding-doors/ by curl. The consultation IS persistently available — `Free Consultation` is a top-level header nav item styled as a solid steel button inside a header that is sticky on desktop and fixed on mobile, plus a mega-menu CTA card, a mobile-nav row and a footer link, which is the placement AI.md:64 records as intended. What is missing is any in-content offer: on the product heroes the two buttons are 'Start your design consultation' (→ a quote form) and 'Instant pricing', never 'Book a free consultation', and no later section reintroduces it. /sliding-sash-windows/ is the exception, carrying `Book a free consultation` as the secondary button in its gallery CTA at 41.5% depth, so the pattern exists and simply was not applied. AI.md:67 describes the visit as the process where the job is priced on an iPad from the same price list as the tool, which is the argument for surfacing it beside the tool rather than only in chrome.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `Book a free consultation` secondary button to the embed copy block at generated-page.php:5162-5178 (per finding 71) so all 20 embed routes gain an in-content route, and copy the /sliding-sash-windows/ gallery-CTA pattern to the homepage. Keep the word 'free' per AI.md:64. Do not add a second consultation button to the product hero button-row: the header already carries one above the fold on the same screen, and three consultation prompts in one viewport is worse than one.
- **Why:** Two links to the same page with different names in one band reads as a rendering bug to a user and dilutes the anchor-text signal. It also wastes 12–25% of a cap that is already truncating the parent-index link off the page.
- **Affected:** All 525 town-matrix pages. template-parts/sections/location-service.php:1437 and :1758
- **Evidence:** location-service.php:1437 `array_merge($product_links, $related_links)`; live band extraction: /double-glazing-luton/ 16 anchors with /windows-milton-keynes/, /doors-milton-keynes/, /composite-doors/, /aluminium-bifold-doors/ each appearing at positions 1-4 and again at 8-13
- **Verification:** The underlying measurement is right; the conclusion drawn from it is wrong, and the wrong part is the part that sets the impact.

CONFIRMED, the body-content count. Counting /book-a-consultation/ occurrences between `</header>` and `<footer` in the live HTML gives 0 on home, composite-doors, casement-windows, aluminium-bifold-doors, patio-doors, french-doors, aluminium-windows, heritage-windows, flush-casement-windows and double-glazing-replacement — exactly the ten routes listed. /sliding-sash-windows/ does carry one, in `fg-sash-gallery-cta__actions` at 41.5% of the HTML, as `<a class="button button--light" ...>Book a free consultation</a>` beside `Get a sash window quote`. So the pattern exists and is unapplied elsewhere, as claimed. I also confirmed on live curl that /bow-bay-windows/ and /aluminium-sliding-doors/ have 0. AI.md:64 and :67 are quoted correctly ('do not quietly drop the word "free" from a consultation CTA'; the iPad/same-price-list process).

REFUTED, the framing. Two claims are false. (1) 'occurrences of "/book-a-consultation/" after </header>: 0' — the real count after </header> is 1 on every one of those pages: the footer's `Book a Free Consultation` link. The finding's own stated metric returns 1, not 0. (2) 'The only route to it is the mega-menu' — false. Besides the mega-menu CTA card, `/book-a-consultation/` is a **top-level header nav item**, `<li class="site-nav__item site-nav__consultation"><a>Free Consultation</a>`, styled as a solid steel button (`.site-nav__consultation>a{padding:.72rem 1rem;border-radius:7px;background:var(--color-steel);color:#fff;font-weight:800}`), inside a header that is `position:sticky;top:0` on desktop and `position:fixed;z-index:1000` under 860px. It is also a row in the mobile nav. I can see it in shots/desktop/casement-windows--fold.png as the dark 'Free Consultation' button beside the green 'Instant Quote'. AI.md:64 explicitly records this as the intended placement: 'The header CTA stays `Free Consultation`, matching the length and title case of `Instant Quote` beside it.' So the consultation is persistently offered above the fold on every page, and 'appears zero times' / 'wastes it' does not survive.

What is left is real but much smaller: the product heroes and the homepage offer a quote route and an enquiry route but never a consultation route in the page's own content, even though /sliding-sash-windows/ shows the pattern. Impact drops from High to Medium and confidence from 95.

#### [80] /3d-visualiser/ — the site's highest-CTR page (136 clicks, 1.76%) — has no in-area exit and no consultation route, and P4 of the site's own audit is unimplemented

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 80% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** P4 of the project's own audit is unimplemented. The live page runs the thin shared quote-tool.php template (141 lines): eyebrow 'Product visualiser', H1 'Visualise your windows and doors with Fenster', one lead sentence, then the WindowCAD embed and the same generic six-required-field form. It carries zero in-content /book-a-consultation/ links — the four on the page are all nav and footer — and states no service area anywhere before the tool. Within the shared template it differs from its five sibling slugs only by heading, lead copy, eyebrow and enquiry `source` (quote-tool.php:24, :25, :39, :106); /online-quote/ has since been given its own 311-line bespoke template with a six-screen walkthrough, so the visualiser is now the thinner of the two. The audit's read is that its search demand is national ('door visualiser', 'window visualiser upload photo uk'), and its 21 consented in-window journeys produced no leads — a signal the audit itself labels directional rather than proven, since 21 journeys would be expected to yield about one lead at the base rate.
- **Recommendation:** Give the page one in-area branch above the tool: a short line naming the coverage (Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire, Bedfordshire, Northamptonshire, Hertfordshire — the wording already on /book-a-consultation/) with two buttons, `Book a free consultation` and `Get a fitted price`, and leave the tool for everyone else. Treat the zero-lead figure as a reason to instrument, not as proof: re-measure the same segment after 30 days with a larger sample, as P4 specifies. Do not de-prioritise the page; its national audience is not a fault.
- **Why:** Tablet is a real share of a home-improvement audience browsing in the evening, and on that device the primary navigation may be unusable. The missing aria-expanded also means a screen-reader user gets a panel that appears on focus with no announcement that it did.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages at viewports >= 861px on touch input. src/js/main.js:2833-2925, :2966; src/scss/main.scss:670-673, :22586; inc/template-tags.php:63-68
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:2866-2867 registers only `pointerenter`/`pointerleave`/`focusin`/`focusout`; no `click` listener exists between lines 2833 and 2925; main.scss:22586 `@media (max-width: 860px)` is the only place `.site-nav` becomes the drawer; template-tags.php:63-68 printf emits `<li class=…><a href=…>Label</a>` with no aria attributes. Not verified on a physical tablet
- **Verification:** The core claim holds. /3d-visualiser/ carries 4 links to /book-a-consultation/ and all 4 are outside <main> (two in the mega nav, one in the mobile nav, one in the footer) — zero in content, as claimed. The rendered <main> text before the enquiry form names no service area: it runs eyebrow 'Product visualiser', H1, one lead sentence, then straight into the embed. The route is on the shared quote-tool.php (generated-page.php:309 lists it in $is_quote_tool; online-quote.php:5-9 records that /online-quote/ was split off and 'the others stay on the shared one until the visualiser gets its own treatment'). SEO-LEAD-AUDIT §P4 is real and unimplemented. Two corrections. (a) 'Its only differentiator from /online-quote/ is the heading' is wrong on both halves: /online-quote/ now runs a bespoke 311-line template with a six-screen walkthrough and its own H1/H2 set, while /3d-visualiser/ runs the thin 141-line shared template — they are structurally different pages; and within the shared template the visualiser differs from its five sibling slugs by four things, not one (quote-tool.php:24 heading, :25 lead copy, :39 eyebrow, :106 enquiry `source`). (b) The title juxtaposes '136 clicks, 0 leads' as if the 136 were the denominator. The 136 is GSC clicks; the zero-lead observation is over 21 consented journeys, and SEO-LEAD-AUDIT §F1 states in bold that at the base rate 21 journeys would be expected to yield about one lead, so 'read this as directional, not proven'. Confidence should reflect that.

#### [81] 62 chat opens produced no capturable lead, and the chat drawer offers no route to the phone, a consultation or a lead record

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 75% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** In the 24-day window `chat_opened` = 62, more than double `form_started` (28) and nearly seven times `phone_click` (9). It is the most-used interactive surface on the site after the embed, and nothing in it can become a lead. inc/legend-assistant.php:73 forbids the assistant from claiming to have submitted an enquiry, and LIVECHAT.md:105 records that chat 'does not submit the chat as a Fenster enquiry... add a CRM lead'. The drawer itself (template-parts/components/legend-assistant.php, 133 lines) contains no phone link, no consultation link and no quick-action chips — its only anchors are 'Who is Legend?' and the Privacy Policy. Separately, inc/legend-assistant.php:389 tells the assistant not to add a telephone alternative unless the visitor asks to speak to someone or cannot use the quote tool; note this is scoped to price answers (it is the third sentence of a 'Do not estimate prices' clause) and the phone and email remain available to the model unconditionally via :76, so it narrows how the phone is offered on pricing questions rather than suppressing it site-wide.
- **Recommendation:** Two changes, in order. (1) The cheaper and lower-risk one first: add a phone chip and a `Book a free consultation` chip to the drawer itself (template-parts/components/legend-assistant.php), so the channel exists in the UI regardless of what the model chooses to say. (2) Then consider widening :389 so that on explicit buying intent (price, timescale, booking, 'can you do X') the assistant may offer the phone and the free consultation alongside the tool — a small edit to a price-scoped clause, not a rewrite of the prompt. (3) A structured 'Ask us to call you' handoff posting name and phone to `fenster_submit_enquiry` with source 'Legend chat' would change the lead-record position in LIVECHAT.md:180, AI.md:234 and the Privacy Policy; it needs the owner's decision and a policy update — do not ship it silently.
- **Why:** These are the last pages before an enquiry. A visitor who has just chosen a handle finish has nowhere to go except the browser back button, and 35 pages funnel into /colour-options/ to arrive at that.
- **Affected:** /online-quote/, /book-a-consultation/, /handle-options/, /colour-options/, /fensa-approved-installers/
- **Evidence:** Content-only out-degree over the live HTML with site-header, site-footer, legend-assistant and fg-cookie-consent blocks removed: online-quote 2, book-a-consultation 2, handle-options 2, colour-options 3, fensa-approved-installers 3; probe-desktop.json `/book-a-consultation/`.ctas = 0; content in-links: colour-options 35, handle-options 14
- **Verification:** Every citation is exact. inc/legend-assistant.php:73 is 'Do not claim to have submitted an enquiry, booked an appointment, checked an account or passed a message to a person.' Line :389 is verbatim as quoted and is the only occurrence of 'telephone alternative' anywhere in the repo. LIVECHAT.md:105 and :180 are correct. The event counts (chat_opened 62, form_started 28, phone_click 9) match SEO-LEAD-AUDIT §4. And the gap is real: template-parts/components/legend-assistant.php (133 lines) contains no tel: link, no consultation link and no quick-action chips — the only anchors are 'Who is Legend?' and two Privacy Policy links. But the characterisation of :389 is wrong. That instruction sits inside a price-specific clause — 'Do not estimate prices. Direct visitors to the instant quote tool unless a price is explicitly published for the exact request. Do not add a telephone alternative unless...' — so it restrains the assistant from bolting the phone onto a *price* answer, not from offering it on buying intent generally. The phone and email are supplied unconditionally in the base prompt at :76 ('When useful, the Fenster team can be reached on %s or at %s'), and :389 itself explicitly permits the phone when the visitor asks to speak to someone or cannot use the tool. AI.md:234 also directs Legend to 'the real contact routes when human action is required'. So 'the surface with the most hand-raisers is prevented from offering the channel most likely to close them' overstates a narrow price-answer rule. The second half of the recommendation still stands and still needs the owner, since AI.md:234 and LIVECHAT.md:105 place chat outside the lead record.

#### [82] No low-friction form entry exists — no callback request, no WhatsApp; every form route demands the same 6 required fields

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 70% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Every form-based conversion route on the site demands the same six required fields (name, phone, email, postcode, free-text project details, privacy), and the alternative is a third-party configurator. Scanning all 38 live pages: zero callback offers — the only two mentions argue against one (`/secondary-glazing/` 'a real figure without waiting for anybody to call you back', and the homepage 'No callback needed to begin' at home-experience.php:274). Zero WhatsApp. probe-desktop.json confirms the form is identical on all 30 routes that carry one: 8 visible controls, 6 required. The phone (`tel:01908429200`, present on every page) and the Legend chat (62 opens in the window) are the only low-commitment surfaces that exist, and neither produces a structured lead — the phone because it depends on the visitor ringing, the chat for the reasons in finding 81. Showroom-visit CTAs do exist beyond /contact/ and /meet-the-team/ — /about/, /why-trust-fenster/ and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ all carry one — but none of the 14 product pages does.
- **Recommendation:** Take it to the owner first: the homepage currently sells 'No callback needed to begin' as a benefit of the instant-quote route, so adding a callback offer is a positioning change, not just a component. If agreed, add one two-field variant — name and mobile, plus the privacy checkbox — labelled 'Ask us to call you back', rendered inside the embed block and beside every product enquiry form. It reuses `fenster_submit_enquiry` with a distinct `source` and a `project_type` of 'Callback request'; the only server change is relaxing the required-field check in inc/enquiries.php:591 for that source. Do not state a response time — AI.md:478 forbids inventing one for repairs and the same discipline should hold here — say 'we will ring you back' and let the office set the expectation.
- **Why:** The footer is the persistent fallback IA on a site with no search and no breadcrumbs. A user looking for doors reads 'Windows and doors', clicks, and lands on a page headed 'Double glazed windows in Milton Keynes' with no doors on it.
- **Affected:** Footer on all 712 pages. template-parts/layout/site-footer.php:9-18 and :19-29
- **Evidence:** site-footer.php:11 `['label' => 'Windows and doors', 'url' => home_url('/windows-milton-keynes/')]`; no `/doors-milton-keynes/`, `/other-services/`, `/composite-doors/`, `/blog/` or `/careers/` string in the file; live footer extraction returns 32 anchors matching the source exactly
- **Verification:** The central gap is real and reproduces: a text scan of all 38 live pages for callback offers returns two hits and neither is an offer — /secondary-glazing/ ('a real figure without waiting for anybody to call you back') and, which the finding missed, home.html ('No callback needed to begin'). WhatsApp: zero across all 38. And probe-desktop.json confirms 30 of 38 routes carry the form with an identical shape: 8 visible controls (name, phone, email, postcode, message, attachments, privacy, company_website honeypot) and 6 required. inc/enquiries.php:591 is exactly the required-field line quoted. Three scope errors, though. (a) 'Showroom-visit CTAs appear only on /contact/ and /meet-the-team/' is false — /about/ carries 'Come and see us... Come and see it', /why-trust-fenster/ carries 'Find the showroom', and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ carries 'Open directions' plus a 'Showroom and directions' section; at least 5 pages, and 10 pages mention it inside <main>. (b) 'No low-commitment entry exists anywhere on the site' is false as written: every page carries `tel:01908429200` (4 instances on the homepage alone) and the site-wide Legend chat drew 62 opens in the window, which is precisely a 'quick question' surface. The true claim is narrower — no *form-based* low-friction entry, i.e. no callback request. (c) The homepage markets 'No callback needed to begin' as a benefit at home-experience.php:274, so the recommendation runs against a positioning line already in the copy and needs the owner rather than being a straight add. Minor: AI.md:478 is inside the Repairs section and is scoped to repair copy, not a site-wide rule — the principle still applies but the citation should say so. Confidence should come down accordingly.

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED

The renderer confirms the cause: template-tags.php:107-112 prints the column heading as `<a … href="<?= $column['url'] ?? $item['url'] ?>">` and :115-119 prints the 'View all {label}' row from the same URL. (2) 'There is no sectors index page anywhere on the site' is true of LIVE only. But the repo's replacement hub, template-parts/sections/commercial-glazing-v2.php:126-183, links all seven — schools, student accommodation, hospitality, care homes, offices and retail, healthcare, industrial — and generated-page.php:3130 renders it for /commercial-glazing/. So the 'All Sectors is a broken promise' defect disappears the moment the in-flight commercial overhaul deploys, and the recommendation to 'build a short sectors index' is moot. What survives is the duplicate-target problem, which the overhaul does not touch: two column headings and their two 'View all' rows all resolve to one URL, and the Products top-level anchor duplicates its own 'Windows' column. #### [295] /double-glazing-replacement/ is the one page linking the glass hub through its redirect

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `fenster_process_enquiry_uploads()` (inc/enquiries.php:352-410) stores visitor attachments with `wp_handle_upload()` at inc/enquiries.php:383, which writes to the default WordPress uploads path and returns a public URL. The `wp_insert_attachment(['post_status' => 'private'])` at :395 marks the attachment *post* private but places no restriction on the file on disk, and `wp_update_attachment_metadata(wp_generate_attachment_metadata(...))` at :400 additionally generates public resized copies of every image. Verified on live: `/app/uploads/` is served statically by nginx with autoindex off, and an existing file under it returns 200 (`/app/uploads/2026/04/2.png` -> 200, 51,445 bytes, image/png). There is no deny rule on the path — a nonexistent file under it falls through to the WordPress 404 (`/app/uploads/2026/08/IMG_0001.jpg` -> 404 with a 93KB WP page, not 403) — and the theme registers no `upload_dir` filter anywhere (grep for `upload_dir` across all theme PHP returns zero hits). Anyone who knows or guesses the filename can fetch a customer's photo or document unauthenticated. Filenames are the visitor's own filename passed through `sanitize_file_name()`, so phone-camera defaults (IMG_1234.jpg) are enumerable in a few thousand requests. Mitigating: the open `/wp-json/wp/v2/media` endpoint does NOT leak them — it returns 1,123 items, all `status: inherit`, newest dated 2026-04, so private enquiry attachments are excluded. Validation is otherwise sound: an 11-type mime whitelist, an 8MB cap and a 5-file limit are all enforced at :376-381.
- **Recommendation:** Confirm with the owner whether enquiry attachments should be private. If so, either (a) scope an `upload_dir` filter to this handler so enquiry files land in a directory outside the web root and serve them through an authenticated admin route, or (b) add an nginx `location` block denying direct access to that subdirectory — note that a blanket deny on `/app/uploads/` would break the 1,123 legacy media files that are legitimately public. If the owner is content with WordPress-default behaviour, record it as a ruling in AI.md so future audits stop raising it.
- **Why:** One extra round trip on a mobile connection, on a link a visitor is likely to follow while deciding whether to upgrade the glass at the same time as the unit — which is the upsell that section exists to make. Trivially cheap to fix and it removes the only redirecting internal link on the site.
- **Affected:** /double-glazing-replacement/ — one anchor.
- **Evidence:** Sweep of 655 unique internal URLs: 654 return 200 on GET. Repeated three times: `GET /obscured-glass/` = 200, `GET /obscure-glass/` = 301 → /obscured-glass/. `grep -o 'fensterglazing.com/obscure\(d\)\?-glass/'` shows /double-glazing-replacement/ as the sole file using the short form; 15 other product pages use /obscured-glass/.
- **Verification:** Reproduced and strengthened. Every code claim is exact at the cited lines: :383 `wp_handle_upload($file, ['test_form' => false, 'mimes' => $allowed_mimes])`, :395 `'post_status' => 'private'`, :406 `'url' => (string) ($handled['url'] ?? '')` stored into `_fenster_attachments` at :690. The original finding hedged to INVESTIGATE because it could not demonstrate an exposed file; I closed that gap. `/app/uploads/2026/04/2.png` returns 200 with real image bytes, proving files under the uploads path are publicly served. The 403-vs-404 split is decisive about the server config: `/app/uploads/`, `/app/uploads/2025/`, `/app/uploads/2026/06|07|08/` all return a 75,193-byte nginx 403 (directory exists, autoindex off) while `/app/uploads-fake/`, `/app/uploads/2019/` and `/app/uploads/2026/12/` return the WordPress 404 — so there is no deny rule, and the 2026/08 month directory exists on live right now, i.e. files are being written there. No `upload_dir` filter exists in the theme. No owner ruling covers this: the only attachment ruling in AI.md is line 173, which is about the office email printing a count rather than filenames, and AUDIT.md:55 praises the mime whitelist and size caps without addressing URL privacy. The privacy policy live says only that uploaded files "may be kept with the related enquiry or customer record" and makes no storage-security promise, so there is no explicit contradiction — but it is customer photos of their own homes at a guessable public URL, which is the finding's point. Impact Low and risk Medium are both fair; I have raised confidence from 62 to 88 and would move it out of INVESTIGATE, since the mechanism is now demonstrated rather than inferred. The only residual uncertainty is the effort needed to guess a filename, not whether the file is reachable.

#### [61] The desktop mega menu has no aria-haspopup/aria-expanded and Escape does not close it; above 860px there is no drawer fallback for touch input

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The mobile drawer is gated solely by `@media (max-width: 860px)` — `.site-nav-toggle` is `display: none` at src/scss/main.scss:232 and only becomes `inline-flex` inside that query at :22664 — so above 861px the mega panel is the only navigation. It opens purely on hover/focus: main.scss:670-673 shows it on `:hover`/`:focus-within` (overriding the `[hidden]` attribute), and src/js/main.js:2874-2877 and :2875-2921 register only pointerenter/pointerleave/pointerover/mouseover/focusin/focusout — I read the whole 2833-2925 block and there is no `click` or `pointerdown` listener. The confirmed defects that follow are accessibility ones: the trigger is a bare `<a href>` with no `aria-haspopup` and no `aria-expanded` (inc/template-tags.php:66-71; the only aria-expanded in the file is on the mobile accordion buttons at :189/:206/:234), so a keyboard or screen-reader user gets a panel that appears on focus with nothing announcing it, and the Escape handler at main.js:2971 is gated on `is-nav-open`, which the resize handler at :2977 strips above 860 — so Escape cannot close an open desktop panel. The touch-tablet consequence is milder than it first looks: the delegated `pointerover` listener does fire on a tap, so the panel opens momentarily, and all three triggers href real hub pages (/windows-milton-keynes/, /doors-milton-keynes/, /commercial-glazing/), so a tap that navigates lands on a working page. The degradation is that a touch user between 861px and desktop width cannot hold the menu open to reach a child route. Not verified on physical hardware.
- **Recommendation:** Two small changes, in priority order. First, the a11y fix, which is unconditional: set `aria-haspopup="true"` on the mega trigger in `fenster_render_nav_fallback()` (inc/template-tags.php:66-71) and keep `aria-expanded` in sync from the same open/close helpers in src/js/main.js:2848-2860, and widen the Escape handler at main.js:2971 so it also closes any open desktop panel and returns focus to its trigger. Second, add a pointer-type guard in the same JS block: on `pointerdown` where `event.pointerType !== 'mouse'`, preventDefault the first tap on a closed panel and open it instead, letting a second tap on the same trigger follow the href.
- **Why:** A hard gate on an early required field, failing with an error message that names no fix, on a field a mobile user is most likely to paste or autofill.
- **Affected:** All 30 form routes; 4 input declarations in one component plus one line of JS.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:51, :131, :156, :270; inc/enquiries.php:502-506; src/js/main.js:2473-2490.
- **Verification:** Every code claim reproduces, and the line cites are accurate. src/js/main.js:2874-2877 registers only pointerenter/pointerleave/focusin/focusout on each desktop item, and the delegated siteHeader listeners at 2875-2921 are pointerover/mouseover/focusin/pointerout/mouseout/focusout — I read the whole 2833-2925 block and there is no click or pointerdown handler in it. src/scss/main.scss:670-673 is exactly `.site-nav__item:hover > .site-nav__mega, .site-nav__item:focus-within > .site-nav__mega { display: block; }`, and because that rule beats the UA `[hidden]` style, the panel is CSS-hover-driven independently of the JS. src/scss/main.scss:22586 is `@media (max-width: 860px)` and it is the only gate: `.site-nav-toggle { display: none }` at :232 globally and `display: inline-flex` only inside that query (:22664), so above 861px there is genuinely no hamburger and no drawer. The resize handler at main.js:2977 tears down `is-nav-open` above 860, and the Escape handler at :2971 is gated on `is-nav-open`, so Escape cannot close a desktop panel. inc/template-tags.php:66-71 emits `<li class="…"><a href="…">Label</a>` with no aria-haspopup and no aria-expanded; the only aria-expanded in the file is on the mobile accordion buttons (:189, :206, :234). The single `@media (hover: none)` block in the stylesheet (main.scss:11516) covers `.fg-case-spec-list` and nothing navigational. What I am revising is the severity framing, not the facts. 'The primary navigation may be unusable' overstates it: all three mega triggers href real hub pages (/windows-milton-keynes/, /doors-milton-keynes/, /commercial-glazing/), so a tablet tap that navigates lands the visitor on a working hub rather than nowhere — degraded, not broken. And the delegated `pointerover` listener does fire on a touch tap in Chrome, so the panel opens before the navigation, meaning the failure mode is 'panel flashes then the page changes', not 'nothing happens'. The unambiguous, evidence-backed defects are the missing aria-haspopup/aria-expanded on a focus-revealed panel and Escape not closing it — both a11y, both fixable in a few lines. The tablet-tap half remains unverified on real hardware (the finding says so itself), and the finding's own confidence of 78 is about right for that half.

#### [121] Four routes position our own products on price, in the exact softer forms TONEOFVOICE.md:164 bans by name

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** TONEOFVOICE.md:159 bans "premium" outright and :164 records the owner instruction of 2026-07-24 banning "budget, cheap, or any wording that positions one of our own products as the low-cost option... This covers the softer forms too: 'at a lower cost than', 'warmer for the money', 'costs less'." PROGRESS.md:3611 shows the enforcement sweep only covered "the whole hub block", which is why these survived. `/sliding-sash-windows/` carries four breaches in `template-parts/sections/generated-page.php`: Ultimate Rose is "The premium choice" (:464), Charisma Rose's eyebrow is "Cost-conscious sash style" (:491), its copy is "The accessible Rose Collection option... for projects balancing appearance and budget" (:493) and its best-for line reads "rental refurbishments" (:497). `/patio-doors/` carries two in `inc/product-hub-data.php`: "the value-led sliding option" (:261) and "the cost-effective sliding option" (:467) — note PROGRESS.md:3611 records fixing "at a lower cost than the aluminium equivalent" on this exact page, so this is the same fault reworded. `/integral-blinds/` carries one, `inc/site-data.php:2143`, "so the operation matches the room and budget" (it renders twice, but it is one string). `/casement-windows/` carries one that the original finding missed: "a fixed pane costs less than an opener the same size", which is the softer form :164 names verbatim.
- **Recommendation:** Eight strings, four files. Charisma Rose's eyebrow (generated-page.php:491) becomes what it physically is — "60mm meeting rail, sculptured profile"; its copy (:493) drops "balancing appearance and budget" and its best-for line (:497) drops "rental refurbishments". Ultimate Rose's "premium choice" (:464) becomes the fact underneath it: "the finest meeting rail in the Rose Collection, at 35mm". The two patio lines (product-hub-data.php:261, :467) say what a slider does that a bifold does not — no swing space, no folding stack — instead of what it costs less than. site-data.php:2143 drops "and budget" and says what actually differs between magnetic and electric (no wiring vs remote or switch control). On casement, "a fixed pane costs less than an opener the same size" becomes what it physically is: no hinges, no gearing, a slimmer border and more glass, which the same sentence already says.
- **Why:** A visitor arriving on "sash window prices" finds no price and a FAQ telling them prices are on the page. That is the fastest possible bounce, and it is a helpful-content and structured-data-accuracy problem on the highest-intent template on the site. It also directly explains part of F4's "price guides are invisible": three of the seven have nothing to rank with.
- **Affected:** 3 of 7 price guides: /sash-window-prices/ (390 words), /aluminium-window-prices/ (387), /patio-french-door-prices/ (391)
- **Evidence:** Regex `£[\d,]+` over `<main>` text: window-door-prices-milton-keynes ['£600','£2,000','£3,500'], composite-door-prices ['£2,000'], bifold-door-cost ['£3,500'], double-glazing-cost ['£600'], sash-window-prices [], aluminium-window-prices [], patio-french-door-prices []. All seven contain the string "Each checked example is a real fitted price". All seven emit FAQPage. Source: inc/generated-pages.php ~line 770 `'price' => 'To confirm from WindowCAD'`.
- **Verification:** Every quoted string is real and I reproduced all of them verbatim from the live HTML and located each in source. The rule is real and quoted correctly. Two scope errors.

RULE CONFIRMED: TONEOFVOICE.md:159 lists "premium" on the never-use line; TONEOFVOICE.md:164 is the owner instruction of 2026-07-24 and reads exactly as quoted, including "This covers the softer forms too: 'at a lower cost than', 'warmer for the money', 'costs less'." PROGRESS.md:3611 records the original sweep and says explicitly it covered "the whole hub block" — which is why the sash page (generated-page.php) and the current patio hub strings were never checked. The patio line PROGRESS.md:3611 says was fixed ("at a lower cost than the aluminium equivalent") has simply been replaced by "value-led" and "cost-effective", the same offence reworded.

SOURCE LOCATIONS I VERIFIED: inc/product-hub-data.php:261 ("value-led sliding option"), :467 ("cost-effective sliding option"); template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:464 ("The premium choice"), :491 (tagline "Cost-conscious sash style"), :493 ("The accessible Rose Collection option... balancing appearance and budget"), :497 ("rental refurbishments"); inc/site-data.php:2143 ("matches the room and budget").

ERROR 1 — title says "Four pages", body and affected say three. Three routes are described.
ERROR 2 — /integral-blinds/ is ONE source string, not two. site-data.php:2143 appears once in source; the live HTML contains it twice because the block renders twice. Same for the sash "Cost-conscious" tagline. Counting rendered occurrences inflates the fix size.
ERROR 3 (in the finding's favour) — the sweep missed a genuine fourth route. /casement-windows/ prints "a fixed pane costs less than an opener the same size", which is the exact softer form TONEOFVOICE.md:164 names. I also checked "cheapest" on /upvc-doors/ ("the cheapest thing on the whole door to improve", about a cylinder upgrade) and /double-glazing-replacement/ ("easiest and cheapest now", about timing) — neither positions one of our products as the low-cost option, so both are clean.

#### [90] 525 of 712 H1s end "designed around your home." — the exact campaign phrasing TONEOFVOICE bans by name

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** Every town-matrix route renders an H1 of the form "<Product> in <Town>, designed around your home." TONEOFVOICE.md:142 lists "Designed around you" as a banned campaign heading by name. STYLE.md is also explicit that an H1 is the name of the thing with no closing full stop: "`Sheerline heritage aluminium doors`, not `The steel-door look, without the steel.` … No closing full stop on an H1. It is a name, not a sentence." This H1 breaks both halves at once: it appends a campaign tail to the name, and it closes with a full stop. Measured over all 712 live pages: 591 H1s carry a closing full stop, 121 do not, and 525 of the 591 are this one pattern. It is the first line of text on 74% of the indexed site.
- **Recommendation:** Cut the tail and the stop: `uPVC casement windows in Bletchley`, `Aluminium doors in Luton`. The persuading already lives in the paragraph below it, exactly as STYLE.md prescribes. One string change in the location-service H1 builder fixes all 525 routes. Leave `/about/`'s `Simple, honest glazing.` alone — STYLE.md carves it out explicitly.
- **Why:** This is the single highest-leverage copy string on the site. It is the H1 Google shows, the first thing a visitor reads, and it currently announces on three quarters of the site that the copy was written from a template brief rather than about their house. The owner banned this exact construction and it was never swept.
- **Affected:** 525 live routes (all product×town matrix pages). Source: the H1 builder in template-parts/sections/location-service.php; sample H1s /casement-windows-bletchley/, /aluminium-doors-luton/.
- **Evidence:** Measured across all 712 live pages fetched 2026-08-13: H1 ending "designed around your home." = 525; H1 with closing full stop = 591, without = 121. Live: `[H1] uPVC casement windows in Bletchley, designed around your home.` Rule: TONEOFVOICE.md:142 and STYLE.md "No closing full stop on an H1."
- **Verification:** Reproduced exactly, to the number.

I parsed the <h1> out of every one of the 712 crawled pages with a node script. Results: 712 pages, 712 with exactly one H1, 525 whose H1 ends 'designed around your home.', 591 with a closing full stop, 121 without. Every figure in the finding matches to the unit. 525/712 = 73.7%, so '74% of the indexed site' is right.

The source is real and it is a single string: template-parts/sections/location-service.php:1460 renders `esc_html($service_label . ' in ' . $location_name . ', designed around your home.')`. One edit fixes all 525 routes, as claimed. Live samples confirmed: 'Aluminium bifold doors in Ampthill, designed around your home.', 'uPVC casement windows in Bletchley, designed around your home.'

Both rules are cited at the right lines and both are violated. TONEOFVOICE.md:142 reads 'Never use campaign headings: "Designed around you", "Explore the possibilities"...' — the H1 tail is that construction with one word swapped, and STYLE.md:262 repeats the ban. STYLE.md:257 is the owner instruction of 2026-07-22 that 'The H1 on a product or service page is the name of the thing, not a line about it', and STYLE.md:258 is unambiguous: 'No closing full stop on an H1. It is a name, not a sentence. This is the one place TONEOFVOICE.md\'s full-stop rule does not apply.' The town-matrix routes are product-and-service pages, squarely in scope. STYLE.md:259 even prescribes the fix the finding proposes — 'the persuading moves down one level: the eyebrow carries the location line, and the lead paragraph directly under the H1 does the selling' — and the pages already have both.

No carve-out exists. `grep -rn 'designed around your home' *.md` returns zero hits across every project doc, so this was never sanctioned; the only other occurrence in the theme is an unrelated meta description at generated-page.php:861. The /about/ exemption the finding preserves is real and is at STYLE.md:261.

The finding cites the STYLE.md rule by quotation rather than line number; for the record it is STYLE.md:257-261.

#### [186] Four routes are still on the generic product-journey template and read as brochure copy, including a dead duplicated block

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** L · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** SEO-LEAD-AUDIT F4/P6 asked for exactly this diagnosis: 'Check coverage in Search Console, internal links into the seven pages'. Measured by exact-href across all 712 crawled pages, each guide has 2–3 inbound links and only one is linked from the product page it prices. `/composite-doors/` → `/composite-door-prices/` exists. But `/sliding-sash-windows/` does not link `/sash-window-prices/`; `/aluminium-windows/` does not link `/aluminium-window-prices/`; `/aluminium-bifold-doors/` does not link `/bifold-door-cost/`; `/patio-doors/` and `/french-doors/` do not link `/patio-french-door-prices/`; `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` does not link `/double-glazing-cost/`. The guides are absent from the header and footer too (checked on the full document of /composite-doors/ outside `<main>`), so almost all of their authority comes from one hub, `/window-door-prices-milton-keynes/`. None of the 525 matrix pages links any price guide — but not for the reason the link-band filter suggests. The `preg_match('/(?:price|prices|cost)/i')` exclusion at location-service.php:1437-1439 lives inside the `if ($is_mk_double_glazing_page)` branch opened at :866 and closed by the `return` at :1447, so it governs `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` alone and explains only that one missing link. The matrix pages render the separate band at :1750-1758, which applies no price filter; they link no guide simply because no guide is ever present in the `$product_links`/`$related_links` pool handed to the template at :15.
- **Recommendation:** Add the matching price guide to each product page's link band — six edits on /sliding-sash-windows/, /aluminium-windows/, /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /patio-doors/, /french-doors/ and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/. For the last of those, the `price|prices|cost` filter at location-service.php:1437-1439 is the specific blocker and can be narrowed or dropped, but note it affects only that route: nothing there will change the 525 matrix pages. If matrix pages should link guides at all, that is a separate change to how `$related_links` is built for those routes (location-service.php:15 / the caller in generated-page.php), and it is a judgement call rather than a bug fix — 525 pages pointing at seven thin guides is not obviously desirable. Re-check GSC impressions for the seven at the October export before writing any more price content.
- **Why:** These are the four highest-ticket or highest-margin products on the site (bifolds, aluminium windows, sliding doors, integral blinds) and they are the four written in the voice the owner has spent four months removing everywhere else.
- **Affected:** /patio-doors/, /aluminium-windows/, /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /integral-blinds/.
- **Evidence:** Third-person "Fenster <verb>" counts in live main content: bifold 7, integral-blinds 6, aluminium-windows 5, patio-doors 5, against 1–2 on all eleven rebuilt routes; template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:4094 `<div class="fg-product-why__panel" hidden>`; no `product-why__panel` reference in assets/js/main.js.
- **Verification:** The measurement is exactly right; the diagnosis of the matrix tier is wrong. Re-running an exact-href inbound count over `<main>` across all 712 crawled pages reproduces the finding's list character for character: composite-door-prices 3 [composite-doors, doors-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes]; sash-window-prices 2 [windows-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes]; aluminium-window-prices 2 [same]; bifold-door-cost 2 [doors-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes]; patio-french-door-prices 2 [doors-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes]; double-glazing-cost 3 [windows-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes, other-services]. Only /composite-doors/ links its own guide. I also checked the whole document minus `<main>` on /composite-doors/ — no guide appears in header or footer, so the header/footer claim holds. But the causal attribution is false. The `preg_match('/(?:price|prices|cost)/i')` filter at location-service.php:1437-1439 sits inside the `if ($is_mk_double_glazing_page)` branch opened at location-service.php:866 and closed by the `<?php return; ?>` immediately after the band at :1447. It applies to `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` and to nothing else. The 525 matrix pages render the other link band at location-service.php:1750-1758, which does `array_slice(array_values(array_merge($product_links, $related_links)), 0, 24)` with no price filter at all — they link no guide because no guide is ever in `$product_links`/`$related_links` (passed in as `$args['links']` at :15), not because anything filters them out. So the filter explains exactly one missing link (/double-glazing-milton-keynes/ → /double-glazing-cost/), and 'reconsider the filter' will not put a single link on a matrix page.
