#### [175] /patio-doors/ key specification says "14 options" while the same page shows sixteen swatches under "Sixteen colours outside"

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The key-specification strip prints `Colour choice: 14 options`. 4,300px further down the same page, the colour section is headed "Sixteen colours outside, matched or white inside." and renders 16 `colours_page_image-*.webp` swatches plus the Smooth White hex fallback. `inc/site-data.php:417` already carries the note "'14 options' was wrong: the door takes the same foil range as the windows, owner-confirmed 2026-08-12, which is 16" — that correction was applied to `upvc-doors` (line 428, now 13) and the identical wrong value was left in the `patio-doors` block 30 lines below it.
- **Recommendation:** Add an output-buffer minifier chained into the existing `fenster_strip_ungated_tracking_output` callback (inc/consent.php:38), which already regexes the whole document. But treat this as a Medium-risk change, not Low: `preg_replace('/>\s+</', '><', $html)` deletes whitespace that is rendering-significant between inline and inline-block elements, and protecting <pre>, <textarea> and <script> does not address that. Either (a) collapse each whitespace run to a single space rather than deleting it — that captures most of the 149 KB on /areas-we-cover/ with no rendering change at all, since the cost there is indentation runs of 20-40 spaces, not the single separator; or (b) if you delete outright, ship it behind a query-string flag first and diff rendered screenshots across the four heaviest routes plus one of each template before enabling it site-wide. Expect roughly 700-1,300 B per page over the wire (I measured 733 B on /areas-we-cover/ with inter-tag collapse; the finding's 1,300 B needs the more aggressive transform), so justify this on halved HTML parse volume on the four routes over 180 KB, not on bandwidth. Separately and independently of the minifier, emit the 550 town links on /areas-we-cover/ root-relative: 732 occurrences of the 26-character `https://fensterglazing.com` prefix is 19,032 B of raw markup for nothing.
- **Why:** The strip's entire effect is that the numbers are checkable. A visitor who counts the swatches finds the headline figure is wrong by two, on the first credibility element of the page, and the page contradicts itself in its own heading.
- **Affected:** /patio-doors/ plus every /patio-doors-<town>/ matrix route reading the same array.
- **Evidence:** inc/site-data.php:447 `['label' => 'Colour choice', 'value' => '14 options']`; the corrective comment sits at inc/site-data.php:417; live /patio-doors/ h2 "Sixteen colours outside, matched or white inside." with 16 distinct colours_page_image-*.webp swatches counted in the markup.
- **Verification:** The forensic byte-splitting is astonishingly accurate and the risk rating is wrong. VERIFIED TO WITHIN 10 BYTES: walking the nested <section> depth in live/areas-we-cover.html, the fg-areas-page__body section is 230,488 B (claimed 230,498) containing exactly 550 `<a ` tags (claimed 550) of which 148,886 B is `\n\s+` whitespace runs (claimed 148,896). Page total 319,910 (claimed 319,876). Fixed chrome: <header> is 15,180 B and <footer> 7,549 B, byte-identical between home.html and contact.html; <head> across four pages ranges 19,118-19,591 B. The output buffer the recommendation wants to hang this on is real and unconditional — inc/consent.php:31 hooks fenster_start_tracking_output_buffer at template_redirect priority 0 and :38 calls ob_start('fenster_strip_ungated_tracking_output'), skipping only admin/ajax/json. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) The compressed saving is smaller than stated. With a conservative `>\s+<` collapse I get areas-we-cover brotli 20,646 -> 19,913, a 733 B saving, not the claimed 1,300; across five pages 115,027 -> 111,223 brotli, 3.3% not 6.0%. My baseline brotli matches the finding's exactly (20,646), so the divergence is that its minifier was more aggressive than inter-tag collapse alone — meaning the stated saving is only reachable with a transform stronger than the `preg_replace('/>\s+</','><')` the recommendation actually proposes. Either way the finding's own honest framing ('a small win, not a large one') survives. (2) Risk is not Low. `>\s+<` deletes whitespace that is rendering-significant between inline and inline-block elements, and the guard list given (pre, textarea, script) does not cover that at all. I checked the specific case: .fg-areas-page__town-panel > summary is display:flex (src/scss/main.scss:5951-5952) so its `<span>`/`<em>` pair is safe, but that is one component out of a 42,407-line stylesheet applied across 712 routes, and a single non-flex inline pair anywhere produces run-together words in production. One further correction in the finding's favour: the absolute-URL saving is bigger than stated — 732 occurrences of `https://fensterglazing.com` at 26 chars = 19,032 B, not ~15 KB.

#### [91] Third-person "Fenster" is on 657 of 712 live pages — 2,305 occurrences of a rule both style documents call absolute

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** STYLE.md:87 ("Write directly as Fenster using `we`, `our` and `you`. Do not describe Fenster in the third person") and TONEOFVOICE.md:122 ("Never 'the company', 'your local specialist' or Fenster in the third person") are unambiguous. Excluding verbatim customer reviews, the consent line and Legend's chat chrome, Fenster acts as a third-party subject 2,305 times on 657 pages. The worst instances flip voice mid-paragraph: on /casement-windows-bletchley/ the lead reads "Fenster helps match the product, survey and installation detail to the property rather than treating every opening the same. We help you compare side-hung or top-hung openings…" — third person and first person in consecutive sentences. COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-2026-08-12.md §4 flagged 15 instances on the 11 commercial routes and stated this "is the fault COPY-AUDIT.md §2 catalogued for the residential template and fixed there". That premise is false: the residential matrix alone carries "Fenster helps match the product…" on 252 routes.
- **Recommendation:** Sweep the two sources that are genuinely unruled, largest first: (1) the town-matrix profile strings in template-parts/sections/location-service.php ('Fenster helps match...' 252 routes, 'Fenster narrows the choice...' 525 routes, 'Fenster helps compare...', 'Fenster can also discuss...') — this is the bulk of the 2,053; (2) the product_content intros in inc/site-data.php ('Fenster specifies Liniar/Sheerline...' → 'We specify...'), 9 routes. Add (3) src/js/main.js:2672, 'Your project details are safely with the Fenster team' — the same phrasing already removed from the PHP notice at enquiry-form.php:57 for this exact reason. DO NOT sweep template-parts/sections/trust-page.php or 'the Fenster quote tool': PROGRESS.md:4200 records both as brand-named copy deliberately kept in the 2026-07-16 sweep ('/why-trust-fenster/... and "the Fenster quote tool"'), and generated-page.php:266 confirms trust-page.php is that route and no other. Separately, correct COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-2026-08-12.md:141-143 on both counts: residential was never fixed, and COPY-AUDIT.md §2 is about copy that talks about the website, not about Fenster in the third person.
- **Why:** The voice is the product on this site. A page that refers to the business as a third party reads as written *about* Fenster by an agency, which is precisely what TONEOFVOICE.md says destroys the trust the About page builds. It also undercuts every "we fit it ourselves" claim elsewhere.
- **Affected:** 657 of 712 live pages, 2,305 occurrences. Concentrated in template-parts/sections/location-service.php (lines 694–1372), inc/site-data.php product_content, template-parts/sections/trust-page.php.
- **Evidence:** Counted over all 712 live pages with review/consent/chat strings excluded: 2,305 hits, 657 pages. Top string "Fenster helps match the product, survey and installation detail…" ×252. Live on /casement-windows-bletchley/: "Fenster helps match the product… We help you compare side-hung or top-hung openings…" in one paragraph.
- **Verification:** The fault, the scale and two of the four sweep targets are real. The other two sweep targets are recorded as deliberate exceptions, which the recommendation would undo.

SCALE — CONFIRMED, and if anything conservative. I counted independently over all 712 pages, restricted to <main>, with the .fg-review-showcase block excised and the form's 'I agree that Fenster can use these details...' consent line stripped, using a deliberately narrow subject-verb regex: 2,053 occurrences on 651 pages. The finding's 2,305 on 657 is the same measurement with a wider verb list. The two named string counts are exact to the unit: 'Fenster helps match the product, survey and installation detail' appears on 252 pages, 'Use the Fenster quote tool' on 17. The voice-flip on /casement-windows-bletchley/ is verbatim: I pulled 'Fenster helps match the product, survey and installation detail to the property rather than treating every opening the same. We help you compare side-hung or top-hung openings' out of the live HTML in one paragraph. Both rules are at the cited lines (STYLE.md:86, one off from the cited :87; TONEOFVOICE.md:122).

COMMERCIAL-AUDIT CRITIQUE — CONFIRMED, and it is worse than stated. COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-2026-08-12.md:141-143 does say 'This is the fault COPY-AUDIT.md §2 catalogued for the residential template and fixed there.' That is false twice over: residential is not fixed (2,053 hits on 651 pages), and COPY-AUDIT.md §2 is not about this fault at all — its heading is 'Template copy that talks about the website, not to the customer' and :63 concerns the reader being referred to in the third person, not Fenster.

CORRECTION — two sweep targets are already ruled. PROGRESS.md:4200 (2026-07-16, 'Week Two: Shared Copy Rewrite') records the third-person sweep that was done and names what was deliberately kept: 'Brand-named copy was deliberately kept where it earns its place: /why-trust-fenster/, About-page process labels, the accreditation trust strip, commercial county intros and "the Fenster quote tool".' Recommendation item (3) targets trust-page.php, and generated-page.php:266 shows that template renders for exactly one slug, 'why-trust-fenster' — the named exception. Item (4) targets 'Use the Fenster quote tool...' verbatim — the other named exception. Sweeping either reverses a recorded decision.

Also worth noting: ACTION-PLAN.md:62 already catalogues this sweep as an open action, naming generated-page.php, site-data.php product_content and the quote/location templates. That is a to-do, not a ruling, so it does not clear the finding — but it means the fault is known and unactioned rather than undiscovered.

One target the finding missed: src/js/main.js:2672 still ships 'Your project details are safely with the Fenster team' as the enquiry success copy, which is the exact phrasing the comment at enquiry-form.php:54-56 records as having been removed from the PHP path for this reason.

#### [174] /patio-doors/ and /aluminium-doors/ show three wrong products under "Real installs, photographed on the day."

- **Severity:** HIGH · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `fenster_case_studies_for_product()` returns EVERY study when nothing claims a route. `generated-page.php:5294` gates only `['aluminium-windows','tilt-turn-windows']`. Both `/patio-doors/` and `/aluminium-doors/` therefore render the identical fallback trio: "Secondary glazing, Winslow", "uPVC casement windows, Leighton Buzzard", "Aluminium bifold doors, Whitehouse" — not one of which is the product on the page, and one of which is not even a door. On `/aluminium-doors/` this strip is 1,766px of a 19,739px mobile page and is the only "our work" block on a route that otherwise carries a single owner-confirmed photograph.
- **Recommendation:** Add `patio-doors` and `aluminium-doors` to `$no_case_study_routes` in `template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:5294`, exactly as tilt-turn was handled on 2026-08-12. Better still, delete the `if ($matched === []) { $matched = $studies; }` fallback at `inc/case-studies-data.php:1701-1703` so the helper behaves like `fenster_case_studies_for_product_group()` and no future route can inherit this; then remove the per-route gate list entirely.
- **Why:** AI.md's own ruling: "A route whose fallback shows the wrong product is worse than a route with no strip." A visitor deciding on a £6k sliding door is shown secondary glazing and casement windows under a heading promising real installs of this product — it reads as either a mistake or a business that has never fitted one.
- **Affected:** 2 routes live (/patio-doors/, /aluminium-doors/). The helper is also called by casement, roof lanterns, heritage doors and three hubs, so the fallback is a standing trap on every future product route.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:5294 `$no_case_study_routes = ['aluminium-windows','tilt-turn-windows']`; inc/case-studies-data.php:1701 `if ($matched === []) { $matched = $studies; }`; live HTML /patio-doors/ and /aluminium-doors/ both render h3s "Secondary glazing, Winslow" / "uPVC casement windows, Leighton Buzzard" / "Aluminium bifold doors, Whitehouse"; measured live at 375px, fg-cs-strip = 1,766px on /aluminium-doors/.
- **Verification:** Mechanism, size and scope all verified, and the Creative/INVESTIGATE typing is the honest call rather than a hedge. src/js/main.js:2810 is `if (!window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {` and :2811-2822 is the Lenis constructor with exactly the options quoted (anchors offset -88, autoRaf true, lerp 0.075, smoothWheel true, syncTouch false, wheelMultiplier 0.95, prevent on iframe/[data-no-smooth-scroll]/[data-lenis-prevent]); :2825 sets data-lenis-ready. No route condition of any kind. The permanent-rAF claim is not an assumption — I read it in the shipped bundle: `raf=e=>{...this.animate.advance(t*.001),this.options.autoRaf&&(this._rafId=requestAnimationFrame(this.raf))}` re-schedules unconditionally for the life of the page. Version string `var eo="1.3.25"` is at the head of live/main.js as claimed. Size: node_modules/lenis/dist/lenis.min.js is 17,722 B, brotli -q 11 = 4,547 B (finding said 17,624 / 4,545 — within 100 B), which is 11.5% of the 39,739 B brotli the server actually sends. WHAT THE FINDING SHOULD HAVE CARRIED, and why I would not act on the conditional-instantiation option lightly: `window.fensterLenis` is read in 8 places across src/js/main.js (:1399, :2665, :4634, :4647, :5520, :5530, :7945, :7959), and the docs record several mechanisms built on top of it — PROGRESS.md:3167 ('window.scrollTo does not move this page, because Lenis owns the scroll'), PROGRESS.md:3137 and :4070 (colour deep links depend on a Lenis pause-and-reassert), HANDOVER.md:1082 (blinds reveal locks Lenis at scrollY 0, which is src/js/main.js:2827-2829), and the Legend chat panel carries data-lenis-prevent on every page. Making instantiation conditional would mean auditing all eight call sites for a null Lenis and would leave scroll feel different between pages, which is itself a consistency defect. There is no owner ruling that fixes this either way — PROGRESS.md:4583 only says do not run a second smooth-scroll plugin alongside the theme's — so INVESTIGATE is right and this is not ALREADY_RULED.

#### [180] Four key-specification strips still carry an adjective where the site's own rule says a figure belongs

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 100% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `inc/site-data.php` records the same correction four times — "Style: Traditional" (flush casement), "Design: Fully customisable" (uPVC doors), "Opening style: Highly versatile" (tilt and turn) and "Sightlines: Ultra slim" (heritage windows) were each removed because they were "an adjective in a strip whose whole job is figures". Four routes still carry one: `aluminium-bifold-doors` prints `Sightlines: Ultra slim` at line 302 — the exact string the comment 44 lines below it says was wrong — plus `aluminium-doors` "Performance: Thermally efficient" (313), `integral-blinds` "Maintenance: Maintenance-free" (399) and `patio-doors` "Design: Space-saving" (448).
- **Recommendation:** Bifold takes Sheerline's published sightline the way heritage did (60.5mm there; the Prestige figure needs the same owner confirmation the flush route got, because 46mm is the fixed-pane number and 88mm the casement one — do not reach for the slim end). Aluminium doors takes a measurement it already owns: the Thermlock banner immediately above prints 1.4 double / 1.0 triple, so use a different one — the maximum leaf size, or the cylinder rating. Integral blinds takes the maximum blind size, which `fg-product-intel` already references. Patio takes the maximum pane width, which the survey copy already says is the governing dimension.
- **Why:** The strip is the first credibility element after the hero and the odometer animation exists to make the numbers count up. An adjective in one of four tiles breaks the pattern and reads as a slot nobody could fill.
- **Affected:** 4 of 15 product strips, plus every town matrix route reading the same arrays.
- **Evidence:** inc/site-data.php:302 (`Sightlines / Ultra slim`), :313, :399, :448; the rule is recorded in the comments at :344-354, :432-438, :457-465 and :417-421.
- **Verification:** Reproduced end to end and it is exactly as described. Live curl of https://fensterglazing.com/what-are-double-glazed-glass-windows/ on 2026-08-13 returns `<title>What Are Double Glazed Glass Windows? | Fester Glazing</title>`, plus og:title and twitter:title carrying the identical misspelling — 3 occurrences of 'Fester' on the page, and grep -rl across the complete 712-file crawl in scratchpad/all/ returns that one file and no other. I located the source: data/pages.json line 74471 `"title_tag": "What Are Double Glazed Glass Windows? | Fester Glazing"` and line 74511 `"content": "...| Fester Glazing"`, and confirmed data/pages.json is the only file in the entire theme containing the string. The override mechanism the recommendation names exists and is wired: fenster_gsc_seo_overrides() is declared at inc/generated-pages.php:252 and consumed at :580 and :623. The traffic figures check out against SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md:106 verbatim — 49,890 impressions, 25 clicks, 0.05% CTR, described there as 'the worst asset on the site by ratio', flagged by ACTION-PLAN.md and SEO-AUDIT.md and unimproved. Nothing in AI.md, STYLE.md, TONEOFVOICE.md, PROGRESS.md or HANDOVER.md rules on it — this is a straight typo, not an owner decision. ONE ADDITION worth carrying into the fix: there is a THIRD 'Fester' in data/pages.json at line 35009, in body copy — '...by choosing Fester Glazing you are choosing a reputable and trusted installer' — sitting after the double-glazing-buckingham slug block. It does not currently render (live /double-glazing-buckingham/ and /fensa-approved-installers/ both return 0 hits, and the 712-page crawl confirms it appears nowhere), but it is a live landmine if that content is ever surfaced. The finding already says to grep pages.json for the misspelling before shipping, which would catch it.

#### [114] /guide-noise-insulation-for-windows/ is unedited US-sourced content — the only page on the site quoting prices in dollars — and it sells DIY instead of us

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 98% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** This is an unedited American article. It prices the whole subject in US dollars — ten figures including "$300 to $1,000 per window" for double-pane, "$400 to $1,200" for laminated glass and "acoustic window seals can cost between $50 and $150 per window" — and it is the ONLY page in the 712-URL sitemap containing a dollar sign. It uses "double-pane" twice on a site that sells double glazing, and six American spellings (specialized ×3, neighborhoods, neighbor's, colors) which are 6 of the 7 Americanisms on the entire site. Its blog title is "Ultimate Guide to Noise Insulation for Windows: Valuable Tips & Tricks" and its teaser opens "Are outside noises disrupting your peace at home? Discover expert…" — "discover" is on the never-use list at TONEOFVOICE.md:159. Substantively it argues the reader out of the sale: an H2 reading "DIY Solutions when considering Noise Insulation for Windows" leads into "For those on a tighter budget, DIY solutions like weatherstripping and acoustic curtains offer a more affordable alternative" and "using heavy curtains or drapes can also help to dampen sound". "Solution(s)" appears 15 times. The page carries no noindex and is in page-sitemap.xml, and it sits beside /soundproof-windows/, which AI.md:43 names among the eight high-impression pages to prioritise, and /secondary-glazing/, the product it should be feeding.
- **Recommendation:** The dollar figures must go regardless of what else happens to the page — they are a straight factual error for a UK installer and no reader forgives them. Either rewrite to British English and British pricing and route the reader to secondary glazing and acoustic glass (both real products with real specs on this site), or noindex it and consolidate into /soundproof-windows/. If it stays: delete the DIY-alternatives section (the only place on the site recommending curtains over the product we sell), fix specialized ×3 / neighborhoods / neighbor's / colors, replace "double-pane" with "double glazed", and drop "Ultimate Guide" and "Discover" from the title and teaser in data/pages.json:10859 and :10927. Also fix "labor" on /what-is-a-door-lintel/ while you are in there — it is the only other Americanism on the site.
- **Why:** It is an unedited US-sourced article sitting next to a priority SEO page, and its main practical advice is not to buy anything from us. /other-services/ already shows how this should read: "Will secondary glazing help with traffic noise? It is the better answer than new windows where the existing frontage has to stay, because the gap between the two panes is doing the work."
- **Affected:** /guide-noise-insulation-for-windows/, plus its title on /blog/. Content in data/pages.json.
- **Evidence:** Live copy as quoted; American spellings confirmed by full-site sweep (this page contributes 6 of the ~14 instances found across 712 pages). Blog listing title: "Ultimate Guide to Noise Insulation for Windows: Valuable Tips & Tricks". "solutions" ×4 on the page.
- **Verification:** Every claim checks out and the finding UNDERSTATES the problem by missing its single most damaging element: the page quotes ten prices in US DOLLARS, and it is the only page on the entire 712-page site that does so. "$300 to $1,000 per window", "$400 to $1,200", "$50 and $150 per window", "$10 to $20", "$50 to $200". It also uses "double-pane" ×2 (US term for double-glazed) — on a site whose product name is double glazing. Spelling count is slightly off in the finding's favour: specialized appears ×3 not ×2. My site-wide Americanism sweep over all 712 pages found 7 instances total, 6 on this page and 1 ("labor") on /what-is-a-door-lintel/ — so this page really does contribute 6, though the site total is 7 not ~14. Everything else verified: no robots noindex meta, present in page-sitemap.xml, blog listing title "Ultimate Guide to Noise Insulation for Windows: Valuable Tips & Tricks" and teaser "Are outside noises disrupting your peace at home? Discover expert…" both at data/pages.json:10859 and :10927; "discover" is on the never-use list at TONEOFVOICE.md:159. H2 "DIY Solutions when considering Noise Insulation for Windows" and both DIY-alternative sentences confirmed verbatim. /soundproof-windows/ is confirmed as a priority page at AI.md:43. No owner ruling exempts imported blog posts from the tone rules — AI.md:282 only says they render through generated-article.php. Raising impact to Medium: dollar pricing on a Milton Keynes installer's indexed page is a hard credibility break, not a style nit.

#### [127] Scrape-era advert titles "Exceptional Roofline Services" and "Need Cat and Dog Flaps?" leak from pages.json into ~56 related-link bands, and one of them is the /roofline/ H1

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** $route_title (generated-page.php:1966-1990) derives a label from fenster_location_matrix_products() only for matrix routes; every other slug falls through to $generated_pages[$slug]['title'], which for /roofline/ and /cat-and-dog-flaps/ is still the scraped advert headline (data/pages.json:63099 and :20952). Both strings render as the fg-link-card__label AND the img alt. Scope is not four routes: $other_service_routes (generated-page.php:1891-1898) groups all seven other-services routes, and the band is inherited by the town matrix — verified live on /roofline/, /cat-and-dog-flaps/, /integral-blinds-bletchley/ and /roof-lanterns-luton/ as well as /integral-blinds/, /secondary-glazing/, /window-and-door-repairs/ and /double-glazing-replacement/. With 25 roof-lanterns and 25 integral-blinds town routes that is roughly 56 pages. Worse, because pages.json title is also registry item 3 (the H1 on the main product route), `curl /roofline/` returns `<h1>Exceptional Roofline Services` — the old advert headline is that page's heading. /cat-and-dog-flaps/ had its H1 fixed on rebuild (PROGRESS.md:4502) but its link label was left behind, which is the registry-sprawl failure AI.md documents.
- **Recommendation:** Set clean `title` values on the two pages.json records ("Roofline", "Cat and Dog Flaps"), which fixes the /roofline/ H1 and all ~56 tile labels and alts in one edit; if the H1 must stay for SEO reasons, add a non-matrix label override map next to $route_title instead. Sweep the sibling family in the same pass: COPY-AUDIT.md:122 records "Market Leading Double Glazing in X" still rendering as link text on ~20 town routes, and the band also carries title-case drift ("Doors In Milton Keynes", "Double Glazed Windows Milton Keynes").
- **Why:** Every share of a Fenster page — WhatsApp to a partner, a Facebook post, a LinkedIn commercial enquiry — currently either shows a slow-loading generic showroom shot or no image at all. It is also 2.37 MB of avoidable fetch for any crawler that renders social previews.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages
- **Evidence:** curl of the og:image URL: HTTP 200, 2,372,438 bytes, image/png, `PNG image data, 1536 x 1024`. Identical `og:image` value on all 38 Tier-1 heads and confirmed in the emitter at inc/generated-pages.php:2175, 2224, 2231.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and the mechanism is exactly as described, but the scope is understated by an order of magnitude and it misses the worse half of the same fault. CONFIRMED: data/pages.json:63099 is `"title": "Exceptional Roofline Services"` and :20952 is `"title": "Need Cat and Dog Flaps?"`; $route_title at generated-page.php:1966-1990 derives matrix labels from fenster_location_matrix_products() but falls through to $generated_pages[$slug]['title'] for every non-matrix route, so both scrape titles reach the tile label AND the img alt. WRONG ON SCOPE: not four routes. $other_service_routes (generated-page.php:1891-1898) puts all seven other-services routes in one family, and the town matrix inherits the band. I curl-verified the bad labels on /roofline/, /cat-and-dog-flaps/, /integral-blinds-bletchley/ and /roof-lanterns-luton/ as well as the four named. urls.txt holds 26 roof-lanterns and 26 integral-blinds URLs, so the real figure is about 56 routes. MISSED THE BIGGER HALF: `curl https://fensterglazing.com/roofline/` returns `<h1>Exceptional Roofline Services` — the advert headline is that page's own H1, not merely a tile label. /cat-and-dog-flaps/ was already fixed at the H1 (PROGRESS.md:4502 records the rebuild) but its related-link label was not, which is exactly the registry-sprawl trap AI.md:571 documents. NOT ALREADY_RULED: COPY-AUDIT.md:122 and its 2026-07-07 re-scan list this as outstanding low-priority work, not an owner decision, alongside the sibling family "Market Leading Double Glazing in X" (×20 town routes) which is still live and should be swept in the same change.

#### [106] Six legacy guide pages position our own products as the cheap or compromised choice

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** Beyond the sash and patio findings, the guide family repeatedly frames products we sell as the budget option, which the owner instruction of 2026-07-24 covers explicitly ("This covers the softer forms too: 'at a lower cost than', 'warmer for the money', 'costs less'"). The worst is /what-is-the-difference-between-upvc-vs-composite-doors/: "Budget: uPVC doors are generally more affordable than composite doors, making them a popular choice for homeowners on a tighter budget. **However, if security and energy efficiency are top priorities, investing in a composite door may be worth considering.**" That tells a reader our uPVC doors are the choice you make when you cannot afford security — about a product with a three-star cylinder and laminated glass upgrade on its own page. Also: /benefits-of-upvc-windows-for-your-home/ heads a section "Lower Cost With UPVC" and says uPVC is "the more affordable alternative to both wooden and aluminium frames"; /different-types-of-window-frame-materials/ says "Wood is considerably more expensive than cheaper PVC windows" and "Typically, one of the cheapest options available"; /soundproof-windows/ — an AI.md-listed priority page — says "secondary glazing is a cheaper, effective alternative"; /consider-composite-doors-for-your-home/ says "If you are on a budget, you need to be aware that a composite door is generally higher in price"; /difference-between-french-doors-and-sliding-patio-doors/ publishes an unsourced discount claim, "Sliding doors are typically 10 to 20 percent cheaper when you select a size that is over 1800 mm", which also conflicts with the rule that prices belong on the price guides with a real figure.
- **Recommendation:** Rewrite each comparison so both products get what they are genuinely best at, in parallel phrasing, and let the specification separate them. Delete the 10-to-20-percent claim outright — it is an unsourced price statement outside the price guides. On the uPVC vs composite page, replace the "Budget" block with what each door actually does: the composite's 44.5mm insulated slab and £5,000 break-in guarantee, against the uPVC door's three-star cylinder, laminated glass option and multi-chamber frame.
- **Why:** These are informational pages that rank and that a researching buyer reads before they reach a product page. Each one hands them a reason not to buy something we sell, and one of them sits on a page AI.md names as an SEO priority.
- **Affected:** 6 guide routes: /what-is-the-difference-between-upvc-vs-composite-doors/, /benefits-of-upvc-windows-for-your-home/, /different-types-of-window-frame-materials/, /soundproof-windows/, /consider-composite-doors-for-your-home/, /difference-between-french-doors-and-sliding-patio-doors/.
- **Evidence:** All quotations taken from the 712 fetched live pages. Rule: TONEOFVOICE.md never-use list, owner instruction 2026-07-24, and "Prices belong on the price guides and the quote tool, where they come with a real figure."
- **Verification:** Every one of the six quotations reproduces verbatim in the fetched live text, and the rule they are measured against is real and quoted accurately. TONEOFVOICE.md:164 reads: 'budget, cheap, or any wording that positions one of our own products as the low-cost option. Owner instruction, 2026-07-24 ... This covers the softer forms too: "at a lower cost than", "warmer for the money", "costs less" ... Prices belong on the price guides and the quote tool, where they come with a real figure.' The finding's paraphrase of that rule is exact. AI.md:43 independently confirms /soundproof-windows/ is a named SEO priority page ('prioritise CTR and internal-link fixes for pages that already have impressions: ... /soundproof-windows/'), so that claim is not inflated. AI.md:511 reinforces rather than excuses the uPVC-vs-composite case ('DO NOT WRITE THAT IT IS CHEAPER'), which makes that page the clearest violation. I searched AI.md, TONEOFVOICE.md, STYLE.md, PROGRESS.md, HANDOVER.md and COPY-AUDIT.md for any exemption covering imported/legacy guide pages and found none: the only 'deliberately not rewritten' carve-out (TONEOFVOICE.md:43) is scoped to guarantee-exclusion copy on /about/ and the hub FAQs, not to price framing. I also checked the recommendation's product facts so it is safe to act on: 44.5mm, the £5,000 figure and laminated glass are all present on /composite-doors/, and 'A three star cylinder is the first upgrade worth asking for' is present on /upvc-doors/. One small correction to the recommendation only: the uPVC frame is a six-chamber Liniar EnergyPlus profile, and the page's strongest security evidence is PAS 24, Secured by Design and a BSI Kitemark to BS EN 12608-1 rather than the phrase 'multi-chamber'. Raising confidence from 88 to 96 since all six quotes and the governing rule reproduced exactly.

#### [95] "Jobs we have finished in <Town>" runs over case studies from a different town on 210 routes, and contradicts its own eyebrow

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The case-study strip prints the H2 "Jobs we have finished in Furzton" over cards labelled "Residential - Whitehouse, Milton Keynes" and "Residential - Broughton, Milton Keynes". The eyebrow directly above reads "Recent work nearby" and the body below reads "...what we have already done close to you", so the page hedges correctly twice and over-claims in the heading between them. The mechanism is deliberate and documented (CASESTUDIES.md:34-39: any study whose location field carries "Milton Keynes" is area proof for all twelve MK suburbs) but the wording was never updated to match. Measured over all 712 live pages: the heading renders on 315 routes; on 210 of them (10 MK suburbs x 21 products - Bletchley, Stony Stratford, Newport Pagnell, Woburn Sands, Great Linford, Shenley Church End, Furzton, Oldbrook, Monkston, Brooklands) not one card is in the named town; on 21 more (Whitehouse) one of the two cards is from Broughton; only 84 routes (Luton, Northampton, Leighton Buzzard, Wolverton) show an exact in-town match. The project already holds itself to this standard in the same file: PROGRESS.md:846 calls the earlier Bedford/Leighton Buzzard version of this exact heading "a false claim of local work, not a loose match", and fixed it by removing the strip rather than by softening the heading.
- **Recommendation:** Do not change the sprintf globally - it renders on 315 routes and on 84 of them the "in" is true and is the stronger claim. Make it conditional on how the cards were matched: fenster_case_studies_for_town() already builds $exact and $area as separate arrays (inc/case-studies-data.php:1625-1650), so return which bucket supplied them and have location-service.php:1704 print "Jobs we have finished in %s" for exact matches and "Jobs we have finished near %s" (or "Recent jobs near %s, photographed the day we finished.", reusing the About page line) for area matches. Keep the MK-suburb sharing logic as is; it is ruled and sound.
- **Why:** It is a checkable falsehood on a page whose whole job is local trust, sitting three lines above photographic proof that disproves it. A Furzton homeowner who reads the card labels will conclude the heading is marketing rather than fact — the precise suspicion the About page is written to defuse.
- **Affected:** 189 routes (9 MK suburbs × 21 products: Bletchley, Stony Stratford, Newport Pagnell, Great Linford, Shenley Church End, Furzton, Oldbrook, Monkston, Brooklands). The heading string itself renders on 315 routes.
- **Evidence:** Live curl of https://fensterglazing.com/double-glazing-furzton/ : eyebrow "Recent work nearby", H2 "Jobs we have finished in Furzton", cards "Residential • Whitehouse, Milton Keynes" and "Residential • Broughton, Milton Keynes". Suburb list at inc/case-studies-data.php:1568-1580; heading at location-service.php:1704; 189 matching sitemap URLs.
- **Verification:** The mechanism and the wording clash are real and reproduce exactly. location-service.php:1704 is the sprintf 'Jobs we have finished in %s' sitting between the eyebrow "Recent work nearby" (:1703) and the body "...what we have already done close to you" (:1705). inc/case-studies-data.php:1565-1580 is fenster_milton_keynes_town_slugs() with twelve suburbs, and :1645 treats any study whose location contains "milton keynes" as area proof for all of them. Live /double-glazing-furzton/ renders exactly as described: eyebrow "Recent work nearby", H2 "Jobs we have finished in Furzton", cards "Residential - Whitehouse, Milton Keynes" and "Residential - Broughton, Milton Keynes". The heading renders on exactly 315 routes, as claimed. But the scope is wrong. I parsed the fg-location-cases section on all 315 routes and compared the heading town against the card location labels: 210 routes across 10 towns have ZERO matching cards, not 189 across 9 - the finding omits Woburn Sands (21 routes, showing the same Whitehouse and Broughton cards). A further 21 Whitehouse routes are partially wrong (one card is Whitehouse, one is Broughton). Only 84 routes (Luton, Northampton, Leighton Buzzard, Wolverton, 21 each) have a genuine in-town match. That last number breaks the recommendation: changing the single sprintf at :1704 to "near %s" would downgrade a true and stronger claim on 84 routes. The fix has to be conditional, and the helper already has the information - fenster_case_studies_for_town() builds $exact and $area separately, so it can return which bucket supplied the cards.

#### [122] Five key-specification strips still carry an adjective where the file's own comments say a figure belongs

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `inc/site-data.php` records the same correction four times — "Style: Traditional" (flush casement, comment at :432-438), "Design: Fully customisable" (uPVC doors, :417-421), "Opening style: Highly versatile" (tilt and turn, :457-465) and "Sightlines: Ultra slim" (heritage windows, :344-354) were each removed because they were "an adjective in a strip whose whole job is figures". Five entries still carry one. `aluminium-bifold-doors` prints `Sightlines: Ultra slim` at :302 — the exact string the comment 44 lines below it says was wrong — plus `aluminium-doors` "Performance: Thermally efficient" (:313), `slide-fold-doors` "Design: Versatile" (:378, missed in the first pass and a live route with its own town matrix), `integral-blinds` "Maintenance: Maintenance-free" (:399) and `patio-doors` "Design: Space-saving" (:448). All five render live. Note the array holds 23 product entries, not 15, and several of the others deliberately carry non-numeric but non-adjectival tiles ("System: Sheerline Prestige", "Frame type: Slim aluminium") — so the rule to apply is the one the comments actually state, which is against adjectives, not against every non-number.
- **Recommendation:** Bifold takes Sheerline's published sightline the way heritage did (60.5mm there; the Prestige figure needs the same owner confirmation the flush route got, because 46mm is the fixed-pane number and 88mm the casement one — do not reach for the slim end). Aluminium doors takes a measurement it does not already spend: the Thermlock banner immediately above already prints 1.4 double / 1.0 triple (verified in the live HTML), so use the maximum leaf size or the cylinder rating instead. Slide-fold doors replaces "Design: Versatile" with the panel count or the maximum leaf width, which is the thing that actually distinguishes it. Integral blinds takes the maximum blind size, which `fg-product-intel` already references. Patio takes the maximum pane width, which the survey copy already says is the governing dimension.
- **Why:** F4 recorded 15 impressions and 1 click across all seven in a full window, and asked whether the cause was indexation, authority or cannibalisation. It is authority: 2–3 internal links each, none from the page that owns the product, none from the 525-page matrix. That is a measured answer to an open question, and the fix is six link entries.

- **Evidence:** Exact-href inbound sources across 712 pages: composite-door-prices ← [window-door-prices-milton-keynes, composite-doors, doors-milton-keynes]; sash-window-prices ← [windows-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes]; aluminium-window-prices ← [windows-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes]; bifold-door-cost ← [window-door-prices-milton-keynes, doors-milton-keynes]; patio-french-door-prices ← [window-door-prices-milton-keynes, doors-milton-keynes]; double-glazing-cost ← [windows-milton-keynes, window-door-prices-milton-keynes, other-services].
- **Verification:** Every line citation is exact and every string is live. The scope is understated and the denominator is wrong.

LINE-BY-LINE CONFIRMED with sed: inc/site-data.php:302 `['label' => 'Sightlines', 'value' => 'Ultra slim']`, :313 `['label' => 'Performance', 'value' => 'Thermally efficient']`, :399 `['label' => 'Maintenance', 'value' => 'Maintenance-free']`, :448 `['label' => 'Design', 'value' => 'Space-saving']`. All four render live — grep of the fetched HTML returns "Ultra slim" on aluminium-bifold-doors.html, "Thermally efficient" on aluminium-doors.html, "Maintenance-free" on integral-blinds.html, "Space-saving" on patio-doors.html.

RULE CITATIONS CONFIRMED: the comment at :344-354 contains "'Sightlines: Ultra slim' was an adjective in a strip whose whole job is figures" at :346 — 44 lines below the surviving instance at :302, exactly as claimed. :417-421 carries the "Design: Fully customisable" ruling, :432-438 the "Style: Traditional" one, :457-465 the "Opening style: Highly versatile" one. All four correct.

SCOPE WRONG: a fifth instance exists that the finding missed — `slide-fold-doors` at inc/site-data.php:378 prints `['label' => 'Design', 'value' => 'Versatile']`, the same fault, and /slide-fold-doors/ is a live route in urls.txt with its own town matrix. Also "4 of 15 product strips" is the wrong denominator: `product_usps` holds 23 keys, not 15. And the "whole job is figures" premise is looser than stated — several strips the docs left alone also carry non-numeric tiles (`aluminium-flush-windows` System: Sheerline Prestige, `roof-lanterns` Glazing option: Solar-control glass, `secondary-glazing` Frame type: Slim aluminium, `window-and-door-repairs` Quoting: Normally free). The rule as written in the comments is against ADJECTIVES specifically, not against non-numbers, and the five cited tiles are all adjectives, so the finding survives — but the argument should be made on that narrower ground.

RECOMMENDATION PREMISE CHECKED AND SOUND: /aluminium-doors/ does print "1.4 W/m²K double glazed and 1.0 triple" in the Thermlock banner, so that figure is indeed already spent.

Not an owner ruling: price-guide.php:5-8 records the 2026-07-20 instruction that placeholder rows must never render (which is why the rows vanish) but nothing sanctions leaving the FAQ asserting prices that are not there, and HANDOVER.md:339 confirms the pages are meant to carry checked figures. One correction to the problem text, which does not change the verdict or the affected list: it names only the aluminium and patio/French records as unconfirmed — the sash guide's three examples at generated-pages.php:740-742 are equally 'To confirm from WindowCAD', which is why sash also renders zero prices. A second instance of the same false claim sits outside the FAQ, at price-guide.php:193: 'It is the same software behind every checked example on this page' — also rendered on the three pages with no examples, and any suppression fix should cover it.

#### [104] /what-is-a-door-lintel/ is AI filler that states the same paragraph four times and still carries the truncation logged in July

COPY-AUDIT.md's 2026-07-07 re-scan lists it under "Still outstanding after the cleanup", item 2, so it has been carrying this for five weeks as stated. #### [102] Three commercial city pages are keyword-stuffed listicles while Leeds is rewritten to standard — and Manchester's H1 miscounts its own contents

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Four city routes, two different standards. /commercial-glazing-leeds/ has been rewritten: first person, named proof ("In Leeds we fitted the aluminium windows at Headrow Court, a conversion of four former office buildings into 108 student studios, completed in October 2025"), sentence-case H3s ("Surveyed before anything is priced", "Repair or replace, answered honestly"), H1 "Commercial glazing in Leeds" with no stop. Three have not been. /commercial-glazing-manchester/ has H1 "Commercial Glazing Manchester: 5 Powerful Refurbishment Strategies for Lower Energy Costs" — a listicle headline with an unearned superlative, against STYLE.md:256 ("The H1 on a product or service page is the name of the thing"). The phrase "glazing Manchester" is forced into sentences 23 times as a noun ("most commercial glazing Manchester refurbishments", "Aluminium Glazing Manchester systems are widely specified", "Cost control in commercial glazing Manchester projects"), which STYLE.md:267 bans by name. The H1 promises five strategies and the page renders four: the card numbers read 01-04 while the headings inside read "2.", "3.", "4.", "5." — strategy 1 is missing. Its opening paragraph fear-frames ("leaving them vulnerable to heat loss, air leakage and rising energy costs", TONEOFVOICE.md:45, owner correction 2026-08-12) and is then repeated verbatim as the body of the "Why choose Fenster for commercial glazing?" section. /commercial-glazing-sheffield/ is the same pattern: H1 "Commercial Glazing Contractors in Sheffield for Multi-Site Property Portfolios", 12 forced "glazing Sheffield" phrases, Title Case H3s. /commercial-glazing-birmingham/ has Title Case H3s and no named proof, but only 2 keyword instances. SEPARATELY, the 47 county routes (Essex among them) are internally consistent — one template, sentence-case headings, no stuffing — and their only breach is the trailing full stop on "Commercial glazing across <County>.", which STYLE.md:258 forbids on an H1. That is a one-line template fix, not a rewrite.
- **Recommendation:** Rewrite Manchester, Birmingham and Sheffield against Leeds. Set the four city H1s to "Commercial glazing in <City>" with no full stop, and strip the trailing full stop from the 47-page county H1 template separately. Strip every forced "commercial glazing <City>" noun phrase back to natural English. On Manchester, delete the numbering or restore item 1, and remove the duplicated opening paragraph from the "Why choose Fenster" section. Each city page needs one named building the way Leeds has Headrow Court — Tottenham Court Road (Heal's) and Coventry (Barn Hotel) are already in the case-study data and unused on these pages. Leave the 47 county pages' body copy alone; they are consistent.
- **Why:** A specifier landing on Manchester reads a content-farm listicle; the same specifier landing on Leeds reads a contractor who has done the work. Both are live. The Manchester page also visibly miscounts its own contents, which is the first thing a technical reader notices.
- **Affected:** 4 live routes: /commercial-glazing-manchester/, /commercial-glazing-birmingham/, /commercial-glazing-essex/, /commercial-glazing-leeds/ (the reference).
- **Evidence:** Live H1s as quoted. "commercial glazing Manchester"/"aluminium glazing Manchester"/"glazing Manchester" counted 23× on /commercial-glazing-manchester/ against 2× on Birmingham. Card numbers render 01–04 while the headings inside read "2. Specifying…", "3. Managing…", "4. Coordinating…", "5. Ensuring…". Rules: STYLE.md H1 rule and SEO-terms rule; TONEOFVOICE.md §2 owner correction 2026-08-12.
- **Verification:** The Manchester evidence is exact but the family is misdescribed and one offending page is missed. Verified on Manchester: H1 is "Commercial Glazing Manchester: 5 Powerful Refurbishment Strategies for Lower Energy Costs"; case-insensitive count of "glazing manchester" in visible text is exactly 23 (Birmingham exactly 2); the card numbers render 01, 02, 03, 04 while the H3s inside read "2. Specifying Aluminium Glazing Manchester…", "3. Managing…", "4. Coordinating…", "5. Ensuring…" — item 1 is genuinely absent; the fear-framing sentence "leaving them vulnerable to heat loss, air leakage and rising energy costs" is present and is rendered TWICE verbatim (hero intro and the "Why choose Fenster" body), which the finding did not spot. Leeds carries Headrow Court as quoted with sentence-case H3s. STYLE.md:267 and :256-258 are quoted accurately. Two scope errors. (1) Essex is NOT an ad-hoc listicle. I pulled the H1 of all 51 /commercial-glazing-*/ routes: 47 of them, Essex included, share one consistent template — "Commercial glazing across <County>." with sentence-case H2s ("Project coverage across Essex and the eastern home counties.", "Survey-led scope checks") and no keyword stuffing. #### [105] A live guide page states uPVC insulates worse than aluminium, contradicting the U-values published on the product pages

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** /how-to-choose-the-right-style-windows-for-your-home/ states: "you need to know that they have values between 1.2 and 1.4 watts per square meter per degree Celsius (w/m2K). This means that UPVC window frames are **not as good at insulating against heat as aluminium** or wood, but they are still better than glass windows." That is false twice over: as physics (uPVC is a far better insulator than aluminium, which is why aluminium frames need a thermal break at all), and against the site's own published figures — /casement-windows/ gives 0.95 W/m²K for the Liniar EnergyPlus uPVC casement with a 36mm triple unit (A+), while /aluminium-windows/ gives 1.0 W/m²K triple glazed as its key specification (footnoted "Lowest achievable") and 1.4 W/m²K double glazed. Like for like on triple glazing, our uPVC is the warmer window and this page says the reverse. It also breaks the owner instruction at TONEOFVOICE.md:162, 2026-07-24, against "any wording that positions one of our own products as the weaker choice on specification", and does it about the product most of the site sells. Adjacent errors in the same paragraph: "UPVC window frames are created with a combination of plastic and metal"; "better than glass windows" is not a comparison that means anything; "square meter" is American; and "w/m2K" is the wrong unit casing against the "W/m²K" used everywhere else.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the paragraph with the site's own confirmed figures, phrased in parallel as TONEOFVOICE.md:162 requires (it supplies the model sentence itself): uPVC reaches the lower whole-window U-value (0.95 W/m²K with a 36mm triple unit, A+); aluminium reaches 1.0 W/m²K triple glazed and holds the slimmer sightline and larger spans. Compare triple with triple, not 0.95 against the aluminium double-glazed 1.4. Fix the unit to W/m²K, and drop "plastic and metal". Also standardise "UPVC" to "uPVC": 131 whole-word uppercase uses survive across 36 pages while the nav, H1s and product pages all use "uPVC".
- **Why:** A prospective buyer researching frame materials on our own site is told our best-selling frame is thermally inferior to our second product. It is false against our own published numbers and it argues the customer out of the sale.
- **Affected:** /how-to-choose-the-right-style-windows-for-your-home/ primarily. The "UPVC" casing issue affects 6 pages: /different-types-of-window-frame-materials/ (13), /how-to-clean-your-upvc-windows-at-home/ (11), /what-front-doors-provide-the-best-security-for-your-home/ (7), this page (6), /choosing-the-right-front-door-for-your-home/ (3), /how-to-know-when-to-replace-windows/ (2).
- **Evidence:** Live quote as given, fetched from https://fensterglazing.com/how-to-choose-the-right-style-windows-for-your-home/. Contradicted by /casement-windows/: "0.95 W/m²K, with the 36mm triple glazed unit, which makes it an A+ window" and /aluminium-windows/ key specification "1.4 W/m²K double glazed". Rule: TONEOFVOICE.md, owner instruction 2026-07-24. UPVC/uPVC counts measured on the fetched pages.
- **Verification:** The core claim is correct and the quote is exact, but two pieces of supporting evidence are wrong and the scope is undercounted. Verified live on /how-to-choose-the-right-style-windows-for-your-home/: "To understand how well UPVC window frames perform in this regard, you need to know that they have values between 1.2 and 1.4 watts per square meter per degree Celsius (w/m2K). This means that UPVC window frames are not as good at insulating against heat as aluminium or wood, but they are still better than glass windows." "UPVC window frames are created with a combination of plastic and metal" is there too. TONEOFVOICE.md:162 confirms the rule verbatim and even supplies the fix: "'uPVC reaches the lower U-value, aluminium holds the slimmest frame' is right". Correction 1: /aluminium-windows/ does NOT publish 1.4 W/m²K as its key specification. Its key-specification strip reads "U-value 1.0 W/m²K*" with the footnote "Lowest achievable"; 1.4 W/m²K appears further down as the double-glazed figure against "1.0 W/m²K triple glazed". So the honest like-for-like is 0.95 W/m²K uPVC triple against 1.0 W/m²K aluminium triple — uPVC is still the warmer of the two, so the finding's conclusion stands, but the 0.95-vs-1.4 framing compares a triple-glazed uPVC window with a double-glazed aluminium one and would not survive a challenge. Correction 2: the UPVC casing scope. The six pages named do total exactly 42 in-body uses, so that number is right, but a whole-corpus count over the 712 crawled pages gives 131 whole-word "UPVC" uses across 36 pages, and the two worst offenders are missing from the list entirely: /the-history-of-upvc-windows/ (29) and /benefits-of-upvc-windows-for-your-home/ (26). /soundproof-windows/ (5), /consider-composite-doors-for-your-home/ (3) and /window-maintenance/ (1) are also missed, plus one instance each on ~25 /upvc-doors-<town>/ matrix pages in a shared FAQ answer, which is a single template fix.

#### [119] The five panels of the /aluminium-windows/ scroll hero all pass the "a competitor could paste this" test — 5,067px of mobile scroll saying nothing specific

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.fg-aw-story` is a sticky-pinned 241-frame scroll-scrubbed sequence (src/js/main.js:4855-4960). On mobile it is `height: calc(var(--fg-aw-panel-count,6) * 104svh)` (src/scss/main.scss:23325; the 118svh at :3203 is the desktop value), measured live at 375×812 as 5,067px of a 21,058px page — 24%, or 6.2 screens. Scrolling is not hijacked and there is a full reduced-motion fallback at main.scss:3339-3385, so it is not a usability defect. The copy is the problem. The five panel headings are "More glass. Less frame.", "Comfort through every season.", "Strong where it matters.", "Your colour. Your configuration." and "Measured, fitted and guaranteed." Every one would survive unchanged on a competitor's site, which is the exact failure TONEOFVOICE.md §2b defines: "If a sentence would survive on a competitor's site unchanged, it is generic." The three real facts about this product (Thermlock multi-chamber core, the 72-80mm system, powder coating) are not in the hero at all, and the two sections that do describe the product — fg-product-why 1,853px and fg-product-intel 1,806px — are together smaller than the opener that precedes them.
- **Recommendation:** Rewrite the five panels against the TONEOFVOICE §2b self-check before touching the length. Each panel gets one checkable fact: the sightline in millimetres instead of "More glass. Less frame."; the Thermlock multi-chamber core and a U-value instead of "Comfort through every season."; the powder-coat spec and the finish count instead of "Your colour. Your configuration." If the owner then decides six screens is still too much for five facts, cut --fg-aw-panel-count to 4 (about 3,400px on mobile). Do not cut the panel count while the copy is still generic — that fixes the cheaper half of the problem and leaves the reader with the same nothing, faster.
- **Why:** Two identical indexable URLs on the site's highest-CTR organic asset is a self-inflicted split of the exact signal that page depends on, and the fix costs one array entry.
- **Affected:** /design-your-windows-and-doors/ (and by extension /3d-visualiser/)
- **Evidence:** Both fetched live 2026-08-13. Stripped `<main>` text: len 5277 both, `a == b` → True, difflib quick_ratio 1.0. Both `<link rel="canonical">` self-referencing. Both present in scratchpad/urls.txt. Template branch: template-parts/sections/quote-tool.php:20 `$is_visualiser = $slug === '3d-visualiser' || str_contains($slug, 'design');`
- **Verification:** Every number is exact — I reproduced all four in a real browser at 375×812: .fg-aw-story = 5067px, page = 21058px, .fg-product-why = 1853px, .fg-product-intel = 1806px, --fg-aw-panel-count = 6. The five panel headings are verbatim. But three things in the framing are wrong. (1) The CSS citation does not govern the measured figure: main.scss:3203 is 118svh and applies at desktop; the mobile block at main.scss:23324-23326 overrides it to 104svh, and 6 × 104% × 812 = the 5,067px measured. Cite 23325 for the mobile claim. (2) "Scroll-jacked" is inaccurate and it matters, because it implies a usability defect that is not present. main.js:4855-4960 is a sticky-pinned canvas scrubbing a 241-frame WebP sequence off scroll position — it never calls preventDefault, scrolling behaves normally, and a full reduced-motion fallback collapses the whole thing to auto height at main.scss:3339-3385. So it does not breach AI.md:898. (3) The type is wrong. The measurable part — 24% of the page, 6.2 screens — is not a defect against any rule the project holds; STYLE.md:345's "a sticky, cinematic or multi-column desktop section needs a simpler mobile equivalent" IS satisfied by the 23324 block. Whether a cinematic opener is worth six screens is exactly the design judgement where reasonable people disagree, and the finding itself rates the risk Medium. What IS objective and rule-backed is the copy: "More glass. Less frame.", "Comfort through every season.", "Strong where it matters.", "Your colour. Your configuration.", "Measured, fitted and guaranteed." all fail TONEOFVOICE.md §2b's own written test — "If a sentence would survive on a competitor's site unchanged, it is generic" — and that should be the finding's spine rather than the pixel count. I found no owner ruling approving or setting the panel count; the story frames were shipped deliberately (PROGRESS.md:4585) but nothing in the docs fixes it at six.

#### [103] /apecs-ingenious-locks-and-hardware/ claims PAS 24 for a component, contradicting the standard AI.md sets for exactly this

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The page states "All APECS & Ingenious locks are rigorously tested to PAS24 and Secured by Design standards, ensuring full compliance with UK security regulations." AI.md records the owner-confirmed position on precisely this error, made about the Kenrick lock: "*capable* is their word and it must survive any rewrite, because a PAS 24 approval belongs to a tested complete window and never to a component." /casement-windows/ follows that rule correctly ("Those approvals belong to a tested complete window rather than to the profile name"), so the two pages contradict each other. "Full compliance with UK security regulations" is also meaningless — there is no such regulation for a lock; Part Q references PAS 24 for the doorset. The page has further faults: an em dash in "fitting APECS & Ingenious locks—offering enhanced security" (one of only four left on the entire site); "[H2] Heightened Security" with no body text at all; "premium", "seamless" ×2, "peace of mind" ×2, "industry-leading", "maximum protection", "maximum peace of mind"; "£5000" and "£5,000" in the same paragraph; an unclosed parenthesis at "(T&C's apply"; and a "5-year manufacturer guarantee" figure in one section against "a manufacturer guarantee" with no figure in the FAQ below it.
- **Recommendation:** Rewrite the PAS 24 sentence to the form /casement-windows/ already uses: name the component, name the standard the complete doorset is tested to, and say the approval belongs to the doorset. Remove the em dash, close the parenthesis, standardise on £5,000, fill or delete the empty "Heightened Security" heading, and reconcile the guarantee figure. Keep the £5,000 break-in guarantee wording — it matches AI.md's confirmed terms including the three named lock components.
- **Why:** It is a technical overclaim on a security page, made against a written internal ruling, and it is checkable by any competitor or trading standards reader. The em dash and empty heading make the page look unfinished on top of it.
- **Affected:** /apecs-ingenious-locks-and-hardware/ (indexable, no noindex).
- **Evidence:** Live copy as quoted. Em dash confirmed by full-site sweep: only 4 em dashes remain across 712 pages, one of them here. Rule: AI.md §Owner-Confirmed Business Facts (Kenrick Excalibur entry). Contradicted by /casement-windows/ FAQ: "Those approvals belong to a tested complete window rather than to the profile name."
- **Verification:** Every sub-claim reproduced, including the one I most expected to fail. The PAS 24 sentence is live verbatim: "Yes. All APECS & Ingenious locks are rigorously tested to PAS24 and Secured by Design standards, ensuring full compliance with UK security regulations." AI.md:62 records the ruling exactly as quoted, including "*capable* is their word and it must survive any rewrite, because a PAS 24 approval belongs to a tested complete window and never to a component." /casement-windows/ does carry the correct form: "Those approvals belong to a tested complete window rather than to the profile name, so we confirm what applies to your configuration." The em-dash claim is the one that needed proving and it survives: a naive `grep -l "—"` hits all 712 pages, but every one of those is inside the inlined consent-JS comments (six per page, 4,272 of the 4,276 total). Filtering script blocks leaves exactly 4 em dashes in visible copy across 3 pages, one of which is "fitting APECS & Ingenious locks—offering enhanced security" on this page. Also verified on the page: `<h2>Heightened Security</h2>` immediately followed by `<h2>In-House Installation Team</h2>` with no intervening body text; "£5,000 break-in guarantee" and "up to £5000 in compensation" in the same paragraph, which also ends "( T&C’s apply" with no closing bracket; "a 5-year manufacturer guarantee" in the installation-team block against the FAQ's "backed by a manufacturer guarantee for peace of mind" with no figure; premium ×1, seamless ×2, peace of mind ×2, industry-leading ×1, maximum protection ×1, exceptional ×1; no noindex on the page.

#### [193] /patio-doors/ never names the system it sells and hedges the manufacturer as "Liniar-style"

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** It is the only Liniar uPVC route with no EnergyPlus tech banner — casement, flush, tilt-turn and uPVC doors all carry one with a chamber count and both glazing figures. It has no entry in `glazing_u_values` (inc/site-data.php:619-658), which is the mechanical reason the banner is absent, yet its key-specification strip still prints `U-value 1.2 W/m²K` from `product_usps` with no source and no star. The body copy then says "Liniar-style uPVC sliding patio door profile" and "Liniar-style multi-chambered uPVC frames" — twice hedging whether it is actually Liniar. A technical buyer leaves with one unattributed number and no system name.
- **Recommendation:** Confirm with the owner which system the sliding patio door is (the WindowCAD collection is `productCollection=2`, labelled "uPVC Sliding Patio Doors"). If it is Liniar, add a `patio-doors` entry to `glazing_u_values` so the EnergyPlus banner renders as it does on the four sibling routes, and delete both "Liniar-style" hedges. If it is not Liniar, remove the 1.2 figure until a sourced one exists — the uPVC doors comment at inc/site-data.php:643-651 is the precedent for how a borrowed figure must be documented.
- **Why:** Every other product page names its system in the first two screens. This one does not, and a hedge like "Liniar-style" tells a reader who knows the trade that we are not sure — on the one route with no photograph of our own work to fall back on.
- **Affected:** /patio-doors/ and its town matrix routes.
- **Evidence:** inc/site-data.php:619-658 contains no `patio-doors` key; inc/site-data.php:446 prints U-value 1.2 from product_usps; live /patio-doors/ has no fg-tech-banner section while casement, flush, tilt-turn and upvc-doors all do; live copy contains "Liniar-style" twice.
- **Verification:** The claim is true, but the finding's stated evidence does NOT establish it and I nearly refuted it on that basis — flagging this because ground-truth rule 1 demands the check be sound. The finding says it verified "by fetching sitemap_index.xml twice"; I did exactly that 3s apart and both returned the IDENTICAL <lastmod>2026-08-13T09:11:30+00:00, which demonstrates the opposite of "always now". The cause is caching: the response carries `cache-control: public, max-age=3600, s-maxage=21600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`, set by fenster_send_public_cache_headers(3600, 21600) right above the emitter. I re-verified properly with cache-busting query strings: three fetches returned 10:42:03, 10:42:08 and 10:42:13 against wall-clock 10:42:02/08/13 — lastmod is the request clock exactly. So the underlying defect is real. Code confirmed: inc/generated-pages.php:1962 is the sole lastmod in the file and is `esc_xml(gmdate('c'))`; the per-URL loop at 2016 emits changefreq only. Counted the local page-sitemap.xml: 712 <loc>, 712 <changefreq>, ZERO lastmod. The recommendation's premise holds — inc/blog-posts.php contains 56 publish_date occurrences. Not ALREADY_RULED: AUDIT.md:178 lists "Sitemap lastmod for the index uses 'now' on every request — meaningless signal" as a problem bullet under section 2.3; that section is marked FIXED 2026-07-03 but its resolution note covers only core-sitemap disabling, the robots filter and the hardcoded host — the lastmod bullet was never addressed, which my live test proves.

Verified the premise that the skipped parents are real, indexable pages: both /case-studies/ and /commercial-projects/ return HTTP 200 live, carry self-referencing canonicals, emit no robots meta and no X-Robots-Tag, and both appear as <loc> entries in page-sitemap.xml. County three-level output confirmed (['Home','Commercial Glazing','Commercial Glazing Bedfordshire']), so the builder demonstrably supports three levels. The /3d-visualiser/ breadcrumb emits name "Design Your Door" against title "Visualise Your Doors & Windows in 3D | Get Instant Pricing" and H1 "Visualise your windows and doors with Fenster." — mismatched with both, as claimed. Grepped all docs for breadcrumb rulings: AI.md:271 mandates theme-generated BreadcrumbList as source of truth but says nothing sanctioning a missing parent level, so this is not an owner decision.
