#### [109] The five oldest /meet-the-team/ bios are AI puffery, and the two founders get the worst copy on the page

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 82% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The /meet-the-team/ page carries 17 bios: Adam Butcher and Nick Baker render as H2 in a leadership block, and 15 more render as H3 cards. Twelve of the H3 bios are good — factual, human, specific ("over 20 years in the trade", "completing the challenging climb up High Cup Nick", and Legend's, which is the best comic writing on the site). Five bios are unedited old-site filler: the two founders, the Installation Manager, the Office Manager, and one installer. Adam Butcher "plays a pivotal role" and works "to the highest standards", "bringing a sense of adventure and creativity to his professional and personal life". Nick Baker is "our dynamic Sales Director" who "brings his passion for business and marketing to the forefront" and "creates innovative strategies that drive our sales success", "drawing inspiration from diverse cultures and experiences". David Foord "is renowned for his excellent leadership abilities. He ensures that all installations are executed flawlessly" — an absolute quality claim no installer can make. Perry Giffin has "organizational prowess" (American spelling). Tom Carter — an Installer, not a director — has "a people-pleasing attitude", "a positive and cheerful energy", a "friendly demeanor" (American spelling) and "embracing the thrill of the journey" ("journey" is on the TONEOFVOICE.md:159 never-use list). Neither founder bio mentions that they founded the company. The About page already says it properly: "Adam Butcher and Nick Baker founded Fenster in 2018 and are still here every day. Nick runs sales and the showroom. Adam runs the commercial side, from schools and care homes to full curtain walling." Note that COPY-AUDIT.md:141 previously cleared team bios as reading well, so this rewrite should be put to the owner rather than treated as an agreed fix.
- **Recommendation:** Rewrite those five to match the standard the other twelve already set: role, one concrete fact, one human detail. Start Adam and Nick from the About page sentence, which is already owner-approved, and say in both that they founded the company in 2018. Change "organizational" to "organisational" and "demeanor" to "demeanour" — these are 2 of only 6 pages site-wide carrying American spellings. Delete "executed flawlessly" and "embracing the thrill of the journey". Flag to the owner that COPY-AUDIT.md:141 previously recorded team bios as checked and cleared.
- **Why:** The team page is proof-of-people, which the About page treats as the core of the offer ("Behind them is a team from the trade, not a call centre"). Fitters currently sound real and directors sound like LinkedIn. It reads as though the founders were written about by an agency and the crew were written about by someone who knows them.
- **Affected:** /meet-the-team/, 5 of 15 bios. Also the source of 2 of the 6 pages carrying American spellings site-wide.
- **Evidence:** Live copy as quoted. American spellings confirmed by full-site sweep: only 6 of 712 pages contain any, and /meet-the-team/ contributes "organizational" and "demeanor". "journey" is on the TONEOFVOICE.md never-use list. Contrasting good copy on the same page: "Johnnie Greenwell is a highly experienced installer… with over 20 years in the trade."
- **Verification:** Every quoted phrase reproduces exactly once on the live page, and the supporting sweep is precisely right, but the bio count and the seniority claim are both wrong. Running a Python H3 extraction over meet-the-team.txt returns 15 names — and Adam Butcher and Nick Baker are not among them, because the two founders render as H2 in a separate leadership block above the 15 H3 cards. So the page carries 17 bios and the finding is about 5 of 17, not 5 of 15. The claim that these are 'the five most senior people' is also wrong: Adam (Commercial Director), Nick (Sales Director), David Foord (Installation Manager) and Perry Giffin (Office Manager) are senior, but Tom Carter is listed as 'Installer' — a fitter, which actually cuts against the finding's own framing that 'fitters currently sound real and directors sound like LinkedIn'. Everything else holds. My own independent American-spelling sweep across all 712 pages returned exactly 6 pages, matching the finding's claim precisely, with meet-the-team.txt contributing 'demeanor' and 'organizational'. 'journey' is confirmed on the TONEOFVOICE.md:159 never-use list, and 'thrill of the journey' appears once in Tom Carter's bio. The About page sentence quoted as the rewrite source is verbatim. One contrary prior ruling the parent should know about: COPY-AUDIT.md:141 lists team bios under '**Not bugs (checked and cleared)** ... team bios (including Legend the Chief Meow Officer) ... all read well'. That is a prior auditor's judgement rather than an owner decision, and it did not test for the specific rule breaches here (a never-use word, two American spellings, and the absolute claim 'executed flawlessly'), so it does not override this finding — but it means the owner has seen a document saying these bios are fine, and the rewrite should be raised rather than assumed approved. Confidence lowered from 88 to 82 for the count and seniority errors.

#### [178] Uncached PHP render is ~150-170 ms on every route and the HTML edge cache only holds for an hour, so most of the 712 long-tail routes serve cold — but raising s-maxage as-is would break the enquiry form's nonce

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 80% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** HTML carries `cache-control: public, max-age=600, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`, which is sensible. But with 712 routes and an hour of shared-cache life, the 525 town/matrix routes and the commercial pages will be cold for a large share of their (by definition thin) traffic. Cache-busting with a random query gives a very consistent 270-303 ms TTFB across /areas-we-cover/, /composite-doors/, the homepage and /patio-doors-aylesbury/, against 90-111 ms warm — roughly 150-170 ms of origin work per request, uniform across page shapes. The probe caught the tail: 813 ms on /windows-milton-keynes/, 398 ms on /book-a-consultation/, 390 ms on /contact/, 356 ms on /doors-milton-keynes/; a random 12-URL sitemap sweep returned 280-470 ms on every cold matrix route. The `ob_start` + 8-pattern `preg_replace` in inc/consent.php:31-54 is NOT a meaningful contributor: measured against the real 320 KB /areas-we-cover/ document in PHP 8.2 it costs 0.17 ms per pass, 0.1% of the render, because the anchor literals are absent and PCRE never backtracks.
- **Recommendation:** Raise `s-maxage` and `stale-while-revalidate` — the pages are deterministic (a fetch with and without consent cookies differs in exactly one unused `fenster_started_at` timestamp) — but you CANNOT do it without first dealing with the nonce. `template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:334` bakes `wp_nonce_field('fenster_submit_enquiry')` into the cached HTML and `inc/enquiries.php:512-515` hard-rejects a stale one with 'The form session expired'; I confirmed the same nonce value is served across independent cache-busted fetches. Logged-out WP nonces last 24 h, so s-maxage=86400 + swr=604800 would routinely serve nonces up to 8 days old and silently kill lead capture. Either (a) fetch the nonce client-side from a small uncached REST endpoint on form focus and stop rendering it into the document, then raise s-maxage to 86400 with swr=604800 and purge on deploy; or (b) keep s-maxage well inside the nonce window (e.g. 21600) until (a) is done. Note the current setting already carries a milder version of this exposure: 3600 + 86400 swr = up to 25 h. Separately, delete the 8-pattern output-buffer strip in inc/consent.php:31-54 — not for speed, but because it is dead belt-and-braces over the `option_*` filters at lines 16-20 that already blank the plugin options.
- **Why:** A visitor on 4G pays several megabytes before reaching a single specification. This is the one route where the performance cost is not a few oversized images but an architectural choice.
- **Affected:** /aluminium-windows/ only.
- **Evidence:** live HTML `data-frame-count="241"`; probe-mobile.json /aluminium-windows/ perf.byType.img = {n:229, bytes:7539460}; probe-desktop.json same route = 12.31MB; heaviest list includes frame-001..frame-050.webp at ~79KB each plus prestige-window-scrub-mobile.mp4 at 254KB.
- **Verification:** The performance measurements reproduce, but one sub-claim is refuted by direct measurement and the recommendation as written would break the site's main lead-capture form. CONFIRMED: `cache-control: public, max-age=600, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400` on live HTML; cache-busted curl (?cb=$RANDOM) gives cold TTFB 0.270-0.303 across /areas-we-cover/, /composite-doors/, / and /patio-doors-aylesbury/, against warm 0.090-0.111 on / and /composite-doors/ — a ~0.17 s delta, matching the claimed 150-170 ms; probe-desktop ttfb outliers are exactly as quoted (/windows-milton-keynes/ 813, /book-a-consultation/ 398, /contact/ 390, /doors-milton-keynes/ 356); my own random 12-URL sitemap sweep returned 0.28-0.47 on cold matrix routes. inc/consent.php:31-54 is exactly as described: template_redirect priority 0 ob_start over 8 preg_replace patterns with .*? and /is. REFUTED sub-claim: 'Part of that render cost is self-inflicted' by that regex pass. I ran the eight real patterns against the real 319,910-byte /areas-we-cover/ document 20 times in PHP 8.2 — 0.17 ms per pass. That is 0.1% of the 150-170 ms, i.e. immeasurable. PCRE bails immediately because the anchor literals are absent (the option_* filters at consent.php:16-20 already blank them), so the .*?//is patterns never backtrack. The regex pass is dead weight worth deleting for tidiness, but it is not part of the render cost and should not be presented as such. NEW MATERIAL RISK the finding misses: raising s-maxage to 86400 with swr=604800 would break the enquiry form. The cached HTML contains a hard `wp_nonce_field('fenster_submit_enquiry', 'fenster_enquiry_nonce')` (enquiry-form.php:334), verified server-side at inc/enquiries.php:512-515, which hard-fails with 'The form session expired. Please refresh the page and try again.' Logged-out WP nonces live 24 h; 86400 + 604800 means a visitor could be served an 8-day-old nonce. I confirmed the nonce is byte-identical across two independent cache-busted fetches (dd07f948be both times), so it IS being cached. VERIFIED SAFE: the page is otherwise fully deterministic — a fetch with and without consent cookies differed in exactly one line, `fenster_started_at`, which is emitted at enquiry-form.php:333 and read nowhere in the theme; `vary: Accept-Encoding` only.

- **Why:** The route is positioned as the trade's answer for steel replacement and offers no evidence of a steel replacement. That gap is documented as the highest-value photograph on the whole wishlist; until it exists the page should stop under-using what it has.
- **Affected:** /heritage-windows/.
- **Evidence:** Live body image inventory: hw-hero-steel-look-2048w.webp (Sheerline), hw-install-stone-gable-1200w.webp (ours), heritage-door-brick-1200w.webp; AI.md Heritage Windows Rule and Imagery Rule; PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md "HERITAGE WINDOWS — one job".
- **Verification:** The pattern is real and I reproduced the counter-example verbatim, but the count is wrong by 8 and the impact framing needs correcting.

WHAT HOLDS, precisely: parsing every `<img>` inside `<main>` on crawl/colour-options.html returns bare colour names — 'White', 'Cream', 'Chartwell Green', ... 'Colza Yellow' — across three swatch families (Liniar uPVC 16, Sheerline aluminium corners 12, RAL door colours 24). Longest is 'Gale Grey Finesse (Anthracite Smooth)' at exactly 37 chars, matching the finding's stated maximum, so we are looking at the same extraction. The counter-example is exact: on crawl/casement-windows.html the identical file `colours_page_image-7016-SM-Grey.webp` carries `alt="Liniar uPVC casement window profile in Anthracite Grey"`. The good pattern genuinely exists in the codebase and the colour hub genuinely dropped it. No doc rules on this.

WRONG — COUNT. There are 52 swatch images with bare colour-name alt, not 44. 16 + 12 + 24 = 52. 44 looks like a count of UNIQUE colour names (I make it 43 unique — 'Anthracite Grey', 'Cream', 'Agate Grey', 'Rosewood', 'Chartwell Green', 'Slate Grey', 'Basalt Grey' and 'Black Brown' each recur across families). Report the image count, not the vocabulary count.

MISSED: five further images in `<main>` carry a completely EMPTY alt — `s2-white-finish.png`, `s2-black-finish.png`, `s2-chrome-finish.png`, `s2-gold-finish.png`, `s2-titanium-finish.png`. I pulled their surrounding text: they sit in the decorative 'Next choice · Handle options' teaser with no adjacent labels, so `alt=""` is defensible there — but it should be a conscious call.

IMPACT FRAMING WRONG: this is an image-SEO gap, not an accessibility failure. Each swatch already carries a visible text label with its reference — the screenshot at scratchpad/mfold/cas-colours.png shows 'White / Foil, RAL 9010' and 'Smooth White / No foil, RAL 9003' beneath the tiles — and AI.md:722 makes that labelling mandatory ('Each tile carries `Standard colour` or its RAL reference'). A screen-reader user therefore gets the material context from adjacent text. The claim that 'an alt of Anthracite Grey alone matches nothing' stands for image search; the implied a11y harm does not.

#### [197] Header logo src is emitted unencoded because fenster_image_attr_string() escapes src with esc_attr instead of esc_url

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `inc/assets.php:155` runs every attribute — including `src` — through `esc_attr()`. `esc_attr` escapes HTML but does not percent-encode, so any path containing a space is emitted as an invalid URI. The site header is the one place this bites today: `template-parts/layout/site-header.php:16` passes `/assets/brand/18931 Fenster Glazing Logo - White Background.png` through the helper and all 712 pages emit three raw spaces inside the `src`. The rest of the codebase already handles it correctly — `template-parts/layout/site-footer.php:34` uses `esc_url()` on an equally spaced dark-background logo and emits `%20` on all 712 pages, and `inc/enquiries.php:431,462` hard-code the `%20` form. Browsers and Googlebot encode and fetch it (200 when encoded); the demonstrated failure is confined to naive parsers — the lead auditor's link checker recorded the one `000` row in a 1,048-URL sweep, though the URL it recorded is the page URL concatenated with the src, i.e. its own relative-resolution failure rather than a server error.
- **Recommendation:** Two changes. (1) In `inc/assets.php:155`, escape the `src` value with `esc_url()` and keep `esc_attr()` for the rest — this closes the class of bug rather than one instance, and matches what `site-footer.php:34` already does. (2) Separately, rename the asset to `fenster-logo-white.png` and update `template-parts/layout/site-header.php:16` (NOT `header.php`, which only calls `get_template_part`). A leading order number and spaces in a shipped brand asset is worth fixing on its own, but the escaping fix is the one that matters.
- **Why:** This window sells on one idea a picture answers instantly. A visitor currently reads about it and then looks at sixteen foil swatches.
- **Affected:** /tilt-turn-windows/.
- **Evidence:** Live measurement at 375x812: product sections 874+796+803+1295 = 3,768px vs glass 800 + colours 1,533 + handles 1,218 = 3,551px; body image inventory returns tilt-turn-room-hero-1920w.webp plus four Liniar hardware jpegs and nothing else; PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md tilt-and-turn entry.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and I reproduced it exactly — but the file cite is wrong, the root cause is wrong, and the headline evidence is a link-checker artifact.

WHAT HOLDS: `grep -l '18931 Fenster Glazing Logo' crawl/*.html | wc -l` = 712/712. Live markup on home.html: `src="https://fensterglazing.com/app/themes/fenster/assets/brand/18931 Fenster Glazing Logo - White Background.png"` — three raw spaces. curl percent-encoded = 200; raw = 000. It is the only spaced `src` on the pages I sampled (home, casement-windows, composite-doors).

WRONG #1 — FILE. `header.php` does not contain the reference; it is essentially one line, `get_template_part('template-parts/layout/site-header')`. The reference is `template-parts/layout/site-header.php:16`. Anyone following the recommendation opens the wrong file.

WRONG #2 — ROOT CAUSE. This is not really a filename problem, it is an escaping bug. `inc/assets.php:136-159` `fenster_image_attr_string()` emits every attribute through `esc_attr()`, including `src` (line 155). `esc_attr` does not percent-encode spaces; `esc_url` does. Proof from the same codebase: `template-parts/layout/site-footer.php:34` passes an equally spaced filename (`18931 - 2026 - Fenster Glazing Logo - Dark Background.png`) through `esc_url()` and emits a correct `...18931%20-%202026%20-%20...png` — grep -l for the raw-spaced dark filename across the crawl returns 0 pages. `inc/enquiries.php:431,462` also hard-code the `%20` form. So two of the three call sites already do it right; only the helper does not. Renaming one asset leaves the helper able to re-emit an invalid URL for any future spaced path.

WRONG #3 — EVIDENCE. The `000` row in linkcheck.tsv is `https://fensterglazing.com/windows-milton-keynes/https://fensterglazing.com/app/themes/fenster/assets/brand/18931 Fenster Glazing Logo - White Background.png` — the page URL concatenated with the absolute src. The checker failed to recognise the scheme because of the spaces and resolved it as relative. The space is the trigger, but 'the request could not be formed' overstates it: real browsers and Googlebot encode this and fetch it fine (the logo renders in every screenshot). Impact Low is right; confidence should come down because the practical breakage is theoretical.

#### [111] Four shared section headings are label-style with no full stop, breaking the TONEOFVOICE heading rule on up to 568 pages each

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** TONEOFVOICE.md:126 requires that headings are complete customer-truth statements in sentence case ending with a full stop, and :141 adds that a heading "should still be worth reading if it were the only text on the page". Four shared section headings fail that test identically, and they are template strings so each one fails at scale: "What Milton Keynes homeowners say" on 568 pages (review-showcase.php:68), "Products, services and nearby areas" on 526 pages (location-service.php:1434 and :1754), "Services, projects and glazing packages" on 47 pages (commercial-county.php:266), and "Products and services mentioned in this guide" on 38 pages (generated-article.php:267). The review one is the sharpest case because it sits directly above a paragraph that does obey the rule and is good: "Real reviews from real installations. Every one is public, so you can go and check them yourself." It is the most-repeated prose section heading on the site, though not the most-repeated H2 overall — six footer and cookie-modal H2s render on all 712 pages.
- **Recommendation:** Fix all four as one batch, since they are four template strings in three files. For the review section, promote the good line into the heading: H2 "Every review is public, so you can go and check them yourself." and let the body carry the figures. For the other three, write statements rather than labels, for example "Everything we fit, and the towns we fit it in." (location-service.php:1434 and :1754), "What we install on commercial sites." (commercial-county.php:266) and "The products this guide is about." (generated-article.php:267).
- **Why:** It is the most-rendered heading on the site and the only one of the shared section headings that fails the voice document's own test, while the sentence that passes it is already written one line below.
- **Affected:** 568 live pages. template-parts/components/review-showcase.php:68.
- **Evidence:** `<h2><?php esc_html_e('What Milton Keynes homeowners say', 'fenster'); ?></h2>` at review-showcase.php:68; string present on 568 of 712 fetched pages. Rule: TONEOFVOICE.md §Headings.
- **Verification:** The core defect is real and every hard number checks out, but the two claims that make it sound distinctive are both false, and correcting them makes the finding more useful rather than less. Confirmed: review-showcase.php:68 reads exactly '<h2><?php esc_html_e('What Milton Keynes homeowners say', 'fenster'); ?></h2>', the string renders on exactly 568 of 712 pages, and TONEOFVOICE.md:126 does require that 'Headings are complete customer-truth statements in sentence case, ending with a full stop', with :141 adding 'The heading should still be worth reading if it were the only text on the page'. The good paragraph beneath it is verbatim as quoted. Refuted, however, is 'the only one of the shared section headings that fails the voice document's own test'. I extracted and ranked every H2 across all 712 pages: 'Products, services and nearby areas' renders on 526 pages (location-service.php:1434 and :1754), 'Services, projects and glazing packages' on 47 (commercial-county.php:266), and 'Products and services mentioned in this guide' on 38 (generated-article.php:267). All three are labels, all three lack a closing full stop, and all three fail the same test identically. Also refuted is 'the most-repeated heading on the site': six H2s render on all 712 pages — 'What we do', 'Fenster', 'Contact', 'Legend the cat' (footer columns) and two cookie-modal headings — though those are chrome rather than prose section headings, so the finding's string is fair to call the most-repeated *content* section heading. Widening the scope to four shared headings in three template files means this can be fixed as one batch. Impact stays Low; confidence lowered from 90 to 85 for the two false claims.

#### [112] /areas-we-cover/ advertises its own link count as a credential and tells the reader not to worry about choosing the right page

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 84% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** In the hero of /areas-we-cover/, the proof panel beside the H1 (<aside class="fg-areas-page__summary">) reads "Start with your nearest town." followed by the figure "25 towns and 525 local service links". That is the site's internal link inventory presented to a customer as a credential. Directly beneath it: "You do not need to choose the perfect page. If your property is nearby, send the postcode and Fenster can point you in the right direction." — the page apologising for its own navigation, using "perfect" (on the TONEOFVOICE.md:159 never-use list) and referring to Fenster in the third person, which STYLE.md:86 and TONEOFVOICE.md:122 both forbid. The same page has "The team checks measurements, access, frame style…", which is also Fenster in the third person under STYLE.md:86 (note: "the team" is not itself on the STYLE.md:255 banned list, which names "the installer", "the company" and "your local specialist", and "Meet the team" is approved copy elsewhere). Two body H2s are label-style with no closing full stop: "Local advice from Milton Keynes" and "Survey-led installation".
- **Recommendation:** Replace the link-count figure with something a customer can use: the actual coverage radius, or "25 towns, one showroom on Alston Drive, our own fitters in all of them". Rewrite the reassurance line without referring to pages and without "perfect" or third-person Fenster: "Not sure which town is closest? Send the postcode and we will tell you." Change "The team checks" to "We check". Give "Local advice from Milton Keynes" and "Survey-led installation" closing full stops and turn them into statements — this is the same batch as the shared-heading fix in finding 111.
- **Why:** This page is the top of the local funnel and the first number it shows a customer is how many links it contains. It is the clearest surviving instance of the "talks about the website, not to the customer" pattern COPY-AUDIT.md §2 was written to remove.
- **Affected:** /areas-we-cover/. Also the heaviest HTML page on the Tier-1 set at 320KB.
- **Evidence:** Live copy on /areas-we-cover/: "25 towns and 525 local service links" and "You do not need to choose the perfect page. If your property is nearby, send the postcode and Fenster can point you in the right direction." Rules: COPY-AUDIT.md §2; STYLE.md third-person rule; TONEOFVOICE.md never-use list.
- **Verification:** All four quoted strings reproduce verbatim on the live page, and the strongest parts of the finding stand, but three supporting details are wrong. Confirmed: '25 towns and 525 local service links' and 'You do not need to choose the perfect page. If your property is nearby, send the postcode and Fenster can point you in the right direction.' are both live and appear exactly once; 'perfect' is on the TONEOFVOICE.md:159 never-use list; and 'Fenster can point you in the right direction' is a clean third-person violation of STYLE.md:86 ('Do not describe Fenster in the third person') and TONEOFVOICE.md:122. /areas-we-cover/ is confirmed the heaviest Tier-1 page — ls -S ranks it first and du reports 316KB. Wrong, though, is the claim that '"the team" is the third-person construction STYLE.md lists beside "the company"'. STYLE.md:255 lists 'the installer', 'the company' and 'your local specialist' — 'the team' is not on it, and TONEOFVOICE.md:101 and :147 actively use 'Meet the team' as approved copy and an approved button label. The objection to 'The team checks' therefore rests only on the general third-person rule at STYLE.md:86, which is a weaker basis than the finding implies, though the suggested change to 'We check' is still right. Second, 'three H2s without closing full stops' overstates: the page body has two statement H2s missing a stop ('Local advice from Milton Keynes', 'Survey-led installation'); the third, 'Nearby town not listed?', ends in a question mark and is arguably compliant. Third, the stat is not in 'the stat position under the H1' — it sits in <aside class="fg-areas-page__summary"> beside the H1 in the hero grid, under the bolded line 'Start with your nearest town.'. The link-count-as-credential point is the real finding and it survives intact. Confidence lowered from 90 to 84.

#### [198] /composite-doors/ case-study cards are titled "Flush casement windows and a composite door" on the composite doors page

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 78% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Both cards in the strip lead with the windows: "Flush casement windows and a composite door, Little Horwood" and "...Wolverton". The same two titles render on `/flush-casement-windows/`, where they are correct. On the door page the visitor reads two headlines about windows under "Real installs, photographed on the day." The same effect hits `/upvc-doors/`, whose single card is titled "Flush casement windows and a composite door, Wolverton" — naming a composite door on a uPVC doors page.
- **Recommendation:** Drop `https://www.fensa.org.uk/` from the sameAs array at `inc/generated-pages.php:2320`. Do NOT plan on swapping it for a FENSA installer-directory URL: `fensa.org.uk/find-an-installer` 404s, and the real directory at `fensa.org.uk/find-installers` is a JS search that renders no per-installer URL and returns no 'Fenster' string in its static HTML — there is nothing crawlable to link to. If a genuine third-party profile is wanted in its place, use one with a real static URL (Checkatrade, Which? Trusted Traders, Bing Places), which is the same citations work SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md:116 already calls for. Separately, `'logo'` at line 2311 points at `assets/brand/favicon-512.png`; point it at the real logo asset once finding 197's rename lands.
- **Why:** This is the strongest page on the site and its proof block currently reads as being about a different product. On /upvc-doors/ it is worse: the card names composite, which AI.md says should barely be mentioned on that route.
- **Affected:** /composite-doors/ (2 cards), /upvc-doors/ (1 card).
- **Evidence:** Live case-study strip h3s on composite-doors and upvc-doors; AI.md Review Showcase Rule notes `fenster_review_cards()` already accepts a context string for exactly this reason.
- **Verification:** The problem is exactly as described at exactly the cited lines. The recommendation is not achievable as written.

WHAT HOLDS: `inc/generated-pages.php:2315` opens `'sameAs' => [`, lines 2316-2320 are the five URLs, 2321 closes — the cite is precise. `https://www.fensa.org.uk/` is the trade body homepage, not a page about this business, and schema.org defines sameAs as a URL that unambiguously indicates the item's identity. Line 2311 confirms `'logo' => FENSTER_THEME_URI . '/assets/brand/favicon-512.png'` — a favicon standing in for the logo. The block is otherwise clean: I enumerated `@type` across all 712 crawled pages and there is no aggregateRating or Review anywhere, consistent with the owner ruling at SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md:108. No doc rules on the FENSA sameAs entry; SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md:116 in fact lists 'FENSA/CPA profile links' as a wanted citation, so the finding runs with the grain of the plan.

WHAT DOES NOT HOLD: the recommendation asserts 'fensa.org.uk carries a per-installer page'. I could not find one. `https://www.fensa.org.uk/find-an-installer` returns 404. The real directory is `https://www.fensa.org.uk/find-installers` (200) and it is a JS-driven search: fetching it with a postcode query returns zero `installer/...` hrefs and zero occurrences of 'Fenster' in the static HTML. There is no crawlable per-installer URL to point sameAs at, so the primary recommendation cannot be executed and the fix reduces to 'drop the entry'.

Also overstated: 'one wrong entry in a five-item array is a quarter of the signal' is rhetoric, not a measurement — the other four are unaffected by the fifth's presence. Impact Low is right; confidence should drop because the actionable half of the recommendation does not exist.

#### [179] About 26 MB of theme images are referenced by nothing — and a further 180 MB in assets/images/imported/ is named only by the legacy pages.json import record, inside a 431 MB assets directory

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 72% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `assets/` totals 431 MB, of which `assets/images/` is 347 MB and `assets/images/imported/` alone is 242 MB across 354 files (150 PNGs at 188.0 MB, 478 JPEGs at 105.6 MB, 1,160 WebPs at 74.3 MB overall). Cross-referencing every image filename on disk against every filename string in any theme .php/.json/.js/.scss returns 919 files / 43.2 MB with no match — but that number must not be reported as-is: 480 of those files and 17.2 MB of that weight are `assets/videos/aluminium-windows-story/frames-desktop` and `frames-mobile`, the live 241-frame scroll story, invisible to the matcher only because src/js/main.js builds `frame-NNN.webp` programmatically from frame-001. The bare-filename matcher UNDER-counts references for generated paths, so 43.2 MB is a ceiling, not a floor; the defensible unreferenced figure is roughly 26 MB, concentrated in products/casement/gallery (3.8 MB), products/colours/liniar-swatches (3.0 MB — genuinely unused, since site-data.php:3223+ names each live swatch by full filename), imported/ (2.8 MB) and products/composite-distinction/styles (1.7 MB). The larger prize is different: 238 files totalling 179.7 MB in assets/images/imported/ are named ONLY by data/pages.json, the imported Yoast content dump, and by no PHP, JS or SCSS in the theme — including Untitled-design-16.png at 17.5 MB, 2-2-2.png at 10.5 MB and 5-1.png at 9.5 MB.
- **Recommendation:** This does not affect page weight, only deploy size, backup time and the risk of someone reaching for a 17 MB PNG because it is sitting in the directory. Before any deletion, rebuild the reference sweep so it understands generated paths — at minimum whitelist `assets/videos/*/frames-*/` and any directory whose filenames match a numeric or width-suffix pattern (`-300w`, `-600w`, `frame-NNN`), because a naive sweep will happily flag the site's flagship scroll asset as dead. Then work the real target: audit which of the 238 imported/ files reachable only through data/pages.json correspond to pages that still render, and archive the rest outside the theme — that is 179.7 MB, seven times the genuinely-unreferenced total. The registry-sprawl problem recorded in project memory (a name lives in 6-7 registries that never check each other) applies directly, and assets/images/imported/ is exactly where a stray reference hides.
- **Why:** This is a written owner instruction dated 2026-07-24 and reconfirmed on 2026-08-12, breached on live pages. It also actively sells against the range: a customer told Charisma is for rentals will not buy it, and one told Ultimate is "premium" now expects a premium price before seeing a figure.
- **Affected:** /sliding-sash-windows/ (4 instances), /patio-doors/ (2), /integral-blinds/ (2).
- **Evidence:** TONEOFVOICE.md "Words And Phrases" never-use list and the 2026-07-24 owner instruction quoted there; live main-content sweep across all 15 pages returns hits only on sliding-sash (premium, budget, cost-conscious, seamless), patio-doors (cost-effective, value-led) and integral-blinds (budget x2).
- **Verification:** I reproduced the headline number to the file — and that is exactly what exposes the flaw. Running the finding's own method (bare-filename match of every image under assets/ against the concatenated text of every theme .php/.json/.js/.scss) I get 869 referenced / 324.7 MB and 919 unreferenced / 43.2 MB, against the claimed 868 / 920 / 43.2 MB. But grouping the 919 by directory shows the top two entries are `assets/videos/aluminium-windows-story/frames-desktop` (240 files, 11.5 MB) and `frames-mobile` (240 files, 5.7 MB) — 480 of the 919 files (52%) and 17.2 MB of the 43.2 MB (40%) are the aluminium-windows scroll story, the single most actively-used asset set on the site, which finding 176 IN THIS SAME BATCH documents loading 12.9 MB on /aluminium-windows/. They register as unreferenced only because src/js/main.js:4948 builds `frame-NNN.webp` programmatically and only frame-001 is named in source. This inverts the finding's central methodological claim: it states 'the matcher is deliberately loose... so it over-counts references, so 43.2 MB is a floor, not an estimate.' The opposite is true — it UNDER-counts references wherever paths are generated, so 43.2 MB is a CEILING. The defensible figure is ~26 MB. Two further factual errors: (1) 'a 347 MB assets directory' — `du -sh assets/` is 431 MB; 347 MB is `assets/images/`, and `assets/images/imported/` alone is 242 MB across 354 files. (2) 'assets/images/imported/... is the main offender' — by this method imported/ contributes only 6 files / 2.8 MB of unreferenced weight, because data/pages.json names the rest; the largest unreferenced dirs are actually products/casement/gallery (3.8 MB), products/colours/liniar-swatches (3.0 MB, and I confirmed these ARE genuinely unused variants since site-data.php:3223+ names swatches individually by full filename) and imported/ (2.8 MB). The named giants — Untitled-design-16.png (17,459,146 B), 2-2-2.png, 5-1.png, 3-2-2.png, 1-2-2.png — are all referenced in data/pages.json and so were never in the unreferenced set. A stronger and better-targeted version of this finding exists that the auditor missed: 238 files / 179.7 MB inside assets/images/imported/ are named ONLY by data/pages.json (the legacy Yoast import record) and by no .php/.js/.scss anywhere. Impact 'Low' and the deploy/backup framing are right.

#### [194] Twelve orphaned informational URLs split three intents (noise, condensation, energy) with no internal signal between them

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 70% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The imported article library contains overlapping intents that were never consolidated, and 12 of the 13 pages involved are orphaned (zero inbound internal links, in-body or otherwise). Noise: /soundproof-windows/ (597 words, "How to Soundproof Your Windows: The Ultimate DIY Guide", 57 clicks / 16,143 impressions at position 26.5), /soundproofing-solutions-how-to-choose-windows-for-a-quieter-home/ (831), /guide-noise-insulation-for-windows/ (2,583 — the longest, and orphaned), /which-is-better-triple-or-acoustic-glazing/ (542). Two of those titles lead on the same head term. Condensation: /condensation-on-new-windows/ (552), /deal-with-condensation/ (1,260), /how-to-prevent-window-condensation-in-winter/ (755). Energy/glazing basics: /are-my-windows-energy-efficient/ (661), /consider-energy-efficient-windows-for-your-home/ (894), /a-guide-to-understanding-u-values/ (642), /what-are-double-glazed-glass-windows/ (1,289), /benefits-of-upvc-windows-for-your-home/ (1,285). IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the product page /secondary-glazing/ is NOT orphaned — it receives 86 in-body internal links and 1,510 including nav/footer, i.e. every page on the site links to it. It is also a local commercial page ("Secondary Glazing Installer Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire") serving a different intent from the DIY informational articles, so it should be treated as the existing internal-link destination for the noise topic rather than as a cannibalising duplicate. The real defect is that 12 orphaned informational URLs split three intents with no internal signal at all between them.
- **Recommendation:** Do the internal-linking fix first and re-measure. Because /secondary-glazing/ already receives 1,510 internal links and is the commercial destination, make it the hub for the noise topic and link the four orphaned noise articles into it (and to each other), rather than consolidating onto /guide-noise-insulation-for-windows/, which nothing currently links to. For condensation and energy, pick one primary per cluster (/deal-with-condensation/ at 1,260 words, and /a-guide-to-understanding-u-values/ or /benefits-of-upvc-windows-for-your-home/ for energy) and hub-and-spoke the rest into it. Only after re-measuring, and only if the split persists, 301 the weakest duplicates. Do not delete before measuring: these pages carry real, if international, click volume. Do not 301 /secondary-glazing/ under any circumstance — it is a money page.
- **Why:** On a front door, security is the objection. Putting the 13 foils and 8 handle finishes in front of it answers the second question before the first.
- **Affected:** /upvc-doors/.
- **Evidence:** Live measurement at 375x812: hero 368 + pulse 311 + config 1062 + open 889 + ways 2193 + colours 1310 + handles 1499 + glass 746 + banner 407 = 8,785px before fg-upd-detail (1,696px); /aluminium-doors/ security band starts at 3,953px.
- **Verification:** The cluster overlap is real and the page-level data is accurate, but the load-bearing evidence claim is false. I built an inbound-link counter over in-<main> anchors across all 712 pages and validated it first (all 712 files contain <main>, so no false orphans; cross-checked with direct greps). Result: 12 of the 13 are genuinely orphaned at zero in-main and zero total inbound links — but /secondary-glazing/ has 86 in-main inbound links and 1,510 links including nav/footer, and a direct `grep -l` shows all 712 pages link to it. The finding's evidence line "all 13 confirmed to have zero inbound internal links" is therefore wrong, and so is the causal argument built on it: "Because every one of these is orphaned, Google has no internal signal at all about which URL is canonical for the intent" collapses for the noise cluster, where the site already funnels 1,510 internal links into /secondary-glazing/. That also undercuts the recommendation to consolidate noise onto /guide-noise-insulation-for-windows/ (which nothing links to — grep finds it in 1 file, itself). Separately, /secondary-glazing/ is a local commercial money page ("Secondary Glazing Installer Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire"), a different intent from the informational DIY articles, so listing it as a cannibalising cluster member is a stretch. Everything else verified: word counts reproduce (597, 831, 2583, 542 for noise; 552/1260/755 condensation; 661/894/642/1289/1285 energy — my secondary-glazing count was 2445 vs the claimed 2126, a whitespace-tokenising difference), all titles verbatim, and the GSC figures are exact at SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md:101 (57 clicks / 16,143 impressions / 26.5). Unrelated bonus bug spotted: /what-are-double-glazed-glass-windows/ ships the live title "What Are Double Glazed Glass Windows? | Fester Glazing" — the brand name is misspelt (missing 'n').

#### [108] Product-page hero CTAs use the invented journey language STYLE.md bans, and land on repair and roofline routes where nothing is designed

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 60% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** On 21 product routes the hero button reads "Start your design consultation" (with the responsive short label "Design consultation"), 19 routes carry the H2 "Get pricing or book a design chat." and 2 carry the button "Book a design chat". STYLE.md:88 requires plain CTA labels that describe the action and bans invented journey language of the "Start your journey" form. PROGRESS.md:3524 already identifies this exact string as "the invented journey language `STYLE.md` bans" and records it as "a separate fix needing owner sign-off" — so it is a known, acknowledged, unfixed item rather than a new discovery. Separately, the design framing lands on routes where design is not the customer's problem: /roofline/ (fascias and guttering), /cat-and-dog-flaps/ and /secondary-glazing/ render "Start your design consultation"; /window-and-door-repairs/ (a door that will not lock) renders "Book a design chat"; /double-glazing-replacement/ (a misted unit) carries the H2 "Get pricing or book a design chat.". PROGRESS.md:1359 records the same fault being caught and fixed on another route, which confirms it is treated as a real defect. NOTE: the "drops the word free" argument does not hold. These CTAs point at #fenster-enquiry, an on-page enquiry form, while the header and footer "Free Consultation" / "Book a free consultation" point at /book-a-consultation/. They are two different actions, and PROGRESS.md:3524 records that adding "free" here was considered and rejected because it "would have described the wrong thing".
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as the owner sign-off that PROGRESS.md:3524 says is outstanding, not as a new fault. Replace "Start your design consultation" and its short label "Design consultation" with a plain enquiry-form label that describes the actual action, such as "Send an enquiry" or "Ask about this product" — it must not say "free consultation", because it does not go to the booking route. On the non-design routes, replace the offer with the one the customer wants: "Request a repair" on /window-and-door-repairs/ (already used elsewhere on that page), and equivalents for /roofline/, /double-glazing-replacement/, /cat-and-dog-flaps/ and /secondary-glazing/. Leave the header "Free Consultation" and footer "Book a free consultation" exactly as they are — AI.md:65 fixes the header label and both already point at the booking route.
- **Why:** Three names for one action on one screen makes a visitor pause to work out whether they are three different things, and the free-ness — the reassurance the owner ruled must always be present — vanishes from the most prominent button. On the repairs page it is also simply the wrong offer.
- **Affected:** 21 routes with "Start your design consultation", 19 with the H2 "Get pricing or book a design chat.", 2 with the button "Book a design chat". Confirmed on /window-and-door-repairs/, /roofline/, /double-glazing-replacement/, /cat-and-dog-flaps/, /secondary-glazing/.
- **Evidence:** Counted across 712 fetched pages. Verified visually in shots/desktop/patio-doors.png: header carries "Instant Quote" and "Free Consultation", hero carries "Start your design consultation" and "Instant pricing". Rules: STYLE.md CTA section; AI.md "Do not quietly drop the word 'free' from a consultation CTA" and "The header CTA stays `Free Consultation`".
- **Verification:** The counts are exact (21 / 19 / 2 across the 712 pages) and both cited rules are verbatim, but the finding's central premise — 'the same action has three different names' — is factually wrong, and the 'free' half of the argument was explicitly ruled on and rejected. PROGRESS.md:3524, under '## 2026-07-28 - Consultations stated as free sitewide', states: '**`Start your design consultation` and the short `Design consultation` were deliberately left alone.** Both point at `#fenster-enquiry` on the same page rather than the booking route, so they are enquiry-form CTAs, not an offer of a free visit, and adding "free" would have described the wrong thing.' I verified this in the live markup rather than taking the doc's word for it: on patio-doors.html the hero CTA is href="#fenster-enquiry" (an on-page enquiry form) while every 'Free Consultation' and 'Book a free consultation' instance resolves to https://fensterglazing.com/book-a-consultation/. These are two different actions with two different destinations, so AI.md:64 ('do not quietly drop the word free from a consultation CTA') does not apply, and following the recommendation would mislabel an enquiry form as a free home visit. What genuinely survives is the other half, which the same PROGRESS.md line flags as still open: 'Worth noting they are also the invented journey language `STYLE.md` bans, which is a separate fix needing owner sign-off.' STYLE.md:88 does ban 'invented journey language such as `Plan my...`, `Start your journey`', and 'Start your design consultation' is structurally that. The wrong-offer-on-non-design-routes point also holds and is corroborated by PROGRESS.md:1359, which records the identical fault being caught elsewhere ('the hero button said "Start your design consultation" on a page where nothing is designed'). One thing the finding missed: there is a fourth variant, the responsive short label 'Design consultation' (span.fg-hero-cta__short), which is what mobile actually shows. Small scope correction: /double-glazing-replacement/ carries only the H2 'Get pricing or book a design chat.', not a design-consultation button. Dropping impact to Low and confidence to 60; type stays Objective because STYLE.md:88 is a written rule, not a preference.


### G. Design system and consistency

#### [1] The global `h2` rule is a malformed clamp that ships as a fixed 48px

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `src/scss/main.scss:1483` reads `h2 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 3rem, 3.4rem); }`. The middle (preferred) argument is `3rem` — a fixed length, not a viewport unit — so the clamp is degenerate and always resolves to 3rem. The minifier proved this: the shipped CSS at `live/main.css` literally contains `h1,h2,h3{margin:0;line-height:1.08}h1{font-size:clamp(2.1rem,3.6vw,3.6rem)}h2{font-size:3rem}`. The clamp was collapsed to a constant. The author clearly meant `3vw`. Consequence: every H2 not caught by a namespaced override renders at exactly 48px at every viewport, desktop and mobile, and never scales. The block that inherits it is `.fg-links-band .section-heading h2` (the "Useful pages" internal-link band), which has no font-size rule anywhere — I checked every `.section-heading`/`.fg-links-band` rule in the SCSS and only three unrelated overrides exist. So the least important block on the page carries the loudest section heading. On /what-is-a-door-lintel/ all 17 real content H2s render at 31.7px and the link band renders at 48px. On /contact/ real content H2s are 32.4–40.3px and the link band is 48px.
- **Recommendation:** Change `main.scss:1483` to `h2 { font-size: clamp(1.45rem, 2.2vw, 2rem); }` — the value STYLE.md:235 already specifies and which the codebase already uses correctly in 26 places in the shipped CSS (e.g. `.fg-about h2`, `.fg-oq-section-head h2`). Then give `.fg-links-band .section-heading h2` an explicit modest size (suggest `clamp(1.3rem, 1.8vw, 1.65rem)`) so a nav/SEO band never out-ranks page content. Re-run the probe and confirm no route reports an H2 at 48px.
- **Why:** On 26 of 38 audited routes the largest section heading on the page belongs to a footer link farm, not to content. It inverts the reading hierarchy on 68% of the site and is the single loudest typographic error on it. Because the value is fixed it is also unresponsive: the same 48px lands on a 375px phone, where it is 12.8% of viewport width.
- **Affected:** Global `h2` element rule, main.scss:1483. 38 rendered H2s at exactly 48px across 26 of 38 audited routes, including /contact/, /meet-the-team/, /obscured-glass/, /what-is-a-door-lintel/, /casement-windows/, /sliding-sash-windows/, /commercial-glazing/, /book-a-consultation/.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:1483 `font-size: clamp(2rem, 3rem, 3.4rem)`; shipped live/main.css byte 27287 `h2{font-size:3rem}` (clamp collapsed by the minifier, proving degeneracy); probe-desktop.json — 38 H2s at size 48 across 26 routes; grep of all `.section-heading`/`.fg-links-band` blocks shows no font-size for the links band.
- **Verification:** Every load-bearing claim reproduced. generated-page.php:1511-1513 is exactly `return $target_slug === 'home' || isset($generated_pages[$target_slug]) || isset($virtual_page_titles[$target_slug]);` (the cited :1946 is the same statement — my sed of 1935-1990 printed it). $known_locations is at :1512-1529 with 16 entries; diffing against fenster_location_matrix_towns() (generated-pages.php:50, 25 towns) the 12 missing are exactly bletchley, wolverton, stony-stratford, newport-pagnell, woburn-sands, great-linford, shenley-church-end, furzton, oldbrook, monkston, brooklands, whitehouse. I rebuilt the slug index the way fenster_generated_pages_index() does (data/pages.json is a LIST of records keyed by page['slug'], not a slug-keyed map — a naive isset() on the raw JSON returns 0/525 and would have faked this result) and got 21 products x 25 towns = 525, of which 106 have a record and 419 do not. $add_related_route at :1991-1995 gates on $route_exists, so those 419 are silently dropped. The else branch that links other towns is at :2051-2055 as described. fenster_slug_matches_location_matrix() exists at inc/generated-pages.php:561, is a pure string check, and its only caller is fenster_gsc_static_seo_overrides() at :581. Live: /casement-windows-bletchley/ band has ZERO Bletchley links and exactly 10 casement-windows-<other town> links (northampton, letchworth, stevenage, toddington, aylesbury, dunstable, flitwick, ampthill, hitchin, luton); /casement-windows-luton/ has exactly 2 Luton-local links (double-glazing-luton, flush-casement-windows-luton) against 21 live Luton product routes in urls.txt. No doc rules this: AI.md:628 and PROGRESS.md:270 only record the $route_title label fix from the 2026-08-12 rename, not the existence gate. Only nit, immaterial: my band extraction counted 24 and 19 total links vs the finding's 26 and 20 (different segment boundary); the local/other-town counts match exactly.

Loading case-studies-data.php under PHP 8.2 with stubs: 13 residential studies, 11 claimed routes, and the first three residential studies are secondary-glazing-winslow, upvc-casement-windows-leighton-buzzard, aluminium-bifold-doors-whitehouse-milton-keynes — precisely the trio the live strips render. WHERE IT IS WRONG: the finding lists 10 ungated routes including /double-glazing/, but that route 301-redirects to /double-glazing-ampthill/ (curl -w '%{http_code}' returns 301, body is 0 bytes) and can never render the strip.
