#### [16] The global `h2` rule is a malformed clamp that ships as a fixed, non-responsive 48px on 26 desktop and 25 mobile routes

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `src/scss/main.scss:1483` reads `h2 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 3rem, 3.4rem); }`. The middle (preferred) argument is `3rem` — a fixed length, not a viewport unit — so the clamp is degenerate and always resolves to 3rem. The minifier proves it: the shipped CSS reads `h1{font-size:clamp(2.1rem,3.6vw,3.6rem)}h2{font-size:3rem}`, the clamp collapsed to a constant. The author meant `3vw`. Consequence: every H2 not caught by a namespaced override renders at exactly 48px at every viewport and never scales. That is 38 headings across 26 of 38 routes at 1440px, and 37 headings across 25 routes at 390px — the same 48px on a phone, where it is 12.3% of viewport width. On /contact/ mobile the affected heading ("Products, services and project examples") wraps to four lines and fills most of the viewport. Two distinct blocks inherit it: the `.fg-links-band .section-heading h2` internal-link band, which has no font-size rule anywhere in the SCSS (I checked all 22 `fg-links-band` blocks), and 12 ordinary content H2s on product routes ("Finish the design with your colours, glass and hardware.", "Privacy where the room needs it.", "Why have us repair it"). Against page content it reads oversized rather than inverted: on /what-is-a-door-lintel/ all 17 real content H2s are 31.7px and this one is 48px; on /contact/ content H2s are 32.4-40.3px and this one is 48px. It is the largest H2 on 8 of the 38 routes, not 26.
- **Recommendation:** Change main.scss:1483 to `h2 { font-size: clamp(1.45rem, 2.2vw, 2rem); }` — the value STYLE.md:231 and AI.md:125 already specify and which the shipped CSS already uses correctly in many namespaced rules. Then walk the 12 content H2s that were relying on the accidental 48px (the `Finish the design with your colours…` band on the seven product routes, `Privacy where the room needs it.`, `Choose your glass and hardware.`, `Why have us repair it`, `All obscured glass options at a glance.`, `Compare the products that affect your budget.`) and give each an explicit size, or they will drop from 48px to 32px in one step. Give `.fg-links-band .section-heading h2` an explicit modest size of its own (`clamp(1.3rem, 1.8vw, 1.65rem)`). Re-run the probe at both 1440 and 390 and confirm no route reports an H2 at 48px.
- **Why:** It is the last thing a visitor sees before submitting an enquiry, and roughly a third of that section's area is empty. Reasonable designers could argue the void is deliberate breathing room, which is why I am marking this creative rather than a defect.
- **Affected:** `.fg-enquiry__grid` on the 14 product routes carrying the shared enquiry section.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:18037 `align-items: stretch`; screenshot /private/tmp/.../shots/desktop/upvc-doors.png cropped at y=9250 showing the empty lower half of the copy panel; STYLE.md:139.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and the mechanism is exactly as described, but the stated consequence is wrong, and the strongest evidence for the finding is one it barely mentions.

CONFIRMED EXACTLY: main.scss:1483 is `font-size: clamp(2rem, 3rem, 3.4rem);`. The middle argument is a fixed length, so the clamp is degenerate. The minifier proves it — live/main.css contains `h1,h2,h3{margin:0;line-height:1.08}h1{font-size:clamp(2.1rem,3.6vw,3.6rem)}h2{font-size:3rem}`, the clamp collapsed to a constant. I grepped every `fg-links-band` rule in main.scss (22 blocks) and in the shipped CSS (21 blocks) — padding, background and colour only, no font-size anywhere, so the band's heading does fall through to the global 48px. The two worked examples are precise: /what-is-a-door-lintel/ has 17 content H2s at 31.7px and the band at 48px; /contact/ has content H2s at 32.4-40.3px and the band at 48px. Probe-desktop: 38 H2s at exactly 48px across 26 of 38 routes.

WRONG: the 'why' claims that "on 26 of 38 audited routes the largest section heading on the page belongs to a footer link farm" and that this "inverts the reading hierarchy on 68% of the site." I computed max H2 size per route. The 48px H2 is the largest H2 on only 8 of 38 routes (/book-a-consultation/, /contact/, /double-glazing-milton-keynes/, /commercial-glazing/, /handle-options/, /obscured-glass/, /casement-windows-bletchley/, /what-is-a-door-lintel/, /composite-door-prices/), and on 13 routes the 57.6px `.fg-enquiry h2` from finding 17 is larger. On the other 18 routes the 48px heading is simply mid-scale.

ALSO WRONG: the affected block is not only the links band. Of the 38 instances, 12 are ordinary content H2s inheriting the same global rule — "Privacy where the room needs it." (/casement-windows/, /upvc-doors/), "Finish the design with your colours, glass and hardware." (7 product routes), "Choose your glass and hardware.", "Why have us repair it", "All obscured glass options at a glance.", "Compare the products that affect your budget." So the fix cannot be scoped to the links band alone.

STRONGEST EVIDENCE, UNDERPLAYED: because the value is a constant, probe-mobile at innerWidth 390 reports 37 H2s at exactly 48px across 25 routes. I cropped shots/mobile/contact.png at y=17750 and the band heading "Products, services and project examples" renders at 48px over four wrapped lines, dominating the viewport. That is the objective, visible defect and it stands on its own.

Citation slip: the `clamp(1.45rem, 2.2vw, 2rem)` value is STYLE.md:231 (and AI.md:125), not STYLE.md:235.

#### [32] Hero eyebrow fails WCAG AA on all 15 photo-hero routes at desktop — the fix exists but is scoped mobile-only

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.eyebrow` is coloured `var(--color-accent)` = #2eac66 (src/scss/main.scss:1449-1455), 0.78rem (12.5px) uppercase at weight 800 — below the WCAG large-text threshold, so it needs 4.5:1. On the 15 `fg-hero--compact` routes it sits on a photographic hero whose overlay (`.fg-hero__shade`, main.scss:3171-3174) is a FIXED-opacity gradient, so the resulting contrast is whatever the underlying photo happens to give. Measured from the desktop fold screenshots the token lands between 1.39:1 and 4.44:1 — every one of the fifteen fails, and worst-case local contrast under individual glyphs runs as low as 1.26:1. The codebase ALREADY contains the fix — `.fg-hero--compact .fg-hero__heading .eyebrow { color: #68d798 }` at main.scss:23267-23270 — but it is inside `@media (max-width: 860px)` (block opens at :22586), so desktop never gets it; verified against the compiled live/main.css, where it is the only override of that selector. Light-panel heroes are no better: /composite-doors/ measures 2.24:1. Note the failing text reads 'Fenster Glazing' on all 14 generic routes, so what is illegible is the brand label, not the product-and-location line STYLE.md:329 describes (only /roof-lanterns/ and /composite-doors/ carry that).
- **Recommendation:** Set the compact-hero eyebrow to `#ffffff` at every width and let the accent green live only on light panels. #68d798 is not enough: moved out of the media query it would still only reach 2.26:1 on aluminium-bifold-doors, 2.61:1 on french-doors and 2.68:1 on casement-windows. White reaches 4.04:1 on the worst route (aluminium-bifold-doors) and 4.65-4.79:1 on the next two, so pair it with strengthening the left stop of `.fg-hero__shade` from `rgba(0,45,58,0.54)` to about `rgba(0,45,58,0.78)` scoped to `.fg-hero--compact`, which lifts all fifteen clear of 4.5:1. Re-measure per route after the change: the photos differ and one global value cannot be assumed to fix all fifteen. /composite-doors/ needs a separate fix — on its light #cae9d9 panel the accent green measures 2.24:1 and should go to `--color-accent-dark` (#20824c) or darker.
- **Why:** Not a user-visible defect today, but it is the exact shape of drift the comment at :3259 was written to prevent: two hand-kept strings that must agree. Two of fourteen routes have already collapsed them, which is how the original mismatch happened in the other direction.
- **Affected:** /double-glazing-replacement/ and /window-and-door-repairs/.
- **Evidence:** scratchpad/live/double-glazing-replacement.html: `<span class="fg-hero-cta__full">Send us the sizes</span> <span class="fg-hero-cta__short">Send us the sizes</span>`. Same shape in window-and-door-repairs.html with "Request a repair". Source: generated-page.php:3258-3267. CSS: main.scss:3428-3430 and 23299-23305.
- **Verification:** The mechanism is confirmed in full and the conclusion is right, but every per-route number is wrong and the finding is too generous — by my measurement not one route passes. Mechanism: src/scss/main.scss:1449-1455 sets `.eyebrow { color: var(--color-accent); font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 800 }`, :47 sets `--color-accent: #2eac66`, :3171-3174 is the fixed-opacity `.fg-hero__shade`, and the `#68d798` override at :23267-23270 is inside the `@media (max-width: 860px)` block that opens at :22586 — I verified this against the COMPILED live/main.css by brace-walking backwards from the `#68d798` declaration to its enclosing at-rule, which returns `@media(max-width: 860px)`. It is the only override of that selector anywhere in the file. At 12.5px/800 weight the WCAG threshold is 4.5:1 (not large text). My own measurement, isolating the eyebrow scanline in each desktop fold screenshot and taking the median background between and around the glyphs, gives: aluminium-bifold-doors 1.39, french-doors 1.60, casement-windows 1.64, integral-blinds 1.97, tilt-turn-windows 2.04, aluminium-doors 2.15, heritage-windows 2.28, window-and-door-repairs 2.28, upvc-doors 2.73, secondary-glazing 3.82, sliding-sash-windows 4.00, patio-doors 4.28, double-glazing-replacement 4.33, flush-casement-windows 4.39, roof-lanterns 4.44, plus composite-doors 2.24 on its light panel. Zero of fifteen pass — patio-doors does not scrape a pass at 4.51, it fails at 4.28. Worst-case per-column contrast is worse still: 1.26 (casement), 1.35 (french-doors), 1.68 (flush-casement), 1.83 (roof-lanterns), 2.07 (double-glazing-replacement), 2.19 (patio-doors). Separately, the 'why' is wrong on one point: on all 14 generic compact routes the eyebrow text is 'Fenster Glazing', not the product-and-location line — only /roof-lanterns/ ('Roof lanterns and roof lights in Milton Keynes') and /composite-doors/ ('Composite doors in Milton Keynes') carry the STYLE.md:329 pattern. So this is a plain WCAG 1.4.3 failure on a brand label, not a loss of an SEO/orientation line. No doc rules low-contrast eyebrows acceptable; STYLE.md:45 and :49 both treat contrast failures as defects to fix.

#### [17] Hero eyebrow fails contrast on 14 of 15 photo-hero routes at desktop — the fix exists but is scoped mobile-only

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `.eyebrow` is coloured `var(--color-accent)` = #2eac66 (src/scss/main.scss:1451), 0.78rem (12.5px) uppercase. On the 15 `fg-hero--compact` routes it sits on a photographic hero whose overlay (`.fg-hero__shade`, main.scss:3171-3174) is a FIXED-opacity gradient, so the resulting contrast is whatever the underlying photo happens to give. Measured from the desktop fold screenshots, the same token lands anywhere from 1.56:1 to 4.51:1. Only `/patio-doors/` scrapes a pass, and only because its photo is dark. Crucially the codebase ALREADY contains the fix — `.fg-hero--compact .fg-hero__heading .eyebrow { color: #68d798 }` at main.scss:23267-23270 — but it is inside `@media (max-width: 860px)`, so desktop never gets it. Light-panel heroes are no better: `/composite-doors/` measures 2.32:1 (#33AE69 on #C5E7D5).
- **Recommendation:** Two changes. (1) Move the `#68d798` eyebrow colour out of the `@media (max-width:860px)` block so `.fg-hero--compact .fg-hero__heading .eyebrow` gets it at every width. (2) #68d798 alone is not enough on the bright photos (it only reaches 2.54:1 on `/tilt-turn-windows/`), so also strengthen the left stop of `.fg-hero__shade` from `rgba(0,45,58,0.54)` to `rgba(0,45,58,0.78)` on `.fg-hero--compact`, or set the compact-hero eyebrow to `#ffffff` (4.54:1 on the worst route) and let the accent green live only on light panels. Verify per-route after the change: the photos differ, so one global value cannot be assumed to fix all 15.
- **Why:** The eyebrow is the only element carrying the product-and-location line that STYLE.md:259 says should do that job. On 14 routes it is effectively invisible, so the SEO/orientation line the design contract relies on is not read by anyone, and the site fails WCAG 2.1 AA 1.4.3 on its highest-traffic template.
- **Affected:** 15 `fg-hero--compact` routes (14 failing): tilt-turn-windows 1.56:1, aluminium-bifold-doors 1.83:1, heritage-windows 2.22:1, secondary-glazing 2.49:1, aluminium-doors 2.52:1, double-glazing-replacement 2.57:1, upvc-doors 2.60:1, casement-windows 2.72:1, french-doors 2.75:1, window-and-door-repairs 2.76:1, sliding-sash-windows 3.07:1, integral-blinds 3.09:1, flush-casement-windows 3.89:1, roof-lanterns 4.45:1. Passing: patio-doors 4.51:1. Also composite-doors (light panel) 2.32:1.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:1451 (`color: var(--color-accent)`), :47 (`--color-accent: #2eac66`), :3171-3174 (fixed shade), :23267-23270 (mobile-only #68d798 override, inside the `@media (max-width:860px)` block opening at :22586). Ratios computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula from pixels sampled out of scratchpad/shots/desktop/<route>--fold.png at the eyebrow band (crop 300x10+130+208). Spot-verified on casement-windows: text #34A468 over backgrounds #4C6563/#647E84/#6B8183 = 1.99:1/1.37:1/1.31:1.
- **Verification:** Every load-bearing claim reproduced, and the project docs support it rather than excusing it.

main.scss:18031-18034 is exactly `.fg-enquiry h2 { max-width: 11ch; font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 4.4vw, var(--fg-font-size-max)); }`. The duplicate at :3772-3776 is exactly `.fg-intent h2, .fg-cta-strip h2, .fg-enquiry h2 { font-size: clamp(2.2rem, 4vw, var(--fg-font-size-max)); }`, and the shipped CSS contains both, later wins. `--fg-font-size-max: 3.6rem` confirmed at main.scss:73 and in the shipped `:root`. The 4.4vw crossover is 57.6/0.044 = 1309.09px, so "wider than ~1309px" is right.

Probe-desktop: 21 H2s at exactly 57.6px, and the 14 routes where the enquiry heading is 1.20x the H1 (57.6 vs 48.2) are exactly the 14 listed. The 15th route carrying the component, /aluminium-windows/, has a 57.6px H1 so its ratio is 1.00 — correctly excluded.

STYLE.md:236 is verbatim "Enquiry/form section headings are supporting content headings, not page heroes. Keep them moderate site-wide." STYLE.md:46 does warn against "oversized form headings". I also found stronger support the finding missed: PROGRESS.md:4734 (2026-07-01) records "Reduced shared enquiry/form section heading sizing so form intro headings no longer render at hero scale" — so this is not merely a rule the code ignores, it is a regression against a change the owner already directed once.

I cropped shots/desktop/upvc-doors.png at y=9100 and looked at it: "Tell us about your project." is set at hero scale over two lines, and "Tell us the basics." inside the actual form is visibly a fraction of it.

One correction that does not change the verdict: "Tell us the basics." is not ~20px. It is `.fg-enquiry-form__body-head strong { font-size: clamp(1.2rem,2vw,1.55rem) }`, which pins at 1.55rem = 24.8px at 1440. The real ratio is 57.6 : 24.8 = 2.3x, not 2.9x. The point stands.

#### [21] Four structurally different enquiry forms hide behind one shared component, split across routes on no discernible rule

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php` renders four different interaction models. (1) Default: a `Homeowner / Business` audience gate with `Continue` buttons, then fieldsets with legends (`Your contact details`), textarea labelled `Tell us about your project` — 19 Tier-1 routes. (2) Default with the gate suppressed via `lock_project_type` but not `compact` — roof-lanterns, heritage-aluminium-doors, flat-rooflights. (3) `compact`: a flat grid, no gate, no fieldsets, no legends, textarea labelled `Project details` — casement-windows, sliding-sash-windows, composite-doors, the whole town matrix (location-service.php:1387,1472), all articles (generated-article.php:256) and the accreditation pages. (4) Consultation: weekday/time first — book-a-consultation. The split is incoherent: `/casement-windows/` gets the compact form while its sibling `/flush-casement-windows/` gets the full gated one; `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/`, one of the highest-value money pages, gets compact and therefore cannot accept a business enquiry at all because `project_type` is locked.
- **Recommendation:** Pick one residential enquiry form and use it on every residential route. If the audience gate earns its place, it belongs on the money pages too — `/casement-windows/` and `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` are the ones most likely to receive a commercial enquiry. If it does not, remove it from the 19 routes rather than keeping two funnels. At minimum unify the textarea label: `Project details` and `Tell us about your project` are the same field. Also add the `fieldset`/`legend` grouping to the compact variant so the form's programmatic structure does not change between routes.
- **Why:** This is the conversion event. Two different interaction models for it means split analytics, two lots of validation behaviour to keep correct, and an inconsistent structure for assistive technology. The locked project type on compact routes silently mislabels business leads on the two pages most likely to attract them.
- **Affected:** 30 form-bearing Tier-1 routes across 4 variants; at template level the compact variant also covers the ~238-URL town matrix and all article routes.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:139 (compact branch, label `Project details` at :159), :192-213 (audience gate, suppressed by `lock_project_type`), :227/:248/:275 (`fieldset.fg-enquiry-form__step` with legends, default branch only). Callers: generated-page.php:5354-5355, casement-windows-v2.php:725-726, location-service.php:1387,1472, generated-article.php:256, roof-lanterns.php:323. Label extraction across scratchpad/live/*.html shows the `Tell us about your project` / `Project details` split 20 vs 8.
- **Verification:** This is the most precisely measured finding in the batch. I re-derived every number independently and the colour maths is right to the second decimal.

Base definition confirmed at main.scss:1449-1456, seven lines, exactly as described: `margin: 0 0 0.75rem; color: var(--color-accent); font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase;`. `.home-hero .eyebrow { color: #ffb1a9; }` is the very next rule at :1458-1460, so the finding's own carve-out is right.

My recount of rule blocks whose selector contains `eyebrow`, after stripping comments: 202 (finding: 205 — a 1.5% difference from selector-splitting, immaterial). Font-size declarations: 84, distinct 46 — EXACT. Colour declarations: 161, distinct 28 — EXACT. Letter-spacings: 7 distinct, and the set matches exactly (0, .08em, .09em, .095em, .12em, .13em, .16em). The eight mints are exactly the eight listed: #68d798, #70da98, #72d99c, #72dc98, #7fd3a4, #7fe0aa, #7fe0ab, #8fe0b1.

I implemented CIELAB and ran the pairwise matrix: max pairwise deltaE 14.35 (finding: 14.3), min 0.53 (finding: 0.5), #7fe0aa vs #7fe0ab = 0.53 (finding: 0.5), #70da98 vs #72dc98 = 1.19 (finding: 1.2). All four match. So the substantive point holds: there are genuinely two different mints in circulation at deltaE 14, which is well above the visible threshold, plus several pairs that are pure entropy.

One thing the finding missed that strengthens it: among the 28 colour values are `var(--color-text)` and `var(--color-ink-soft, #5b6770)`, and neither `--color-text` nor `--color-ink-soft` is defined anywhere in the shipped CSS (grep for the definition returns 0 for both). `--color-ink-soft` has a literal fallback so it renders; `var(--color-text)` has none, so that declaration is invalid at computed-value time and the eyebrow silently inherits instead. That is a live bug sitting inside the same 202 blocks and should be fixed in the same pass.

#### [4] The shadow system is two tokens and 212 hand-typed values; only 7.8% of shadows use a token

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `:root` defines exactly two shadow tokens (`--shadow-soft: 0 18px 48px rgba(0,45,58,.14)` and `--shadow-strong`). The compiled CSS contains 334 `box-shadow` declarations with 212 distinct values; only 26 of those declarations (7.8%) reference a token. Within a single visual family — a soft steel drop shadow on a white card, `0 Ypx Bpx rgba(0,45,58,.0X)` — there are 117 distinct values. The clustering is pure noise: `0 18px 48px`, `0 18px 46px`, `0 18px 44px`, `0 18px 42px`, `0 18px 40px`, `0 16px 44px`, `0 16px 42px`, `0 16px 40px`, `0 14px 38px`, `0 14px 36px`, `0 14px 34px` all appear at the same 0.08 alpha. The token's own geometry `0 18px 48px` is retyped by hand at four further alphas (.08, .09, .10, .12), so editing `--shadow-soft` would move some cards and not others.
- **Recommendation:** Define a four-step elevation scale in `:root` — `--shadow-1: 0 8px 22px rgba(0,45,58,.06)`, `--shadow-2: 0 14px 34px rgba(0,45,58,.08)`, `--shadow-3: 0 18px 48px rgba(0,45,58,.12)`, `--shadow-4: 0 30px 90px rgba(0,45,58,.28)` — and replace the 117-value soft-card family with `--shadow-2`/`--shadow-3`. Nobody can distinguish a 34px blur from a 38px blur at 8% alpha; this is a mechanical substitution, not a redesign.
- **Why:** Elevation is the main cue separating a card from the page canvas. With 212 values there is no consistent elevation language, cards at the same conceptual depth sit at visibly different weights across routes, and the two tokens that exist cannot be used to retune the site because 92% of shadows ignore them.
- **Affected:** Site-wide. 334 box-shadow declarations across all 38 routes; 117 distinct values in the primary card family alone.
- **Evidence:** live/main.css — 334 `box-shadow:` declarations, 212 distinct values, 26 matching `box-shadow: var(--shadow`; 117 distinct values matching `0 \d+px \d+px rgba(0,45,58,.0X)`; tokens at src/scss/main.scss:68-69.
- **Verification:** Reproduced on PHP 8.2.32. data/pages.json is exactly 4,514,266 bytes with 274 records. Timing: file_get_contents 3.32ms, json_decode 11.95ms (finding said 2.12/13.86 — same ~16ms total, within run-to-run noise). memory_get_peak_usage(true) = 18.31MB, matching the claim to the decimal. Field weights: sections 1.92MB, seo 0.71MB, images 0.53MB, links 0.30MB — all match. fenster_generated_pages_payload() is at inc/generated-pages.php:12-30 and does exactly `json_decode((string) file_get_contents($file), true)` with a per-request static; there is no transient, no wp_cache_get, no per-slug file. The 'every uncached front-end request' claim holds: inc/generated-pages.php:1842 registers fenster_maybe_render_generated_page on template_redirect at priority 0, and the resolver calls fenster_generated_pages_index() at :1506. On the dead records, my first sweep over-caught 38/286KB because I applied the -milton-keynes and -designer suffix rules without their guards; re-running with the actual guards from fenster_redirect_target() (:1676) — the -milton-keynes branch only fires when the prefix is in fenster_location_matrix_products(), the -designer branch only when the base is in the index or the matrix — gives exactly 32 records / 231,553 bytes (226.1KB). Composition matches the finding's list precisely: 12 *-designer slugs, door-designer, enquire-now, instant-pricing, dunstable-casement-windows, bow-and-bay-windows-northampton, tilt-and-turn-windows-northampton, commercial-glazing-london-2, healthcare_safeguarding_in_construction, nick-test-baboon, our-new-website and the retired case-study routes. Two trivial imprecisions: 226KB not 222KB, and the retired case-study routes number 10 not 9. The 108 town-suffixed records claim is exact — 108 records, 1.89MB.

#### [18] Latent breach of the 3.6rem hard ceiling on /sliding-sash-windows/, invisible at the 1440px QA viewport and live on every wider desktop

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `main.scss:31609`, inside `@media (min-width: 861px)` (opened at :31528), sets `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-sash-gallery__head h2 { font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 4vw, 4rem); }`. The upper bound is 4rem = 64px, 11% above the `--fg-font-size-max` ceiling of 3.6rem/57.6px. It is invisible to QA because at the 1440px audit viewport the preferred value 4vw resolves to exactly 57.6px — identical to the ceiling — so the page reports as compliant. The breach begins at 1441px, not 1600px: between 1440 and 1600 the heading tracks 4vw from 57.6px up to 64px, and only saturates at the 4rem cap above 1600px. That means it is already over the ceiling on 1512px and 1536px laptops as well as 1920px desktops. STYLE.md:44 claims "Existing oversized clamps have been capped at this token" and PROGRESS.md:4282 claims the source "contains no remaining font-size maximum above 3.6rem"; both are false. I independently scanned all 42,407 SCSS lines: exactly two font-size clamps exceed the ceiling — this one and `.fg-cas-num` at :37685 (70.4px).
- **Recommendation:** Change main.scss:31609 to use the token as the upper bound: `font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 3vw, var(--fg-font-size-max));` — dropping the preferred value from 4vw to 3vw as well, otherwise the heading still sits at the ceiling on every desktop and the fix only removes the last 6.4px. Given STYLE.md:231, `clamp(2rem, 3vw, 2.5rem)` is the better target, 2.5rem being the documented art-directed H2 maximum. Separately, fix the QA method: the ceiling check must run at a viewport wider than 1440px (1920 is the obvious choice) or it will keep passing clamps whose vw term happens to equal the ceiling at the audit width.
- **Why:** AI.md:43 names `/windows-milton-keynes/`, `/doors-milton-keynes/` and `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` as the pages that already have Search Console impressions and should be prioritised for CTR work. FAQ rich results are the cheapest CTR gain available on exactly those pages, and the markup is already being generated correctly 20 routes away. The town matrix is roughly a third of the sitemap getting none of it.
- **Affected:** 5 routes in the Tier-1 sample, but at template level: at least 238 of the 712 sitemap URLs match a product-town pattern and are served by location-service.php, plus the 3 product hubs and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/.
- **Evidence:** probe-desktop.json `schemaTypes`: 19 routes have `BreadcrumbList,FAQPage,HomeAndConstructionBusiness`; 18 have `BreadcrumbList,HomeAndConstructionBusiness`. Grep of scratchpad/live/*.html for FAQ section classes + question count vs presence of the string `FAQPage`. Live curl of /composite-doors-wolverton/ returns `class="fg-location-faq"` and `grep -c FAQPage` = 0. urls.txt: 238 URLs match the product-town pattern.
- **Verification:** The breach is real and the 'invisible at the QA viewport' insight is the best part of the finding — but the breach threshold is stated 160px too high, which understates the exposure.

CONFIRMED: main.scss:31609 is `font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 4vw, 4rem);` on `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-sash-gallery__head h2`, and the enclosing at-rule is `@media (min-width: 861px)` opened at :31528 (the two preceding @media blocks close at :31427 and :31506). 4rem = 64px against a 57.6px ceiling, an 11% breach. The shipped CSS carries it unaltered: `sash-gallery__head h2{max-width:13ch;margin:0;color:#fff;font-size:clamp(2.4rem,4vw,4rem);line-height:.98}`, with the mobile variant `clamp(1.55rem,7vw,2rem)` separately fine. I re-ran the static scan myself over all 42,407 SCSS lines and got exactly two font-size clamps with an upper bound above 57.6px: :31609 (64px) and :37685 `.fg-cas-num` (70.4px, the casement chapter number). Zero fixed font-sizes above the ceiling. So that claim is independently reproduced. Probe-desktop confirms "Roseview sash windows in real homes." renders at exactly 57.6px at innerWidth 1440. STYLE.md:44 does say "Existing oversized clamps have been capped at this token," and PROGRESS.md:4282 goes further — "confirmed the source contains no remaining font-size maximum above 3.6rem" — which is demonstrably false. No sash-specific ruling exists: nothing in STYLE.md, PROGRESS.md, SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md or AI.md mentions this heading or a 4rem exception.

WRONG: "It only breaches above 1600px viewport width." The preferred value is 4vw, so the rendered size is 4vw for any viewport between 1440px and 1600px — that is 57.6px to 64px, already over the ceiling from 1441px upward. 1600px is where it *saturates* at the 4rem cap, not where the breach begins. Correcting this widens exposure from '1920px desktops' to essentially every desktop wider than the QA viewport, including 1512px and 1536px laptops.

#### [6] `.eyebrow` — the smallest component in the system — is redefined 205 times with 46 font sizes and 28 colours

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `.eyebrow` is a one-job component: a small uppercase label above a heading. Its base definition at `main.scss:1449` is seven lines (`0.78rem`, weight 800, `letter-spacing: 0.08em`, uppercase, `color: var(--color-accent)`). It is then overridden across 205 rule blocks containing 84 font-size declarations with 46 distinct values, 161 colour declarations with 28 distinct values, and 7 distinct letter-spacings (0, .08em, .09em, .095em, .12em, .13em, .16em). The colours include eight mint greens used on dark panels: #68d798, #70da98, #72d99c, #72dc98, #7fd3a4, #7fe0aa, #7fe0ab, #8fe0b1. Several pairs are literally imperceptible (#7fe0aa vs #7fe0ab at deltaE 0.5; #70da98 vs #72dc98 at 1.2), which is pure entropy, but the overall spread is deltaE 14.3 — meaning there genuinely are two different mints in circulation, so the eyebrow colour visibly drifts between pages.
- **Recommendation:** Add two tokens — `--fg-eyebrow-on-light: var(--color-accent)` and `--fg-eyebrow-on-dark: #72dc98` (pick one mint; the four-value cluster around it is invisible anyway) — and reduce the 205 override blocks to those two plus a single size and letter-spacing. Keep only genuine exceptions such as `.home-hero .eyebrow` (#ffb1a9), which is a deliberate contrast choice.
- **Why:** The eyebrow appears above almost every section on the site, so its inconsistency is seen more often than any other component's. Eight greens for one label is the clearest single indicator that the system is maintained per-page rather than per-component.
- **Affected:** Site-wide; `.eyebrow` renders on effectively every route. 205 rule blocks in main.scss.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:1449 base definition; 205 rule blocks whose selector contains `eyebrow`; 84 font-size decls / 46 distinct; 161 colour decls / 28 distinct; 7 letter-spacings; CIELAB deltaE matrix across the eight mints, max pairwise 14.3, min 0.5.
- **Verification:** Reproduced, and the finding is if anything conservative. Extracting every [data-*] attribute selector from src/js/main.js gives exactly 213 distinct selectors — the finding's number to the unit. My orphan pass (not in any theme .php, not in any of the 38 live pages) returned 38 candidates, five more than the finding's 33. Checking why, the author was right to exclude the extras: data-legend-typing is created at runtime by src/js/main.js:599 `indicator.dataset.legendTyping = ''`, so it is a false positive that a naive grep produces and the finding correctly does not list. 33 is therefore a defensible floor, not an overstatement. The traveller is dead by construction as described: inc/assets.php:177-180 `function fenster_product_scroll_videos(): array { return []; }` under a docblock at :163-175 reading verbatim '**This map is empty and the traveller therefore renders nowhere.**' and 'If it is still empty next time someone reads this, it is worth deleting properly' and 'keep it even if the traveller does go' about bifold-video.webm — so the finding's recommendation is literally what the code asks for. $product_scroll_video_src is assigned at generated-page.php:437 from fenster_product_scroll_video_for_slug($slug), and the two markup gates are at :3309 (data-fg-product-video-start) and :4056 (data-fg-product-video-final) exactly as cited. In src/js/main.js, scrollVideoBlocks is declared at :4810 and its forEach block at :4994; the traveller controller `document.querySelectorAll('[data-fg-product-video-final]')` is at :5187. fenster_preload_product_scroll_video is hooked to wp_head at inc/assets.php:336. Spot-check on integral blinds: /integral-blinds/ is among the 38 live pages and emits zero data-fg-integral-blinds-* attributes, and no template-parts file emits them either, so those three are genuine orphans and not a fetch artefact. One imprecision in the evidence string only: it claims all four markers are present in assets/css/main.css and the live main.css, but only fg-product-traveller-float is in the CSS — the three data-* attributes are JS-only. Immaterial to the finding.

#### [22] 25 of 40 routes give the same in-page anchor between two and five different CTA labels

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `#fenster-enquiry` is the single enquiry destination on product pages, and it is labelled ten different ways site-wide: `Start your project`, `Start your enquiry`, `Start your design consultation`, `Start a product enquiry`, `Ask about this product`, `Send us the sizes`, `Request a repair`, `Send us a style name`, `Ask about handles`, `Ask about glass options`. Worse, the labels collide within a single page: `/aluminium-bifold-doors/` uses five distinct labels for `#fenster-enquiry` on one page; `/french-doors/`, `/integral-blinds/` and `/patio-doors/` use four. The same happens for pricing: `/casement-windows/` labels `#fenster-product-quote` both `Instant pricing` and `Get an instant price`; `/home/` and `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` label `/online-quote/` both `Get an instant price` and `Get an instant quote`; both price guides label `#fenster-instant-pricing` both `Price your own job` and `Try it on your job`.
- **Recommendation:** Define one label per destination and centralise it. Suggested: `#fenster-enquiry` → `Start your enquiry` everywhere except the three routes with a genuinely different action (repairs → `Request a repair`, replacement → `Send us the sizes`, sash style → `Send us a style name`); `/online-quote/` and `#fenster-product-quote` → `Get an instant price` everywhere, retiring `Get an instant quote`, `Instant pricing`, `Price one yourself`, `Try it on your job` and `Price your own job`. Put the strings in one place in `inc/site-data.php` so a route cannot invent a new one.
- **Why:** STYLE.md:264 says buttons state the next action; ten strings for one action means the visitor cannot learn the site's vocabulary, and any click tracking keyed on label text fragments a single conversion into five buckets, which makes the funnel unmeasurable on exactly the pages that matter.
- **Affected:** 25 of 40 Tier-1 routes carry at least one destination with conflicting labels. Worst: aluminium-bifold-doors (5 labels for #fenster-enquiry), french-doors / integral-blinds / patio-doors (4 each), double-glazing-milton-keynes (3 for #fenster-mk-enquiry plus 2 more collisions).
- **Evidence:** Extracted every `<a class="button…" href=…>` inside `<main>` across scratchpad/live/*.html and grouped by href. Site-wide, `#fenster-enquiry` resolves to 12 distinct label strings; `https://fensterglazing.com/online-quote/` to 2 (`Get an instant price` on 12 routes, `Get an instant quote` on 5); `#fenster-product-quote` to 5.
- **Verification:** Every headline number reproduces almost exactly against the shipped stylesheet. main.css: 1,176 font-size declarations, 349 distinct values, 71 distinct static rem values, 271 distinct clamp() font-size values, 1,109 clamp() uses drawing on 666 distinct expressions — all four match to the digit. The .9/.91/.92/.93/.94/.95/.96/.97/.98 run exists verbatim (9 values spanning 0.08rem = 1.28px). Per-route histogram lengths match exactly: min 13 on /case-studies/, max 43 on /aluminium-windows/ AND /aluminium-bifold-doors/. :root at main.scss:41-79 confirmed to hold no type-scale token, only --fg-font-size-max (a ceiling) and --fg-tag-size; no owner ruling in STYLE.md or AI.md sanctions the absence of a scale. Two trivial drifts, both in the finding's own favour of understating: adjacent static pairs <=0.03rem is 49 not 46 (45 if the threshold is strict <0.03), and distinct rendered H2 sizes across the 38 routes is 32 not 30 (16, 17.3, 21.6, 24, 24.5, 25.9, 26.4, 28, 28.1, 28.8, 31.2, ... 57.6). Neither changes the finding. Correctly typed Objective: this is a measurable consistency defect, not a preference — no individual size is being judged.

#### [23] The `.button` component renders at seven different heights on desktop, and one 42px rule puts three /3d-visualiser/ controls at 43px — including the mobile primary action

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.button` sets `min-height: 46px; padding: 0.75rem 1.05rem; border-radius: 6px` (main.scss:1501). Thirteen further rules override `min-height` with eight distinct values. Resolving media-query scope by brace-tracking, the desktop-active set is 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, 52 and 54px — seven heights for one component. The primary submit is the worst case: `.fg-enquiry-form__footer .button` is 54px, `.fg-roof-lantern-form/.fg-heritage-door-form … .button` is 56px at top level but 48px from `@media (min-width: 700px)`, and `.fg-location-hero__form … .button` is 44px, so the same submit action is 44px, 48px or 54px depending on route. Label font-size varies across seven rules from 0.68rem to 0.94rem (a 1.2rem eighth value exists but is on `.fg-enquiry-form__footer .button i`, an icon). One rule breaches the project's own 44px tap-target line (STYLE.md:280, which sits under '## Forms'): `.fg-quote-hero__embed-actions .button` at `min-height: 42px; padding: 0.6rem 0.8rem` (main.scss:21524). It governs three controls, all inside `.fg-quote-hero__embed-actions` on /3d-visualiser/: 'Expand view' and 'Open in new tab' at 43px on desktop, and — the one that actually matters — 'Open quote tool' at 43px on mobile, which is the page's primary action on a phone. `.fg-product-quote-embed__actions .button` also sets 42px but computes to ~45px and does not breach.
- **Recommendation:** Raise `.fg-quote-hero__embed-actions .button` (main.scss:21524) from `min-height: 42px` to 44px and its padding from `0.6rem 0.8rem` to `0.7rem 0.9rem`; that single edit clears 44px for all three controls including the mobile 'Open quote tool'. Then add `--fg-control-h: 46px` and `--fg-control-h-lg: 52px` and reduce the thirteen min-height overrides to those two.
- **Why:** This is the flagship product page and the one AI.md:62 says carries the most load-bearing product copy on the site. Social proof placed below the conversion form is proof nobody reads before deciding, and the missing links band removes it from the internal-linking mesh that AI.md:43 says is the priority fix for high-impression pages.
- **Affected:** /casement-windows/ (all three defects). Order rail also missing from /sliding-sash-windows/, /composite-doors/, /roof-lanterns/, /window-and-door-repairs/. Links band also missing from /sliding-sash-windows/, /composite-doors/, /roof-lanterns/. Reviews-after-enquiry also on /roof-lanterns/.
- **Evidence:** Section-order extraction from scratchpad/live/*.html: 11 routes render `FAQ > ORDER > QUOTE > REVIEWS > … > ENQ > LINKS`; casement-windows renders `QUOTE > FAQ > CASES > ENQ > REVIEWS`. template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:3560-3561 (early return), :5361 (`if (! empty($related_links) && $slug !== 'sliding-sash-windows' && ! $is_composite_doors)` — casement not named). template-parts/sections/casement-windows-v2.php:668 (FAQ), :689 (cs-strip), :708 (enquiry), review-showcase after. AI.md:239 Order Process Rule.
- **Verification:** The core claim holds and the fix is right, but three details are wrong and the affected scope is understated. VERIFIED: base .button at main.scss:1501-1514 is min-height:46px / padding:.75rem 1.05rem / border-radius:6px. Brace-tracked parse of compiled main.css (proper stack, not nearest-preceding-@media) gives the desktop-active set exactly as claimed: 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, 52, 54 = seven heights; .fg-enquiry-form__footer .button 54px, .fg-roof-lantern-form/.fg-heritage-door-form footer .button 56px top-level overridden to 48px at @media(min-width:700px), .fg-location-hero__form footer .button 44px — the same submit action really is 44/48/54px by route. Every cited line number opens on the right selector. probe-desktop.json /3d-visualiser/ carries {'Expand view', h:43, 'button button--light'} and {'Open in new tab', h:43} exactly as quoted. The .fg-product-quote-embed__actions 42px rule genuinely does not breach (42px min-height + .62rem*2 padding + .9rem*1.6 + 2px = ~45px, and it appears in no smallTargets list on 14 pages that carry it). CORRECTIONS: (1) there are 13 min-height overrides plus the base = 14 rules, not 15, and 8 distinct values (42,44,46,48,50,52,54,56), not 9. (2) The .button font-size spread is 7 rules / 7 values but the 1.2rem is on `.fg-enquiry-form__footer .button i`, an icon glyph, not a label — the label spread is 0.68rem to 0.94rem. (3) SCOPE UNDERSTATED: a third control breaches, and it is the worst one. probe-mobile.json /3d-visualiser/ shows {'Open quote tool', h:43, 'button fg-quote-hero__mobile-open'} — the mobile primary action. I traced it in 3d-visualiser.html: it sits inside .fg-quote-hero__embed-actions, so it inherits the same main.scss:21524 42px rule. So the single recommended edit fixes three controls, one of which is a real touch target on a phone. (4) STYLE.md:280 sits under the '## Forms' heading, so citing it as a site-wide tap-target law for two desktop mouse targets is a stretch; the mobile 'Open quote tool' is the unambiguous breach.

#### [43] The obscured-glass secondary hero CTA uses .button--light on a white panel and renders as plain text with no button chrome

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** STYLE.md:265 fixes the CTA pair as green primary `.button` plus dark `.button--steel`, with `.button--light` reserved for dark panels where a dark secondary would disappear. `/obscured-glass/` uses `.button--light` (generated-page.php:2937) on a hero whose copy column sits on a pure-white veil (`.fg-obscure-hero__veil` is `linear-gradient(90deg,#ffffff 0%,#ffffff 40%,rgba(255,255,255,.94) 50%,...)`, copy capped at `max-width:min(46rem,52%)`). `.button--light` resolves to `background:#f3f8f7; border-color:#d6e0e3` — both invisible against white. In the rendered fold screenshot 'Ask about glass options' has no discernible border or fill; it reads as a text link next to a solid green button. That also breaks STYLE.md's rule that anything acting as a call to action is a button, never a text link. `/colour-options/` gets this right with `.button--steel` on an identically white hero. Separately and objectively: `/colour-options/` and `/handle-options/` are near-dead-ends — stripping header and footer, they carry 3 and 2 internal links respectively (and two of those are each other), against 19 on `/obscured-glass/`, which alone carries an `fg-links-band`. The eyebrow difference and the single-vs-pair CTA count are real but are Creative judgement: the three pages are three separately-authored bespoke hero components, not one shared template that has drifted.

Then add an `fg-links-band` to `/colour-options/` and `/handle-options/` — obscured-glass already proves the pattern works on this page family, and it would take those two pages from 2-3 onward links to ~20. Treat the eyebrow wording and the lone `Ask about handles` CTA as a separate design call for the owner, not a defect.
- **Why:** These read as live routing. A session reading the dispatch block will believe /upvc-colours/ renders the colour hub and /instant-pricing/ renders the quote tool, and may 'fix' one of them by editing a branch that can never execute. It also hides the real rule: redirects win, so a slug can only be in one of the two lists.
- **Affected:** template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:164, :309, :1914, :1916; inc/generated-pages.php:2071
- **Evidence:** Executed `fenster_redirect_target()` against each: upvc-colours->colour-options, aluminium-colours->colour-options, instant-pricing->online-quote, door-designer->online-quote, window-handles->handle-options, obscure-glass->obscured-glass. `add_action('template_redirect', 'fenster_maybe_render_generated_page', 0)` at inc/generated-pages.php:1842, with the redirect+exit at :1861-1865 preceding any template dispatch.
- **Verification:** Every extraction reproduces, but the framing is wrong in two directions. WRONG: these are not 'the same page type' rendered by one template — they are three separately-built bespoke hero components (`.fg-colour-hub-hero--wall`, `.fg-obscure-hero`, `.fg-window-handle-hero--photo`), each with its own SCSS block. 'Standardise the eyebrow' is therefore a Creative preference, not a template-consistency defect. UNDERSTATED: the button-variant point is not an ambiguous 'one of them is on the wrong panel' — it is definitively obscured-glass, and the consequence is a real objective defect. Both hero panels are white (obscure-hero's veil is `linear-gradient(90deg,#ffffff 0%,#ffffff 40%,...)` and the copy sits in the left 52%), and `.button--light` resolves to `border-color:var(--color-line) #d6e0e3; background:var(--color-soft) #f3f8f7`. I cropped the fold screenshot at 2x: 'Ask about glass options' renders with NO visible border and NO visible fill — it reads as plain body text beside a solid green primary. That breaks STYLE.md:265 ('The one exception is a dark panel') AND STYLE.md's 'Anything that acts as a call to action is a button, never a text link.' The dead-end claim is confirmed and is the other genuinely objective half: body-only internal links (header/footer stripped) are colour-options 3, handle-options 2, obscured-glass 19. #### [5] 168 hex colours where 113 are perceptually redundant; one token defined and never used

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 94% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The palette is 11 named tokens, but the compiled CSS contains 168 distinct hex values plus 384 distinct rgba() values. Clustering the hexes in CIELAB at deltaE<5 (the threshold below which users read two colours as the same) yields 18 clusters covering 113 collapsible values. The worst: 41 distinct near-whites (#ffffff plus 40 off-whites like #f7fbfa, #f4f7f6, #f8fbfa, #f5f7f7, #f7fbf9, #f7faf8 — all indistinguishable); 20 distinct pale border greys around `--color-line`; 7 near-twins of `--color-steel` (#002d3a, #0c313b, #022b35, #0b3039, #082c35, #0a313c, #16333d); 7 of `--color-ink`. The brand green `--color-accent: #2eac66` has two invisible shadows (#31b86e, #2fb66d) and `--color-accent-dark: #20824c` has two (#087943, #248a52). Token adoption is weak in specific places: `--color-surface` is referenced 6 times while literal `#ffffff` appears 488 times, and `--color-light-blue: #4c7b86` is defined in `:root` and referenced zero times anywhere. There are also 621 rgba() literals of the steel colour spanning 39 distinct alpha steps including .025/.03/.035 and .05/.055/.06.
- **Recommendation:** Delete `--color-light-blue` (dead). Collapse the 41 near-whites to `--color-surface` and `--color-soft`, the 20 pale greys to `--color-line`, and the steel/ink twins to their tokens — this is a find-and-replace of exact hex strings, verifiable by re-running the deltaE clustering and confirming cluster count falls. Add an alpha ladder (`--steel-a06`, `--steel-a12`, `--steel-a24`…) at six stops and map the 39 ad-hoc alpha steps onto it.
- **Why:** Near-duplicate colours are the difference between a site that feels manufactured and one that feels assembled. Panels that should share a background sit a shade apart between routes, and nobody can retune the brand green because 90% of colour is hard-coded past the tokens.
- **Affected:** Site-wide, all 38 routes. 168 hex values, 384 rgba values, 11 tokens.
- **Evidence:** live/main.css hex extraction + CIELAB deltaE<5 greedy clustering: 18 clusters, 113 redundant values; `var(--color-light-blue)` count = 0; `var(--color-surface)` count = 6 vs 488 `#ffffff`; 621 `rgba(0,45,58,…)` literals across 39 alpha steps; tokens at src/scss/main.scss:42-51.
- **Verification:** I rebuilt the block-to-template map from scratch in Python and landed on the finding's numbers exactly. assets/css/main.css is 698,156 bytes (681.8 KiB, hence the '682KB' in the title) and gzips to 111,323 bytes. src/scss/main.scss is 42,407 lines with `grep -c '^@use\|^@import'` = 0. Extracting `.fg-*` selectors and reducing to base blocks gives 640 distinct selectors over 570 base blocks. Counting how many .php files mention each base: 77 blocks in zero templates, 427 in exactly one, 25 in two, 13 in three — 427 and 77 both match the finding to the unit. The conservative pass (block name appears in no .php file anywhere AND not in src/js/main.js, so dynamically composed class names cannot produce a false positive) returned 64 blocks, and the name list is IDENTICAL to the finding's examples: fg-cd-v2-config/-range/-options/-selector/-swatches/-hardware/-heading, fg-about-intro/-process/-proof/-values/-showroom/-feature/-section-head, fg-contact-cards/-methods/-map/-route-card/-trust, fg-home-system-lab/-panel/-card, fg-home-route-board/-card, fg-county-selector, fg-hero-quote, fg-scroll-video, fg-trust-care/-products/-visual-proof, fg-upd-chart/-finish/-threshold-row. Weighing the rules whose selectors mention only orphan blocks: 500 rules / 55,099 bytes (53.8KB) against the finding's 491 / 53.2KB — a tokenizer difference of under 2KB, not a disagreement. Independent cross-check: I grepped 12 of the orphan names against all 38 fetched live pages and got zero hits on every one, including fg-about-intro against about.html and fg-contact-cards against contact.html, which are precisely the pages that would have to carry them. inc/assets.php:20-25 does enqueue one unconditional main.css. The single-template blocks are spread widely (86 in generated-page.php, 27 in location-service.php, 27 in casement-windows-v2.php, 22/20 in the two case-study templates), so the proposed one-partial-per-bespoke-template split is structurally plausible rather than blocked by everything living in the router.

#### [11] The `--fg-font-size-max` ceiling token governs only 31% of display type; nine rules retype its value by hand

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 94% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** STYLE.md:229 instructs that "New large type must use the shared token as the maximum value." In practice, of 154 `font-size: clamp()` rules whose upper bound is 2.5rem or larger, only 48 reference `var(--fg-font-size-max)` — 106 hardcode a rem value instead. Worse, nine of those hardcode literally `3.6rem`, the token's own current value (main.scss:901, 1479, 4142, 24432, 26856, 28533, 29331, 30541 and others). The ceiling is therefore not enforceable: changing `--fg-font-size-max` would move 48 rules and silently leave 106 behind, nine of which would keep rendering at the old ceiling while appearing to comply. The upper bounds that were hardcoded also drift with no pattern — 2.5, 2.55, 2.6, 2.65, 2.75, 2.85, 3, 3.1, 3.15, 3.2, 3.4, 3.45, 3.55, 3.6rem.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the nine literal `3.6rem` font-size upper bounds with `var(--fg-font-size-max)` — a safe, zero-visual-change edit that makes the token authoritative. Then map the remaining 97 hardcoded bounds onto three display steps (`--fg-display-sm: 2.6rem`, `--fg-display-md: 3.1rem`, `--fg-display-lg: var(--fg-font-size-max)`).
- **Why:** The ceiling is the project's one hard numeric design rule and the mechanism meant to enforce it does not reach 69% of the type it governs. Any future decision to lower the ceiling would produce a site that is half-changed.
- **Affected:** 154 display-type clamp rules in src/scss/main.scss; 106 bypass the token, 9 duplicate its literal value.
- **Evidence:** `var(--fg-font-size-max)` appears 48 times in src/scss/main.scss; parsed clamp upper bounds ≥2.5rem total 154, of which 106 are literal rem; literal `3.6rem` font-size bounds at main.scss:901, 1479, 4142, 24432, 26856, 28533, 29331, 30541; STYLE.md:229.
- **Verification:** Every cited line and every redirect verified by grep -n, not by counting. inc/generated-pages.php:1842 = `add_action('template_redirect', 'fenster_maybe_render_generated_page', 0);`; :1861 = `$redirect_target = fenster_redirect_target($slug);` with the wp_safe_redirect(...,301)+exit at :1862-1865, ahead of all template dispatch — so a redirected slug can never reach generated-page.php. The redirect map (:1710-1727) contains upvc-colours=>colour-options, aluminium-colours=>colour-options, instant-pricing=>online-quote, door-designer=>online-quote, window-handles=>handle-options, obscure-glass=>obscured-glass. generated-page.php:164 is exactly `$is_colour_options = in_array($slug, ['colour-options', 'upvc-colours', 'aluminium-colours'], true);` and :309 is the $is_quote_tool line including 'instant-pricing' and 'door-designer'. inc/generated-pages.php:2071 is the virtual-slug array_merge and it does contain 'upvc-colours' and 'aluminium-colours', which line 2072's `fenster_redirect_target($virtual_slug) !== ''` test filters straight back out. On the $product_families aliases: :1914 and :1916 carry the 'tilt-and-turn-windows' and 'bow-and-bay-windows' keys, and the matcher at :2020-2022 is `$slug === $family_prefix || str_starts_with($slug, $family_prefix . '-')`. I checked the source of truth rather than trusting the claim — data/pages.json contains exactly three slugs with those prefixes (bow-and-bay-windows-northampton, tilt-and-turn-windows-northampton, tilt-and-turn-windows-designer) and all three are redirected: the first two by the explicit map entries at :1715-1716, the third by the `-designer` branch at :1738-1750 which rewrites the base to tilt-turn-windows. None of the four appears anywhere in urls.txt. So the aliases are genuinely unreachable.

#### [7] The type scale is a continuum, not a scale: 349 distinct font sizes, 46 adjacent pairs under half a pixel apart

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** There is no type-scale token of any kind — `--fg-font-size-max` is a ceiling, not a scale. The compiled CSS carries 1,176 font-size declarations with 349 distinct values: 71 static rem values and 271 distinct `clamp()` expressions. Of the 71 static values, 46 adjacent pairs sit 0.03rem or less apart — 0.16px to 0.48px, differences no human can perceive. The run .90, .91, .92, .93, .94, .95, .96, .97, .98 is nine "different" sizes spanning 1.28px. Inside STYLE.md's stated body-copy band there are 23 distinct values across 340 declarations. Responsiveness shows the same pattern: 1,109 `clamp()` uses draw on 666 distinct expressions, so roughly 60% of every clamp on the site is unique to its one rule. A typical page renders 32–43 distinct font sizes (max 43 on /aluminium-windows/ and /aluminium-bifold-doors/, min 13 on /case-studies/), and H2s alone render at 30 distinct sizes across the 38 routes.
- **Recommendation:** Define an eight-step scale in `:root` (suggest .78 / .88 / 1 / 1.15 / 1.35 / 1.65 / 2.1 / 2.6 rem plus the existing 3.6rem ceiling) and snap every static font-size to the nearest step — 46 of the 71 static values collapse with zero visible change by construction. Then reduce the 666 clamp expressions to a handful of named responsive steps. Do this incrementally, one namespace at a time, verifying against screenshots.
- **Why:** This is the difference between "almost finished" and "finished". No individual value is wrong, but 349 sizes means no page can be typographically consistent with another, and every new section adds a 350th. It is also the root cause of most of the other type findings.
- **Affected:** Site-wide. 1,176 font-size declarations across all 38 routes.
- **Evidence:** live/main.css: 1,176 font-size decls, 349 distinct values, 71 static rem, 271 distinct clamps; 46 adjacent static pairs ≤0.03rem; 666 distinct clamp expressions across 1,109 uses; probe-desktop.json fontSizes histogram lengths 13–43 per route; 30 distinct H2 sizes across 38 routes.
- **Verification:** Reproduced with an independent write/read parser over all theme PHP (node_modules excluded). All 18 named variables have writes and zero reads: journey_options 3W/0R, journey_option_eyebrow 2W/0R, journey_option_heading 2W/0R, journey_heading 2W/0R, journey_steps 2W/0R, journey_type_label 1W/0R, journey_gallery_eyebrow 2W/0R, journey_gallery_heading 2W/0R, journey_trust_heading 1W/0R, journey_trust_copy 1W/0R, designer_sections 1W/0R, scroll_story_sections 2W/0R, is_bifold 1W/0R, composite_door_gallery 1W/0R, composite_palette 1W/0R, product_hub_support_image 1W/0R, window_handle_intro 1W/0R, upvc_pick 1W/0R. The chain is exactly as described: $upvc_colour_routes:1212 -> $is_upvc_colour_product:1224 -> $product_colours:1225-1262 (sixteen uPVC entries plus the aluminium/bifold override at :1253-1262) -> $journey_options:1308 -> nothing, with the two overrides at :1330 and :1339 and the pet-flap dead assignments at :1325-1326. Cited line numbers all exact: $designer_sections:127-130, $scroll_story_sections:131-137, $is_bifold:150. The live journey strings the finding says to keep are genuinely read: journey_intro_heading at :3544, journey_why_heading at :4079, journey_faq_heading at :5034, journey_order_heading at :5054. One near-miss my parser flagged and I chased down: $upvc_colour_routes appears at template-parts/sections/upvc-doors-v2.php:32, which would break the recommended deletion — but reading it, that occurrence is inside the file's docblock prose ('by taking this slug out of `$upvc_colour_routes`'), not a code read, so the deletion is safe. That docblock is itself further proof the array is dead: it claims /upvc-doors/ was taken OUT of $upvc_colour_routes, yet 'upvc-doors' is still sitting at line 1219 and nothing noticed. The drift claim checks out precisely. Loading site-data.php and reading colour_options.materials.upvc.colours gives 17 entries: Smooth White, White, Cream, Chartwell Green, Irish Oak, Golden Oak, Rosewood, Anthracite Grey, Black Brown, Agate Grey, Silver Grey, Basalt Grey, Slate Grey, Gale Grey Finesse (Anthracite Smooth), Blue, Dark Green, Dark Red. The dead $product_colours list says 'Steel Blue' where live says 'Blue', omits Gale Grey Finesse and Smooth White entirely, and adds a 'Custom RAL' entry the live uPVC range does not carry. All four divergences confirmed.

- **Recommendation:** Rewrite STYLE.md:329 to describe what exists: name `/composite-doors/` as the lead-paragraph-plus-fact-strip hero, and describe `fg-hero--compact` (`/roof-lanterns/`, `/heritage-aluminium-doors/`) as the second documented pattern with its own rules — eyebrow, H1, CTA pair over full-bleed media, lead copy moved into the section below. Separately, replace the `Fenster Glazing` default at generated-page.php:894 with a product-plus-location string per route, following the form `/composite-doors/` ('Composite doors in Milton Keynes') and `/roof-lanterns/` ('Roof lanterns and roof lights in Milton Keynes') already use.
- **Why:** Compiled assets are the deliverable and they are unverifiable: nobody can rebuild the deployed JavaScript from this repository. That makes every future JS change ship an invisible dependency upgrade alongside it, and it makes the smoke test 'does the build still match' impossible to run — which is the one guard this theme most needs, given it has no tests at all.
- **Affected:** package.json (lenis ^1.3.23), package-lock.json (1.3.23), assets/js/main.js (139,580 bytes, embeds 1.3.25), live main.js
- **Evidence:** `./node_modules/.bin/esbuild src/js/main.js --bundle --minify` output differs from assets/js/main.js at char 19; head of committed and live main.js = `var eo="1.3.25"`, head of fresh build = `var eo="1.3.23"`; package-lock.json node_modules/lenis version 1.3.23. Same command reproduces assets/css/main.css exactly (698,156 bytes, byte-identical).
- **Verification:** The core claim is correct and the finding understates it. STYLE.md:329 and :259 are the right lines and read exactly as quoted. `/roof-lanterns/` does render `fg-hero fg-hero--compact` with eyebrow, H1 and CTA pair over a full-bleed autoplay video (not even a photograph), with no lead paragraph and no three-fact list in the hero — confirmed in the live markup.

But I fetched the second named reference, which nobody checked, and `/heritage-aluminium-doors/` diverges the same way: identical `fg-hero fg-hero--compact`, a full-bleed `fg-hero__image` with `fg-hero__shade`, eyebrow `Heritage aluminium doors in Milton Keynes`, H1, CTA pair, and nothing else — no lead paragraph, no reassurance list, no photograph alongside. And `/composite-doors/` does not use a shared hero at all; it uses a bespoke `fg-cd3-hero` with `fg-cd3-hero__grid` / `__copy` / `__lead` / `__media`, followed by a separate `fg-cd3-brief` strip. So the pattern STYLE.md calls 'the one shared by composite doors, heritage doors and roof lanterns' is shared by none of them: composite is bespoke and one-of-a-kind, heritage and lanterns share a different pattern with each other.

The eyebrow half needs its scope corrected but the route list is exactly right. `generated-page.php:894` hardcodes `$hero_eyebrow = 'Fenster Glazing'`, overridden only at :896 (commercial), :898 (composite) and :900 (Sheerline Classic / heritage-windows). Extracting the first `.eyebrow` from every live page returns `Fenster Glazing` on precisely the 14 routes named, plus `/home/`. But they are not '14 of the 15 compact routes': `/aluminium-windows/` uses `fg-aw-story`, not `fg-hero--compact`, and of the 15 routes that do carry `fg-hero--compact`, 13 show `Fenster Glazing` (heritage-windows shows `Sheerline Classic`, roof-lanterns shows the product-and-location line). The correct framing is 'every shared-hero route except the three overridden at :896-900'.

Unrelated but found while doing this and worth passing on: both `/roof-lanterns/` and `/heritage-aluminium-doors/` render a nested duplicate landmark — `<main id="main-content" class="site-main"> <main id="main-content" class="fg-roof-lantern-page">` — a duplicate `id` and a `main` inside a `main`. That is a separate defect from this finding.

#### [8] The `.button` component renders at seven different heights on desktop, including two below the 44px tap-target rule

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `.button` sets `min-height: 46px; padding: 0.75rem 1.05rem; border-radius: 6px`. Fifteen rules then override `min-height` with nine distinct values. Checking media-query scope properly by brace-tracking (not by "nearest preceding @media", which is wrong in flat CSS), the desktop-active set is 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, 52 and 54px — seven heights for one component. The primary submit button is the worst case: `.fg-enquiry-form__footer .button` is 54px, `.fg-roof-lantern-form/.fg-heritage-door-form … .button` is 56px at top level but 48px from `@media (min-width: 700px)`, and `.fg-location-hero__form … .button` is 44px — so the same submit action is 44px, 48px or 54px depending on route. Font size varies too, across seven values from 0.68rem to 1.2rem. Two rules drop below STYLE.md:280's "Tap targets should be at least 44px high": `.fg-quote-hero__embed-actions .button` and `.fg-product-quote-embed__actions .button`, both `min-height: 42px` at top level. I verified the rendered outcome rather than assuming: the quote-hero one measures 43px in the probe (0.86rem × 1.6 line-height + 2×0.6rem padding + 2px border = 43.2px), confirmed on /3d-visualiser/ for both "Expand view" and "Open in new tab". The product-quote one computes to ~45px and does not actually breach, so only the /3d-visualiser/ pair is a real tap-target defect.
- **Recommendation:** Decide per route and make one mechanism enforce it. If Milton Keynes should not be in the sitemap, remove it from the `$add_related_routes([...])` call at template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:2061 (NOT :2062, which is commercial-glazing-northamptonshire) and add it to `fenster_slug_is_noindex()` (inc/generated-pages.php:1755) so a single function decides indexability; if it should be indexed, delete it from `$excluded_slugs` at :1974. Either way, move the `$excluded_slugs` and gone/redirect/noindex test out of the first loop into a `fenster_sitemap_should_list(string $slug): bool` called by all five emit loops at :1988, :2020, :2033, :2047 and :2071, so an exclusion cannot be bypassed by whichever loop emits the route. AI.md:272 already states the governing rule.
- **Why:** The button is the most repeated interactive object on a lead-generation site. Seven heights means the primary CTA has a different physical weight on nearly every template, and the 43px pair on /3d-visualiser/ misses the accessibility minimum the project set for itself.
- **Affected:** Site-wide `.button`; 15 min-height overrides. Tap-target breach confirmed on /3d-visualiser/ (2 controls).
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:1501 (46px base), :3974 (42px), :5238 (44px), :18448 (52px), :18600 (54px), :21524 (42px), :29978 (56px), :30080 (48px), :35790 (44px); media scope resolved by brace-tracking; probe-desktop.json /3d-visualiser/ smallTargets `{"txt":"Expand view","h":43,"cls":"button button--light"}` and `{"txt":"Open in new tab","h":43}`; STYLE.md:280.
- **Verification:** Every claim reproduced. inc/generated-pages.php:1969 opens $excluded_slugs; :1974 = commercial-glazing-milton-keynes, :1975 = commercial-glazing-northamptonshire. `grep -n excluded_slugs` returns exactly two hits (1969 declaration, 1990 the single isset test), so the array is consulted only in the first loop. The other emit loops are at :2020 (location matrix), :2033 (commercial counties), :2047 (price guides) and :2071 (virtual slugs) — the county loop echoes unconditionally, and the virtual loop checks gone/redirect/noindex but not $excluded_slugs, so 'four loops, different filter subsets' is accurate. fenster_commercial_county_pages() (:902-914) builds 'commercial-glazing-' . $county_slug over fenster_commercial_county_profiles(), which contains 'northamptonshire' — so Northamptonshire is re-added by the county loop, and it is line 644 of urls.txt. Milton Keynes is not a county profile and is absent from urls.txt. curl of https://fensterglazing.com/commercial-glazing-milton-keynes/ returns 200 with a self-referencing canonical and NO robots meta tag at all. generated-page.php:2059-2063 does add both to the commercial related-links band. AI.md:272 actively supports the recommendation ('Add new debris to these lists rather than only excluding it from the sitemap; sitemap exclusion alone does not stop indexing'), so this is not an owner ruling in the other direction. ONE CORRECTION: the recommendation says remove Milton Keynes 'at generated-page.php:2062' — it is at :2061; :2062 is commercial-glazing-northamptonshire. Acting on the stated line would delete the wrong slug.

#### [28] No global spacing scale: 514 distinct padding values and 175 distinct gap values against a `:root` with no spacing token

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The main `:root` (src/scss/main.scss:41-79) contains no spacing token — no scale, no rhythm unit. The only spacing tokens anywhere are component-scoped, in a second `:root` at main.scss:14054 that defines `--fg-tag-padding` and `--fg-tag-gap` for the tag component. Against that, the compiled CSS carries 1,038 `padding` declarations across 514 distinct values and 978 `gap` declarations across 175 distinct values. The 42 static rem gaps include .12, .15, .16 and .18 — increments of 0.16rem, or 0.5px to 1px apart. Section vertical rhythm is entirely hand-tuned: between 58 distinct `padding: clamp(…) 0` expressions (strict count, 88 declarations) and 236 distinct expressions if every clamp-based vertical padding is counted, drawing on 27 to 60 distinct upper bounds spanning .8rem to 8rem. STYLE.md:176 deliberately says 'Avoid giving every section identical top and bottom padding', so the variety is intended. The defect is not that padding varies; it is that it varies continuously with no underlying unit, so 'a generous handoff' and 'a tight handoff' are not repeatable decisions.
- **Recommendation:** Standardise: eyebrow `Specification hub` on all three; a CTA pair on all three (add `Get an instant price` alongside `Ask about handles` on handle-options); pick the secondary variant from the actual panel colour and make colour-options and obscured-glass agree if their panels agree; add `fg-links-band` to colour-options and handle-options so all three feed the internal-link mesh.
- **Why:** These three are the destinations product pages hand visitors off to mid-decision. Arriving at three pages that look like three different templates undermines the impression of one considered specification system, and two of the three are dead ends with no onward links.
- **Affected:** /colour-options/, /handle-options/, /obscured-glass/.
- **Evidence:** Extraction from scratchpad/live/{colour-options,handle-options,obscured-glass}.html — colour-options: 4 sections, eyebrow `Specification hub`, CTAs [`Get an instant price` .button, `Book a consultation` .button--steel], no links band. handle-options: 8 sections, eyebrow `Specification hub`, CTAs [`Ask about handles` .button], no links band. obscured-glass: 5 sections, eyebrow `Glass privacy choices`, CTAs [`Try the glass preview` .button, `Ask about glass options` .button--light], links band present. STYLE.md:265; AI.md:659.
- **Verification:** The substance is right and the two headline counts are exact, but the absolute claim in the title is not literally true and the section-rhythm figure does not reproduce. VERIFIED EXACTLY: live/main.css carries 1,038 padding declarations across 514 distinct values and 978 gap declarations across 175 distinct values; there are 42 distinct static rem gap values and they do include .12, .15, .16 and .18rem (0.5px-1px apart). The main `:root` at main.scss:41-79 holds colours, gradient geometry, --container, --site-header-main-height, --fg-font-size-max and a star mask — no spacing token. STYLE.md's Section Continuity block is at 171-184 and does say 'Avoid giving every section identical top and bottom padding', so the finding's careful distinction between intended variety and unrepeatable variety is fair and correctly stated. CORRECTIONS: (1) 'zero spacing tokens' is not literally true. A second `:root` at main.scss:14054 defines a tag component token set including `--fg-tag-padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem` and `--fg-tag-gap: 0.45rem`. It is one component, so the argument survives, but the absolute framing does not. (2) The section-rhythm number does not reproduce. Strict `padding: clamp(...) 0` yields 88 declarations across 58 distinct expressions with 27 distinct upper bounds, not 94 expressions across 40 bounds. Broadening to any padding/padding-top/padding-bottom/padding-block whose value starts with clamp() yields 320 declarations, 236 distinct expressions and 60 distinct upper bounds. Every one of the 40 upper bounds the finding lists does exist in the file, so the list is not fabricated — the filter is just undocumented and unreproducible, and the honest range is 'between 58 and 236 distinct vertical-rhythm expressions'. Neither correction changes the conclusion or the recommendation.

#### [3] Latent breach of the 3.6rem hard ceiling on /sliding-sash-windows/, invisible at the 1440px QA viewport

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `main.scss:31609`, inside `@media (min-width: 861px)`, sets `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-sash-gallery__head h2 { font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 4vw, 4rem); }`. The upper bound is 4rem = 64px, which exceeds the `--fg-font-size-max` ceiling of 3.6rem/57.6px by 11%. It does not show up in any QA pass because at the 1440px audit viewport 4vw resolves to exactly 57.6px — identical to the ceiling — so the page reports as compliant. It only breaches above 1600px viewport width, which covers the common 1920px desktop. STYLE.md's "Important Updates" claims "Existing oversized clamps have been capped at this token"; this one survived that sweep precisely because it is invisible at the viewport the sweep was verified at. A static scan of all 42,407 SCSS lines found only two clamps whose upper bound exceeds the ceiling: this one and `.fg-cas-num`.
- **Recommendation:** Change the upper bound to the token: `font-size: clamp(2.4rem, 4vw, var(--fg-font-size-max));` at main.scss:31609. Given STYLE.md:236's H2 guidance this heading is oversized regardless, so `clamp(2rem, 3vw, 2.5rem)` would be the better fix — 2.5rem is the documented art-directed H2 maximum.
- **Why:** It is a real breach of the one hard, numeric, site-wide typographic rule the project has, on a designated reference page, and it is structurally invisible to the project's own QA method. Any future ceiling audit run at 1440px will keep passing it.
- **Affected:** /sliding-sash-windows/ — `.fg-sash-gallery__head h2` ("Roseview sash windows in real homes."). Breaches on any viewport ≥1600px CSS px.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:31609 `clamp(2.4rem, 4vw, 4rem)` inside `@media (min-width: 861px)`; probe-desktop.json innerWidth=1440 reports maxFontSize 57.6 (4vw of 1440 = 57.6 exactly); rem base confirmed 16px (no html/:root font-size override; 3.6rem renders 57.6px on 19 routes).
- **Verification:** Every factual claim I could check is accurate; the impact rating is not supported. Verified line-by-line: inc/site-data.php primary_nav_fallback:152, product_usps:297 (23 keys), glazing_u_values:619 (13), product_media:767 (26), product_hub_groups:1124, product_gallery_groups:1337 (26), product_content:1693 (27), colour_options:3208; inc/generated-pages.php fenster_location_matrix_products:81 (21), fenster_location_matrix_product_profiles:225 (21), fenster_gsc_seo_overrides:252 (67); template-parts/sections/location-service.php $services:188, $product_profiles:688; inc/product-hub-data.php $data:34, $energyplus_routes:549, $thermlock_routes:559, $glazing_by_route:588, $chambers_by_route:634; template-parts/sections/generated-page.php $upvc_foil_routes:350, $aluminium_colour_routes:375, $product_quote_embeds:904, $no_instant_price_routes:939, $hero_overrides:942, $upvc_colour_routes:1212, $window_routes:1867, $door_routes:1879, $other_service_routes:1891, $product_families:1910. I loaded site-data.php and generated-pages.php under PHP 8.2 and counted the key sets: 23/13/26/26/27/21/21/67 — every single cited count matches. The comment at product-hub-data.php:596-599 reads verbatim 'The two are separate arrays and nothing joins them, so change both or neither'; the six-vs-four chamber contradiction is documented at :621-635; the Thermlock branch at :674+ does read from glazing_u_values as claimed. Two of the finding's cited line numbers are off by 2-5 ($no_instant_price_routes is 939 not 941, $hero_overrides is 942 not 947) — trivial. WHERE IT IS WRONG: Impact High. There is no live defect. Both contradictions the finding cites as consequences (six-vs-four chambers, 0.95-vs-1.2 flush casement) are already fixed in the code it quotes — the quotes are from the comments explaining the fixes. The recommendation is a build-time reporting script with explicitly no behaviour change. That is a maintainability investment against latent risk, which is Medium. I also note some of the listed 'registries' ($no_instant_price_routes, $no_case_study_routes, $upvc_foil_routes) are per-route behaviour flags, not duplicated product names, so '20 registries a rename must reach' slightly overstates the rename surface — AI.md:625-632 and PROGRESS.md:259-275 put the rename-critical set at seven and I could not find an eighth that carries a product NAME. Not ALREADY_RULED: the docs describe the sprawl at length but record no decision against consolidating it.

#### [9] About 271 styled classes and roughly 81KB (11.8%) of the shipped stylesheet are dead code

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** Of 1,853 distinct `.fg-*` classnames styled in the SCSS, 309 never appear in any PHP, JS, JSON or HTML in the theme.
