Verify each by grepping the class against all PHP/JS before removal, and re-render the affected routes. Separately, decide whether `fg-heritage-door-turntable` needs styles or the markup should go.
- **Why:** It is roughly 81KB of the 694KB stylesheet parsed on every page load for markup that no longer exists, and it actively misleads: an agent reading the SCSS for the contact page finds two complete competing card systems with no way to tell which one renders.
- **Affected:** src/scss/main.scss; ~271 classes; ~81KB of 694KB compiled CSS (~11.8%).
- **Evidence:** 1,853 styled `.fg-*` classes vs 309 absent from all source, 271 after excluding 47 dynamic-construction prefixes; byte attribution over compiled main.css = 81,683 bytes; `fg-cd-v2` = 183 SCSS lines / 14,372 compiled bytes and zero PHP/JS references; contact.html emits `fg-contact-hub-card` not `fg-contact-card`; template-parts/sections/team.php:120 confirms the dynamic pattern I excluded.
- **Verification:** Independently reproduced, to the byte. I ran the repo's own build commands with output redirected into the scratchpad (no repo file touched): `./node_modules/.bin/sass src/scss/main.scss <scratch>/rebuild-main.css --style=compressed --no-source-map` gives md5 6c047bce61e33a693e3cd135246b95e1, identical to the committed assets/css/main.css (698,156 bytes) — CSS reproduces exactly. `./node_modules/.bin/esbuild src/js/main.js --bundle --minify` gives 138,870 bytes opening `(()=>{var eo="1.3.23"`, while the committed assets/js/main.js is 139,580 bytes opening `(()=>{var eo="1.3.25"`. A byte-walk confirms the finding's exact numbers: first difference at byte 19, common tail 227 bytes. package.json:24 declares `"lenis": "^1.3.23"`; package-lock.json:2169-2171 pins node_modules/lenis at 1.3.23; node_modules/lenis/package.json says 1.3.23 and node_modules/lenis/dist/lenis.mjs contains the literal `version = "1.3.23"`, which confirms `eo` is the lenis version constant. The deployed artifact is the committed one: md5 of the fetched live main.js and the committed assets/js/main.js are both 20948f42f8fd1cff21cccc6e261e1892. Note the drift is an upgrade, not a downgrade, so the recommendation to pin "1.3.25" (rather than rebuilding on 1.3.23) is the correct direction — rebuilding as-is would silently ship a downgrade to production.

#### [15] The router's dispatch is a 1,033-line linear if-chain of 30 early returns whose precedence is mostly positional, with ~750 lines of page markup embedded inside it

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Between generated-page.php:2104 and :3136 there are 30 top-level `if (…) { … return; }` branches evaluated strictly top to bottom. Twenty-three are the clean `get_template_part(); return;` form; three are entire page bodies inlined into the dispatch chain (`$is_window_handles` :2341-2529, `$is_colour_options` :2531-2822, `$is_obscure_glass` :2832-3091, roughly 750 lines of markup between two routing decisions). Above them sit eight 'bespoke middle' routes (:171 `$is_flush_bespoke` through :243 `$is_tilt_turn_bespoke`) that deliberately do not early-return and instead null out bands further down. Precedence is partly written and partly not: line :339 does state that ten flags outrank the product journey, and the comment at :155-158 does explain why `$is_case_study` must precede the commercial fall-through — but `$is_trust_page` at :2824 beating the `$is_utility_page` catch-all at :3108, when `why-trust-fenster` is a member of both lists (:266 and :311), rests on nothing but line order and carries no comment. The conditions are computed 1,750-2,990 lines before the branches that consume them, so no flag and its branch are ever on the same screen. The cost is recorded in-file at :3125-3129: the commercial hub was moved out on 2026-08-12 because it was "~280 lines inline in a template already past 3,000, which is most of why nobody spotted that it linked five of the twelve commercial routes."
- **Recommendation:** Two separable moves. First, finish the job started on 2026-08-12: extract the three inlined page bodies (`$is_window_handles`, `$is_colour_options`, `$is_obscure_glass`) into their own templates, exactly as the commercial hub was. That removes ~750 lines from the chain and is the change with the documented precedent. Second, extract the dispatch itself into `fenster_route_template(string $slug, array $page): ?string` in a new inc/routing.php as an ordered array of [predicate, template] pairs, with the precedence comments moved next to the pairs — starting with the `$is_trust_page` before `$is_utility_page` case, which is the one genuinely undocumented ordering dependency. Leave the eight bespoke-middle flags alone; their comments at :165-263 are the best documentation in the codebase.
- **Why:** Motion consistency is a large part of whether interactions feel like one product. Six curves that no one can distinguish is maintenance cost with no design benefit, and the dual ms/s notation makes the stylesheet unsearchable for anyone trying to retune timing.
- **Affected:** Site-wide. 106 distinct transition values, 8 cubic-bezier curves.
- **Evidence:** live/main.css: 106 distinct `transition:` values; 8 distinct `cubic-bezier()` values; `transform .18s ease` ×3 and `transform 180ms ease` ×5; no transition or easing custom property in the `:root` block at src/scss/main.scss:41-79.
- **Verification:** The structural problem is real and I reproduced the anchors, but three of its counts are wrong and one of its two headline examples is the single place where precedence IS documented.

WHAT HOLDS: generated-page.php is 5,376 lines. The flag block genuinely runs :150-345. The commercial-hub comment at :3125-3129 is verbatim as quoted ("~280 lines inline in a template already past 3,000, which is most of why nobody spotted that it linked five of the twelve commercial routes"). `why-trust-fenster` really is in both `$is_trust_page` (:266) and `$is_utility_page` (:311), and the `$is_trust_page` branch at :2824 really does precede the `$is_utility_page` catch-all at :3108 with no comment explaining why — that is a clean, undocumented, positional-only precedence.

WHAT IS WRONG:
(1) "21 `if (…) { get_template_part(…); return; }` blocks" is an undercount. `grep -n 'return;'` gives 30 top-level early-return branches between :2116 and :3135 (2116, 2121, 2138, 2150, 2161, 2169, 2180, 2191, 2202, 2212, 2219, 2226, 2233, 2240, 2247, 2256, 2271, 2280, 2291, 2302, 2317, 2330, 2338, 2528, 2821, 2829, 3090, 3105, 3121, 3135). Only 23 are the clean get_template_part form; three are large inline page bodies (`$is_window_handles` :2341-2529, `$is_colour_options` :2531-2822, `$is_obscure_glass` :2832-3091, ~750 lines of markup sitting inside the dispatch chain), which the recommendation's "extract the map" fix does not address.

(3) "order is the only rule and nothing states it" is overstated. Line :339 (`$use_product_journey = $is_product && ! $is_home && ! $is_case_study && ! $is_team && ! $is_about_page && ! $is_contact && ! $is_product_selector_hub && ! $is_commercial_hub && ! $is_commercial_county && ! $is_location_service && ! $is_colour_options;`) is a written, belt-and-braces statement of precedence for ten of the flags — including the `$is_location_service` over `$is_product` case the finding cites as positional-only.
(4) The `$is_case_study` / `$is_commercial` example is the weakest one available. `$is_commercial` has no branch of its own; the only commercial branches are county (:2141), product (:2153) and hub (:3124), and I confirmed `commercial-projects` is not a commercial product page (zero `'commercial-projects' =>` keys in inc/commercial-product-data.php), so nothing at :2119 is beating a commercial branch. What it beats is the bottom-of-file product journey — and that exact precedence is documented in the comment at :155-158.

Type Creative is correct: this is a maintainability judgement with no user-facing defect.

#### [14] 86 page namespaces, 53 of them used on one page or none: this is a component library of about a dozen shared parts plus fifty bespoke pages

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** High · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The brief asks for an honest judgement, so: it is not a design system with some bespoke pages, it is a set of bespoke pages with a small shared core. There are 85 `.fg-*` namespace roots and 649 distinct namespace classnames (1,853 counting BEM elements). Measured against the 40 sampled pages, 29 roots appear on none and 24 on exactly one — 53 of 85 (62%) are single-page. Only 12 roots reach 10 or more pages, and those are the genuine system: `fg-cookie` and `fg-accreditation` (40 pages), `fg-stars`, `fg-review`, `fg-enquiry` (30), `fg-form` (27), `fg-product` (24), `fg-links` (23), `fg-contact` (21), `fg-quote` (20), `fg-hero`, `fg-cw`, `fg-order` (15). Everything else — `fg-cas`, `fg-cd3`, `fg-rp`, `fg-lv`, `fg-sg`, `fg-mk`, `fg-oq`, `fg-upd`, `fg-aw` — is one page's private stylesheet. Importantly, some of this is sanctioned: STYLE.md explicitly blesses `.fg-cas` as a one-page exception and instructs that it not be normalised. The problem is not that bespoke namespaces exist; it is that there is no shared layer beneath them, so each new page re-solves section padding, heading size, card radius and shadow from scratch — which is the direct cause of the 349 font sizes, 212 shadows and 514 paddings above.
- **Recommendation:** Do not attempt to merge the namespaces; that would be a rewrite with high regression risk and would violate the casement ruling. Instead extract the primitives the bespoke pages all re-implement — section wrapper, section-heading, card, panel, eyebrow, button, spacing rhythm — into a documented base layer of roughly 15 classes, and require new pages to compose from it and only add a namespace for genuinely novel art direction. Measure success by whether the next new page adds fewer than 20 new classes.
- **Why:** Every bespoke namespace is a place where a future change has to be made again. At 85 namespaces a global adjustment such as lowering the type ceiling or restyling cards is 85 separate edits, which is why the existing ceiling sweep and CTA-rule sweep both left pages behind.
- **Affected:** src/scss/main.scss, 42,407 lines. 85 namespace roots, 1,853 classnames; 53 roots on ≤1 of 40 sampled pages.
- **Evidence:** 85 `.fg-*` roots and 649 distinct root-level classnames in src/scss/main.scss; page-usage distribution across 40 live HTML files (29 roots on 0 pages, 24 on 1, only 12 on ≥10); STYLE.md:26-33 sanctioning `.fg-cas` as a one-page exception.
- **Verification:** Reproduced in full, and the 'stale not merely idle' claim is stronger than stated. inc/generated-pages.php:937-946 is the home branch whose `$index['home'] ?? [...]` fallback guarantees an array, and :1940 is the `exit` after get_footer(), so fenster_maybe_render_generated_page() (template_redirect priority 0, :1842) always renders and exits for the front page — front-page.php is unreachable for any normal request. `grep -rn 'sections/home-hero'` and `'sections/service-grid'` return exactly one hit each, both inside front-page.php (:10 and :11), so nothing else references them. home-hero.php emits `class="container home-hero__inner"`; the fetched live home.html contains `container fg-home-hero__inner` twice and zero occurrences of a bare home-hero__inner, and that class comes from template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:115 — confirmed. Line counts match to the line: front-page.php 13, home-hero.php 20, service-grid.php 25. The 410 branch does include get_query_template('404') at :1874, so 404.php is genuinely live and correctly excluded from the deletion list. Additional support: the data these dead templates read, inc/site-data.php:3309-3323, is itself stale — eyebrow 'Bedfordshire aluminium glazing specialists', title 'Fenster Glazing' and a primary CTA to /contact/, none of which is on the live homepage. No owner ruling protects any of the three files: grep of all *.md finds nothing on front-page.php, home-hero.php or service-grid.php, and the documented homepage rulings (HOMEPAGE.md:530, AI.md:141, STYLE.md:371) concern the separate inactive fg-home-hero-3d branch. AUDIT.md:395 already flags a related-but-different pocket of unreachable homepage markup inside generated-page.php, so the class of problem is recorded but this instance is not.

#### [19] The shadow system is two tokens and 212 hand-typed values; 91% of shadows bypass the tokens, so the tokens cannot retune anything

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `:root` (main.scss:69-70) defines exactly two shadow tokens: `--shadow-soft: 0 18px 48px rgba(0,45,58,.14)` and `--shadow-strong: 0 30px 90px rgba(0,45,58,.28)`. The compiled CSS contains 334 `box-shadow` declarations with 212 distinct values; only 29 (8.7%) reference a token. Within one visual family — a single-layer steel drop shadow, `0 Ypx Bpx rgba(0,45,58,α)` — there are 189 declarations carrying 118 distinct values. At the single alpha `.08` there are 22 distinct geometries: 0 8px 20px, 0 8px 22px, 0 10px 24/26/28px, 0 12px 26/28/30/36px, 0 14px 34/36/38px, 0 16px 38/40/42/44px, 0 18px 40/44/46/48/50/52px. The token's own geometry `0 18px 48px` is separately hand-typed at .08, .09, .1 and .12, so editing `--shadow-soft` moves some cards and not others. The differences are below perceptual threshold — the cost is not that the site looks wrong, it is that the elevation system cannot be adjusted from one place.
- **Recommendation:** Define a four-step elevation scale in `:root` — `--shadow-1: 0 8px 22px rgba(0,45,58,.06)`, `--shadow-2: 0 14px 34px rgba(0,45,58,.08)`, `--shadow-3: 0 18px 48px rgba(0,45,58,.12)`, `--shadow-4: 0 30px 90px rgba(0,45,58,.28)` — then map the 189-declaration single-layer steel family onto them by alpha band (.05-.07 to --shadow-1, .08-.1 to --shadow-2, .11-.16 to --shadow-3, above to --shadow-4). Do this as a mechanical substitution in main.scss and verify by re-running the count: `box-shadow` distinct values should fall from 212 toward the low tens and `var(--shadow` references should exceed 200. Do not touch multi-layer or non-steel shadows in the same pass. Screenshot-diff two representative card routes before and after to confirm no visible delta — the premise is that there is none.
- **Why:** Product pages are the pages a paid or organic visitor lands on with buying intent, and they are the only page family on the site with zero credibility signal before the first scroll. The component built to solve that is present and switched off.
- **Affected:** 14 routes using `fg-hero--compact`: casement-windows, flush-casement-windows, tilt-turn-windows, sliding-sash-windows, heritage-windows, upvc-doors, french-doors, patio-doors, aluminium-doors, aluminium-bifold-doors, integral-blinds, secondary-glazing, double-glazing-replacement, window-and-door-repairs (roof-lanterns also uses the class but renders its own hero markup).
- **Evidence:** template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:3254, :3292-3299. src/scss/main.scss:3393, :3402. Byte measurement across casement-windows/upvc-doors/patio-doors/french-doors/tilt-turn-windows html: hidden panel = 1100 bytes each, hidden intro = 256-344 bytes. probe-desktop.json headings for /casement-windows/, /upvc-doors/, /patio-doors/ all contain `{"lvl":2,"text":"Get pricing or book a design chat.","size":21.6,"hidden":true}`. Confirmed visually against shots/desktop/casement-windows--fold.png (no lead, no card) vs composite-doors--fold.png (lead + fact strip present).
- **Verification:** The measurements are close to exact — I reproduced them independently — but the 'why' argues against itself, and the impact rests on a user-visible claim the finding itself disproves two sentences earlier.

MY RECOUNT of live/main.css: 334 `box-shadow` declarations (finding: 334, exact), 212 distinct values (exact), 118 distinct values in the single-layer steel family `0 Ypx Bpx rgba(0,45,58,α)` across 189 declarations (finding: 117 — one off, from a slightly narrower alpha pattern). The `.08` cluster is real and I listed it: 0 8px 20px, 0 8px 22px, 0 10px 24/26/28px, 0 12px 26/28/30/36px, 0 14px 34/36/38px, 0 16px 38/40/42/44px, 0 18px 40/44/46/48/50/52px — 22 distinct geometries at one alpha. The token's own geometry `0 18px 48px` is retyped at .08, .09, .1 and .12, exactly as claimed, so editing `--shadow-soft` would indeed move some cards and not others. Tokens confirmed at main.scss:69-70.

CORRECTIONS: token-referencing declarations are 29, not 26, giving 8.7% not 7.8%. Family distinct count is 118, not 117. `0 18px 42px` is listed in the finding's `.08` cluster but does not exist at that alpha.

WHY IT NEEDS REVISING, not just renumbering: the 'why' says "cards at the same conceptual depth sit at visibly different weights across routes," and the recommendation says "Nobody can distinguish a 34px blur from a 38px blur at 8% alpha." Both cannot be true. The measurable fact is that the values are noise; the visual consequence is asserted with no evidence and contradicted in the same finding. I found no screenshot pair demonstrating two same-depth cards reading differently. What is left is a genuine, well-measured maintainability defect — the two tokens are decorative because 91% of shadows bypass them — which is worth fixing but is not a High/Medium user-facing problem. Type stays Objective (consistency is on the objective list); impact drops to Low.

#### [26] `--fg-font-size-max` governs 48 of ~153 display clamps; eight rules retype its value by hand

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** STYLE.md:229 instructs that 'New large type must use the shared token as the maximum value'. `var(--fg-font-size-max)` is referenced 48 times in main.scss; a further ~105 `font-size: clamp()` rules with an upper bound of 2.5rem or more hardcode a rem literal instead. Eight of those hardcode literally `3.6rem`, the token's own current value (main.scss:901, 1479, 4142, 24432, 26856, 28533, 29331, 30541). Nothing renders wrong today — STYLE.md:44 records that existing oversized clamps were already capped at the token's value — but the token is not authoritative: lowering `--fg-font-size-max` would move 48 rules and silently leave ~105 behind, eight of which would keep rendering at the old ceiling while appearing to comply. The hardcoded bounds also drift with no pattern (2.5, 2.55, 2.6, 2.65, 2.7, 2.75, 2.8, 2.85, 2.9, 3, 3.1, 3.15, 3.2, 3.25, 3.3, 3.35, 3.4, 3.45, 3.5, 3.55, 3.6rem). Two rules exceed the ceiling outright: `.fg-cas-num` `clamp(2.6rem, 5vw, 4.4rem)` at main.scss:37685, which is the 70.4px measured on /casement-windows/ and is covered by the fg-cas exception at STYLE.md:30-40, and `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-sash-gallery__head h2` `clamp(2.4rem, 4vw, 4rem)` at main.scss:31609, which has no recorded exception and should be checked.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the eight literal `3.6rem` upper bounds (main.scss:901, 1479, 4142, 24432, 26856, 28533, 29331, 30541) with `var(--fg-font-size-max)` — a zero-visual-change edit that makes the token authoritative. Ask the owner whether the sliding-sash 4rem at main.scss:31609 is intended; if not, cap it at the token. Then map the remaining hardcoded bounds onto three display steps (`--fg-display-sm: 2.6rem`, `--fg-display-md: 3.1rem`, `--fg-display-lg: var(--fg-font-size-max)`).
- **Why:** A design contract whose named reference contradicts it stops being usable. Every future page built "like roof lanterns" will inherit the divergence, and the eyebrow slot STYLE.md:259 reserves for the location line is spent on the brand name the header logo already states, on 14 pages.
- **Affected:** /roof-lanterns/ (pattern divergence). Brand-name eyebrow on 14 routes: casement-windows, flush-casement-windows, tilt-turn-windows, sliding-sash-windows, aluminium-windows, upvc-doors, french-doors, patio-doors, aluminium-doors, aluminium-bifold-doors, integral-blinds, secondary-glazing, double-glazing-replacement, window-and-door-repairs. Compliant: composite-doors, roof-lanterns, heritage-windows ("Sheerline Classic").
- **Evidence:** STYLE.md:329 and :259. scratchpad/shots/desktop/roof-lanterns--fold.png (eyebrow, H1, CTA pair, full-bleed photo, no lead, no fact list) vs composite-doors--fold.png (eyebrow, H1, lead, CTA pair, image alongside, four-fact strip). Section order for roof-lanterns: `fg-hero--compact | fg-product-pulse | fg-tech-banner | fg-roof-lantern-views | fg-roof-lantern-intro`. Eyebrow extraction across scratchpad/live/*.html.
- **Verification:** The mechanism is real and the safe edit is correct, but the count is off by one rule and the framing overstates it. VERIFIED EXACTLY: `var(--fg-font-size-max)` appears 48 times in main.scss. The literal-3.6rem clamp upper bounds sit at main.scss:901, 1479, 4142, 24432, 26856, 28533, 29331 and 30541 — the eight lines the finding lists. CORRECTIONS: (1) there is no ninth. `grep -n 'font-size:.*3\.6rem' main.scss` returns exactly 8 lines, so 'nine rules retype its value' should be eight. (2) My parse of clamp font-size rules with a literal upper bound >=2.5rem gives 105, not 106 (48 + 105 = 153, not 154) — immaterial but the number should be stated as approximate. The hardcoded bounds do drift as described; I recovered 2.5, 2.55, 2.6, 2.65, 2.7, 2.75, 2.8, 2.85, 2.9, 3, 3.1, 3.15, 3.2, 3.25, 3.3, 3.35, 3.4, 3.45, 3.5, 3.55, 3.6, plus 4 and 4.4. (3) The rule cited does not say what the finding implies. STYLE.md:229 says 'NEW large type must use the shared token' — forward-looking — and STYLE.md:44 records that 'Existing oversized clamps have been capped at this token', i.e. the existing hardcodes were already brought under the ceiling by value. So the 105 hardcoded bounds are not rule breaches today; nothing renders wrong. The only unambiguous defect is the 8 literal duplicates of the token's own value, and the only cost is a hypothetical future ceiling change. That makes this Low impact, not Medium. (4) A genuine addition the finding missed: two source rules exceed the 3.6rem ceiling outright — `.fg-cas-num` at main.scss:37685 `clamp(2.6rem, 5vw, 4.4rem)` (this is the 70.4px the lead auditor measured on /casement-windows/, and STYLE.md:30-40 sanctions the fg-cas namespace as its own brief) and `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-sash-gallery__head h2` at main.scss:31609 `clamp(2.4rem, 4vw, 4rem)`, which has no documented exception.

#### [30] Title-tag separator and length conventions break on four routes

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** There is no transition or easing token in `:root` — src/scss/main.scss:41-79 is the entire block and holds colour, gradient, two shadows, container width, header height and the type ceiling, nothing about motion. The compiled CSS contains 106 distinct `transition` values and eight distinct `cubic-bezier()` curves, six of which are the same ease-out to within rounding: (0.16,0.72,0.2,1), (0.2,0.7,0.2,1), (0.2,0.72,0.18,1), (0.2,0.75,0.25,1), (0.2,0.8,0.2,1) and (0.22,0.7,0.2,1). Durations are written in both notations for identical values — `transform .18s ease` appears 4 times alongside `transform 180ms ease` 34 times — so a grep for one misses the other. Twenty-five distinct ms durations are in use (80 through 900) plus four in `s` notation (.18s, .2s, .28s, .55s), with no rule about which applies to what; 180ms accounts for 110 of the declarations and 160ms for 43, so a three-step scale would already cover most of the file.
- **Recommendation:** Add `--fg-ease: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.72, 0.2, 1)`, `--fg-dur-fast: 120ms`, `--fg-dur: 180ms`, `--fg-dur-slow: 260ms` to the `:root` block at src/scss/main.scss:41-79. Replace the six near-identical beziers with `--fg-ease` (a no-visual-change edit, the differences are below perception) and convert the four `s`-notation values to `ms`. Keep (0.22,1,0.36,1) and (0.5,0,0.2,1) as separate named tokens since they are genuinely different curves.

Mixed ms/s notation confirmed. Two numeric details in the description are wrong and understate the problem: `transform .18s ease` occurs 4 times (not 3) and `transform 180ms ease` occurs 34 times (not 5); and the duration inventory is far wider than the seven values listed — the transition declarations alone use 80, 120, 140, 150, 160, 180, 200, 220, 240, 260, 280, 320, 360, 430, 450, 480, 500, 520, 600, 620, 650, 700, 720, 800 and 900ms, plus .18s, .2s, .28s and .55s in the other notation. No project doc rules on motion tokens (only STYLE.md:288, 'Remove motion that does not help comprehension or conversion', which is unrelated), so this is not an owner decision. #### [27] `button--outline` is emitted on two pages but has zero CSS, so an intended secondary renders as a green primary

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The SCSS defines exactly three button variants: `.button--ghost`, `.button--light`, `.button--steel`. `button--outline` has zero rules in the 42,407-line stylesheet and zero in the compiled 694KB main.css, yet it is emitted from two templates — template-parts/sections/roof-lanterns.php:263 and template-parts/sections/flat-rooflights.php:117 — and appears on both live pages. The element falls through to base `.button` and renders as a solid green primary. In practice it is the only CTA in its `.fg-roof-related__card` cross-link block, so the visual result is a lone green button that looks fine (verified on shots/desktop/roof-lanterns.png); the defect is that a class written in the template has no effect and nothing in the build warns. STYLE.md:39 already records this deviation on the roof lantern and heritage pages and rules that the current CTA standard wins, so the intent is documented — it simply has not been actioned. Separately, `.button--ghost` has two rule blocks (main.scss:1525 and the panel-scoped `.fg-customer-portal-help .button--ghost` at :31882) and is emitted from four PHP call sites (customer-portal.php:17 and :59, about.php:159, home-hero.php:17), rendering live on /about/ and /customer-portal/.
- **Recommendation:** Change `button--outline` to `button--steel` in BOTH roof-lanterns.php:263 and flat-rooflights.php:117 so the class matches a variant that exists. Do NOT delete `.button--ghost`: it has four call sites and a panel-scoped rule at main.scss:31882, and removing it would turn the two dark-panel CTAs on /customer-portal/ into green primaries. If the owner wants the ghost variant retired, convert all four call sites first (`button--light` on the dark panels, `button--steel` on /about/), re-render those routes, then remove both rule blocks.
- **Why:** A price page is where a visitor decides whether the number is credible, and it is the one page family carrying no evidence that anyone was happy with the work. The component exists, is already used on 28 routes, and takes a context argument built for exactly this.
- **Affected:** 5 routes worth changing: /composite-door-prices/, /window-door-prices-milton-keynes/, /colour-options/, /handle-options/, /obscured-glass/. 5 further routes without reviews where it is arguably correct.
- **Evidence:** Section-index scan of scratchpad/live/*.html for `fg-review-showcase|fg-trust-reviews`: index -1 on areas-we-cover, case-studies, colour-options, commercial-glazing, composite-door-prices, fensa-approved-installers, handle-options, obscured-glass, what-is-a-door-lintel, window-door-prices-milton-keynes. AI.md:215-224 contains no per-route gate.
- **Verification:** The unstyled class is real; the stated consequence is not, the scope is half of what it should be, and the second half of the recommendation would break live pages. VERIFIED: `grep -c 'button--outline' src/scss/main.scss` = 0 and it is also 0 in the compiled live/main.css, while roof-lanterns.html contains it — so it does fall through to base `.button` and render green. CORRECTIONS: (1) SCOPE. It is emitted by two templates, not one: template-parts/sections/roof-lanterns.php:263 and template-parts/sections/flat-rooflights.php:117. I curled https://fensterglazing.com/flat-rooflights/ (200) and found the class there too. Fixing only roof-lanterns leaves the identical defect on /flat-rooflights/. (2) CONSEQUENCE IS WRONG. The claim that 'the visitor sees two identical green primaries' does not hold. I read the live markup: the link is the only CTA inside `.fg-roof-related__card`, a lone cross-link card. I then cropped shots/desktop/roof-lanterns.png at y=3300-4400 and looked at it — 'View flat rooflights' renders as a single solid green pill in a white card with no second button anywhere in the block. Nothing about the rendered page reads as a broken CTA hierarchy; the defect is that a class the author wrote has no effect, which is a source-integrity problem, not a visual one. That drops the impact to cosmetic/none today. (3) THE GHOST RECOMMENDATION IS UNSAFE. `.button--ghost` is emitted from four PHP call sites — customer-portal.php:17 and :59, about.php:159, home-hero.php:17 — and I curled https://fensterglazing.com/customer-portal/ (200) and found 2 occurrences. It also has a dedicated scoped rule `.fg-customer-portal-help .button--ghost` at main.scss:31882 written for that dark panel. 'Used exactly once across 40 pages' is true of the sample but the sample is 40 of 712; deleting the variant would silently turn the customer portal's dark-panel CTAs into green primaries. (4) The STYLE.md citation is line 39, not 35, and that line already names this exact deviation ('The heritage and roof lantern pages ... use button--outline / button--ghost / button--light as secondary actions ... the rule wins'), so the 'nothing warns about it' framing is wrong — the project docs already flag it. It is a recorded known deviation rather than a deliberate owner ruling, so it is still worth fixing.

#### [20] 168 hex colours where 113 are perceptually redundant, 60 ad-hoc steel alphas, and one token defined and never used

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The palette is 10 named colour tokens at main.scss:42-51, but the compiled CSS contains 168 distinct hex values plus 384 distinct rgba() values. CIELAB clustering at deltaE<5 yields 20 multi-member clusters covering 113 collapsible values: 41 near-whites (#ffffff plus 40 off-whites such as #f7fbfa, #f4f7f6, #f5f7f7, #eef3f2), 20 pale border greys around `--color-line: #d6e0e3`, 7 members in the `--color-steel` cluster (#002d3a plus #0c313b, #022b35, #0b3039, #082c35, #0a313c, #16333d) and 7 in the `--color-ink` cluster. Token adoption is weak in specific places: `var(--color-surface)` is referenced 6 times while literal white appears 488 times (40 `#ffffff` + 448 `#fff`), and `--color-light-blue: #4c7b86` is defined at main.scss:51 and referenced zero times anywhere — a dead token. The 621 `rgba(0,45,58,…)` literals span 60 distinct alpha values once `.05`/`0.05` forms are normalised, including the indistinguishable .025/.03/.035 and .05/.055/.06 steps. The differences are below perceptual threshold, so the cost is that the brand cannot be retuned from the tokens, not that the site visibly mismatches.
- **Recommendation:** Three safe moves and one unsafe one to avoid. Safe: (1) delete `--color-light-blue` from main.scss:51 — zero references, verifiable by grep. (2) Add a steel alpha ladder (`--steel-a06`, `--steel-a08`, `--steel-a12`, `--steel-a16`, `--steel-a24`, `--steel-a45`) and map the 60 ad-hoc alpha steps onto the nearest rung. (3) Collapse the `--color-steel` and `--color-ink` clusters to their tokens. UNSAFE without an exclusion list: collapsing the 41 near-whites. `--fg-page-gradient` at main.scss:64-68 ends `linear-gradient(135deg, #eef5f4, #ffffff 44%, #e8f1f0)`, and #eef5f4 sits at deltaE 4.72 from #ffffff — inside the cluster. A blind replace flattens the site background gradient. Exclude every hex that appears inside a `gradient(` declaration before running the substitution, and screenshot-diff the homepage and one product page afterwards.
- **Why:** Three identical headings in one document is a genuine outline defect for screen-reader users navigating by heading, and it wastes the two strongest on-page heading slots on a string the H1 already owns. The fix pattern is already written and proven on two routes.
- **Affected:** 5 routes: /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /aluminium-windows/, /french-doors/, /integral-blinds/, /patio-doors/. A further 7 repeat it twice (H1 + pulse only): casement-windows, upvc-doors, sliding-sash-windows, heritage-windows, flush-casement-windows, aluminium-doors, and roof-lanterns near-repeats it (H1 "Sheerline S1 roof lanterns" vs pulse H2 "Sheerline S1 roof lantern").
- **Evidence:** probe-desktop.json headings. /french-doors/: idx0 H1 "French Doors", idx1 H2 24.5px "French Doors", idx3 H2 46.1px "French Doors" (immediately preceding H3 "Classic double opening"). Same shape on /patio-doors/, /integral-blinds/, /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /aluminium-windows/. Gate at template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:4031; admission at :174 and :3525-3534.
- **Verification:** The headline measurements reproduce, but three secondary numbers are wrong and — more importantly — the recommendation is not the Low-risk find-and-replace it is billed as.

REPRODUCED EXACTLY: 168 distinct hex values, 384 distinct rgba values, 621 `rgba(0,45,58,…)` literals, `var(--color-surface)` used 6 times, `#ffffff` literal 40 + `#fff` literal 448 = 488, `var(--color-light-blue)` used ZERO times while `--color-light-blue: #4c7b86` is defined at main.scss:51 — that token is genuinely dead. My own CIELAB deltaE<5 greedy clustering over the 168 normalised hexes gives 55 clusters, 20 of them multi-member, covering 113 redundant values — the '113 collapsible' figure is exact. The 41-member near-white cluster is exact (#ffffff, #f4f7f6, #f7fbfa, #f5f7f7, #f8fbfa, #f3f8f7, #f7faf8, #f7fbf9, #eef3f2 …). The 20-member pale-grey cluster around `--color-line: #d6e0e3` is exact. The `--color-ink` cluster has 7 members.

WRONG: (1) "11 named tokens" — main.scss:42-51 defines 10 colour tokens (ink, muted, line, surface, soft, accent, accent-dark, steel, steel-90, light-blue). (2) "39 distinct alpha steps" for the steel rgba literals — normalising `.05`/`0.05` duplicates, there are 60 distinct alpha values, not 39. Worse than claimed. (3) "7 near-twins of --color-steel" — the cluster is 7 members total, so 6 twins plus the token itself. The listed hexes are all real.

RISK IS UNDERSTATED, and this is the substantive revision. "Collapse the 41 near-whites to --color-surface and --color-soft" would break the page gradient. `--fg-page-gradient` at main.scss:64-68 ends with `linear-gradient(135deg, #eef5f4, #ffffff 44%, #e8f1f0)` — three deliberately different near-whites whose whole purpose is to differ. I measured #eef5f4 at deltaE 4.72 from #ffffff, so a <5 clustering rule swallows it and a blind find-and-replace would flatten the site's background gradient to flat white. The same trap applies to any near-white used as a gradient stop or as a hairline against another near-white. The recommendation needs an explicit exclusion for values inside gradient declarations, and the risk is Medium, not Low.

Also, as with finding 19, the 'why' is self-defeating: deltaE<5 is by the finding's own definition the threshold below which two colours read as the same, so "panels that should share a background sit a shade apart between routes" cannot follow from a <5 clustering. This is maintainability debt, not a visible defect. The brand-green twins (#31b86e, #2fb66d) and accent-dark twins (#087943, #248a52) each appear exactly once in the whole stylesheet, so their practical cost is near zero.

#### [25] Four components break the 8px card-radius guidance, including an 18px card on ~51 county pages that the 40-page sample hid

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** STYLE.md:209 says 'Cards should normally use `8px` border radius or less'. 8px is indeed dominant (294 of 41 distinct radii). The breaches, ordered by how many pages actually render them: `.fg-county-operations__cards article` is 18px and renders on the ~51 `/commercial-glazing-<county>/` pages (emitted at template-parts/sections/commercial-county.php:204; confirmed live on /commercial-glazing-buckinghamshire/ — it is absent from the 40-page sample, not from the site); `.fg-order-process__card` is 12px on 15 sampled pages (main.scss:11078); `.fg-cs-card`, the case-study card, is 12px on 14 (main.scss:12886); `.fg-ph-tile` 10px on 3; `.fg-handle-colour-banner__panel` 12px on 1. `.fg-cookie-consent__panel` is 20px (main.scss:1592, with a deliberate 16px `@media (max-width: 560px)` override at :1873) and appears on all 40 pages, but it is a modal dialog rather than a card, so whether the card rule governs it is a judgement call. `.fg-cd3-types__panel` 22px, `.fg-cd3-tile` 16px, `.fg-composite-colour-card` 10px and `.fg-home-case-card` 14px render on zero pages and belong to the dead-code finding.
- **Recommendation:** Set `.fg-county-operations__cards article` (18px), `.fg-cs-card` (main.scss:12886) and `.fg-order-process__card` (main.scss:11078) to `border-radius: 8px`, taking the county pages first since they are the widest breach. Add `--fg-radius: 8px` and `--fg-radius-pill: 999px` as tokens so the next component inherits the decision. Leave the cookie dialog alone unless the owner wants dialogs to follow the card rule — decide that explicitly rather than as a side effect.
- **Why:** A screen-reader user landing on the strip hears a broken sentence, and the redundant aria-label duplicates a heading that is already in the accessibility tree. It is a two-line fix and it stops the same bug recurring as more routes get sentence titles.
- **Affected:** /tilt-turn-windows/ (verified in live HTML) and /aluminium-flush-windows/ (same code path, not in the Tier-1 set). The redundant-label issue affects all 13 Tier-1 routes rendering the strip.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/components/product-pulse.php:60 `aria-label="<?php echo esc_attr($pulse_title . ' key specifications'); ?>"`. generated-page.php:3536-3538 sets the sentence titles. scratchpad/live/tilt-turn-windows.html renders `aria-label="Liniar EnergyPlus, in four figures. key specifications"`.
- **Verification:** Every measurement reproduces, but one component was wrongly dismissed as dead and it is the second-widest breach on the site. VERIFIED: live/main.css has 41 distinct border-radius values with 294 uses of 8px; .fg-cs-card 12px (main.scss:12881 selector, radius on :12886), .fg-order-process__card 12px (:11066/:11078), .fg-cookie-consent__panel 20px (:1587/:1592), .fg-ph-tile 10px, .fg-handle-colour-banner__panel 12px. Render counts across the 40 live pages match exactly: cookie panel 40, order-process card 15, cs-card 14, ph-tile 3, handle banner 1. fg-cd3-types, fg-cd3-tile, fg-composite-colour-card and fg-home-case-card are correctly identified as rendering nowhere (fg-cd3-types/fg-cd3-tile do not appear in composite-doors-v2.php at all). CORRECTIONS: (1) `.fg-county-operations__cards article` at 18px is NOT dead code. It is emitted at template-parts/sections/commercial-county.php:204-206 and I curled https://fensterglazing.com/commercial-glazing-buckinghamshire/ (200) and found 6 occurrences of fg-county-operations. There are 51 /commercial-glazing-<county>/ URLs in the sitemap, so this 18px card — the largest breach in the list — renders on ~51 pages, more than fg-order-process__card (15) and fg-cs-card (14) combined. It was invisible only because county pages are not in the 40-page sample; the finding's own method (grep the sample) is what produced the error. (2) The STYLE.md line is 209, not 208, and it reads 'Cards should normally use 8px border radius or less' — 'normally' makes it guidance, not a hard rule. (3) The 16px cookie value at main.scss:1873 is not 'a second, different radius elsewhere in the file': it is a deliberate `@media (max-width: 560px)` override that also drops the dialog itself to 16px. And .fg-cookie-consent__panel is a modal dialog, not a card, so applying the card rule to it is a design judgement rather than a rule breach — that portion of the finding is Creative. The .fg-cs-card / .fg-order-process__card / .fg-county-operations part remains Objective.

#### [12] `button--outline` is used in live markup but has no CSS, so it renders as a green primary instead of a secondary

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 89% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The SCSS defines exactly three button variants: `.button--ghost`, `.button--light`, `.button--steel`. `roof-lanterns.html` emits `button--outline`, which has zero rules anywhere in the 42,407-line stylesheet — I confirmed the count is 0. The element therefore falls through to base `.button` and renders as a solid green primary. Wherever the author intended a secondary action on that page, the visitor sees two identical green primaries, which contradicts STYLE.md:264's rule that the CTA pair is "green then dark". Separately, `.button--ghost` carries two rule blocks (main.scss:1525 and :31882) but is used exactly once across all 40 sampled pages — one link on /about/ — and STYLE.md:35 already records that `button--ghost` contradicts the current CTA rule. `button--next`/`button--prev` appear 30 times each in HTML but only ever as `.fg-review-showcase__button--next/prev`, so those are correctly scoped and not orphans.
- **Recommendation:** In `roof-lanterns.html`'s source template, change `button--outline` to `button--steel` (or `button--light` if it sits on a dark panel) so the CTA pair reads green-then-dark. Then delete `.button--ghost` (main.scss:1525 and :31882) and convert the single /about/ usage to `button--steel`, which removes the variant STYLE.md already flags as contradicting the rule.
- **Why:** A class that exists in markup with no styling is a silent failure — it looks deliberate in the template and wrong on the page, and nothing in the build warns about it. It also means a page the project treats as a reference is shipping the wrong CTA hierarchy.
- **Affected:** /roof-lanterns/ (button--outline, 1 instance); /about/ (button--ghost, 1 instance). Variant definitions at src/scss/main.scss:1525, :31882.
- **Evidence:** `grep -c 'button--outline' src/scss/main.scss` = 0 while roof-lanterns.html contains it; `.button--ghost` defined at main.scss:1525 and :31882, 1 occurrence across 40 live HTML files (about.html); STYLE.md:35 and :264.
- **Verification:** Both halves check out, and the counts were re-measured rather than trusted. I evaluated inc/site-data.php in PHP 8.2 and called fenster_site_data(): window_handles.finishes 6, door_handles.finishes 8, patio_handles.finishes 5, lift_slide_handles.finishes 5, upvc_door_renders 13, notan_blind_colours 9, colour_options.materials.upvc 17, .aluminium 13 — every number in the finding's evidence block is exactly right, including the 17/13 that are 16 foils + Smooth White and 12 colours + Any RAL (which is why the recommendation's parenthetical matters: a naive count assertion at 16 and 12 would fail). inc/product-hub-data.php:747 is the sprintf with the $words map; :727, :768 and :789 are the three hardcoded sibling headings, exactly as quoted. All fourteen colour-count prose sites opened and confirmed: casement-windows-v2.php:183 ('Sixteen foils, plus smooth white…') and :534 ('the same sixteen colours'); tilt-turn-windows-v2.php:125 ('Sixteen colours outside'); generated-page.php:2495 ('Sixteen uPVC foils'); upvc-doors-v2.php:313 ('Thirteen foils, bonded on…'); heritage-windows-v2.php:123 and :280; heritage-aluminium-doors.php:441 and :479; aluminium-doors-v2.php:108; blind-colour-grid.php:34; blinds-visualiser.php:184; generated-page.php:2549 and :4160; product-hub-data.php:321. If anything the scope is understated, not overstated — a case-insensitive sweep also finds the same hardcoded numbers in inc/site-data.php:2065 and :2100, inc/generated-pages.php:378 and inc/blog-posts.php:2098/:2111. Corroborating rather than contradicting: components/upvc-colour-grid.php:25-26 records in a comment that this component previously hardcoded 'Sixteen colours outside' and that it was wrong on the doors route, i.e. this exact class of bug has already fired once here.

#### [31] The enquiry copy panel stretches to the form's height, leaving two thirds of it empty on 16 product routes

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `main.scss:18036-18041` sets `.fg-enquiry__grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(360px, 0.78fr) minmax(620px, 1.22fr); gap: 1.25rem; align-items: stretch; }`. The left copy panel holds only an eyebrow, the heading, two lines of copy and a phone/email line, while the right column holds the full multi-field form. Because the grid stretches, the copy panel is forced to the form's height. Measured on shots/desktop/upvc-doors.png: the panel spans y=9451 to y=10342 (891px), its last content ends at y≈9753, leaving ~590px — 66% of the panel — as flat dark-teal with only a faint decorative glow in it. STYLE.md:139 says 'Do not use excessive empty space as a substitute for hierarchy.' Note `align-items: stretch` is also redundant here, since stretch is the grid default.
- **Recommendation:** Change `align-items: stretch` to `align-items: start` at src/scss/main.scss:18040 so the copy panel sizes to its content, or move reassurance content that already exists elsewhere on these pages (the FENSA/Trustpilot strip) into the panel to fill it with something useful. `align-items: start` is preferable — it is one line and reads calmer. Re-check /composite-doors/ and /aluminium-windows/ after the change, since they carry the same grid and were not in the original affected list.
- **Why:** Muscle memory matters on the one form a returning trade contact fills in twice. There is no reason for the two contact fields to swap places when a third is added, and it is the kind of drift that indicates the commercial branch was written rather than derived.
- **Affected:** /commercial-glazing/ (and, at template level, other commercial routes using the same branch).
- **Evidence:** probe-desktop.json `forms[0].fields` — 28 routes: `name,phone,email,location,message,attachments[],privacy`. /commercial-glazing/: `name,company,email,phone,location,message,attachments[],privacy`. /book-a-consultation/ is the third variant (no attachments field).
- **Verification:** Real, and I reproduced the void, but three details are wrong. (1) Line cite: the `.fg-enquiry__grid` block opens at src/scss/main.scss:18036 and `align-items: stretch` is at :18040 — 18037 is `display: grid`. The declaration is also redundant, since `stretch` is the grid default, so the recommended one-line change to `start` is correct and sound. (2) Coordinates and magnitude: on shots/desktop/upvc-doors.png (1440x11746) the copy panel spans y=9451 to y=10342 (891px tall); its last content, the phone/email line, ends at y≈9753. That leaves ~590px empty, 66% of the panel, not 'roughly the bottom half', and the section starts at y≈9370, not y≈9250. (3) Scope: 16 of the 40 sampled routes carry `fg-enquiry__grid`, not 14 — the 14 listed plus aluminium-windows and composite-doors. I confirmed the town-matrix pages do NOT carry it (`grep -c fg-enquiry__grid` = 0 on the live /composite-doors-wolverton/ fetch), so the scope does not extend to the 525-page matrix. STYLE.md:139 is quoted correctly and verbatim. Creative/Low is the right call.

#### [13] fenster_ad_attribution_request_allowed() is defined in website-tracking.php but also used by ad-attribution.php, with nothing at the call site naming where it lives

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 45% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** inc/ad-attribution.php:195 registers fenster/v1/ad-click with 'permission_callback' => 'fenster_ad_attribution_request_allowed', a function defined in inc/website-tracking.php:136 and used there for fenster/v1/ad-attribution at :132. Nothing at either site records the dependency. This is a readability cost only, not a fragility one: the callback is a string resolved when rest_api_init dispatches, and functions.php:41-43 require_once's the whole $fenster_required_files list before that, so reordering the list cannot break it and only deleting or renaming the function can — which would surface as a PHP fatal from WP_REST_Server's call_user_func(), not a silent loss of attribution. Separately, and independently of where the function lives, the check itself (inc/website-tracking.php:138-141) is `hash_equals($site_host, $origin_host)` on the request's Origin header, which any non-browser client sets freely; it is CSRF hardening rather than authentication. The consequence stays bounded because both handlers only write transients keyed on a journey id validated against `^FG(?:2|A)-[A-Z0-9-]{8,80}$` and the click id against a tight gclid/gbraid/wbraid pattern (:155-158).
- **Recommendation:** Low priority. Either add a one-line comment at inc/ad-attribution.php:195 naming inc/website-tracking.php as the defining file — the way functions.php:27-28 documents the traffic-classification ordering — or move the four-line function into inc/traffic-classification.php, which both consumers already load. Do not justify the move as a load-order fix; it is not one.
- **Why:** Spacing is what STYLE.md:171-184 calls section continuity, and it is the dimension most responsible for a page reading as one composition rather than stacked blocks. With 514 padding values, that quality is re-decided from scratch in every section and cannot be reviewed or repeated.
- **Affected:** Site-wide, all 38 routes. 514 padding values, 175 gap values, 94 section-rhythm expressions.
- **Evidence:** `:root` at src/scss/main.scss:41-79 contains no spacing token; live/main.css 514 distinct padding values, 175 distinct gap values, 42 static rem gaps, 94 distinct `padding:clamp(…) 0` section expressions across 40 distinct upper bounds; STYLE.md:171-184.
- **Verification:** The facts are right but the mechanism — which is the whole substance of the finding — does not hold. Confirmed: `grep -rn fenster_ad_attribution_request_allowed` returns exactly three hits (inc/ad-attribution.php:195 registration, inc/website-tracking.php:132 registration, inc/website-tracking.php:136 definition); functions.php:34 requires website-tracking.php and :35 requires ad-attribution.php, with the documented ordering comment at :27-28 for traffic-classification.php; and the check at :138-141 is indeed Origin-header equality, i.e. CSRF hardening, not authentication. REFUTED, though: 'it works only because functions.php happens to require website-tracking.php first' and 'reordering $fenster_required_files breaks a route registered in a different file'. The permission_callback is a STRING, and it is passed to register_rest_route() inside fenster_register_ad_click_route(), which is hooked on rest_api_init (inc/ad-attribution.php:189). Every entry in $fenster_required_files is require_once'd in the foreach at functions.php:41-43, long before rest_api_init fires, and PHP function definitions are global once included — so the name is never resolved at include time and load order is irrelevant here. There is no file-scope call to the function in ad-attribution.php. The 'silent break' claim is also wrong in the other direction: WP_REST_Server calls the permission callback with call_user_func(), so a missing function is a PHP fatal / 500, not a silently lost attribution. What survives is much smaller: a function is defined in a different file from one of its two consumers, with no comment saying so. That is a code-locality preference, not a fragility hazard, so the type moves to Creative and the confidence drops.


### H. Mobile

#### [203] Colour, handle and configuration heading blocks never collapse to one column at 390px — 17 pages, 7 selectors

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.fg-upvc-colours__heading`, `.fg-handle-finishes__heading`, `.fg-alu-colours__heading`, `.fg-heritage-door-colours__heading`, `.fg-blind-colours__heading`, `.fg-heritage-door-configurations__heading` AND `.fg-heritage-door-use__heading` — seven selectors, not six — share one rule: `display:grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 0.8fr) minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: clamp(2rem,6vw,7rem); align-items:end`. There is no media-query override for this selector anywhere in the compiled CSS (verified against all 185 @media blocks by brace-depth scan). At 390px the computed value is `148.438px 185.562px` — the H2 sits in a 148px column and the intro paragraph in a 186px column. The arithmetic confirms it independently: a 32px gap (the clamp floor) inside a 366px container splits 0.8:1 to exactly 148.44/185.56. On /casement-windows/ the H2 "Sixteen colours outside, matched or white inside." wraps to five lines in its 148px column, sitting bottom-aligned under a large empty gap because of `align-items: end`, while the paragraph beside it runs nine lines of three to five words. The eyebrow above spans the full 366px (`.eyebrow{grid-column:1/-1}`), so the reader gets a full-width label followed by two starved columns. This is a desktop composition rendered verbatim on a phone, against STYLE.md:343 ("Use the 860px breakpoint") and STYLE.md:345 ("A sticky, cinematic or multi-column desktop section needs a simpler mobile equivalent").
- **Recommendation:** Add to the same rule block — and make sure the seventh selector `.fg-heritage-door-use__heading` is included, it is in the same comma list and is easy to miss: `@media (max-width: 860px) { grid-template-columns: 1fr; column-gap: 0; row-gap: .75rem; align-items: start; }`. That single media query fixes all 17 affected pages. Do NOT bother removing the `max-width: 20ch` on the H2 — at 390px that h2 computes to 23.2px so 20ch is ~232px, well clear of the 148px column; the grid column is the only thing starving it and the max-width never binds at mobile.
- **Why:** `/composite-doors/` and `/roof-lanterns/` have no other way to browse the range — the wall is the range. Anyone not using a mouse currently cannot reach the 33 doors or 26 lanterns past the first screenful.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:1007-1133`. Two routes: `/composite-doors/` (33 doors + 33 aria-hidden clones), `/roof-lanterns/` (26 cards).
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:1045-1053` (`tick` writes `viewport.scrollLeft` per frame), `1114-1117` (scroll listener bails while `frame !== null`), `1067-1075` (only pointerenter/pointerleave pause). Markup: `<div class="fg-cd3-wall__viewport" data-fg-door-wall tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Composite door styles. Drag or scroll sideways to explore.">` in `live/composite-doors.html`.
- **Verification:** The defect is real, visually confirmed and the numbers reproduce to three decimal places. I am revising it because the affected scope is understated by six pages — including one the finding itself measured — the selector list is incomplete, and one line of the recommendation is unnecessary.

FULLY REPRODUCED: the compiled live CSS carries the base rule exactly as quoted (`display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0, 0.8fr) minmax(0, 1fr);column-gap:clamp(2rem,6vw,7rem);align-items:end`). I verified the 'no media-query override' claim properly rather than by grep: I parsed all 185 `@media` blocks in live/main.css, computed their character ranges by brace-depth scan, and tested all 4 occurrences of `fg-upvc-colours__heading` — every one is at BASE, none inside any media block. Zero overrides, confirmed.

The 148.438/185.562 measurement is arithmetically self-consistent, which is the strongest possible check on a CDP number: at 390px, `clamp(2rem, 6vw, 7rem)` = clamp(32, 23.4, 112) = 32px gap; with a 366px container, (366-32) x 0.8/1.8 = 148.44 and x 1/1.8 = 185.56. Exact. The eyebrow spanning full width is confirmed by the companion rule `.fg-upvc-colours__heading .eyebrow{grid-column:1/-1}`.

I looked at scratchpad/mfold/cas-colours.png. It is worse than described and plainly broken: a full-width 'COLOUR' eyebrow, then a bottom-aligned H2 stranded in a narrow left column under a large empty gap (the `align-items:end`), with the paragraph beside it running nine lines of three-to-five words. The finding says the H2 is 4 lines; in the screenshot it is 5 ('Sixteen / colours / outside, / matched or / white inside.'). STYLE.md:343 and :345 are quoted verbatim and correctly.

SCOPE UNDERSTATED. I grepped each heading class across all 712 crawled pages. The union is 17 pages, not 11. The finding's list omits `/composite-doors/` — which its own evidence section says it measured at the same 148.438/185.562 split — and also omits `/bow-bay-windows/`, `/french-casement-windows/`, `/aluminium-flush-windows/`, `/aluminium-sliding-doors/` and `/heritage-aluminium-doors/`. `/composite-doors/` is in the 38-route Tier-1 set, so the Tier-1 count is 12, not 11.

SELECTOR LIST INCOMPLETE. The shared rule carries a seventh selector the finding does not list: `.fg-heritage-door-use__heading`. Anyone applying the fix to only the six named classes leaves that one broken on `/heritage-aluminium-doors/`.

UNNECESSARY RECOMMENDATION. 'remove the `max-width: 20ch` on the H2 below 860px' does nothing. That h2 is sized `clamp(1.45rem, 2.2vw, 2rem)` = 23.2px at 390px, so 20ch is roughly 232px — well above the 148px grid column, which is what is actually starving it. Collapsing the grid to one column is the whole fix. (This also confirms 202 and 203 are independent, not duplicates: these H2s carry their own clamp and are not among the 48px ones.)

#### [223] The base `h2` clamp is inert — every unstyled H2 renders a hard 48px at 390px

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `[data-fg-aw-story]` drives a 241-frame WebP sequence from scroll position. `handleScroll` requests `desiredFrame ± 14` on every scroll event (src/js/main.js:4978-4981), so scrolling through the section once fetches essentially every frame. Measured byte-exact: desktop 241 files / 12,246,326 bytes (11,959KB, avg 50KB, first frame 169,230 bytes); mobile 241 files / 6,092,202 bytes (5,949KB, avg 25KB). Both sets return 200 on live. The lead auditor's recorded weights (main.css 694KB, main.js 139KB, HTML 93-320KB) do not include any of it, so /aluminium-windows/ is roughly forty times heavier than its recorded number for a desktop visitor who reads the page. The canvas is `aria-hidden="true"`, so none of the payload carries content value or is indexable. Three things bound the exposure and should be stated: `useMobileFrames` is `max-width: 700px` (4866), so a phone pulls the 5,949KB set, not 12MB; `preloadFrames()` only seeds its every-24th skeleton when the section is within 1.2 viewports (4962-4965), so a visitor who never scrolls that far downloads one 169KB frame; and main.js:4972 forces `progress = 0` under `prefers-reduced-motion`, pinning `desiredFrame` at 0 so a reduced-motion visitor fetches roughly 25 frames rather than the sequence.
- **Recommendation:** Two options, in order of preference. (1) Replace the frame sequence with the all-intra H.264 scrub the project already built for `[data-fg-scrub-video]` — PROGRESS.md:2889 records that the scrub videos were re-encoded all-intra with a half-width mobile encode, and prestige-window-scrub.mp4 does the same job in 573,329 bytes. (2) If frames must stay, halve the sequence to ~120 frames, re-encode lower (50KB average is high for a canvas capped at 1.5x DPR by `sizeCanvas`), and narrow the ±14 preload window at src/js/main.js:4978 to ±4, leaning on the existing every-24th skeleton. Either way, gate the whole thing on `navigator.connection.saveData` / `effectiveType` the way `video[data-fg-lazy-video]` already does at src/js/main.js:4822-4827.
- **Why:** 48px display type is the single largest driver of wasted vertical space on 25 of 38 Tier-1 routes at mobile, and it is applied indiscriminately — the same size lands on "Privacy where the room needs it." (an art-directed product moment) and on "Related products and service areas" (a link list header). Fixing one line recovers roughly 100–170px per occurrence and restores the intended type hierarchy across the whole site.
- **Affected:** 37 H2 elements at exactly 48px across 25 of 38 Tier-1 routes at 390px. Worst: /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /aluminium-doors/, /aluminium-windows/, /flush-casement-windows/, /french-doors/, /heritage-windows/, /integral-blinds/, /obscured-glass/, /patio-doors/, /tilt-turn-windows/, /upvc-doors/, /window-and-door-repairs/ (2 each).
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:1482-1484 `h2 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 3rem, 3.4rem); }`. Live measurement at 390x844 via CDP: `section.fg-links-band > div.container > div.section-heading > h2` computed fontSize = 48px on /contact/ and /double-glazing-milton-keynes/; `.fg-product-gallery-band--glass .section-heading--wide > h2` = 48px on /casement-windows/. probe-mobile.json headings: 37 lvl-2 headings at 48.0px across 25 routes; probe-desktop.json: 38 at 48.0px — identical count at 1440px, proving zero viewport response.
- **Verification:** Every number is exactly right — I recomputed them from the files rather than from `du` — but two mitigations are missing and two citations in the recommendation are wrong. Verified byte-exact: frames-desktop 241 files / 12,246,326 bytes = 11,959KB, avg 50KB, frame-001 = 169,230 bytes; frames-mobile 241 files / 6,092,202 bytes = 5,949KB, avg 25KB. `data-frame-count="241"` and `aria-hidden="true"` are both on the canvas in live/aluminium-windows.html. Both frame sets are live: frames-desktop/frame-060.webp → 200, 60,086 bytes; frames-mobile/frame-241.webp → 200. The ±14 preload loop is at src/js/main.js:4978-4981 exactly as described, plus an every-24th skeleton at 4964. Missing mitigations that change the picture: (1) main.js:4972 is `const progress = reduceMotion ? 0 : clamp(-rect.top / scrollable)` — a reduced-motion visitor pins `desiredFrame` at 0, so they fetch only frames 1-15 plus the ~10 skeleton frames, not the sequence. (2) `useMobileFrames` is `max-width: 700px` (4866), so a phone gets the 5,949KB set and only a desktop scrolling the section pulls 11.96MB; and `preloadFrames()` (4960-4966) only seeds the skeleton when the section is within 1.2 viewports, so a visitor who never scrolls that far downloads one 169KB frame. Wrong citations in the recommendation: the all-intra rationale is at PROGRESS.md:2889 ('scrub videos are all-intra now, with a half-width mobile encode listed first'), not at main.js:5050 — the comment there is about the scrub video not being the bifold traveller and about verification by asserting on the seek. The `saveData`/`effectiveType` gate is real but at main.js:4822-4827, not 4825 exactly. `prestige-window-scrub.mp4` is 573,329 bytes as claimed. No owner ruling covers this: the only doc mention is PROGRESS.md:4585, which records adding the frame folders to git so the story works on test.

#### [228] "The tool on the right is live" — there is no right at 390px

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 99% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The /online-quote/ page lists three reassurance bullets above the quote tool. The first reads "The tool on the right is live. Start clicking whenever you like". At 390px the layout is single column and the WindowCAD iframe sits 518px below the bullet, not to its right. A phone visitor is told to look somewhere that does not exist. This is the only spatial-direction copy on the site that breaks at mobile — the other `left-hand`/`right-hand` matches in the codebase are legitimate product descriptions (handle handing variants at inc/site-data.php:2372, sash-bar positions at casement-windows-v2.php:110) and code comments.
- **Recommendation:** Change `template-parts/sections/online-quote.php:152` from "The tool on the right is live. Start clicking whenever you like" to a direction-free phrase such as "The tool is live. Start clicking whenever you like" — the "Open quote tool" button directly above already handles wayfinding on both layouts. No CSS change needed.
- **Why:** It is a one-word fix on a high-intent conversion page, and the current sentence makes the site look like it was written for desktop and shipped to mobile without a read-through — which undermines the credibility of the quote tool it is trying to introduce.
- **Affected:** /online-quote/ (1 route, 1 line). The same section template is not reused on /3d-visualiser/, which carries the same iframe but different copy.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/sections/online-quote.php:152 `<li><?php esc_html_e('The tool on the right is live. Start clicking whenever you like', 'fenster'); ?></li>`. Screenshot scratchpad/mfold/online-quote-top.png at 390x844 shows the bullet at y~800 CSS px with "The quote tool LIVE" heading and the iframe starting below it. CDP measurement: iframe getBoundingClientRect = {w:364, h:518, y:712} on a single-column layout.
- **Verification:** Reproduced line for line. `src/js/main.js:4472` is `carousel.setAttribute('tabindex', '0');` and 4506 is `slide.setAttribute('aria-hidden', absOffset < 0.5 ? 'false' : 'true');` inside `render()`, so with six slides exactly one is exposed. `template-parts/sections/heritage-aluminium-doors.php:235` is `<div class="fg-colour-carousel fg-heritage-door-configurations__carousel" data-fg-colour-carousel>` — no `role`, no `aria-label`, and the only accessible names anywhere in the block are the prev/next button labels and the bare `<span data-fg-colour-count>01 / 06</span>` at 250 with no live region. The slides are `<article>` elements containing an `<img>`, `<h3>` and `<p>` with no focusable descendants, so the recommendation to stop writing `aria-hidden` is safe. The contrast with the site's own pattern is real and I verified it live: `data-fg-colour-rail-viewport tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="uPVC colours. Scroll or swipe sideways."` and `data-fg-door-wall tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Composite door styles. Drag or scroll sideways to explore."` are both in the served HTML. Scope is right: `data-fg-colour-carousel` appears in exactly one PHP file and `curl https://fensterglazing.com/heritage-aluminium-doors/` returns it live. Nothing in AI.md/STYLE.md/HANDOVER.md rules on it.

#### [225] Sash and case-wall carousel pagination buttons are 6px and 9px tall — mobile-only controls

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `@media(max-width:860px) .fg-sash-carousel__dots button { width:28px; height:6px; padding:0 }` (48x6 when `aria-pressed=true`) and `@media(max-width:860px) .fg-home-case-wall__dots button { width:9px; height:9px; padding:0 }`. These are real `<button>` elements with real labels (`aria-label="Show Heritage Rose"`, `"Show Ultimate Rose"`, `"Show Charisma Rose"`) that switch the sash model. They exist only at mobile — the desktop layout hides them (`display:none` at base). A 28x6px target with an 8px gap fails WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): the control is under 24x24 CSS px and the spacing exception does not apply because 24px circles centred on these buttons would overlap. STYLE.md:350 states plainly that no mobile work is complete with unusable tap targets. Mitigating: prev/next arrow controls exist alongside the sash dots and measured above 44px, so the dots are a secondary path.
- **Recommendation:** Keep the pill and dot visuals exactly as they are, but make the button itself the hit area: `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button { height: 44px; padding: 19px 0; background: none; }` with the coloured pill moved to a `::before` at `height:6px; width:28px`. Same treatment for `.fg-home-case-wall__dots button` (44px box, 9px `::before` dot). Reduce `gap` to `.25rem` to compensate for the wider hit boxes.
- **Why:** On the sash page these dots are the only visible indicator of which of three Rose models is on screen, and on the homepage they are the only pagination for the case-study wall. A 6px-tall control on a phone is a miss on the first attempt for most thumbs, and it is the kind of defect that reads as unfinished rather than minimal.
- **Affected:** /sliding-sash-windows/ (3 dots, 28x6 and 48x6) and / (homepage case wall, 9x9 dots). Mobile viewports only (<=860px).
- **Evidence:** Compiled CSS: `@media(max-width: 860px) .fg-sash-carousel__dots button{width:28px;height:6px;padding:0;border:0;border-radius:999px}` and `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button[aria-pressed=true]{width:48px}`; `@media(max-width: 860px) .fg-home-case-wall__dots button{width:9px;height:9px;padding:0}`. probe-mobile.json smallTargets on /sliding-sash-windows/: `{tag:button, txt:"Show Heritage Rose", w:28, h:6}` x2 and `{txt:"Show Ultimate Rose", w:48, h:6}`. Markup in live/sliding-sash-windows.html: `<button type="button" data-fg-sash-dot="1" aria-label="Show Heritage Rose" aria-pressed="false"></button>`.
- **Verification:** Reproduced exactly. `src/js/main.js:2972` reads `if (event.key !== 'Escape' || !siteHeader.classList.contains('is-nav-open')) return;` and `is-nav-open` is only ever set by the `.site-nav-toggle` click handler (2941) and cleared by the <=860px resize guard (2978) — it is the mobile drawer state, so Escape is inert for the desktop panel. There are exactly three `Escape` listeners in the whole file (837 = Legend chat, 2972 = mobile drawer, 7019 = gallery lightbox); none of them touches `.site-nav__mega`. The desktop panel is opened by `item.addEventListener('focusin', openPanel)` at 2866 and closed only by `focusout` after an 80ms `item.contains(document.activeElement)` check (2853-2859), i.e. only when focus has already left the whole item. Markup confirmed: `inc/template-tags.php:74` emits `echo '<div class="site-nav__mega" hidden>';` and the `<li>` at line 52 builds `$item_classes` with no `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`; live `home.html` shows `<li class="site-nav__item has-children has-mega-menu"><a href="https://fensterglazing.com/windows-milton-keynes/">Products</a><div class="site-nav__mega" hidden>` — zero aria state. One correction that strengthens rather than weakens the finding: the Products mega contains 34 anchors plus a `data-mobile-menu-back` button (balanced-div parse of home.html), not 'twenty', and Commercial contains 18. Impact/type/scope all stand.

#### [188] Nine of fifteen pages exceed 15,000px on mobile, and on nine of them the fixed tail is longer than everything said about the product

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** Measured live at 375x812: casement 21,752; aluminium-windows 21,058; flush-casement 20,362; upvc-doors 19,817; aluminium-doors 19,739; patio-doors 17,806; heritage 17,517; bifold 17,113; tilt-turn 16,626. The repeating tail — FAQ, order rail, quote embed, reviews, case studies, enquiry, related links — measures 6,000–9,100px and is essentially fixed regardless of what the page is selling. On /patio-doors/ the product gets 4,138px of 17,806 (23%); on /aluminium-windows/ 3,659px of 21,058 (17%); on /aluminium-bifold-doors/ 4,558px of 17,113 (27%); on /aluminium-doors/ 5,081px of 19,739 (26%). The two biggest tail blocks are `fg-enquiry` (1,520px) and `fg-links-band` (up to 1,777px of nine image tiles plus up to eighteen town chips).
- **Recommendation:** Attack the tail, not the product content. Three specific cuts, in order: collapse `fg-links-band` on mobile to a single column of six text links with no images (saves ~1,100px on eleven routes); drop the generic "Specification choices" preamble as above (~450px on eight); hide the mobile quote iframe as composite already does (~490px on eleven). That is ~2,000px off nine pages without touching a word of product copy. Only then consider whether both the review wall and the case-study strip need to run at full height on the same page.
- **Why:** A 20,000px mobile page is roughly 25 screens. The material a buyer needs is 20–27% of it on the four weakest routes, and everything they do not need is the part that repeats.
- **Affected:** 9 of 15 audited routes over 15,000px mobile; the tail components render on 13.
- **Evidence:** Live per-section measurement at 375x812 on all 15 routes (page heights and section heights listed above); e.g. /aluminium-doors/ tail = gallery 800 + colours 1254 + handles 1499 + FAQ 974 + order 1131 + quote 892 + reviews 921 + cs-strip 1766 + enquiry 1520 + links 1690 = 12,447px of 19,739.
- **Verification:** Reproduced on every number. `template-parts/sections/commercial-county.php:268` is `foreach (array_slice(array_values($related_links), 0, 24) as $link)` inside the `.generated-links` div, exactly as cited. I extracted that div from crawl/commercial-glazing-kent.html: exactly 24 anchors, the first six being /commercial-glazing/, /commercial-windows-and-doors/, /curtain-walling/, /louvre-vents/, /commercial-automation/, /commercial-projects/, then counties bedfordshire → greater-london in slug order, terminating at Greater London as claimed. Inbound-link count across the full 712-page crawl (whole document, not just `<main>`, so nav and footer are included): 51 county pages, 19 with 51 inbound sources and 32 with zero — the 32 are precisely the alphabetically-after-Greater-London set the finding lists, including commercial-glazing-northamptonshire and commercial-glazing-oxfordshire. The /commercial-areas/ escape hatch is dead as described: it returns 200 with `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow,max-image-preview:large">`, links 47 county slugs, appears 0 times in page-sitemap.xml, is absent from the 712-page crawl and has 0 inbound internal links of its own — so it discovers nothing. The AI.md precedent is cited correctly: the Commercial Hub Rule records 'The hub linked five of twelve until 2026-08-12', the identical orphaning class, fixed at the hub tier and not swept down to the county tier.

#### [229] The header Call and Menu buttons shrink to 40px tall below 560px

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `@media(max-width:860px)` sets `.site-header__mobile-call { min-height:46px; font-size:.9rem }` and `.site-nav-toggle { min-height:46px }` — correct. A second block at `@media(max-width:560px)` then overrides both back down to `min-height:40px` with `padding-inline:.65rem` and `font-size:.84rem`. Measured live at 390x844: the "Call us" pill renders 87x40 and the brand link 142x36. The Call pill is the only persistent phone affordance anywhere on mobile — there is no sticky bottom call bar and no `tel:` link in the mobile nav panel — and it is simultaneously the smallest interactive control in the header. It appears in probe-mobile.json smallTargets on all 38 of 38 routes.
- **Recommendation:** Add `role="status" aria-atomic="true"` to the `<figure class="fg-rp-diag__part" data-fg-diag-panel>` at `template-parts/sections/window-door-repairs.php:570` — that is the element containing `[data-fg-diag-sub]`, `[data-fg-diag-name]`, `[data-fg-diag-what]` and `[data-fg-diag-fix]`. There is no `.fg-rp-diag__panel` in the file. No JavaScript change is needed: `showPart()` (main.js:8149) already writes into those nodes. Note the figure is server-rendered empty and filled by the controller's first `showPart` call, so expect one announcement at hydration; if that is unwanted, set the attribute in JS after the initial `showPart` rather than in the markup.
- **Why:** Phone calls are the highest-value conversion for a local installer, and on mobile this button carries all of that traffic. Taking it from 46px to 40px saves six pixels of header height and costs first-tap accuracy on the one control that matters most.
- **Affected:** Every route, at viewports <=560px. probe-mobile.json flags `site-header__mobile-call` at 87x40 on 38 of 38 routes.
- **Evidence:** Compiled CSS: `@media(max-width: 860px) .site-header__mobile-call{min-height:46px;padding:.55rem .8rem;font-size:.9rem}` then `@media(max-width: 560px) .site-header__mobile-call{min-height:40px;padding-inline:.65rem;font-size:.84rem}` and `@media(max-width: 560px) .site-nav-toggle{min-height:40px;padding-inline:.65rem}`. Live CDP at 390x844: headerBtns = [{t:'Fenster Glazing', w:142, h:36}, {t:'Call us', w:87, h:40}, {t:'Menu', w:67, h:45}], header height 77px, position:fixed.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and reproduced; only the recommendation's selector is wrong. CONFIRMED: `grep -c 'aria-live\|role="status"' template-parts/sections/window-door-repairs.php` → 0, while `grep -rl 'aria-live' template-parts/` returns five other files (generated-page.php, handle-chooser.php, blinds-visualiser.php, enquiry-form.php, legend-assistant.php) and not this one. `src/js/main.js:8149-8188` `showPart()` writes `panel.image.src/alt`, `panel.sub`, `panel.name`, `panel.what`, `panel.fix` and `panel.caption` by `textContent` and toggles `.is-active` on the SVG groups, with no announcement anywhere; the only AT signal is `aria-pressed` flipped in `selectSymptom` at 8193. WRONG: the recommendation names `.fg-rp-diag__panel`, which does not exist in the file. The wrapper holding `[data-fg-diag-name]`, `[data-fg-diag-what]` and `[data-fg-diag-fix]` is `<figure class="fg-rp-diag__part" data-fg-diag-panel>` at window-door-repairs.php:570. Applying the fix as written would silently do nothing. Also worth flagging: those nodes are empty on server render and populated by the controller's first `showPart` call, so a naive `role="status"` will fire an announcement on initial hydration — the attribute should go on the `<figure>` and the initial population should happen before the attribute is meaningful, or be set with `aria-atomic="true"` and accepted as one extra announcement.

#### [130] Eleven of sixteen product pages exceed 15,000px on mobile, and the fixed tail is 6,000-9,100px of it regardless of the product

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Measured live at 375x812: casement 21,752; aluminium-windows 21,058; flush-casement 20,228; upvc-doors 19,976; aluminium-doors 19,739; patio-doors 17,722; french-doors 16,953; heritage 17,455; bifold 17,113; tilt-turn 16,626; integral-blinds 15,039.
