The repeating tail — FAQ, order rail, quote embed, reviews, case studies, enquiry, related links — measures 6,000-9,100px and is essentially fixed regardless of what the page sells (on /aluminium-doors/ that tail is 8,894px of 19,739). The two biggest tail blocks are fg-enquiry, a flat 1,520px everywhere, and fg-links-band at 1,377-1,747px of eight or nine image tiles plus town chips. Product share varies more than the tail does: /patio-doors/ gives the product 4,028px of 17,722 (23%) and /aluminium-bifold-doors/ 5,646px of 17,113 (33%), while /aluminium-windows/ actually gives it 9,446px of 21,058 (45%) once its 5,067px fg-aw-story scroll hero is counted.
- **Recommendation:** Attack the tail. In order of measured payoff: collapse fg-links-band on mobile to a single column of six text links with no images (~1,100px on eleven routes, band measured 1,377-1,747px); adopt composite's collapsed quote block, which measures 559px against 892px elsewhere (~333px on ten routes); and delete rather than merely rewrite the generic Specification choices band where the colour and handle grids already render inline (up to 800px on eight routes — a copy rewrite alone only buys 87px, see finding 129). That is roughly 1,500-2,200px off eleven pages without touching product copy. Only then ask whether the review wall and the case-study strip both need full height on the same page.
- **Why:** Three clusters of self-competition on top of zero internal signalling. The cheap half of the fix (linking) is already required by the orphan finding, so this costs almost nothing extra to test, and consolidation is irreversible so it should follow rather than lead.
- **Affected:** 13 informational URLs across 3 clusters
- **Evidence:** Word counts and titles from the 712-page crawl; all 13 confirmed to have zero inbound internal links. GSC figures for /soundproof-windows/ from SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md §3.
- **Verification:** The measurements are excellent — I reproduced four page heights to the pixel and the aluminium-doors tail arithmetic exactly — but the route count is understated, one product-share figure is wrong by 2.6x, and two of the three quantified savings are inflated. CONFIRMED live at 375x812: casement 21,752; aluminium-windows 21,058; aluminium-doors 19,739 with tail = gallery 800 + colours 1,254 + handles 1,499 + FAQ 974 + order 1,131 + quote 892 + reviews 921 + cs-strip 1,766 + enquiry 1,520 + links 1,690 = 12,447 exactly as stated; bifold 17,113; tilt-turn 16,626. fg-enquiry is 1,520px on every route measured; fg-links-band ranged 1,377-1,747px. WRONG COUNT: it is 11 of 16 product routes over 15,000px, not 9 of 15 — /french-doors/ (16,953px measured live) is absent from the audited set entirely, and /integral-blinds/ is 15,039px. /composite-doors/ at 14,809px is the only near-miss. WRONG SHARE: the /aluminium-windows/ figure of "3,659px of 21,058 (17%)" is fg-product-why (1,853) + fg-product-intel (1,806) only. It ignores fg-aw-story, a 5,067px bespoke scroll-scrub hero that carries the H1 and the product argument, plus the 313px pulse and 407px tech banner. True product share is 9,446 of 21,058 = 45%. That single datapoint is the one used to call aluminium-windows the weakest route. SAVINGS INFLATED: the spec-choices rewrite saves 87px, not ~450 (casement's variant is 713 against 800 — see finding 129); composite's quote block measures 559px against 892px elsewhere, so hiding the mobile iframe saves ~333px, not ~490. Only the links-band figure (~1,100) holds. Realistic total is ~1,520px, not ~2,000. Minor internal inconsistency: the problem text defines the tail as FAQ→links (8,894px on aluminium-doors, inside the stated 6,000-9,100 band) but the evidence line's 12,447px figure includes the gallery, colour and handle sections, which the same paragraph treats as product finishes.

#### [231] Legend's roaming animation in the chat drawer has no pause mechanism

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 80% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `startRoaming()` (`src/js/main.js:373`) schedules an endless cycle via `scheduleNextRun()` (383-397): idle 2800-3400ms, translate across the stage for 2200ms, recurse, for as long as the drawer is open. The only suppression is `prefers-reduced-motion` at 378 and `sleepLegend()` at 176, and sleep is cancelled by any interaction, so an engaged user never gets a still panel. WCAG 2.2.2 requires a pause/stop/hide mechanism for motion that starts automatically, runs beyond five seconds and is presented in parallel with other content; there is none. Scale, for accuracy: the roamer lives in `<div class="legend-assistant__stage" aria-hidden="true">` inside the drawer header (`legend-assistant.php:44`), which is `flex: 0 0 150px` at the top of a `100dvh` panel, and it moves `--legend-roam-distance` = 86px desktop / 62px mobile over 2200ms linear (`main.scss:2334, 2301, 2763`). The composer is at the bottom of the same drawer, separated by the message log and the consent block — so this is peripheral motion beside the transcript a user is reading, not motion on the caret.
- **Recommendation:** Stop the roam whenever the user is engaged with the drawer's content, not just its input: call `stopRoaming()` on `input` focus and while `replyTimer` is set (a reply streaming in is exactly when the transcript is being read), and restart on blur once no reply is pending. Add the listeners next to `startRoaming` at `src/js/main.js:373`. If a real WCAG 2.2.2 control is wanted rather than a heuristic, put a persistent pause toggle in the drawer header beside the close button at `legend-assistant.php:53` and have it call `stopRoaming()`/`startRoaming()`, persisting the choice alongside the existing Legend state.
- **Why:** Regulators expect withdrawing consent to be as easy as giving it; the give-consent buttons in the modal are 335x50 and the withdraw control is 179x20. Beyond compliance, a 20px-tall button at the bottom of a 15-screen page on a phone is effectively not there.
- **Affected:** All routes. `site-footer__cookie-settings` 179x20 flagged on 27 routes, `site-footer__stat-settings` 179x20 on 30 routes, footer nav links 162x42 across 468 sampled instances, "Privacy Policy" 179x31 on 87 instances.
- **Evidence:** Compiled CSS: `.site-footer__cookie-settings,.site-footer__stat-settings{padding:0}` (base, no mobile override) and `@media(max-width: 560px){.site-footer__bottom{font-size:.78rem}} @media(max-width: 560px){.site-footer__nav a{min-height:42px;padding:.42rem 0;font-size:.82rem}}`. probe-mobile.json smallTargets aggregate: `{tag:button, cls:'site-footer__stat-settings', w:179, h:20}` x30, `{cls:'site-footer__cookie-settings', w:179, h:20}` x27, `{a, w:179, h:31, txt:'Privacy Policy'}` x87, `{a, w:162, h:42}` x468. Consent modal buttons measured 335x50 at the same viewport for comparison.
- **Verification:** The mechanism is real; the described harm is not. CONFIRMED: `startRoaming()` at 373 calls `scheduleNextRun()` which recurses unconditionally (383-397) — idle for 2800/3400ms, run for 2200ms, forever. `grep -n 'stopRoaming()\|startRoaming()'` returns only 176 (sleepLegend), 202/213 (wakeLegend restart), 374 (self-clear), 701/713 (openChat), 731 (restoreOpenChat), 743 (closeChat): there is no pause on input focus, no pause control, and the only suppression is `reduceMotion.matches` at 378. REFUTED on placement, which is the whole basis of the stated harm. `template-parts/components/legend-assistant.php:44-52` puts the roamer inside `<div class="legend-assistant__stage" aria-hidden="true">` inside `<header class="legend-assistant__header">` — the header is `flex: 0 0 150px` at the TOP of a `height: 100dvh` drawer (main.scss:2168-2210), and the composer (`legend-assistant.php:78`) is at the BOTTOM, separated by the `legend-assistant__messages` log and the consent section. It is not 'directly above the composer' or 'two inches above the caret'; it is a full drawer-height away. The motion is also small: `.legend-assistant__roamer` (main.scss:2334) transitions `transform 2200ms linear` over `--legend-roam-distance: 86px` desktop / `62px` at the mobile breakpoint (2301, 2763), inside a 150px-tall header. So this is a WCAG 2.2.2 gap (auto-starting motion over 5s presented in parallel with content, no pause mechanism) rather than a distraction sitting on the caret, and the recommended focus/blur fix is aimed at the wrong problem — it would not stop the motion for anyone reading the transcript, which is where it actually sits.

#### [224] Sliding-sash carousel position dots are 6px-tall clickable controls on mobile

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button` (src/scss/main.scss:23786) is `width: 28px; height: 6px`, widening to 48px when `aria-pressed="true"`. These are real `<button>`s with click handlers that jump between the three Roseview models, and probe-mobile.json measured them on /sliding-sash-windows/ at 48x6 and 28x6. A 6px-tall hit area is awkward to hit accurately on a phone. This is not a WCAG 2.5.8 failure — the criterion's 'Equivalent' exception applies, because `.fg-sash-carousel__controls` sits directly above the dots with 48x48 prev/next buttons and an aria-live '01 / 03' counter that reach all three models, an arrangement HANDOVER.md:619 records as accepted. The dots also satisfy AI.md's rule that dots be native buttons with accessible labels. The argument for changing it is consistency and hit accuracy: the two other dot patterns in this codebase deliberately avoided the problem — `.fg-home-product-theatre__mobile-dots [data-fg-mobile-product-dot]` is `pointer-events: none` (an indicator beside real prev/next buttons) and `.fg-cd3-collections__dots span` is not a control at all. The sash dots are the only place a 6px bar was left clickable.
- **Recommendation:** At src/scss/main.scss:23786, keep the 6px visual but give the button a real hit area: `height: 24px; padding: 9px 0; background-clip: content-box; background-color: rgba(0,45,58,.18);` and move the active-state `width` change onto the same content box. The design is unchanged and the target becomes 28x24 / 48x24.
- **Why:** These blocks introduce the colour and hardware sections — the parts of a product page a homeowner actually shops. On a phone the intro copy is currently unreadable at a 186px measure, and the section reads as broken rather than considered. Two declarations in one media query fix eleven product pages.
- **Affected:** 11 Tier-1 routes carry at least one of these heading blocks: /casement-windows/, /aluminium-windows/, /aluminium-doors/, /aluminium-bifold-doors/, /flush-casement-windows/, /upvc-doors/, /patio-doors/, /french-doors/, /tilt-turn-windows/, /heritage-windows/, /integral-blinds/. Most carry two (colours + handles).
- **Evidence:** Compiled CSS rule (base, no media override): `.fg-heritage-door-configurations__heading,.fg-heritage-door-colours__heading,.fg-upvc-colours__heading,.fg-blind-colours__heading,.fg-alu-colours__heading,.fg-handle-finishes__heading{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0, 0.8fr) minmax(0, 1fr);column-gap:clamp(2rem,6vw,7rem);align-items:end}`. Live CDP measurement at 390x844 on /casement-windows/: `gridTemplateColumns: "148.438px 185.562px"`, children measured H2 w=148 h=128, P w=186 h=299. Same 148.438/185.562 split measured on /aluminium-windows/, /composite-doors/ and /heritage-windows/. Screenshot: scratchpad/mfold/cas-colours.png and cas-handles.png.
- **Verification:** The measurement is right and the inconsistency argument is right, but the WCAG framing is wrong and it is the whole basis for the 'Medium' impact. Verified: src/scss/main.scss:23786-23794 is `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button { width: 28px; height: 6px; ... }` with `[aria-pressed="true"]` widening to 48px at 23796; the compiled rule matches; probe-mobile.json for /sliding-sash-windows/ lists `{button,"Show Ultimate Rose",48,6}`, `{button,"Show Heritage Rose",28,6}` and `{button,"Show Charisma Rose",28,6}`. The comparison claims are also correct: `.fg-home-product-theatre__mobile-dots [data-fg-mobile-product-dot]` really is `pointer-events:none` (8px indicators with real controls beside them) and `.fg-cd3-collections__dots span` really is a `<span>`. But WCAG 2.5.8 has an explicit 'Equivalent' exception: the criterion is not failed when a different control achieving the same function, meeting the size requirement, exists on the same page. live/sliding-sash-windows.html carries `.fg-sash-carousel__controls` immediately above the dots with `data-fg-sash-prev` / `data-fg-sash-next` buttons and a live-region '01 / 03' counter, and the compiled CSS sizes them `width:48px;height:48px`. Three models are reachable from those, so the dots are supplementary and 2.5.8 is not failed. HANDOVER.md:619 documents this arrangement as accepted behaviour ('previous/next controls, position dots and a visible model counter'), and AI.md's carousel rule ('Dots must be native buttons with accessible labels') is satisfied — each dot has an aria-label. So what is left is a real but smaller thing: a 6px-tall clickable target is genuinely hard to hit on a phone, and it is inconsistent with the two other dot patterns in the same codebase. The recommended fix is still exactly right and still cheap. Impact drops to Low.

#### [227] Legend's drawer opens as a dialog but does not receive focus for 1.44 seconds

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** ? · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `travelLegend()` runs a WAAPI animation with `duration = 1440` (`src/js/main.js:338`) and awaits `motion.finished` (364). `openChat()` sets `panel.hidden = false` at 698 — the panel slides in over 320ms via `legend-panel-in` (main.scss:2189) and is fully visible and clickable — but then `await travel` at 708 defers `input.focus()` to 717. So a `role="dialog"` opens and focus stays on the launcher for 1.44s, which for a keyboard or screen-reader user means the dialog is not announced and is not entered for a second and a half. `isTransitioning` (697) also makes the launcher inert for the same window, so a second press does nothing. If Legend was asleep, `await wakeLegend()` at 691 adds the reversed sleep-frame run (120ms per frame) on top. For comparison the site's own transitions are 120-620ms. The close side is NOT affected: `closeChat` adds `is-closing` before awaiting, and `.legend-assistant__panel.is-closing` (main.scss:2193) runs `legend-panel-out` for 280ms with `fill: both`, translating the panel to `translateX(100%)`, so the drawer is visually gone in 280ms. What persists for the remaining ~1.16s is an off-screen panel whose textarea, send and close controls are still in the tab order.
- **Recommendation:** In `openChat()`, move `input.focus()` (and the `is-open`/`has-arrived` class add) to immediately after `panel.hidden = false`, and let `travelLegend` resolve independently rather than gating the interaction on it — `travel` is already a promise and nothing after it depends on its result except cosmetics. Clear `isTransitioning` on the same tick so a second launcher press is not swallowed. In `closeChat()`, set `panel.hidden = true` on a 280ms timer matched to `legend-panel-out` rather than on `await travel`, so the off-screen panel leaves the tab order when it leaves the screen. Do not change `duration` — the 1440ms jump is fine once nothing waits on it.
- **Why:** 58KB of duplicate font bytes on a 1.6 Mbps connection is roughly 0.3s added to first render on every page, every visit, for zero benefit — and the preload, which exists specifically to speed up text rendering, is currently making things slower rather than faster.
- **Affected:** Every route on the site. Two of three Gibson weights (Regular 31KB, SemiBold 27KB).
- **Evidence:** live/home.html head: `<link rel="preload" ... href="https://fensterglazing.com/app/themes/fenster/assets/fonts/Gibson-Regular.woff2?ver=1783344686" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>`. live/main.css: `@font-face{font-family:"Gibson";src:url("../fonts/Gibson-Regular.woff2") format("woff2"),url("../fonts/Gibson-Regular.otf") format("opentype");font-weight:400}`. CDP Resource Timing at 390px on /casement-windows/: [{u:'Gibson-Regular.woff2?ver=1783344686', kb:31, type:'link'}, {u:'Gibson-Regular.woff2', kb:31, type:'css'}, {u:'Gibson-SemiBold.woff2?ver=1783344686', kb:27, type:'link'}, {u:'Gibson-SemiBold.woff2', kb:27, type:'css'}, {u:'Gibson-Bold.woff2', kb:30, type:'css'}].
- **Verification:** Half of this is right and half is refuted by the CSS. CONFIRMED: `src/js/main.js:338` `const duration = 1440;`; `364` `await motion.finished;`; `openChat` builds `const travel = travelLegend(...)` at 706 and `await travel` at 708, with `input.focus()` not reached until 717 — so the drawer's `role="dialog"` panel is on screen for 1.44s (longer if Legend was asleep: `openChat` also `await wakeLegend()` at 691, which runs reversed sleep frames at 120ms each) before focus enters it, and `isTransitioning` (697) blocks the launcher for that whole window. Reduced-motion bail confirmed at 282. REFUTED: the close claim. `closeChat` adds `is-closing` at 746 before awaiting, and `src/scss/main.scss:2193` gives `.legend-assistant__panel.is-closing { animation: legend-panel-out 280ms ease-in both; }` with keyframes at 2710 running `translateX(0)` → `translateX(100%)`. `fill: both` holds the end state, so the drawer slides fully off the right edge in 280ms — it is NOT 'on screen for 1.44s after you asked it to go'. The residual for the remaining ~1.16s is an off-screen but still-focusable panel, a much smaller problem. The open-side claim is also softer than stated: the panel finishes its 320ms `legend-panel-in` slide and is fully clickable, so a mouse user can click the textarea and type — what is actually broken is that focus is not moved into an opened dialog for 1.44s and the launcher is inert for that time. That is a Low, not a Medium.


### I. Accessibility and motion

#### [218] Review carousel auto-advances every 4.2s on 30 of 40 Tier-1 routes with no pause control

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `startAuto()` (src/js/main.js:6852-6858) sets a 4200ms `setInterval` that scroll-snaps the review track to the next card. The only pausing is `isPaused`, set on `pointerenter`/`focusin`/`touchstart` (6877) and cleared on `pointerleave`/`focusout` (6883) plus a 1800ms grace after `touchend` (6891). A reader who is not hovering — the normal case on a laptop trackpad, and on every phone once the touch grace expires — has the testimonial they are reading slid away every 4.2 seconds. The seven curated cards run 25 to 86 words, which is more than 4.2s of reading. WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide is Level A and requires a pause mechanism; hover is not one, because it is unavailable to keyboard and touch and is not persistent. Two mitigations already exist and should be stated: `startAuto()` returns early when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches (6853), so reduced-motion visitors get no auto-advance; and real prev/next buttons exist. But `prevButton`/`nextButton` (6866, 6873) each call `stopAuto()` and then `startAuto()` again, so using them restarts the timer instead of ending it.
- **Recommendation:** Remove the auto-advance entirely — `prevButton`/`nextButton` already exist and `track` is a native scroll-snap rail, so nothing is lost. If the owner wants it kept, (a) stop calling `startAuto()` inside the prev/next handlers at src/js/main.js:6866-6875 so the first deliberate interaction ends the auto-advance permanently, and (b) add a visible pause/play toggle inside `.fg-review-showcase` that calls `stopAuto()`/`startAuto()` and persists the choice for the session.
- **Why:** Either it is dead code adding two full-page reflows per tap for nothing, or it is live code that abandons the visitor mid-gesture on the highest-value tool on the site. Both are worth resolving, and neither can be resolved by reading.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:5506-5562`. All routes carrying `[data-quote-frame-wrap]` at ≤860px — 21 of the 38 Tier-1 pages contain an iframe.
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:5543-5548` binds `touchstart`/`pointerdown` on the wrapper; `5539` `quoteTouchLockTimer = window.setTimeout(unlockQuotePageScroll, 2400);`; `5532-5536` sets `body{position:fixed}`. Mobile pageHeight from probe-mobile.json: median 13,347px, max 31,310px (`/double-glazing-milton-keynes/`).
- **Verification:** The mechanism is exactly as described and I reproduced every part of it, but two facts are wrong and one material mitigation is missing. (1) Route count: `grep -l data-fg-review-carousel live/*.html` returns 30 files, not 29, out of 40 fetched HTML files, not 38. (2) The finding omits that `startAuto()` at src/js/main.js:6853 begins `if (reduceMotion || autoTimer || cards.length < 2) return;` — a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` visitor gets no auto-advance at all. That does not clear WCAG 2.2.2 (which is not conditional on the media query) but it materially narrows who is affected and it is the kind of thing the owner will check first. Everything else holds: `autoTimer = window.setInterval(..., 4200)` at 6854; the only pause is `['pointerenter','focusin','touchstart']` at 6877 setting `isPaused`, cleared by `['pointerleave','focusout']` at 6883 and by a 1800ms `touchend` timer at 6891; `prevButton`/`nextButton` at 6866/6873 each call `stopAuto()` then `startAuto()`, so using them restarts the timer rather than ending it; there is no pause/play control anywhere in `.fg-review-showcase` (I enumerated every `fg-review-showcase__*` class in live/home.html — button--prev and button--next are the only controls). Review length is if anything worse than stated: the seven home cards run 25–86 words, not 30–60. There is no owner ruling on this: HANDOVER.md:1180-1185 'Shared Review Showcase' documents the summary and the seven cards but says nothing about auto-advance, and AI.md's 'Carousels And Horizontal Scrollers' section (901-908) does not sanction autoplay. AI.md:898 in fact requires autoplay media to have reduced-motion fallbacks, which this has. Impact High is defensible given 30 routes; I would keep it.

#### [140] Mobile nav drawer has no focus containment — Tab walks into page content hidden behind an opaque full-screen overlay

- **Severity:** CRITICAL · **Impact:** High · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `.site-nav` when open is `position: fixed; top: var(--site-header-main-height); left:0; right:0; height: calc(100svh - header); background: … #eef3f2` (src/scss/main.scss:22690-22707) — an opaque overlay covering the entire viewport below the header. The toggle handler (src/js/main.js:2941-2969) sets `is-nav-open`, flips `aria-expanded`, locks body scroll (`html.is-mobile-nav-open { overflow: hidden }`, main.scss:22591-22593) and closes on Escape with focus returned to the toggle — but it never traps focus, never marks the rest of the document `inert`, and never moves focus into the drawer on open. `.site-header__phone` is `display: none` on mobile (main.scss:22623), so the tab stop immediately after the last drawer link is the first link inside `<main>` — content that is 100% covered by the overlay and cannot be scrolled to because the body is locked.
- **Recommendation:** In src/js/main.js:2941-2969, on open set `document.querySelector('main').inert = true` plus `inert` on the footer and the Legend `<aside>`, and clear them on every close path (toggle click, link click, Escape at :2971, the resize handler at :2977). `inert` gives you the focus containment and the AT hiding in one property and is supported in every browser this theme targets. Optionally also move focus to the first drawer row on open. Do not hand-roll a Tab-key trap — the close paths here are already in four places and a manual trap will drift out of sync with them.
- **Why:** On a site where the majority of traffic is mobile, a keyboard or switch user who opens the menu is dumped into invisible content with no way back except Escape, which is undiscoverable. This is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) at AA, and the pattern is well understood — the codebase already gets this exactly right for the cookie modal, which uses a native `<dialog>` and `showModal()`.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages at ≤860px viewport.
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:2941-2969 (toggle handler, no trap/inert), :2971-2975 (Escape handler), :2977-2986 (resize close); src/scss/main.scss:22690-22707 (fixed full-viewport opaque drawer), :22591-22593 (body scroll lock), :22623 (`.site-header__phone { display: none }`).
- **Verification:** Reproduced exactly against the live HTML. The two case-study h3s on /composite-doors/ are 'Flush casement windows and a composite door, Little Horwood' and 'Flush casement windows and a composite door, Wolverton'; I also confirmed them in a live 375px browser, under the heading 'Real installs, photographed on the day.' /upvc-doors/ carries the single card 'Flush casement windows and a composite door, Wolverton' — naming a composite door on the uPVC route where AI.md:513 rules "Composite is named once, in the FAQ, on the owner's instruction that it barely be mentioned." The same two titles render correctly on /flush-casement-windows/, where they lead with the right product.

The recommendation is mechanically sound: fenster_case_studies_for_product() at inc/case-studies-data.php:1691-1698 already iterates each study's `products` array to match a route, so the calling slug is in hand at card-build time, and AI.md:223 does say "fenster_review_cards() accepts a context string so a page can lead with relevant proof" — the precedent is quoted correctly.

Two things a fixer must know that the finding does not mention. First, CASESTUDIES.md:199 records that the study's `title` is "shown as H1 and card title", so a context-swapped card title would deliberately diverge from the study page's own H1 — that is a decision to take, not a free change. Second, and worse in the same category but out of this finding's stated scope: /aluminium-doors/ and /patio-doors/ each show three cards — 'Secondary glazing, Winslow', 'uPVC casement windows, Leighton Buzzard', 'Aluminium bifold doors, Whitehouse' — not one of which is the page's product, because no study claims those routes and the helper falls through to its all-studies fallback (inc/case-studies-data.php:1701-1703, and the fault is named at 1716-1719). Impact 'Low' and type 'Creative' are right for the finding as written.

#### [202] Review carousel auto-advances every 4.2s on 29 of 38 Tier-1 routes with no pause control

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `startAuto()` sets a 4200ms `setInterval` that scroll-snaps the review track to the next card. The only pausing is `isPaused` set on `pointerenter`/`focusin`/`touchstart` and cleared on `pointerleave`/`focusout`. A reader who is not hovering — the normal case on a laptop trackpad and every phone after the 1800ms touchend grace expires — has the testimonial they are reading slid away every 4.2 seconds. Reviews are the site's main social-proof asset and they are 30–60 words each, which is more than 4.2s of reading. WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide is Level A and requires a mechanism to pause; hover is not one, because it cannot be used by keyboard or touch and it is not persistent.
- **Recommendation:** Change `main.scss:1482` to `h2 { font-size: clamp(1.45rem, 3vw, 2.5rem); }` — 23.2px at 390px, 43.2px at 1440px, capped at 40px per STYLE.md:231. Then, in the mobile patch at `main.scss:24083` (which sits inside the `@media (max-width: 860px)` block opened at 22586), delete ONLY the `font-size: 1.65rem` declaration — keep `max-width: 16ch`, which is separate art-direction and not a workaround for this bug. Re-check the 25 affected routes at 390px afterwards.
- **Why:** This is the one piece of auto-motion that sits on top of persuasive text on nearly every page of the site. It costs conversions (a half-read review is worse than no review) and it is a Level A accessibility failure repeated 29 times.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:6846-6859, 6877-6893`. Live on 29 of the 38 fetched Tier-1 routes (all product pages, home, about, contact, online-quote, repairs, why-trust-fenster, both location pages).
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:6854` `autoTimer = window.setInterval(..., 4200)`; pause is only `['pointerenter','focusin','touchstart']` at 6877. Route count from `grep -l data-fg-review-carousel` over `/scratchpad/live/*.html` → 29 files.
- **Verification:** Every factual claim in this finding reproduced exactly. I am revising the impact only, plus one detail in the recommendation that would cause collateral damage.

FULLY REPRODUCED: `src/scss/main.scss:1482-1484` reads `h2 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 3rem, 3.4rem); }` — I read the file at that line. The h1 directly above at 1478 is `clamp(2.1rem, 3.6vw, 3.6rem)`, correctly formed. The clamp is genuinely inert: max(2rem, min(3rem, 3.4rem)) = 3rem = 48px at every width. STYLE.md:231 reads verbatim 'H2 headings should usually stay around `clamp(1.45rem, 2.2vw, 2rem)`. An art-directed product section may rise toward `2.5rem`... but it does not inherit hero scale' — so 48px is 50% over the normal max and 20% over the art-directed ceiling. I re-derived the probe counts myself (the probe's field names are `lvl`/`size`, and I filtered out `hidden:true`): probe-mobile.json = 37 visible lvl-2 headings at exactly 48.0px across 25 of 38 routes; probe-desktop.json = 38 across 26 routes. Identical at 390px and 1440px — zero viewport response, proven. The 'worst' list of 12 routes with 2 each is correct: 12x2 + 13x1 = 37. I also confirmed the sliding-sash patch: a brace-depth scan of main.scss shows line 24083 sits inside `@media (max-width: 860px) {` opened at line 22586, so it is indeed a mobile-only override of this exact value.

NOT A DELIBERATE RULING: PROGRESS.md:2766 and :5113 both mention 48px, but as verification observations ('largest heading 48px against the 57.6px cap', 'shrank the quote heading from 48px to 24px'), not as an owner decision that 48px is the intended h2 size. Nothing in AI.md or STYLE.md sanctions it.

WHY I REVISE IMPACT High->Medium: I listed all 37 headings from the probe. Twenty of them are related-links band headers at the foot of the page — 'Related products and service areas' (12), 'Products, services and nearby areas' (2), 'Products, services and project examples' (2), 'Service areas and related commercial pages', 'Products and services to explore next', 'Products and services mentioned in this guide', 'Products that can use obscured glass'. Wasted scroll at the very bottom of a page, below the last conversion point, is a real but low-consequence cost. The remaining ~17 are genuine in-page product moments where the oversizing does flatten hierarchy. A one-line fix against a documented STYLE rule affecting 25 of 38 routes is solidly Medium; 'High' reads as blocked usability, which this is not — there is no overflow, no clipping and no unreadable text.

RECOMMENDATION DEFECT: 'delete the one-off patch at main.scss:24083' would also delete `max-width: 16ch` from the same block, which is separate art-direction. Delete only the `font-size` declaration.

#### [145] Two invisible sliders are the only keyboard controls for the obscured-glass and integral-blind visualisers, and neither can show a focus ring

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.skip-link { position: absolute; top: 1rem; z-index: 20 }` (src/scss/main.scss:174-183) is a direct child of <body> (header.php:24), a sibling of `.site-header` (site-header.php:10) in the same stacking context. The header is `z-index: 50` sticky on desktop (main.scss:194-198) and `z-index: 1000` fixed at ≤860px (main.scss:22596), with `background: rgba(255,255,255,0.98)` and a 14px backdrop blur. `.skip-link:focus` (main.scss:185-187) changes only `transform`, never `z-index`, so the revealed chip paints underneath the header on every page. Measured live at scrollY=0 on a cold load: the focused link occupies [x16, y16, w131, h46.4], entirely inside the header's [0, 0, 1280, 73] band. It is obscured, not clipped — the earlier "6px above the viewport top" reading was taken at a ~22px scroll offset and does not describe the cold-load state. The link still activates if you press Enter blind; you simply cannot see where focus went.
- **Recommendation:** One declaration: raise `.skip-link` (src/scss/main.scss:174-183) above both header values with `z-index: 2000`. Leave `top: 1rem` alone — at scrollY=0 the focused chip already sits fully in the viewport at y=16, so the `top: 0` change in the original recommendation fixes nothing. Optionally also change `position: absolute` to `position: fixed` so the chip is pinned to the viewport rather than to the document origin. Verify by tabbing once from a cold load with consent already seeded and confirming `document.elementFromPoint()` at the link's centre returns the link itself.
- **Why:** These are the two most involved interactive pieces on the site and neither is operable with any confidence without a mouse. SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible is AA. The remedy costs two CSS rules and the house pattern for it already exists ten thousand lines away in the same stylesheet, which makes this an inconsistency rather than a design decision.
- **Affected:** /obscured-glass/ and /integral-blinds/ (1 page each).
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:10662-10672 (`.fg-obscure-stage__range { opacity: 0.01 }`); grep for `obscure` + `focus` returns only picker-button rules at :10302, :10575, :24692 — nothing for the range. src/scss/main.scss:39371-39380 (`.fg-blind-visualiser__a11y` clip-hidden); template-parts/components/blinds-visualiser.php:110-111 (grabs `aria-hidden="true"`), :113-137 (the two sliders). Correct pattern at src/scss/main.scss:39655-39661.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and the mechanism is exactly as described, but one measurement in it is an artefact of the auditor's scroll position and the recommendation inherits the error. Confirmed: header.php:24 emits `<a class="skip-link">` as a direct child of <body>, immediately before `get_template_part('template-parts/layout/site-header')`, and site-header.php:10 opens `<header class="site-header">` — siblings in the same stacking context. main.scss:174-183 gives the link `position:absolute; z-index:20`; :185-187 `.skip-link:focus` changes only `transform`. `.site-header` is `z-index:50` sticky on desktop (main.scss:194-198) and `z-index:1000` fixed at ≤860px (main.scss:22596), so the header always paints over it, and its background is rgba(255,255,255,0.98) plus a 14px backdrop blur. I confirmed on the live site that the compiled bundle contains only two `.skip-link` rules, neither touching z-index. REFUTED sub-claim: "its box is x=16 y=-6 … 6px above the viewport top, so it would be clipped even without the header." On a cold load at scrollY=0 I measured the focused geometry directly (the link's resting transform is matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-69.586) = translateY(-150%) of its 46.39px height; applying the :focus value translateY(0) puts it at exactly [16, 16, 131.07, 46.39]) against a header rect of [0, 0, 1280, 73]. It is fully inside the viewport and fully inside the header band — obscured, not clipped. The -6 came from measuring at a scroll offset of ~22px. Consequently the `top: 1rem → 0` half of the fix is unnecessary. I could not complete the live elementFromPoint hit-test because the first-visit cookie <dialog> is open and modal (`:modal === true`), which puts it in the top layer and blocks hit-testing; I did not dismiss it, as that is a consent action. The z-index ordering is deterministic from the CSS regardless.

#### [208] Sliding-sash carousel position dots are 6px tall controls on mobile

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button` is `width: 28px; height: 6px` (48px wide when active). These are real `<button>`s with click handlers that jump between the three Roseview models, and the mobile probe measured them at 48x6 and 28x6 on `/sliding-sash-windows/`. WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is Level AA in WCAG 2.2 and requires 24x24 CSS px. Six pixels is a quarter of that vertically. The pattern is inconsistent with the rest of the site: `.fg-home-product-theatre__mobile-dots [data-fg-mobile-product-dot]` is deliberately `pointer-events: none` (an indicator, with real prev/next buttons beside it) and `.fg-cd3-collections__dots span` is a `<span>`, not a control. The sash dots are the only place a decorative 6px bar was left clickable.
- **Recommendation:** At `src/scss/main.scss:23786`, keep the 6px visual but give the button a real hit area: `height: 24px; padding: 9px 0; background-clip: content-box; background-color: rgba(0,45,58,.18);` and move the active-state `width` change to the same content box. That leaves the design identical and takes the target to 28x24 / 48x24.
- **Why:** It is a two-line CSS change that removes a measurable AA failure on a product page, and it is exactly the kind of drift the rest of the codebase already avoided on purpose.
- **Affected:** `src/scss/main.scss:23786-23799`, rendered on `/sliding-sash-windows/` at ≤860px. Three dots.
- **Evidence:** Compiled rule `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button{width:28px;height:6px;...}`; probe-mobile.json `/sliding-sash-windows/` smallTargets includes `{tag:button, txt:"Show Ultimate Rose", w:48, h:6}` and `{tag:button, txt:"Show Heritage Rose", w:28, h:6}`.
- **Verification:** Every element of this reproduced.

CSS, extracted from live/main.css with the enclosing media context proved by brace-walk: at `@media(max-width: 860px)` — `.site-header__mobile-call{display:inline-flex;...;min-height:46px;margin-left:auto;padding:.55rem .8rem;...;font-size:.9rem;...}` and `.site-nav-toggle{...;min-width:62px;margin-left:0;min-height:46px;...}`. Then at `@media(max-width: 560px)` (offset 418680, context confirmed) — `.site-nav-toggle{min-height:40px;padding-inline:.65rem}` and `.site-header__mobile-call{min-height:40px;padding-inline:.65rem;font-size:.84rem}`. The override back down to 40px is exactly as described.

Scope claim verified independently: I iterated all 38 routes of probe-mobile.json looking for a smallTargets entry with cls `site-header__mobile-call` and got 38/38, all at w:87 h:40. Also 38/38 for `site-brand` at 142x36.

'Only persistent phone affordance' verified: `mobile-cta`, `sticky-cta`, `fg-mobile-bar` and `call-bar` all occur 0 times in the 694KB compiled CSS, so no sticky bottom call bar exists. And the mobile nav panel has no tel link — the `site-mobile-nav` block in home.html contains only page links (About Us, Contact, Instant Quote, Free Consultation and the accordion product lists); the single `tel:` in the header region belongs to `.site-header__phone`, which is `display:none` at `@media(max-width: 860px)`.

One clarification that does not change the verdict: 40px is not a WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 failure (the minimum there is 24x24) — this is a breach of the 44px platform convention and of STYLE.md:350, which is how the finding frames it. It does not overclaim.

#### [144] Desktop mega menu cannot be dismissed from the keyboard, and its trigger has no aria-expanded

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The mega panel opens on `focusin` as well as hover (src/js/main.js:2841-2866, plus the CSS fallback `.site-nav__item:focus-within > .site-nav__mega { display: block }` at main.scss:670-673). Once open it overlays the page. The only Escape handler in the header (src/js/main.js:2971-2975) is gated on `siteHeader.classList.contains('is-nav-open')`, which is the *mobile* drawer class — so on desktop, Escape does nothing and the only way to close the panel is to keep tabbing until focus leaves the item. I confirmed the open behaviour live: focusing the "Products" link gives `panel.hidden === false`, `display: block`, `aria-expanded: null`, `aria-haspopup: null`.
- **Recommendation:** Two changes in src/js/main.js around :2841-2880. (1) Add a document-level `keydown` for `Escape` that, when `document.activeElement` is inside a `.site-nav__item.has-children`, hides that item's panel and returns focus to the item's own `<a>`; it must also add an `is-dismissed` class the CSS honours (`.site-nav__item.is-dismissed > .site-nav__mega { display: none }`), otherwise the `:focus-within` rule at main.scss:670 will immediately re-show it. (2) Set `aria-expanded="false"` on the top-level `<a>` in `fenster_render_nav_fallback()` (inc/template-tags.php:65-70) and keep it in sync in `openPanel`/`closePanel`, so a screen-reader user is told a submenu opened rather than silently discovering more links.
- **Why:** WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA) requires content revealed by hover or focus to be dismissible without moving the pointer or focus. A magnifier user at 400% zoom has a panel covering their entire viewport with no way to close it; a screen-reader user gets no announcement that anything opened. It is on all 712 pages and it is the primary navigation.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages (the mega menu markup appears 19,936 times across the corpus). Desktop / pointer-and-keyboard viewports above 860px.
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:2971-2975 (only Escape handler, gated on `is-nav-open`); :2841-2866 (`openPanel`/`closePanel` on pointerenter/focusin); src/scss/main.scss:670-673 (`:focus-within` display fallback); inc/template-tags.php:65-70 (trigger `<a>` rendered with no aria attributes). Live check on fensterglazing.com: focusing "Products" → `{hiddenAfterFocus:false, display:"block", ariaExpanded:null, ariaHaspopup:null}`.
- **Verification:** Reproduced in full, including every line citation. src/scss/main.scss:47 `--color-accent: #2eac66`, :48 `--color-accent-dark: #20824c`, :1426 `.site-header__phone { color: var(--color-accent) }`, :1449 `.eyebrow { color: var(--color-accent); font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 800 }`, :1503-1515 `.button { border: 1px solid var(--color-accent); background: var(--color-accent); color: #fff; font-weight: 800 }`, :1517 `.text-link`. All survive into the shipped bundle (live/main.css carries the identical compiled rules). Contrast recomputed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula: #2eac66 on #ffffff = 2.913:1; #20824c on #ffffff = 4.818:1 (passes AA); #2eac66 on #061d24 = 5.963:1 (passes, so the carve-out is right). Pixel-sampled shots/desktop/home--fold.png myself: header CTA fill is exactly (46,172,102) with (255,255,255) glyphs; the header phone is (46,172,102) on (254,254,254) = 2.888:1. Live computed styles on fensterglazing.com/composite-doors/ confirm the large-text exemption does not apply: `.button` primary is 16px / weight 800 white on rgb(46,172,102) ("Get an instant price"), `.site-header__phone` 15.04px / 700, `.eyebrow` 12.48px / 800 — all normal text needing 4.5:1. The focus-ring claim also holds: the compiled CSS has `.site-nav-toggle:focus-visible,…{outline:3px solid var(--color-accent);outline-offset:2px}` (main.scss:22681-22688) on a white header, 2.91:1 against the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 needs. Probe corroborates: 584 of 834 sampled lowContrast entries (70%) involve rgb(46,172,102), on 38 of 38 routes. Nothing in AI.md, STYLE.md or PROGRESS.md rules on the accent green's contrast — the only related entries (STYLE.md:45, :49, :281) demand readable contrast rather than sanctioning this. Two caveats that do not change the verdict: the `.eyebrow` affected count is raw class occurrences, and a real subset already ships `--color-accent-dark` (consultation page, /about/, price guide, composite family) or a light green on dark (#7fe0ab, #72dc98, #ffb1a9), so the failing population is smaller than 6,041 — the finding's own recommendation already carves those out. Also `--fg-green` (main.scss:77) is an alias of `--color-accent`, so the composite-door `.fg-cd3-*` eyebrows fail identically and should be in the same edit.

#### [147] The image lightbox declares aria-modal="true" but never traps focus

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The lightbox is created with `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-label="Image preview"` (src/js/main.js:6945-6948), moves focus to the close button on open and restores `previousFocus` on close (:6990-6996, :6967-6976), and closes on Escape and backdrop click. What it does not do is contain Tab, and nothing behind it is made `inert`. `aria-modal="true"` tells the screen reader to ignore everything outside the dialog, but it has no effect on the browser's tab order — so pressing Tab from "Next image" walks into the page underneath, where the screen reader now reports nothing because the author told it not to. The user is silently stranded with no way to know where they are.
- **Recommendation:** In `openLightbox()` (src/js/main.js:6988-6996) set `inert` on the page's top-level children (`main`, `footer`, the Legend `<aside>`) and clear it in `closeLightbox()` (:6967-6976). That is the minimum that makes `aria-modal="true"` an honest claim. If `inert` is unacceptable, remove `aria-modal` and add a Tab/Shift+Tab wrap across the three buttons — but `inert` is the smaller change and cannot desynchronise.
- **Why:** Declaring `aria-modal` while leaving the tab order open is worse than declaring nothing: it actively silences the content the user is about to land on. The galleries are the product-evidence surface of the site, so this is the moment a low-vision buyer is looking closely at the doors.
- **Affected:** 32 pages, 132 lightbox trigger links (product galleries and case studies).
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:6942-7028. Declaration at :6945-6948; `closeButton?.focus()` at :6995; `previousFocus?.focus?.()` at :6975; Escape at :7017-7021. No `inert`, no keydown Tab handling, no focus-wrap anywhere in the block.
- **Verification:** Markup reproduced byte-for-byte in live/composite-doors.html: `<span class="fg-review-showcase__platform" aria-label="Review on Google"><span class="fg-review-showcase__glyph" aria-hidden="true">G</span></span>`, with `<span class="fg-stars" role="img" aria-label="5 out of 5 stars">` three lines below in the same card — so the house pattern for the fix genuinely is already adjacent. Source located at template-parts/components/review-showcase.php:149, which emits the aria-label with no role for both the Google and Trustpilot variants. The outer span has no role, so it computes to `generic`, and ARIA 1.2 prohibits author naming on `generic`; Chrome and Firefox drop the label. I confirmed on the live page that the only rendered content is the single character "G" and that it carries `aria-hidden="true"`, so nothing else can substitute — I read the card's full text via the DOM: "Digger / a month ago / G / We have used Fensters for years…", i.e. the platform contributes nothing announceable. Counts are consistent: 211 Google badges and 1 Trustpilot badge across 30 of my 38 local pages, ~7 per page, which extrapolates cleanly to the claimed 3,977 / 568 pages. The footer variants are real too — `<div class="site-footer__trust" aria-label="Accreditations">` and `<div class="site-footer__socials" aria-label="Fenster Glazing social media">` both appear on home.html with no role. One caveat that does not change the fix: "announce nothing" is exact for Chrome and Firefox, while some Safari/VoiceOver builds still surface a name on a labelled generic — the `role="img"` addition is correct either way, and the footer groupings are lower stakes because each mark inside them still has its own alt text.

#### [213] The repairs diagnostic swaps its whole answer panel with no live region

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `liniar-casement-exterior.jpg` is 1600x900 (16:9 landscape) and is rendered into a 390x473 box (0.82:1 portrait) with `object-fit: cover; object-position: 50% 50%`. The cover scale factor is max(390/1600, 473/900) = 0.526, producing an 842x473 rendered image of which only the centre 390px is visible — 46% of the frame, with 54% cropped off the sides. The result in the mobile fold is a gable end with the windows largely behind the H1 and sub-paragraph overlay, and the wider elevation the shot was taken to show entirely gone. STYLE.md:196 states "Mobile image crops need a clear focal point". The product-page heroes do not have this problem: /casement-windows/ renders `casement-stone-cottage-1600w.webp` (1600x1067, 1.5:1) into 390x300 (1.3:1), barely cropping at all. This is confined to /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ — it is the only route in the 38-page sweep that uses `fg-mk-hero`, and neither /windows-milton-keynes/ nor /doors-milton-keynes/ uses that component or `fg-county-hero` (grep returns zero on both).
- **Recommendation:** Add `role="status"` (or `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`) to the `.fg-rp-diag__panel` wrapper that contains `[data-fg-diag-name]`, `[data-fg-diag-what]` and `[data-fg-diag-fix]` in `template-parts/sections/window-door-repairs.php`. No JavaScript change is needed — `showPart()` already writes into those nodes, so the announcement follows for free.
- **Why:** The page exists to answer "what has broken". The answer is the one thing that is not announced.
- **Affected:** `/window-and-door-repairs/`. `template-parts/sections/window-door-repairs.php`; controller `src/js/main.js:8149-8189`.
- **Evidence:** `grep -c "aria-live" template-parts/sections/window-door-repairs.php` → 0; `grep -rln "aria-live" template-parts/` lists five other files but not this one. `src/js/main.js:8160-8164` writes name/what/fix/caption with no announcement.
- **Verification:** The crop is real and the arithmetic is exactly right; only the scope note at the end is wrong. Confirmed from the live HTML: `<img src=".../products/curated/liniar-casement-exterior.jpg" class="fg-mk-hero__image" ... width="1600" height="900">`. Confirmed from main.css: `.fg-mk-hero__image{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;object-position:center}` (which computes to the reported 50% 50%) and `.fg-mk-hero{min-height:clamp(500px,72svh,680px)}` with `@media(max-width: 860px){.fg-mk-hero{min-height:auto}}`, so at 390px the box is content-driven — consistent with the reported 473px. I re-derived the crop independently: cover scale = max(390/1600, 473/900) = 0.5256, rendered width 841px, visible 390 of 841 = 46.4%, so 53.6% is cropped away. The finding's 0.526 / 842 / 46% / 54% all reproduce. I measured the hero band in scratchpad/mfold/double-glazing-milton-keynes-top.png (y=110 to y=818 at 1.5x device scale = 472 CSS px) which corroborates the 473px box, and the image shows exactly what is claimed: a gable end, mostly sky and brickwork, with the windows sitting behind the H1, the lead paragraph and both CTAs. STYLE.md:196 is verbatim 'Mobile image crops need a clear focal point', so this is measured against the project's own written standard rather than taste. WHAT IS WRONG: the 'affected' claim that /windows-milton-keynes/ and /doors-milton-keynes/ 'share the fg-mk-hero / fg-county-hero family' and are worth checking. They do not — `grep -c` returns 0 for both `fg-mk-hero` and `fg-county-hero` on both pages; /windows-milton-keynes/ opens on a flush-casement hero image and /doors-milton-keynes/ on a composite-door hero, neither using the component. Across the 38 fetched routes, `grep -l fg-mk-hero__image *.html` returns exactly one file. This is a single-page defect, not the head of a family.

#### [219] Door / lantern wall drift discards keyboard scrolling and never pauses on focus (desktop, motion-allowed only)

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The wall is a correctly-labelled `role="region" tabindex="0"` scroll container, so a keyboard user can focus it and press Arrow keys. But `tick()` writes `viewport.scrollLeft = offset` on every animation frame (src/js/main.js:1051) while the `scroll` listener that would resynchronise `offset` deliberately bails during the drift (`if (dragging || frame !== null) return;`, 1113-1116). A native arrow-key scroll is therefore reverted on the next frame. Focus does not pause the drift either — only `pointerenter` does (1067). So the affordance the region label promises ('Drag or scroll sideways to explore') is unusable from the keyboard: the visitor can see every card because the drift carries them past on its own, but cannot stop on one or go back. The same code has no pause mechanism other than hover, which is a WCAG 2.2.2 Level A gap. Scope is narrower than it looks: `shouldDrift()` (1036-1037) requires `min-width: 861px` and `!prefers-reduced-motion`, so mobile and reduced-motion visitors get a plain native scroll rail that works correctly.
- **Recommendation:** In src/js/main.js:1067, add `focusin`/`focusout` handlers on `viewport` that set the `hovering` flag (rename it `held`) exactly as `pointerenter`/`pointerleave` do, so focusing the region stops the drift and blurring resumes it via `resumeSoon()`. Then either drop the `frame !== null` guard on the scroll listener at 1113, or call `stop()` from a `keydown` handler for Arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown before the native scroll happens. Add a visible pause toggle in `.fg-cd3-wall` for 2.2.2.
- **Why:** On a sixteen-screen page the decision to enquire is made in the middle, not at the top, and there is currently nothing to act on when it happens. This is the largest missing interaction on the site.
- **Affected:** All product and location routes at ≤860px. Measured: probe-mobile.json `pageHeight` across 38 routes.
- **Evidence:** probe-mobile.json pageHeight: median 13,347 (`/double-glazing-replacement/`), max 31,310 (`/double-glazing-milton-keynes/`), 21,708 (`/casement-windows/`), 21,563 (`/aluminium-windows/`). Live check at 375x812: `[data-fg-enquiry-form] input[name="name"]` measured `getBoundingClientRect().top` = 18,589 on `/casement-windows/` from scrollY 0. `grep position:sticky` over `assets/css/main.css` → 16 selectors, none a CTA. No `back-to-top`/`scroll-to-top` token anywhere in `src/js/main.js` or `src/scss/main.scss`.
- **Verification:** The code defect is real and I reproduced the whole chain, but the scope and the consequence are overstated and one count is wrong. Real: `tick()` writes `viewport.scrollLeft = offset` every frame (main.js:1051); the `scroll` listener that resynchronises `offset` bails while the drift runs — `if (dragging || frame !== null) return;` (main.js:1113-1116); the only pause handlers are `pointerenter`/`pointerleave` (1067-1075) with no `focusin`/`focusout`; the viewport really is `tabindex="0" role="region"` with the label 'Drag or scroll sideways to explore.' in live/composite-doors.html and live/roof-lanterns.html. So a focused keyboard user's arrow-key scroll is written back over on the next frame. Wrong or overstated: (1) `canDrift = window.matchMedia('(min-width: 861px)')` at main.js:1012 and `shouldDrift()` at 1036-1037 also tests `!reduceMotion.matches`. So the drift is OFF entirely at ≤860px and OFF for reduced-motion users, where native scroll and arrow keys work fine. The broken population is desktop ≥861px, no reduced-motion preference, keyboard-only. (2) '26 lanterns' is wrong: the lantern track has 26 `<li>` of which 13 are `aria-hidden` clones — 13 real layouts, matching PROGRESS.md:3669 'thirteen real cards plus 13 clones'. Composite doors is right at 33 + 33 clones. (3) 'cannot reach the 33 doors past the first screenful' is false — the drift itself carries every card past the viewport at ~54px/s (PROGRESS.md:3669 measured this), and the wall contains zero anchors (I parsed the track: 0 `<a>` tags), so nothing inside it is a missed destination. The genuine harm is loss of control, not loss of access. AI.md:712 documents the component and its hover/drag pausing as accepted behaviour, but says nothing about focus or keyboard, so this is not an owner ruling on the defect. AI.md's own accessibility rules ('Do not rely on hover-only controls') point the other way.

#### [146] The enquiry form suppresses the browser focus ring and replaces it with a 1.17:1 glow

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `.fg-enquiry-form input:not([type="checkbox"]):focus, select:focus, textarea:focus { border-color: var(--color-accent); outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(46,172,102,0.16) }` (src/scss/main.scss:18498-18503). The `outline: 0` removes the platform ring. What replaces it: the 4px glow at 16% alpha composites to rgb(222,242,231) over a white panel — 1.17:1 against the field's white background, i.e. essentially nothing — and over the dark form panel it composites to roughly 1.29:1. The remaining signal is a 1px border going from the resting colour to #2eac66, a change of about 2.90:1 on the dark panel and less on light. `.fg-commercial-form` repeats the same rule at main.scss:18528-18534. The one place it is done properly is `.fg-home-showroom .fg-enquiry-form … :focus` (main.scss:18791), which uses `--color-accent-dark`.
- **Recommendation:** In src/scss/main.scss:18498-18503 and :18528-18534, delete `outline: 0` and add `outline: 3px solid var(--color-accent-dark); outline-offset: 2px`, keeping the border-colour change as decoration. Raise the glow to `rgba(32,130,76,0.45)` if you want to keep it. Do not rely on the glow alone at any alpha below ~0.4 — 0.16 over white is invisible at any monitor gamma.
- **Why:** This is the field-by-field focus indicator on the primary lead form on 669 pages. Anyone completing it by keyboard cannot tell which of six fields they are in without looking at the caret, and the caret is not a focus indicator. SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast expects 3:1 for the visual information that identifies a component's state; 1.17:1 is not a state indicator, it is a rounding error.
- **Affected:** 669 pages carry `.fg-enquiry-form`; `.fg-commercial-form` on the commercial estate (~40 pages).
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:18498-18503 (`outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(46,172,102,0.16)`), :18528-18534 (`.fg-commercial-form`, same), :18791 (`.fg-home-showroom` variant, correctly uses `--color-accent-dark`). Computed: rgba(46,172,102,0.16) over #ffffff = rgb(222,242,231), 1.17:1 vs white; over #002d3a = rgb(7,65,65), 1.29:1 vs panel.
- **Verification:** Reproduced against the source at the cited lines. src/js/main.js:2942-2957 is the toggle click handler: it toggles `is-nav-open` on the header, toggles `is-mobile-nav-open` on <html>, flips `aria-expanded`, sets `mobileNav.hidden`, swaps the button label — and does nothing else. :2959-2969 closes on drawer-link click, :2971-2975 closes on Escape and returns focus to the toggle, :2977-2986 closes on resize. `grep -n '\binert\b' src/js/main.js` returns NOTHING; the only `querySelector('main')` in the whole 8,234-line file is at :638 and reads textContent for the chat index; there is no Tab-key handler and no focus trap anywhere ('trap' matches only a comment about trapezia at :3735). The overlay is as described: main.scss:22690-22707 gives `.site-nav` `position:fixed; top:var(--site-header-main-height); left/right:0; height:calc(100svh - …); z-index:1001` over an opaque `#eef3f2` base, and `.site-header.is-nav-open` takes `bottom:0; height:100svh` (main.scss:22608-22611); body scroll is locked at :22591-22593. The tab-order claim holds against the header markup: site-header.php orders brand (12), mobile call (20), toggle (27), nav#site-navigation (31), phone (35), and `.site-header__phone` is `display:none` at ≤860px (main.scss:22623), which removes it from the tab order — so the stop after the drawer's last link is the first link in `<main>`, fully covered and body-locked. The cookie-modal comparison is also accurate: I confirmed live that `dialog.fg-cookie-consent` matches `:modal`, i.e. a real `showModal()`. No ruling covers this — AI.md's Accessibility Rules (974-981) say nothing about focus containment.

#### [150] Autoplaying looping hero video has no pause control, and reduced-motion only defers it to the first keypress

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The homepage and roof-lantern heroes are `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline>` with no `controls` attribute and no pause button anywhere (template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:110, roof-lanterns.php:71). The lazy-video controller (src/js/main.js:4821-4852) does read `prefers-reduced-motion`, but only to set `interactionOnly = true`, which defers loading until the first `pointerdown`, `keydown` or `touchstart` anywhere on the window — and then calls `loadVideo()`, which ends in `video.play()`. So a reduced-motion visitor sees the poster, presses Tab or clicks once, and a looping video starts behind the H1 with no way to stop it. The only reduced-motion CSS for it is `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .fg-home-hero__video { transform: scale(1.03) } }` (main.scss:26584-26587), which adjusts framing, not motion.
- **Recommendation:** In src/js/main.js:4821-4852 split the two concerns: keep `interactionOnly` as the bandwidth/small-viewport deferral it was designed to be, and add a separate hard branch — if `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, never call `loadVideo()` at all and leave the poster in place, which is what AI.md's "static or simplified content" rule asks for. Independently, add a small pause/play toggle to the hero (bottom-right of the video, above the shade layer) for everyone else; a `<button>` toggling `video.paused` is about fifteen lines and satisfies SC 2.2.2 properly.
- **Why:** A full-bleed video looping behind the page's only H1 is the most motion-intense thing on the site, and it currently reaches the exact users who asked not to see it — one keystroke is all it takes, and Tab is the first keystroke a keyboard user makes. SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide is Level A. The poster images are good enough that suppressing the video costs the reduced-motion visitor almost nothing visually.
- **Affected:** Homepage plus /roof-lanterns/; 9 pages in the 712-corpus carry an autoplaying video, none with `controls`. The homepage hero asset is ~9.8MB.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/sections/home-experience.php:110 and template-parts/sections/roof-lanterns.php:71 (`autoplay muted loop`, no `controls`); src/js/main.js:4821-4852 (`interactionOnly` computed from `prefersReducedMotion` at :4829-4830, `loadVideo()` ending in `video.play()` at :4842, interaction listeners at :4846-4850); src/scss/main.scss:26584-26587. Corpus scan: 9 pages with `<video … autoplay>`, 0 with `controls`.
- **Verification:** Every cited fact checks out. src/js/main.js:2971-2975 is the only header Escape handler and line 2972 reads `if (event.key !== 'Escape' || !siteHeader.classList.contains('is-nav-open')) return;` — `is-nav-open` is set and cleared only by the mobile drawer path (:2961, :2979), so Escape is a no-op on desktop. `grep -n Escape src/js/main.js` returns exactly three handlers site-wide: :837 (Legend chat), :2972 (mobile drawer), :7019 (lightbox) — nothing for the mega panel. The open-on-focus behaviour is real and doubled: per-item `focusin` → `openPanel` at :2864 (openPanel/closePanel defined :2849-2860), plus a delegated `siteHeader.addEventListener('focusin', …)` at :2890-2895 that also unhides the panel. src/scss/main.scss:670-673 is verbatim `.site-nav__item:hover > .site-nav__mega, .site-nav__item:focus-within > .site-nav__mega { display: block; }`, which is why the recommendation's `is-dismissed` class is genuinely necessary. inc/template-tags.php:66-71 prints the trigger as `'<li class="%s"><a href="%s">%s</a>'` with no aria attributes at all, inside `fenster_render_nav_fallback()` (declared at :44) — the function name in the recommendation is correct. I confirmed the rendered output rather than trusting the template: live home.html contains `<li class="site-nav__item has-children has-mega-menu"><a href="…/windows-milton-keynes/">Products</a><div class="site-nav__mega" hidden>` — no aria-expanded, no aria-haspopup. No ruling in AI.md/STYLE.md covers the mega menu's keyboard behaviour. One cosmetic quibble that does not change the verdict: 'the mega menu markup appears 19,936 times' is 28 class-string occurrences × 712 pages; there are only 2 dismissible desktop panels per page (`site-nav__item has-children` occurs twice in home.html). The per-page count is 2, not 28.

#### [211] Legend's drawer takes 1.44 seconds to open to a usable state and 1.44 seconds to close

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `travelLegend()` runs a WAAPI keyframe animation with `duration = 1440`. `openChat()` awaits `motion.finished` before it calls `input.focus()`, and `closeChat()` awaits it before it sets `panel.hidden = true`. So pressing the launcher gives you a visible drawer you cannot type into for 1.44s, and pressing the X leaves the drawer on screen for 1.44s after you asked it to go. For comparison, the site's own transitions are 120–620ms and the mega-menu close delay is 80ms. Reduced motion skips the travel entirely (`travelLegend` returns at line 282), which is the right behaviour and confirms nothing depends on the animation completing.
- **Recommendation:** Decouple the character animation from the interaction. In `openChat()`, call `input.focus()` immediately after `panel.hidden = false` and let the jump play out behind it; in `closeChat()`, hide the panel on a short fade (160ms, matching `.legend-assistant` transitions) and let the traveller finish independently. If the jump's arc reads badly at speed, cut `duration` to ~600ms; the five-keyframe arc still works.
- **Why:** The chat launcher is the site's live-assistance entry point. A 1.44s dead zone between click and typing, and a close button that appears not to work for a second and a half, are both worse than having no animation.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:338` (duration), `688-718` (openChat awaits travel before focusing input), `736-763` (closeChat awaits travel before hiding panel). Every page.
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:338` `const duration = 1440;`; `364` `await motion.finished;`; `openChat` at 706 `const travel = travelLegend(launcherCharacter, roamer, 'up');` then awaits before `input.focus()` at 717.
- **Verification:** Every number reproduces exactly. Recomputed WCAG relative luminance: #2eac66 on #ffffff = 2.913:1, #20824c on #ffffff = 4.818:1 — the finding's 2.91 and 4.82 are correct. Tokens confirmed in live/main.css: `--color-accent: #2eac66`, `--color-accent-dark: #20824c`. The CSS backs the claim: `.button{...border:1px solid var(--color-accent);background:var(--color-accent);color:#fff;font-weight:800}` (no font-size, so it inherits 16px — under the 18.66px bold large-text exemption, so 4.5:1 applies); `.eyebrow{margin:0 0 .75rem;color:var(--color-accent);font-size:.78rem;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase}` = 12.48px, also under the exemption; `.site-header__mobile-call{...background:var(--color-accent);color:#fff}` with a mobile override to `font-size:.84rem` = 13.44px, matching the probe's 13.44 exactly. Tallying the probe's lowContrast arrays myself: eyebrow #2eac66-on-white at 12.48px = 115+26+25 = 166 (matches), white-on-#2eac66 = .button 52, .fg-order-process__number 50, .fg-hero-cta__short 15, unclassed 38+25. Note these arrays are capped at 25 per route and ALL 38 routes hit the cap, so 166 is a floor, not an inflated figure — the finding understates. The probe's known over-reporting bug (walking up the DOM for a background) does not apply here: `.button`, `.site-header__mobile-call` and `.fg-order-process__number` all set the green fill on the element itself. No owner ruling protects this: I grepped AI.md, STYLE.md, TONEOFVOICE.md, PROGRESS.md and HANDOVER.md for contrast/WCAG/green rulings and found nothing sanctioning it; STYLE.md's Colour And Tone section (lines 215-221) says only 'use green mainly for action, highlights, proof and small emphasis'. The site already applies the recommended fix in several scopes, which supports feasibility: `.fg-about .eyebrow{color:var(--color-accent-dark)}`, `.fg-price-guide__example-copy .eyebrow`, `.fg-composite-family__body .eyebrow`, `.fg-mk-enquiry__copy .eyebrow`, `.fg-consultation-page__hero-copy .eyebrow`. ONE CAVEAT the finding misses, which makes the problem worse and the fix incomplete: eyebrows sit on the page canvas `--fg-page-gradient`, whose linear-gradient stop is `#eef5f4 -> #ffffff 44% -> #e8f1f0`, not pure white. On #eef5f4 the current green is 2.64:1, and #20824c is only 4.36:1 — still a marginal AA fail. So swap (1) for `.button` is sound as stated; swap (2) for `.eyebrow` clears AA on white cards/panels but not on the mint end of the canvas, where a slightly darker step is needed.

#### [220] The gallery lightbox does not trap focus and gives no feedback when you arrow between images

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 88% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The lightbox is built with `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` and does the hard parts right — it stores `previousFocus`, focuses the close button on open, restores focus on close, handles Escape and backdrop clicks, and locks page scroll via `html.fg-gallery-lightbox-open { overflow: hidden }`. But nothing constrains Tab: after the three lightbox buttons, focus moves into the page behind, which `aria-modal` has told screen readers does not exist and which the visitor cannot see. `moveLightbox()` swaps `lightboxImage.src` and `.alt` with no live region and without moving focus, so arrowing through a gallery is silent for a screen-reader user. On touch there is no swipe gesture — the arrows are the only way through.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `keydown` Tab handler on `lightbox` that cycles between `closeButton`, `prevButton` and `nextButton` (three elements, so a simple first/last wrap is enough) at `src/js/main.js:7018`. Give the `<figure>` `role="status"` or wrap the image in an `aria-live="polite"` container so the new alt is announced. Add horizontal swipe on the figure using the same axis-locked pointer pattern already proven in the obscured-glass divider at `src/js/main.js:3188-3232`.
- **Why:** The lightbox is on every product page's gallery and it is currently a dialog that a keyboard user falls out of the back of.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:6942-7029`. Every route with `[data-fg-gallery-lightbox]` links (product galleries).
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:6947-6949` sets `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"`; the only keydown handler is `7018-7028`, which handles Escape/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and never Tab; `setLightboxImage` at 6977 writes `src`/`alt` with no announcement; scroll lock confirmed as `html.fg-gallery-lightbox-open,html.fg-gallery-lightbox-open body{overflow:hidden}` in `assets/css/main.css`.
- **Verification:** I re-ran the analysis independently and it reproduces exactly. `updateDepthItems` at src/js/main.js:5662-5670 has no `prefers-reduced-motion` test anywhere in the function or its listener registration at 5672-5676. Parsing the live compiled CSS with brace-matching, `var(--fg-parallax-y` appears in exactly 13 rules and the selectors are precisely the 13 the finding lists; there are 27 (not 26 — trivial) `@media(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` blocks, and only one of the 13 selectors appears in any of them: `.fg-cas-lock__art{transform:none;transition:none}`. I also checked for a universal reduced-motion reset that might catch the others — there is none. The LCP claim is correct and I nearly refuted it: on /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ all 9 depth items are lazy-loaded `fg-mk-*` images, but on /casement-windows-bletchley/ the hero really is `<img class="fg-location-hero__image" ... loading="eager" fetchpriority="high" data-fg-depth="0.05">` and the CSS rule is `.fg-location-hero__image{--fg-parallax-y:0px;...;transform:translateY(var(--fg-parallax-y)) scale(1.01)}` with no guard. Two small evidence corrections: the contract is at HANDOVER.md:422, not AI.md:422 ('It has no reduced-motion check of its own, so every consumer needs its own @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { transform: none; }'), and live `data-fg-depth` markup is on 4 fetched routes, not 3 — /casement-windows/ carries one (`.fg-cas-lock__stage` at 0.15), which is the single guarded consumer. This is a documented contract the code breaks, not an owner ruling: AI.md's Accessibility Rules explicitly say 'Respect prefers-reduced-motion'.

#### [149] The composite door wall drifts continuously and overwrites keyboard scrolling instead of pausing for it

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** The wall is correctly exposed to the keyboard — `tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Composite door styles. Drag or scroll sideways to explore."` — but the drift loop fights the user. `tick()` writes `viewport.scrollLeft = offset` on every animation frame (src/js/main.js:1043-1052), and the `scroll` listener that would sync the user's position is short-circuited while the loop is running: `if (dragging || frame !== null) return;` (:1112-1115). So an arrow-key scroll is applied by the browser and then overwritten ~16ms later. The pause conditions are `pointerenter`/`pointerleave` only (:1066-1074) — there is no `focusin`/`focusout`, so focusing the region does not stop it. The comparison that makes this a defect rather than a judgement call is inside the same file: the review carousel pauses on `focusin` as well as pointer (src/js/main.js:6877-6884).
- **Recommendation:** In src/js/main.js:1066-1074 add `viewport.addEventListener('focusin', () => { hovering = true; stop(); })` and a matching `focusout` that calls `resumeSoon()` — reusing the existing `hovering` flag so `shouldDrift()` needs no change. Better still, add a visible pause/play button so there is a real SC 2.2.2 mechanism rather than one that only exists for people who can hover.
- **Why:** The region advertises itself to assistive technology as scrollable and then discards keyboard scroll input, so SC 2.1.1 Keyboard is not met for the one interaction it offers. Separately, continuously moving content with no pause control available to a non-pointer user is SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide, a Level A criterion. Constant lateral drift beside body copy is also a reading problem for dyslexic and low-attention users well beyond the strict conformance question.
- **Affected:** 2 pages (/composite-doors/ and one other carrying `data-fg-door-wall`), desktop only — `canDrift` requires `min-width: 861px`. Drift rate SPEED 0.9px/frame ≈ 54px/s.
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:1007-1130. `tick()` writing scrollLeft at :1043-1052; scroll listener short-circuit at :1112-1115; pointer-only pause at :1066-1074; `shouldDrift()` at :1037; `canDrift = matchMedia('(min-width: 861px)')` at :1012. Markup verified in live/composite-doors.html (`tabindex="0" role="region"`, `<li>` items, no focusable children). Contrast: focusin pause at src/js/main.js:6877-6884. Reported from source rather than live test — the browser automation context in this environment proved to be rendering a different viewport than the pane, so I did not trust its timing measurement.
- **Verification:** Reproduced in full, including the scope claim. src/js/main.js:5660-5676 is exactly as described: `depthItems` collected at :5660, `updateDepthItems` at :5662-5670 writing `--fg-parallax-y` from a ±180px × strength clamp at :5667-5668, and scroll/resize listeners at :5673-5674 with no motion query anywhere in the block. `grep -c 'prefers-reduced-motion' src/scss/main.scss` returns 27, matching the claim; I dumped all 27 blocks and none touches `--fg-parallax-y` or the transforms that read it — the nearest is :4959-4965 which resets `[data-fg-mk-reveal]` only, and the location hero image immediately below it at :4983-4989 is a parallax consumer that gets no reset. 24 `--fg-parallax-y` references in the stylesheet, at 4478, 4710, 4744, 4989, 5494, 6176, 6444, 6621, 20894, 20956, 21018, 21076, 38025 among others. The contrast cases are all real: main.js:1011, 2810, 3385, 5061, 5603, 6342 each open with a `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` guard. Template scope confirmed: location-service.php carries exactly 7 `data-fg-depth` instances (:1160, 1318, 1321, 1353, 1454, 1530, 1647) plus generated-page.php:3835, 4001 and casement-windows-v2.php:433. AI.md:980-981 does say 'Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`' and 'Reduced-motion users should receive static or simplified content, not broken content', so the codebase is failing its own written rule and this is not an owner ruling. The 528/712 page figure holds up: I curled a 12-URL systematic sample from urls.txt and 9 of 12 carried data-fg-depth (5 occurrences each) — 75% of 712 ≈ 534, consistent with 528. The three misses were /aluminium-windows/, /roof-lanterns/ and /commercial-glazing-warwickshire/, i.e. hub and commercial pages, exactly as the finding implies.

#### [216] Every hyphen in body text is rewritten to a non-breaking hyphen, which breaks find-in-page and copy-paste

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `preventHyphenatedWordSplits()` walks the whole body with a TreeWalker on load and replaces every `letter-letter` hyphen with U+2011 NON-BREAKING HYPHEN. Browsers do not normalise U+2011 to U+002D in find-in-page, so Ctrl+F for "A-rated", "multi-point", "low-maintenance" or "tilt-turn" finds nothing on pages that visibly contain those words, and copying a phrase out of the page and pasting it into a search box or a form produces a character that will not match. It also runs on every page load over the entire DOM regardless of whether any element is actually at risk of a bad break.
- **Recommendation:** Scope it instead of applying it globally. Restrict the TreeWalker root to headings and short display copy — the places a mid-word break actually looks wrong — e.g. `document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, .eyebrow, .fg-hero *')` rather than `document.body`, at `src/js/main.js:1531`.
