Better still, do the same job in CSS with `hyphens: none` plus `overflow-wrap: break-word` on those selectors and delete the walker, which removes the text-mutation problem entirely.
- **Why:** It silently degrades two things every visitor uses — browser search and copy-paste — across the whole site, in exchange for a typographic nicety that only matters in a handful of large headings.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:1529-1558`. Every page, all body text.
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:1550` `textNode.nodeValue = (textNode.nodeValue || '').replace(/([A-Za-z])-([A-Za-z])/g, '$1‑$2');` with root `document.body` at 1531.
- **Verification:** I re-derived every number from the two probe files independently and they match to the pixel. /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ 31310 mobile / 17172 desktop = 1.82, 37.1 screens at 844. /casement-windows/ 21708 / 15171 = 1.43, 25.7. /aluminium-windows/ 21563 (25.5), /flush-casement-windows/ 20228 (24.0), /upvc-doors/ 19976 (23.7), /aluminium-doors/ 19690 (23.3), /patio-doors/ 17763 (21.0), /french-doors/ 17512 (20.7), /heritage-windows/ 17455 (20.7), /aluminium-bifold-doors/ 17006 (20.1), /tilt-turn-windows/ 16593 (19.7) — the worst-11 list is correct and in the right order. 'Over 12,000px' returns exactly 23 of 38. /sliding-sash-windows/ is 9393 / 8891 = 1.06, 11.1 screens, confirming it as the sole outlier. The mobile-specific sash CSS is at src/scss/main.scss:24079-24090 as cited, including `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-product-gallery-band .section-heading h2{max-width:16ch;font-size:1.65rem}` and `.generated-page--sliding-sash .fg-product-gallery-band .section-heading > p:not(.eyebrow){display:none}`, followed by the `overflow-x:auto; scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` choice-map rail. Three of the four cited sash components exist in the live HTML (`fg-sash-carousel` x4, `fg-sash-mobile-specs`, `fg-sash-heading--mobile`); `fg-sash-gallery--mobile` does not exist anywhere in the theme — a fabricated class name, but the only error I found and it does not affect the argument. The hero anchor claim checks out: /casement-windows/ hero CTAs point at `#fenster-product-quote` and `#fenster-enquiry`, and by character position within `<main>` those targets sit at 58.0% and 76.6% of the page, consistent with the reported 13,656px and 18,057px on a 21,708px page. Crucially, this is NOT ruled out by the docs — it is endorsed by them. PROGRESS.md:4194 records exactly this reasoning already applied once: 'Reassessed the full phone journey after the first carousel pass remained too long. The rendered mobile page was roughly 18,600px high because the model decision was repeated through the detail run, generic Product information, More information checks, furniture catalogue, order process and related-link band.' SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md documents the same page being turned 'from a long, repetitive product brochure into a visual, responsive buying journey', and STYLE.md:52 sets it as a regression standard. Type Creative and category INVESTIGATE are the right calls — the numbers are objective but 'this page is too long' is a judgement, and the finding correctly says to prove it on /casement-windows/ first before rolling out. Only nit: the median mobile-to-desktop ratio is 1.65, not 1.63.

#### [142] Enquiry form: on submit, focus is thrown to <body> and the success message is never focused despite having tabindex="-1"

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 70% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The feedback panel is authored ready to receive focus — `<div class="fg-enquiry-form__feedback" data-fg-enquiry-feedback tabindex="-1" hidden>` (template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:77) — but `showFeedback()` (src/js/main.js:2595-2615) never calls `.focus()` on it. Worse, the success path calls `submitButton?.blur()` (src/js/main.js:2664) immediately before showing the message, which moves focus to `<body>`: a keyboard user's next Tab restarts from the top of the document, past the whole header and mega menu, with no indication the form succeeded. The announcement is also fragile: `role` and `aria-live` are set on the element *after* the content has already been inserted and unhidden (main.js:2612-2614), so the live region is registered post-mutation, which NVDA and VoiceOver announce inconsistently.
- **Recommendation:** Drop the 'move the French-doors install up' step: alu-door-french-flag-install-1600w.webp is already the first body image on the route, under 'The door that matches the windows.', and AI.md:533-535 records that placement (and its exclusion from the hero) as a measured decision. What is actually left is (a) gating the case-study strip, which is finding 1's fix and belongs there, and (b) the hero, which AI.md:535 and PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md:97 both record as an open owner decision awaiting a wide aluminium-entrance-door asset. The only new proposal worth putting to the owner is the interim `.fg-lv-placeholder` panel in place of the uPVC-reading hero — and that is a judgement call about whether a marked gap looks better than a wrong-material photograph, not a defect fix.
- **Why:** This is the conversion event of the entire site, on 669 pages. A keyboard or screen-reader user currently has no reliable confirmation their enquiry sent and loses their place in the document entirely, so the likeliest behaviour is to submit again or abandon. It is also the difference between passing and failing SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA). The author already wired the fix (`tabindex="-1"`); only the call is missing.
- **Affected:** 669 pages carry `.fg-enquiry-form`. Both the success and error branches.
- **Evidence:** template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:77 (`tabindex="-1"` present, unused); src/js/main.js:2595-2615 (`showFeedback` — no `.focus()`, role/aria-live set after content insertion at :2612-2614); src/js/main.js:2664 (`submitButton?.blur()`).
- **Verification:** The observation reproduces exactly. I inventoried every <img> inside <main> on live/aluminium-doors.html in document order: hero products/curated/sheerline-aluminium-door.jpg, then trust marks, then the Thermlock logo, then five body images — alu-door-french-flag-install-1600w.webp (French doors, ours), alu-door-invisihinge.webp (supplier composite), alu-door-thermlock-cutaway.webp (CGI), alu-door-low-threshold.webp (threshold crop) — then 12 Classic corner renders, 8 handle cut-outs, and a case-study strip that is indeed the wrong-product fallback (cs-winslow-secondary-glazing-card.jpg, cs-leighton-buzzard-casement-front.jpg, cs-mk-whitehouse-bifold-closed.jpg). I looked at shots/desktop/aluminium-doors--fold.png: the hero is an interior kitchen scene with pale framing, exactly as AI.md:662 describes. So "no photograph of a single aluminium entrance door on a house" holds. What is wrong is the recommendation. (1) "Move the French-doors install up to the opening section" is ALREADY DONE — it is the very first body image, sitting under the heading "The door that matches the windows." AI.md:533-535 explains this placement was a measured decision (the hero is a 3.2:1 letterbox and a tall symmetric subject would be cropped to handles and blinds), so the finding is recommending the state that already exists. (2) The hero is documented as an open owner decision, not an oversight: AI.md:535 "The hero therefore still needs a genuinely wide asset and remains the owner's deferred decision", and PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md:97 tracks it as "Aluminium doors — new gap" with the bank's Doors/aluminium folder empty. (3) Gating the case-study strip is finding 1's recommendation, not new here (verified: generated-page.php:5294 `$no_case_study_routes = ['aluminium-windows','tilt-turn-windows']` — aluminium-doors is absent, so the fallback fires). Net: the synthesis is fair and worth stating, but nothing in the recommendation is both new and actionable, so the impact of ACTING on this finding is lower than claimed.

#### [217] The WindowCAD quote tool is rendered at 70% scale on mobile, shrinking its own type and controls

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 60% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** On /online-quote/ the third-party WindowCAD configurator is embedded with a scale trick: `.fg-oq-hero__frame` sets `--fg-quote-tool-scale: 0.7` at `<=860px`, and the iframe is sized `width/height: calc(100% / 0.7)` then `transform: scale(0.7)` from the top-left. At 390px the frame is `min(520px, 64vh)` = 520px tall, so the embedded document is laid out in a 520 x 740 CSS-px viewport and displayed at 364 x 518 — the 364x518 figure from `getBoundingClientRect` is the post-transform visual box, not the viewport the tool sees. So the tool is not being squeezed into a phone-width layout; it gets tablet-width room. The residual risk is the inverse: everything the tool draws is displayed at 70% of its intended size, so its 16px labels appear at ~11px and its 44px controls at ~31px. Nested-scroll containment is already handled (`overscroll-behavior: contain` on both frame and iframe, `data-lenis-prevent` on the wrapper, plus a bordered card with an `fg-oq-ring` attention cue), and STYLE.md:51 is satisfied — the desktop `Expand view` / `Open in new tab` pair is hidden at `<=860px` and replaced by a same-tab `.fg-oq-hero__start-mobile` "Open quote tool" link. What has not been established is whether the tool is legible and tappable at 70%: it is cross-origin, and 12 seconds of headless observation on a throttled connection showed only a loading bar.
- **Recommendation:** Test the WindowCAD retail interface on a real iPhone at 390px and record two things specifically: whether its type is readable at the 0.7 scale, and whether its own controls remain tappable once shrunk to ~31px. If legibility fails, raise `--fg-quote-tool-scale` toward 0.85 at `<=560px` (which narrows the internal viewport to ~428px — check the tool still lays out at that width) and raise the frame to `min(660px, 78vh)` so the taller box absorbs the reduced scale. If the tool cannot be made comfortable at any scale, drop the inline frame at `<=560px` and make the existing `.fg-oq-hero__start-mobile` "Open quote tool" link the only mobile route. Do not add a scroll boundary — `overscroll-behavior: contain` and `data-lenis-prevent` are already in place.
- **Why:** Two embedded tools where the first interaction after arriving is dropped. On the customer portal that first interaction is a customer trying to look up their own order.
- **Affected:** `src/scss/main.scss:115`; exceptions at 4054, 21169, 21565, 41419. Affects `/contact/` and the customer-portal route.
- **Evidence:** `node_modules/lenis/dist/lenis.mjs:1000` `if (this.isScrolling === "smooth") className += " lenis-smooth";`; `src/js/main.js:2816` `lerp: 0.075`; `grep -n "lenis-smooth" src/scss/main.scss` returns exactly five rules — the blanket one plus four quote-wrapper exceptions; `contact.php:177` and `customer-portal.php:43` are the two uncovered iframes.
- **Verification:** The central premise is a measurement artefact, and the cited CSS belongs to a different component. The finding reads `getBoundingClientRect()` on an element carrying a CSS transform: `.fg-oq-hero__frame iframe{width:calc(100%/var(--fg-quote-tool-scale));height:calc(100%/var(--fg-quote-tool-scale));transform:scale(var(--fg-quote-tool-scale));transform-origin:top left}` with `@media(max-width: 860px){.fg-oq-hero__frame{height:min(520px,64vh); --fg-quote-tool-scale: 0.7}}`. getBoundingClientRect returns the POST-transform visual box, so 364x518 is what you see, not what the embedded document gets. The WindowCAD retail interface is actually laid out in a 364/0.7 = 520 x 518/0.7 = 740 CSS-px viewport and then visually shrunk to 70%. That is the opposite of the stated problem: the scale trick exists precisely to hand the tool a tablet-width viewport on a phone. 'A full window-configurator UI in 364x518 is a demanding target' is therefore not the question to test. The quoted rule is also the wrong one: `.fg-product-quote-embed__frame{height:clamp(360px,44vh,520px)}` / `@media(max-width:860px){clamp(390px,58vh,560px)}` governs the PRODUCT-page embeds (and correctly predicts casement's 488px: 58vh of 844 = 489.5 less 2px border), while /online-quote/ uses `.fg-oq-hero__frame` with `min(520px,64vh)` = 520px less 2px border = 518, which is what was measured. Two further claims fail. 'Nested vertical scroll inside a scrolling page is a known mobile trap' — already mitigated: `.fg-oq-hero__frame` sets `overscroll-behavior:contain`, the iframe sets it too, the wrapper carries `data-lenis-prevent`, and the frame is a bordered, shadowed card with an animated `fg-oq-ring` focus cue, so the recommendation to 'add a visible scroll boundary' asks for something already present. And the assessment of STYLE.md:51, while reaching the right verdict, gets there by the wrong route: the visible desktop actions ('Expand view', 'Open in new tab', the latter `target="_blank"`) are hidden on mobile by `@media(max-width:860px){.fg-oq-hero__start,.fg-oq-hero__tool-actions{display:none}}`; the requirement is met instead by a separate `.fg-oq-hero__start-mobile` link, 'Open quote tool', same-tab, revealed only at `<=860px`. What survives, and is worth a device test, is a different question: at 70% scale the tool's own 16px type renders at ~11px and its own 44px controls at ~31px, so the risk is legibility and tap-target shrinkage inside a correctly-sized viewport, not a layout that does not fit.

#### [206] Gibson Regular and SemiBold are downloaded twice on the first page of a visit — 58KB of dead preload

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The `<link rel="preload">` tags in the head point at `.../fonts/Gibson-Regular.woff2?ver=1783344686` and `.../fonts/Gibson-SemiBold.woff2?ver=1783344686`, but the `@font-face` rules in main.css resolve to the same files with no query string. Different URLs means the preload never satisfies the font request, so each file is fetched twice. Corroborated by probe-mobile.json's own resource accounting on `/`: `byType.link` n=5 and `byType.css` n=3 with 89,240 bytes, against curl-measured file sizes of Regular 31,000 + SemiBold 27,432 + Bold 29,908 = 88,340 — all three weights via CSS, two of them also via preload. 58,432 duplicated bytes. Because the files are cached after first fetch, the cost lands once per cold cache on the first page of a visit (probe shows link/css bytes 0 on later routes), not on every page view. Gibson-Bold has no preload and is fetched once, correctly.
- **Recommendation:** Strip the `?ver=` query from the two preload hrefs so they match the `@font-face` `src` byte for byte — or add the same version string to the `@font-face` URLs in `src/scss/main.scss`. Either way the two sides must be identical. Verify by loading with a cold cache and confirming exactly three woff2 entries in Resource Timing, not five, and that the two remaining Regular/SemiBold entries have initiatorType `link` rather than `css`.
- **Why:** A disabled 623-line block is the thing that gets accidentally re-enabled, and it would throw `ReferenceError: THREE is not defined` on the homepage the instant it did. It also makes every future search of main.js noisier.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:7075-7697` (623 lines). No markup anywhere: `data-fg-studio-step` and `data-fg-home-studio-progress` appear in zero PHP files and zero live pages.
- **Evidence:** `sed -n '7075p' src/js/main.js` → `if (false) {`; `grep -c THREE src/js/main.js` → 74; `grep -c "WebGLRenderer" assets/js/main.js` → 0 and same for the live bundle; AI.md:140 "there is no `three` package"; STYLE.md:373.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and I reproduced it three independent ways; only the frequency claim in the rationale is wrong.

CONFIRMED — URL mismatch: live/home.html head carries `<link rel="preload" data-clarity-unmask="true" href="https://fensterglazing.com/app/themes/fenster/assets/fonts/Gibson-Regular.woff2?ver=1783344686" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>` and the same for Gibson-SemiBold. Extracting every `@font-face` block from live/main.css gives four rules, all with `src:url("../fonts/Gibson-<W>.woff2")` and no query string. Gibson-Bold and Gibson-Light have no preload.

CONFIRMED — the duplicate transfer, from the probe's own data rather than the finding's: probe-mobile.json `/` perf.byType shows `link {n:5, bytes:345732}` and `css {n:3, bytes:89240}`. curl -I gives Gibson-Regular 31,000, SemiBold 27,432, Bold 29,908 — sum 88,340, which matches the css-initiated 89,240 (transfer overhead) almost exactly. So all THREE weights are fetched by the stylesheet while TWO of them are also fetched by the preload links. 31,000 + 27,432 = 58,432 bytes duplicated, matching the finding's 58KB.

REVISED — 'every page, every visit' is wrong. probe-mobile.json perf.byType for /casement-windows/, /composite-doors/ and /online-quote/ all show `link` and `css` bytes 0, i.e. served from cache after the first page. The waste is 58KB once per cold cache, on the first page of a visit — not on every page view. That is still a real first-impression cost and the preload is still a net negative today, but the impact is smaller than stated. NOT already-ruled: AI.md:38 records 'WOFF2 Gibson fonts with critical font preloads' as intentional, which makes this a bug inside a deliberate feature rather than a decision to leave alone.

#### [221] Colour-hub deep links stop Lenis and re-assert a scroll position four times over a second, in two copies of the same code

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 97% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `data-fg-integral-blinds-reveal` appears in no PHP template and on none of the fetched live pages, yet everything that served it is still present: the controller and chroma-key loop (src/js/main.js:1292-1527, 236 lines), the `.fg-integral-blinds-reveal` stylesheet block (src/scss/main.scss:25681-25766), `fenster_integral_blinds_reveal_url()` at inc/assets.php:200 with no caller, the `fg-blinds-reveal-locked` Lenis stop/start hook at main.js:2827-2830, and assets/videos/product-scroll/integral-blinds-chroma.mp4 (7,060,256 bytes — 5.9x the next largest file in that folder). generated-page.php:3138 still stamps `generated-page--integral-blinds-reveal` on the article, and it is present in live/integral-blinds.html with nothing to style. The real cost is documentation: HANDOVER.md:1072-1097 still documents the whole feature under 'Current accepted behaviour' with a nine-point spec and a 'Runtime files' list that names generated-page.php as the markup, which is now false; AI.md:971 still lists the video as an optimised asset; and no entry in PROGRESS.md or LIVECHANGES.md records the removal. None of this reaches a visitor: the video is never requested, the dead block never runs, and `fg-blinds-reveal-locked` is only ever added at main.js:1314 inside that same dead block, so the `lenis.stop()` branch cannot fire.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the five-timer race with a `ResizeObserver` on the target section (or `document.body`) that re-runs `settle()` whenever the measured offset moves by more than a few pixels, disconnecting on first user input or after 3 seconds — the chapter-stack controller at `src/js/main.js:5848` already uses exactly this pattern for exactly this problem. Then delete the duplicate deep-link block from the coverflow controller at `src/js/main.js:4620-4679`, since `[data-fg-colour-carousel]` only exists on `/heritage-aluminium-doors/`, which has no colour deep links.
- **Why:** Colour deep links are the landing target for colour-specific search and ad traffic; landing short of the swatch wastes the click. And the same fragile logic exists in two places, one of which is unreachable.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:7934-7988` (live) and `4620-4679` (duplicate, unreachable). `/colour-options/`.
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:7968` `[120, 350, 700].forEach((delay) => window.setTimeout(...))` plus a further `setTimeout(..., 950)` at 7971 and an immediate `settle()` at 7967; `data-fg-colour-carousel` appears only in `template-parts/sections/heritage-aluminium-doors.php:235` and on no live page carrying a `colour` query parameter.
- **Verification:** Every artefact claim checks out; only the risk narrative is overstated. Verified: `grep -rn 'data-fg-integral-blinds' --include='*.php'` returns nothing, so the markup is gone. src/js/main.js:1292 is `const integralBlindsReveal = document.querySelector('[data-fg-integral-blinds-reveal]');` and the block ends at 1527 (`video.load();` / closing braces, with `preventHyphenatedWordSplits` starting at 1529) — 236 lines, exactly as claimed. src/scss/main.scss:25681 `html.fg-blinds-reveal-locked` through the `.fg-integral-blinds-reveal{display:none}` media query ending at 25766. `fenster_integral_blinds_reveal_url()` is at inc/assets.php:200 and is referenced nowhere else in any PHP file. The Lenis hook is at main.js:2827-2830. generated-page.php:3138 still emits `generated-page--integral-blinds-reveal` and `grep -c` on live/integral-blinds.html gives 1 for that class and 0 for `fg-integral-blinds-reveal__canvas`. `assets/videos/product-scroll/integral-blinds-chroma.mp4` is 7,060,256 bytes, the largest file in that folder by 5.9x. HANDOVER.md:1072-1097 does still describe the reveal under 'Current accepted behaviour' with a nine-point spec and a 'Runtime files' list naming generated-page.php as the markup — which is now false. No doc records the removal (PROGRESS.md's last entries are 2026-06-23/24 building it; AI.md:971 still lists the video as an optimised asset). Overstated: 'the dead fg-blinds-reveal-locked branch is a live lenis.stop() path that could be triggered by accident' — the class is added at main.js:1314 only, inside the same dead block, so nothing can set it. And 'a 7.06MB video still shipped' reads as page weight; it is repo/deploy weight only, since no page requests it. Impact should drop to Low: the real cost is documentation rot plus ~330 lines and 7MB of dead repo, none of which reaches a visitor.

#### [148] Enquiry form: on successful submit, focus is thrown to <body> and the success message is never focused despite having tabindex="-1"

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `header.php:26` opens `<main id="main-content" class="site-main">` for every request, and six section templates then open a second `<main>` inside it: roof-lanterns.php:37, flat-rooflights.php:21 and heritage-aluminium-doors.php:83 each repeat `id="main-content"` verbatim, while generated-page.php:2344 (handle options), generated-page.php:2734 (colour hub) and customer-portal.php:8 open an unnamed second `<main>`. HTML permits only one `<main>` per document; screen-reader landmark navigation lists two "main" regions and the user cannot tell which is the content. The duplicated id also means the skip link's `#main-content` target is ambiguous — it happens to resolve to the outer one, so the skip still works, but any future anchor or script keyed on that id will pick whichever the browser reaches first.
- **Recommendation:** In `showFeedback()` (src/js/main.js:2595-2615): (a) move the `role`/`aria-live` assignment (currently :2613-2614) to before `feedback.replaceChildren()` at :2598 — or better, put `role="status"` statically in enquiry-form.php:77 and only swap it to `role="alert"` on the error branch; (b) add `feedback.focus({ preventScroll: true })` as the last statement, which is what the existing `tabindex="-1"` was clearly put there for; (c) delete the `submitButton?.blur()` at src/js/main.js:2666 (NOT :2664 — that line is `const submittedHeight = …` and is load-bearing for the post-submit height lock). Note the blur is on the success path only; the error branch at :2712-2717 already leaves focus on the button, so (a) and (b) are the fixes that matter there.
- **Why:** Landmark navigation is how a screen-reader user skips a header they have already heard 40 times. Two mains makes the shortcut unreliable, and the duplicate id is an HTML validity error sitting directly under the site's own accessibility affordance. It is a small, contained edit — but it is currently the only structural semantics defect in an otherwise flawless 712-page corpus, which is why it is worth closing.
- **Affected:** 5 live routes verified in the 712-page corpus: /roof-lanterns/, /flat-rooflights/, /heritage-aluminium-doors/, /colour-options/, /handle-options/ (the first three also carry the duplicate id). customer-portal.php is a sixth template with the same pattern.
- **Evidence:** Scan of all 712 pages: exactly 5 files contain more than one `<main …>` tag; 3 of those contain `id="main-content"` twice. Sources: header.php:26; template-parts/sections/roof-lanterns.php:37; flat-rooflights.php:21; heritage-aluminium-doors.php:83; generated-page.php:2344; generated-page.php:2734; customer-portal.php:8.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and reproduces exactly, but one cited line number is wrong in a way that would break the build if acted on. Verified true: template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php:77 is literally `<div class="fg-enquiry-form__feedback" data-fg-enquiry-feedback tabindex="-1" hidden></div>`; showFeedback occupies src/js/main.js:2595-2615 exactly as cited, with `feedback.append(icon, content)` at :2610, `feedback.hidden = false` at :2611, and `setAttribute('role'…)` / `setAttribute('aria-live'…)` at :2613-2614 — i.e. the live region is registered after the mutation, as claimed. Grepping the whole file for `showFeedback` returns only the definition (:2595) and two call sites (:2671 success, :2713 error); there is no `.focus()` on the feedback element anywhere. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) `submitButton?.blur()` is at src/js/main.js:2666, NOT :2664. Line 2664 is `const submittedHeight = Math.ceil(form.getBoundingClientRect().height);` — deleting :2664 as the recommendation instructs would remove the height lock and break the success layout. (2) `affected` overstates: `submitButton?.blur()` sits only inside the success path (:2666, before the `catch` at :2712), so focus is thrown to <body> on SUCCESS ONLY. On the error branch focus stays on the submit button — still no focus move to the message, still the post-mutation live region, but not the 'lost in the document' symptom. Impact, type and the substantive fix are unchanged.

#### [152] Multi-step enquiry form changes step without announcing it

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 94% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.fg-enquiry-form input:not([type="checkbox"]):focus, select:focus, textarea:focus { border-color: var(--color-accent); outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(46,172,102,0.16) }` (src/scss/main.scss:18498-18504). The `outline: 0` removes the platform ring and nothing restores it. What replaces it: the 4px glow at 16% alpha composites to rgb(222,242,231) over a white field — 1.17:1, i.e. essentially nothing — and over the dark form panel to rgb(7,65,65), 1.28:1. The remaining signal is a 1px border moving from rgb(46,83,93) to #2eac66, a state change of 2.87:1, just under the 3:1 threshold. `.fg-commercial-form` repeats the same rule at main.scss:18528-18534 (alpha 0.18). CRUCIALLY there is no correct variant anywhere: the `.fg-home-showroom` / `.fg-quote-page` / `.fg-oq-form` / `.fg-contact-form` group at main.scss:18791-18805 darkens the border to `--color-accent-dark` but never re-declares `outline`, so the `outline: 0` from :18500 still applies to those forms too. There is also no global `:focus-visible` fallback in the stylesheet to catch it.
- **Recommendation:** In all three rules — src/scss/main.scss:18498-18504, :18528-18534 and the group at :18791-18805 — delete `outline: 0` (the third rule needs `outline: 3px solid var(--color-accent-dark); outline-offset: 2px` added explicitly, because removing `outline: 0` from :18502 alone is what fixes it and the group already inherits nothing else). Keep the border-colour change as decoration. Raise the glow to `rgba(32,130,76,0.45)` if you want to keep it; do not rely on the glow alone at any alpha below ~0.4 — 0.16 over white is invisible at any monitor gamma.
- **Why:** Losing your place in a multi-step form is the most common reason people abandon one, and a silent backwards jump reads as the form breaking. It is a single attribute plus one string, on the site's main conversion path.
- **Affected:** Stepped enquiry forms (a subset of the 669 pages carrying `.fg-enquiry-form`; the stepped mode is viewport-dependent via `isSteppedForm()`).
- **Evidence:** src/js/main.js:2500-2526 (`updateSteps`, `progressText.textContent = ...` at :2515-2517); :2556-2576 (`showStepForInvalidField`, calls `updateSteps(invalidStep)` then `reportValidity()` with no announcement); template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php — grep for `aria-live` in the theme returns 12 elements, none of them the enquiry progress text.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and the arithmetic is right, but the finding's one piece of good news is false — which makes the problem slightly worse than described, and makes the recommendation incomplete. VERIFIED: src/scss/main.scss:18498-18504 is verbatim `border-color: var(--color-accent); outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(46,172,102,0.16)` (the rule closes at :18504, not :18503); `.fg-commercial-form` repeats it at :18528-18534 with alpha 0.18. I recomputed the composites independently: rgba(46,172,102,0.16) over #ffffff = rgb(221.6, 241.7, 230.5) → relative luminance 0.8481 → 1.169:1 against white, so 1.17:1 is correct. Over #002d3a the same glow gives rgb(7,65,65), L 0.0421 vs panel L 0.0219 → 1.28:1 (finding said 1.29 — rounding). The border state change: resting rgba(255,255,255,0.18) over the panel composites to rgb(46,83,93), L 0.0756; focus #2eac66, L 0.3105 → 2.87:1, matching the quoted ~2.90:1 and sitting just under the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 threshold. There is no global `:focus-visible` fallback for inputs in the stylesheet, so `outline: 0` really does leave nothing. CORRECTION: 'The one place it is done properly is `.fg-home-showroom …` (main.scss:18791)' is wrong. That selector group (:18791-18805, which also covers `.fg-quote-page`, `.fg-oq-form` and `.fg-contact-form`, not just the showroom) declares only `border-color: var(--color-accent-dark)` and the same `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(46,172,102,0.16)`. It never re-declares `outline`, so the `outline: 0` from :18500-18504 still wins by default and the platform ring is suppressed there too. There is no correct implementation anywhere on the site; the darker border only lifts the state-change ratio, it does not restore an indicator. The fix must therefore also cover :18791-18805.

#### [210] The two footer consent buttons collapse to 20px tall on mobile because the padding rescue only targets links

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.site-footer__cookie-settings, .site-footer__stat-settings { padding: 0 }` is set in the base stylesheet and never overridden. At `@media(max-width:560px)` the footer bottom bar drops to `font-size:.78rem` and the rescue rule `.site-footer__bottom a { padding:.35rem 0 }` gives the sibling links breathing room — but it is scoped to `a`, and these two controls are `<button>`, so they get nothing and collapse to the bare line box. Measured 179x20: 'Opt out of anonymous statistics' on 30 routes and 'Cookie settings' on 27 (probe-mobile.json; 27 of 38 routes hit the probe's 30-item cap, so these are floors). The neighbouring Privacy Policy, Cookie Policy and Terms links render 179x31 for the same font size purely because the `a` rule reaches them — the inconsistency is the tell that this is an oversight rather than a decision. This is not a WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 failure: at 20px tall with an 8px grid gap the 24px-circle spacing exception is satisfied. It is a usability and internal-consistency defect (STYLE.md:350). Note that 'Cookie settings' ships with the `hidden` attribute and is revealed by JS only once a consent choice has been recorded, which is correct and should not be changed.
- **Recommendation:** In the `@media(max-width:560px)` footer block, change the selector `.site-footer__bottom a { padding:.35rem 0; text-align:center }` to `.site-footer__bottom a, .site-footer__bottom button { padding:.35rem 0; text-align:center }` so the two consent buttons pick up the same treatment as their neighbours, or add `.site-footer__cookie-settings, .site-footer__stat-settings { min-height:44px; padding:.7rem 0 }` explicitly. One selector edit. Leave `.site-footer__nav a { min-height:42px }` as it is — 42px clears every applicable standard and changing it to 44 is a preference, not a fix.
- **Why:** main.js is 8,234 lines and roughly a tenth of it never runs. That is the difference between a person being able to read this file and not, and it is why the audit brief itself was wrong about two of the site's headline interactions.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js` — 6365-6466, 6735-6790, 4810 + 4994-5048, 966-995, 6900-6940, 2414-2420 (+ the stepped-form block), 1197/1249-1254, 6476. Plus the static/scroll theatre split at 6468-6665.
- **Evidence:** Scripted sweep of every `querySelector(All)('[data-…]')` / `('.class')` token in `src/js/main.js` against all theme `*.php` and all 38 `scratchpad/live/*.html`. `data-fg-product-theatre-mode="static"` is the only occurrence of that attribute across the live set (`grep -o 'data-fg-product-theatre-mode="[a-z]*"' *.html`), and `data-fg-home-product-story` returns 0 in both PHP and live HTML.
- **Verification:** The CSS and the two headline measurements are exactly right; one supporting count is wrong by 2.5x, the compliance framing does not survive checking, and the footer-nav sub-claim is a preference rather than a defect.

CONFIRMED — CSS: base rule `.site-footer__cookie-settings,.site-footer__stat-settings{padding:0;border:0;background:rgba(0,0,0,0);color:hsla(0,0%,100%,.86);cursor:pointer;font:inherit;text-decoration:none}` with no mobile override. At `@media(max-width: 560px)` (context proved by brace-walk): `.site-footer__bottom{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:.5rem;margin-top:.9rem;padding-top:.9rem;font-size:.78rem}` and `.site-footer__bottom a{padding:.35rem 0;text-align:center}`. The padding rescue is scoped to `a` only, so the two `<button>` elements get nothing and collapse to the line box. `.site-footer__nav a{min-height:42px;padding:.42rem 0;font-size:.82rem}` is also inside the 560px block, confirmed.

CONFIRMED — counts I recomputed myself from probe-mobile.json: site-footer__stat-settings 179x20 on 30 routes; site-footer__cookie-settings 179x20 on 27 routes; 162x42 across 468 instances (plus 144 more at 162x44 where a label wraps).

WRONG — 'Privacy Policy 179x31 on 87 instances'. The true figure is 34. Cookie Policy is 31 and Terms & Conditions is 22. There is one of each per page, so 87 is not achievable across 38 routes. Also worth flagging for anyone reusing these numbers: 27 of the 38 routes hit the probe's 30-entry smallTargets cap (I compared len(smallTargets) against smallTargetCount per route), so all of these are floors, not exact counts.

OVERSTATED — the WCAG/regulatory framing. At 20px tall inside a grid with `gap:.5rem` (8px), adjacent control centres are at least 28px apart, so 24px-diameter circles centred on each do not intersect and the SC 2.5.8 spacing exception is satisfied. There is no conformance failure. The 'as easy to withdraw as to give' principle concerns the availability and reachability of the control, not its pixel height, and the control is present in the footer of every page.

CONTEXT the finding missed: `<button type="button" class="site-footer__cookie-settings" data-fg-cookie-settings hidden>Cookie settings</button>` ships `hidden`, with `.site-footer__cookie-settings[hidden]{display:none}` in CSS. It is revealed by JS only after a consent choice has been recorded — which is correct behaviour, and explains why the probe (run with consent pre-seeded) sees it while a first-time visitor does not.

NOT A DEFECT — the `.site-footer__nav a{min-height:42px}` '2px short' point. 42px clears WCAG 2.2's 24px minimum comfortably; 44px is a platform convention, not a requirement. Calling a deliberate 42px a defect is a preference dressed as one.

#### [214] The compare-wipe's two labels are aria-hidden, contradicting the component's own accessibility note

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The /about/ hero pairs `<a class="button">Get an instant price</a>` with `<a class="button button--light">Book a free consultation</a>` (about.php:122-123). The effective `.button--light` rule is `border-color:#fff; background:#fff; color:var(--color-steel)` — a white fill with a white border, so it has no visible edge at all. (The `hsla(0,0%,100%,.88)` variant with a `rgba(0,45,58,.42)` border is scoped to `.fg-cookie-consent` and does not apply here.) `.fg-about-hero` sets no background, so it sits on the near-white `--fg-page-gradient` canvas, and at 390px the second action reads as a bold centred word on a white bar rather than a button. STYLE.md:265 is explicit: "The CTA pair is green then dark ... The one exception is a dark panel, where a dark secondary disappears into the background: use `.button--light` there instead." The /about/ hero is not a dark panel. The pattern repeats across the page: about.php uses `button--light` at lines 123, 201, 214, 253, 279 and 300, several of them on the same light canvas.
- **Recommendation:** Change the /about/ hero secondary from `button button--light` to `button button--steel` (about.php:123), matching /windows-milton-keynes/ and the composite-doors hero. Then audit the other five `button--light` instances in about.php (lines 201, 214, 253, 279, 300) and switch the ones on the light canvas — 'Meet the team' in `.fg-about-founders` and 'Contact us' in `.fg-about-visit` at minimum — to `button--steel` as well. Finally sweep the remaining theme instances (generated-page.php, location-service.php, case-studies-residential.php, generated-simple.php, roof-lanterns.php) and correct any that are not inside a dark panel. Do not change `inc/consent.php`, whose `button--light` is scoped by `.fg-cookie-consent` to its own rule and is unaffected.
- **Why:** It is a one-line default in a component whose comment already states the intent. Everything else about this component is the best interaction work on the site.
- **Affected:** `template-parts/components/compare-wipe.php` (the `fg-wipe__tag` spans and the `$sr_label` default). Two routes: `/flush-casement-windows/`, `/double-glazing-replacement/`.
- **Evidence:** `compare-wipe.php`: `<span class="fg-wipe__tag fg-wipe__tag--overlay" aria-hidden="true">` and `--base` likewise, against the file's own note "the two tags name both sides". `$sr_label` defaults to 'Reveal the second photograph over the first'.
- **Verification:** The conclusion is right and the mobile screenshot proves it, but the CSS the finding quotes is the wrong rule, and the scope is much larger than 'possibly other routes'. CONFIRMED: the markup is exactly as stated, at template-parts/sections/about.php:122-123 — `<a class="button" href="<?php echo esc_url($quote_url); ?>">Get an instant price</a>` followed by `<a class="button button--light" href="<?php echo esc_url($consult_url); ?>">Book a free consultation</a>` — inside `<section class="fg-about-hero">`, which has no background of its own (`.fg-about-hero{padding-top:clamp(2rem,3.2vw,2.75rem)}` is the entire rule) and therefore sits on the pale `--fg-page-gradient` canvas. It is not a dark panel, so STYLE.md:265's sole exception does not apply. I read scratchpad/shots/mobile/about--fold.png: 'Book a free consultation' renders as a white bar with no discernible edge against the pale mint/grey gradient, directly beneath a solid green 'Get an instant price'. The affordance gap is real and if anything worse than described. WRONG EVIDENCE: `.button--light{border-color:rgba(0,45,58,.42);background:hsla(0,0%,100%,.88);color:var(--color-ink);box-shadow:none}` is not the base rule — I located all four `.button--light` declarations in main.css by offset and walked back to each selector start; that one is `.fg-cookie-consent .button--light` (cookie banner only). The rule actually in force is `.button--light{border-color:#fff;background:#fff;color:var(--color-steel)}`, and the same declaration appears in the inlined critical CSS at inc/assets.php:72. So the border is white on white — there is no faint 42%-opacity border to see, which is precisely why the button has no visible edge. There is no `.fg-about`-scoped override. WRONG SCOPE: about.php alone uses `button--light` six times (lines 123, 201, 214, 253, 279, 300), including 'Meet the team' in `.fg-about-founders` and 'Contact us' paired with a green Call button in `.fg-about-visit`, both on light surfaces — so this is a page-wide pattern on /about/, not one hero instance. A theme-wide grep also shows it in generated-page.php, location-service.php, case-studies-residential.php, generated-simple.php and roof-lanterns.php, some of which are legitimately on dark panels; those need checking individually rather than a blanket swap.

#### [151] The obscured-glass divider slider is invisible and can show no focus ring, so it is the one keyboard control on the site with no focus indicator

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.fg-obscure-stage__range { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; opacity: 0.01; pointer-events: none }` (src/scss/main.scss:10662-10672) hides a real `<input type="range">` (template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:2968) that is still tabbable, but at 1% opacity the platform focus ring is invisible too, and there is no `:has(:focus-visible)` rule anywhere for `.fg-obscure-stage` — the only focus rules in the whole obscured-glass block are for the picker buttons (main.scss:10302, 10575, 24692). A sighted keyboard user tabs onto the divider control and gets no indication they have it; they only discover it by pressing an arrow key and watching the divider move. The theme already ships the correct solution ten thousand lines away: `.fg-wipe__range` is invisible in exactly the same way and `.fg-wipe__stage:has(.fg-wipe__range:focus-visible) { outline: 3px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 3px }` (main.scss:39657-39661) puts the ring on the stage instead. NOTE: the integral-blinds visualiser is NOT affected — main.js:4337-4338 tracks which slider has focus and main.js:4021-4026 strokes a #2eac66 ring around the matching magnet on the canvas, which is what the comment at main.scss:39365-39370 is describing.
- **Recommendation:** Copy the `.fg-wipe__stage` pattern verbatim. Add one rule to src/scss/main.scss near :10662: `.fg-obscure-stage:has(.fg-obscure-stage__range:focus-visible) { outline: 3px solid var(--color-accent-dark); outline-offset: 3px }`. Use `--color-accent-dark` (#20824c) rather than `--color-accent` (#2eac66) so the ring clears 3:1 against the light stage. No change is needed to the integral-blinds visualiser.
- **Why:** The dots are the only way to reach models 2 and 3 of the sash range on a phone besides swiping, and this is a page selling a premium product to an older, period-property audience — precisely the users with the least steady tap accuracy. The fix is invisible and costs one pseudo-element. The dots themselves are otherwise exemplary: real `<button>`s with `aria-label="Show Ultimate Rose"` and `aria-pressed`, exactly as AI.md:906 requires.
- **Affected:** /sliding-sash-windows/, mobile viewports only. 3 dots.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:23786-23805 (`width: 28px; height: 6px`, `[aria-pressed="true"] { width: 48px }`, `gap: 0.5rem`); probe-mobile.json smallTargets for /sliding-sash-windows/: `{txt:"Show Ultimate Rose", w:48, h:6}`, `{txt:"Show Heritage Rose", w:28, h:6}`, `{txt:"Show Charisma Rose", w:28, h:6}`; markup verified in live/sliding-sash-windows.html.
- **Verification:** Half of this is right and half is refuted by code the finding did not read. CONFIRMED, part (a): src/scss/main.scss:10662-10672 is verbatim `.fg-obscure-stage__range { position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:8; width:100%; height:100%; margin:0; opacity:0.01; cursor:ew-resize; pointer-events:none; }`. I listed all 70-odd `.fg-obscure-stage*` selectors in the stylesheet and grepped for `obscure` + `focus`: the only focus rules are :10302 and :24692 (picker buttons) and :10575 (background button). Nothing draws a ring for the range, and there is no `:has()` rule for `.fg-obscure-stage`. The input is at generated-page.php:2968, is a real focusable `<input type="range">`, and `opacity:0.01` suppresses the platform ring — real SC 2.4.7 failure on /obscured-glass/. REFUTED, part (b): the blind visualiser DOES show focus. src/js/main.js:4337-4338 registers focus/blur listeners on both sliders that set a `focused` variable ('tilt' or 'lift') and call `nudge()`; the canvas renderer at :4021-4026 then strokes a #2eac66 rounded rect around the matching magnet at `lineWidth = Math.max(1.8, m.w * 0.14)`, offset outward by 30% of the magnet width. So a sighted keyboard user gets a visible, thick, accent-coloured ring on the exact control they are on, and it distinguishes tilt from lift. The SCSS comment at main.scss:39365-39370 documents this as the deliberate design: '…Focus is shown by a ring drawn round the matching magnet on the canvas.' The finding's claim that the user 'only find[s] out by pressing an arrow key' is wrong for /integral-blinds/, and its recommendation to un-hide the two sliders on focus is unnecessary work. Correcting scope from 2 pages to 1 and impact from Medium to Low accordingly. The referenced house pattern is real and correctly located (`.fg-wipe__stage:has(.fg-wipe__range:focus-visible)` at main.scss:39657-39661, one line off the cited 39655).

#### [204] Sash carousel pagination dots are 6px tall on mobile (sliding-sash page only)

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `@media(max-width:860px) .fg-sash-carousel__dots button { width:28px; height:6px; padding:0 }` (48x6 when `aria-pressed=true`). These are real `<button>` elements with real labels that switch the sash model, and they exist only at mobile (base rule sets `display:none`). probe-mobile.json confirms 28x6 and 48x6 on /sliding-sash-windows/. A 6px-tall control is well under the 44px platform convention and breaches STYLE.md:350 ('No mobile work is complete with ... unusable tap targets'). It is NOT a WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 failure: at 28px wide with an 8px gap the centres are 36px apart, so the 24px-circle spacing exception is satisfied. Mitigating, and stronger than the original finding claimed: directly above the dots sit 48x48 prev/next buttons and an aria-live status block showing the model name ('Ultimate Rose') and the position counter ('01 / 03'), so the dots are a third redundant path, not the only indicator. The equivalent `.fg-home-case-wall__dots` rule is dead code — that component is not rendered on any live page.
- **Recommendation:** Keep the pill visual exactly as it is, but make the button the hit area: `.fg-sash-carousel__dots button { height:44px; padding:19px 0; background:none; }` with the coloured pill moved to a `::before` at `height:6px;width:28px` (and `width:48px` on `[aria-pressed=true]`). Reduce `gap` to `.25rem` to compensate for the wider hit boxes. Do nothing about `.fg-home-case-wall__dots` — separately, that whole block in src/scss/main.scss:21037-26244 and src/js/main.js:6735 is dead and could be deleted.
- **Why:** It is a documented rule the codebase itself no longer keeps, and the drift is on the largest, highest-priority image on the whole location-page family. Vestibular-sensitive users have asked the browser to stop this and the site does it anyway.
- **Affected:** 12 selectors: `.fg-mk-cascade__media img`, `.fg-mk-deep-guide__media img`, `.fg-mk-showroom__media img`, `.fg-location-hero__image`, `.fg-location-local-guide__media img`, `.fg-location-gallery img`, `.fg-location-quote__preview img`, `.fg-sash-model__media img`, `.fg-sash-detail figure img`, `.fg-home-system-lab__steps figure`, `.fg-home-route-card img`, `.fg-home-dual img`, `.fg-home-case-card img`. Live with real `data-fg-depth` attributes on `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` (9), `/casement-windows-bletchley/` (5), `/sliding-sash-windows/` (3).
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:5660-5676` has no `prefers-reduced-motion` test (contrast with 5726 and 5777, which do). Parsed `assets/css/main.css`: 13 rules use `var(--fg-parallax-y`, 26 reduced-motion blocks, only `.fg-cas-lock__art` appears in both sets. AI.md:422 states the contract.
- **Verification:** The sash half is exactly right; the homepage half does not exist, the WCAG citation is arithmetically wrong, and the stated rationale is false.

CONFIRMED: base rule `.fg-sash-carousel__controls,.fg-sash-carousel__dots,...{display:none}` (main.css offset 110833, no media context) and `@media(max-width: 860px){.fg-sash-carousel__dots button{width:28px;height:6px;padding:0;border:0;border-radius:999px}}` plus `[aria-pressed=true]{width:48px}` (offset 400824, media context confirmed by brace-walk = @media(max-width: 860px)). probe-mobile.json /sliding-sash-windows/ smallTargets contains exactly {Show Ultimate Rose 48x6}, {Show Heritage Rose 28x6}, {Show Charisma Rose 28x6}. Markup verified in live/sliding-sash-windows.html.

REFUTED — homepage case wall: `fg-home-case-wall` appears in ZERO live HTML files (grep -l across scratchpad/live/*.html returns nothing), zero PHP templates (`grep -rn 'fg-home-case-wall\|fg-case-dot' --include=*.php` over the whole theme returns nothing), and `curl -s https://fensterglazing.com/ | grep -c fg-home-case-wall` = 0. It exists only in src/scss/main.scss (lines 21037-26244) and src/js/main.js:6735. It is dead code. There are no 9x9 dots on the homepage.

REFUTED — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8: the finding says the spacing exception fails because 24px circles would overlap. Dots are 28px wide with `gap:.5rem` (8px), so adjacent centres are 36px apart (48/28 pair: 24+8+14 = 46px). 24px-diameter circles centred on each do NOT intersect, so the spacing exception APPLIES and SC 2.5.8 is met. This is an internal-standard breach (STYLE.md:350 'No mobile work is complete with ... unusable tap targets'), not an accessibility conformance failure.

REFUTED — 'the only visible indicator of which of three Rose models is on screen': directly above the dots the markup carries `<div class="fg-sash-carousel__status" aria-live="polite"><strong data-fg-sash-name>Ultimate Rose</strong><span data-fg-sash-count>01 / 03</span></div>`, flanked by prev/next buttons measured in CSS at `width:48px;height:48px` (offset 399946, @media max-width 860px). The model name, the position counter and two 48px arrows are all present.

#### [215] Legend runs back and forth inside the open chat drawer indefinitely, beside the text input

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 92% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** /book-a-consultation/ has 63 sub-44px interactive targets, the highest of any Tier-1 route and double the site median of 31. 26 of them are calendar day cells at 41x43, plus two 40x40 month-navigation arrows (`.fg-consultation-booking__calendar-head button{width:2.5rem;height:2.5rem}`). The seven-column grid sits in a 330px card whose 308px inner track, split by `.22rem` (3.52px) gaps, yields exactly 41px per cell; the 43px height comes from `grid-template-rows:repeat(6, minmax(2.7rem, auto))`, which the `<=520px` block never overrides even though it does drop `min-height` to `2.35rem`. This clears WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24x24) but sits under Apple HIG 44pt, Material 48dp, and — most directly — STYLE.md's own Forms rule that "Tap targets should be at least `44px` high", on the first step of the site's most valuable conversion. Only 12 cells are actually enabled at any time (weekdays inside the booking window), so the mistap risk is concentrated on adjacent live dates rather than spread across all 26.
- **Recommendation:** At `<=520px`, raise the row floor to `grid-template-rows: repeat(6, minmax(2.875rem, auto))` (46px) — note that changing `min-height` alone will not do it, because the existing `minmax(2.7rem, auto)` row track already governs the rendered height. For width, the 41px is set by the 308px track, so reclaim horizontal room: drop `.fg-consultation-booking__calendar` padding-inline to 0 at `<=430px` and cut `.fg-consultation-booking__days` gap to `.1rem`, which gives (330 - 0 - 6x1.6)/7 = 45.8px cells. Do not raise the gap to 4px as previously suggested — the gap is already 3.52px and increasing it makes the cells narrower. Also raise the two month arrows from `2.5rem` to `2.75rem` (44px). The card has the vertical room: the calendar block is ~500px in an 844px viewport.
- **Why:** The drawer is where a visitor writes the question that becomes a lead. Perpetual motion two inches above the caret is the one place on this site where the character costs something.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:373-398`. Every page, whenever the Legend drawer is open.
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:383-397` `scheduleNextRun()` recurses unconditionally; pause exists only via `reduceMotion.matches` at 378 and `stopRoaming()` from `sleepLegend()` at 176.
- **Verification:** The defect is real and I reproduced every target measurement, but the geometry the finding uses to justify its fix is wrong and the fix as written does not work. CONFIRMED: probe-mobile.json /book-a-consultation/ has smallTargetCount 63 — I sorted all 38 routes and it is the highest (next is /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ at 54), and the true median is 31, so 'more than double the median' is right. Grouping the smallTargets array gives exactly 26 entries of `{tag:'button', w:41, h:43}` labelled 1-26, plus `{button, 40x40, '←'}` and `{button, 40x40, '→'}`. The CSS explains the numbers: `.fg-consultation-booking__days button{min-height:2.7rem}` = 43.2px base, `.fg-consultation-booking__calendar-head button{width:2.5rem;height:2.5rem}` = 40x40 exactly. The finding also UNDERSELLS its own case by not citing the strongest evidence available: STYLE.md's Forms section states 'Tap targets should be at least `44px` high' — this is the project's own written standard, not just Apple HIG, and the calendar breaks it. WRONG GEOMETRY: the finding says 'a seven-column grid inside a 358px card leaves ~41px per cell with ~6px gutters'. The real gap at 390px is `.22rem` = 3.52px, set by `@media(max-width: 520px){.fg-consultation-booking__days{gap:.22rem}}`, not ~6px. And I measured the calendar card in scratchpad/mfold/booking-390.png (left edge x≈70, right edge x≈853 at a 2.369x display scale) at 330px wide, not 358 — which the arithmetic independently confirms: card 330 less 2x`.7rem` mobile padding = 308px track, and (308 - 6x3.52)/7 = 41.0px, exactly the measured cell width. BROKEN RECOMMENDATION: '7 x 46 + 6 x 4 = 346px, inside the 358px container' does not hold — 346px does not fit a 308px track, and raising the gap from 3.52px to 4px would make cells NARROWER, not wider. More fundamentally, `min-height` only governs height; it cannot change the 41px width, which is the dimension furthest below 44. To get 44px wide at 390px you must reclaim the card's horizontal padding and cut the gap to near zero: (330 - 22.4)/7 = 44.0 at gap 0. One severity nuance the finding does not note: the screenshot shows only 12 of the cells are enabled (13, 14, 17-21, 24-28); the rest are disabled weekends/past dates, so a mistap on most cells is inert and the real risk is confined to adjacent enabled weekdays.

#### [222] A 623-line dead Three.js house-tour block is carried inside the production JS entry point

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** src/js/main.js:7075-7697 is a complete WebGL scene — house shell, hinged bifold pivots, a swinging composite door, a six-stop scroll-keyed camera tour, ACES tone mapping — written against a bare `THREE` global that is never imported and is not in package.json, guarded by a literal `if (false)`. esbuild strips it, so the runtime cost is genuinely zero (assets/js/main.js and the live bundle contain no `THREE`, `WebGLRenderer` or `PerspectiveCamera`). The cost is purely maintenance: 623 lines, 7.6% of an 8,234-line file, 74 references to an undefined identifier, dead `data-fg-studio-step` / `data-fg-home-studio-progress` handling, and a call into the live `updateDepthItems()` at 7620. Important context the original write-up missed: this is not undocumented. HANDOVER.md's '## Three.js Status' section names the `if (false) { ... THREE.* ... }` block explicitly, confirms it is absent from the compiled bundle, and rules 'Do not revive or work around the old Three.js/canvas experiment unless the owner explicitly asks for 3D again'; AI.md:140 says the same. So it is not a landmine and the handover is not misleading here — deleting it is tidiness, not defect repair.
- **Recommendation:** Optional housekeeping, owner's call. If taken: delete src/js/main.js:7075-7697 and replace the HANDOVER.md 'Three.js Status' bullet about the inactive block with one line recording that the source was removed, so the ruling ('do not reintroduce 3D unless the owner asks') survives the deletion. Do not do this in the same change as anything that touches `updateDepthItems`.
- **Why:** It is the cheapest available smoothness win on the four heaviest pages, and it costs nothing visually because Lenis already limits the effective update rate to one per frame.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:5662-5675`, `5729-5744`, `4969-4991`, `6582-6587`. Routes: `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/`, `/casement-windows-bletchley/`, `/sliding-sash-windows/`, `/casement-windows/`, `/aluminium-windows/`, `/`.
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:5673` `window.addEventListener('scroll', updateDepthItems, { passive: true });` — `updateDepthItems` at 5662 does `item.getBoundingClientRect()` then `item.style.setProperty` per item with no frame guard. Same shape at 5742 (`updateLockArrive`), 4986 (`handleScroll`) and 6634 (`syncScroll` → `updateFromScroll` at 6545). Compare 5830, 5649, 6452, 5182, which all guard.
- **Verification:** Every measurement is right, but the justification is refuted by the project docs and the type should change. Verified: src/js/main.js:7075 is `if (false) {`, the block closes at 7697 (623 lines of an 8,234-line file = 7.6%), `grep -c THREE src/js/main.js` → 74, `grep -c THREE assets/js/main.js` → 0 and the live scratchpad/live/main.js → 0, `grep -c WebGLRenderer assets/js/main.js` → 0. `data-fg-studio-step` and `data-fg-home-studio-progress` appear in zero PHP files. `updateDepthItems()` is called at 7620 inside the dead block (definition at 5662). AI.md:140 and STYLE.md:369-373 exist and say what is quoted. But the finding's 'why' — that this is a landmine nobody knows about and that the docs would mislead — is contradicted by the docs themselves. HANDOVER.md has a whole '## Three.js Status' section (immediately after the Review Showcase section) that states: package.json has no `three`, main.js imports Lenis only, inc/assets.php enqueues no Three.js, the compiled bundle contains no `THREE`/`WebGLRenderer`, 'There is inactive legacy source/styling for an old homepage 3D hero experiment: fg-home-hero-3d, data-fg-home-3d and an if (false) { ... THREE.* ... } block', and 'Do not revive or work around the old Three.js/canvas experiment unless the owner explicitly asks for 3D again.' AI.md:140 repeats it. So the dead block is precisely, accurately and repeatedly documented as accepted inactive legacy — the opposite of the integral-blinds case in finding 221. What remains is a housekeeping preference (delete recorded dead code vs. leave recorded dead code), which is a judgement call, not a defect. This borders on ALREADY_RULED; I stop short only because no doc actually says the block must stay.

#### [209] The Legend prompt bubble covers the bottom-right of the mobile viewport and its 29px dismiss control is undersized

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 80% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `.legend-assistant` is `position:fixed;right:0;bottom:0;z-index:1100;pointer-events:none`. At 390x844 the container occupies roughly x 112-380, y 734-840 — 71% of the width and the bottom 116px of the viewport. Once the visitor scrolls past 240px the 'Need a hand?' prompt bubble appears inside it and covers page content in that corner: in shots/mobile/windows-milton-keynes--fold.png it obscures the card labels 'uPVC Casement Windows' and 'uPVC Flush Sash Windows'. Its dismiss button is `.legend-assistant__prompt-close{width:1.8rem;height:1.8rem}` = 28.8px, flagged at 29x29 on 15 routes in probe-mobile.json. Two things that are NOT wrong and should not be changed: the bubble is scroll-gated at 240px in main.js (`Ie=240`, `qe=()=>{G||et()<Ie||...}`), which LIVECHAT.md:25 documents as the intended behaviour, so it is not unsolicited; and the z-index of 1100 over `.site-nav` (1001) is deliberate per LIVECHAT.md:315 (commit `46d9289`, 'Kept the mobile drawer above the fixed site header'), with the mobile-nav screenshot showing Legend sitting in empty space well below the last menu row, intercepting nothing.
- **Recommendation:** One change: raise `.legend-assistant__prompt-close` to a 44x44 hit area by keeping the 1.8rem circle as a `::before` and giving the button `width:44px;height:44px;padding:0;background:none`. Leave the z-index and the 240px scroll gate alone — both are recorded owner decisions in LIVECHAT.md. If the bottom-right obstruction is judged worth acting on, the cheap version is to shorten the bubble's dwell time or auto-collapse it to the launcher after a few seconds, not to move or re-layer the assistant.
- **Why:** The mega menu is the primary navigation on desktop and it currently traps keyboard users in a twenty-link panel with no exit, and announces nothing about its own state.
- **Affected:** `src/js/main.js:2844-2925` and `2971-2975`; `inc/template-tags.php` mega markup. Every page (site header).
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:2972` `if (event.key !== 'Escape' || !siteHeader.classList.contains('is-nav-open')) return;`. Live markup from `live/home.html`: `<li class="site-nav__item has-children has-mega-menu"><a href="...">Products</a><div class="site-nav__mega" hidden>` — no aria-expanded anywhere on the item.
- **Verification:** The measurements are right, but the two claims that carry the recommendation are wrong — one is contradicted by the shipped JavaScript, the other is a documented owner decision.

CONFIRMED: `.legend-assistant{position:fixed;right:0;bottom:0;z-index:1100;display:grid;justify-items:end;...;pointer-events:none}`; `.site-nav{...z-index:1001}`; `.site-header{...z-index:1000}`. `.legend-assistant__prompt-close{display:grid;width:1.8rem;height:1.8rem;padding:0;...}` = 28.8px, matching the probe's 29x29 on 15 routes. I opened shots/mobile/windows-milton-keynes--fold.png and the prompt bubble does sit over the product grid, covering the card labels 'uPVC Casement Windows' and 'uPVC Flush Sash Windows'. Measuring the widget in that image gives roughly x 112-380, y 734-840 in CSS px — within a couple of px of the finding's [111, 728, 279, 116].

REFUTED — 'appears without user action'. The compiled main.js contains `Ie=240` and the gate `qe=()=>{G||et()<Ie||(G=!0,oe.classList.add("is-prompt-visible"))}`, where `et()` is the max of every scroll-position source. The bubble cannot appear until the visitor has scrolled 240px. LIVECHAT.md:25 states this in words: 'Its `Need a hand?` speech bubble starts hidden, appears after the visitor scrolls 240px'. The recommendation to 'delay it until the user has scrolled past 50% of the page' is therefore asking for a gate that already exists, only further along.

ALREADY_RULED — the z-index/nav point. LIVECHAT.md:315 records commit `46d9289` 'Kept the mobile drawer above the fixed site header' as a deliberate fix, and LIVECHAT.md:46 records the `pointer-events` design specifically so the wrapper 'cannot block footer or cookie controls'. LIVECHAT.md:9 says 'Legend is complete, live and fully verified... Treat this section as settled unless a new Legend feature is deliberately started.' I also opened scratchpad/mfold/mobilenav-390.png: with the nav open the last row ('Free Consultation') ends at about 45% of the screen height and Legend sits alone in empty space in the bottom right. No menu row is covered and none can be intercepted, so STYLE.md:354 ('A hero, carousel or product card must never intercept taps meant for the menu') is not breached. Lowering z-index to 900 would work against a documented decision for no measured gain.

What survives: a 29x29 dismiss control below the 44px convention, and a scroll-triggered bubble that occupies the bottom-right 279x116 of the viewport and covers whatever content is there. That is a small, contained issue, not a Medium-impact one.

#### [141] /sliding-sash-windows/ is the only window route whose key-specification strip omits a U-value, while the comparison table below it publishes 1.2 W/m²K

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 60% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The strip prints Energy rating A rated, Sash models 3 Rose options, Profile system Roseview, Guarantee 10 years (inc/site-data.php:472-477). Every other window route with a strip carries a U-value. The model comparison lower on the same page prints Best U-value 1.2 / 1.2 / 1.4 W/m²K for Ultimate, Heritage and Charisma Rose (template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:3818, mirrored at :3916 for mobile), so the page does publish a figure that the strip omits. The absence is NOT caused by `glazing_u_values` having no sash key: product-pulse.php only uses that array for the derived lowest-achievable/star treatment, and a plain `['label'=>'U-value',…]` row would render like any other tile. The missing Thermlock/EnergyPlus banner is likewise unrelated — `fenster_tech_banner_args()` (inc/product-hub-data.php:549-568) gates on two hardcoded slug lists and Roseview is in neither by design.
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as an editorial question for the owner, not a data fix. The naive edit — adding `'sliding-sash-windows' => ['double' => '1.2 W/m²K']` to `glazing_u_values` — would print an unstarred 1.2 as the route's figure, which is untrue of Charisma Rose (1.4). If the owner wants the number at the top of the page, the honest form is a tile whose value carries the model qualifier (e.g. `U-value` / `From 1.2 W/m²K`) added directly to `product_usps['sliding-sash-windows']` in place of `Profile system: Roseview`, which the Roseview section immediately below already establishes. Do not add a `glazing_u_values` key unless the route genuinely has one figure.
- **Why:** Social proof is the persuasion engine of this site and "who said it, on which platform" is what makes a review worth anything. The information is presented to sighted users and silently withheld from screen-reader users, which is exactly the equivalence SC 1.1.1/4.1.2 exists to protect. The fix is one attribute and the house pattern for it is already in the same file.
- **Affected:** 3,977 platform badges across 568 pages (Google and Trustpilot variants). Plus `site-footer__trust` and `site-footer__socials`, 712 pages each.
- **Evidence:** Sitewide scan of the 712-page corpus: `<span class="fg-review-showcase__platform" aria-label="Review on Google">` ×3,977 / 568 pages, `aria-label="Review on Trustpilot"` ×1; inner `<span class="fg-review-showcase__glyph" aria-hidden="true">G</span>`; correct sibling `<span class="fg-stars" role="img" aria-label="5 out of 5 stars">` in the same card (see composite-doors.html). 5,469 total `aria-label`-on-generic-element instances found sitewide.
- **Verification:** The observation reproduces: the live strip prints only Energy rating / Sash models / Profile system / Guarantee (no U-value), while the model comparison on the same page prints "Best U-value 1.2 W/m²K option". Every other window route that renders a strip does carry a U-value (casement 0.95, flush 1.2, tilt-turn 0.93*, aluminium-windows 1.0*, aluminium-flush 1.0*, heritage 1.4). But three parts of the finding are wrong. (1) MECHANISM: the strip does NOT depend on `glazing_u_values` to print a U-value. product-pulse.php:73-98 only takes the derived branch when `$double !== ''`; a `['label'=>'U-value','value'=>'…']` row in `product_usps` renders as a plain tile like any other. So "the strip cannot render it" is false. (2) The missing tech banner has nothing to do with `glazing_u_values`: `fenster_tech_banner_args()` (inc/product-hub-data.php:549-568) gates the banner on two hardcoded slug lists, EnergyPlus (Liniar) and Thermlock (Sheerline). Sash is a Roseview route and is in neither, so adding a glazing key would produce no banner. (3) The recommended data edit would publish a figure the page does not support: the comparison row is 1.2 / 1.2 / 1.4 across Ultimate, Heritage and CHARISMA Rose (generated-page.php:3818), and the strip mechanism would print a single unstarred 1.2 as the route figure — untrue of one of the three models. Any change here therefore has to state the figure model-by-model or not at all, which makes this an editorial call about which four facts fill four tiles, not a bug. No owner ruling found either way (AI.md "Sliding Sash Roseview Rule" 756-763, SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md:94 list "Best U-value option" as a deliberate comparison row and say nothing about the strip).

#### [212] The shared colour/handle label tier has no mobile handling, so two-word finish names wrap to three lines in 114px cells

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 60% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The site's caption/label/spec-value tier is set in absolute rem with no media query anywhere: `.78rem` (12.5px) on 872 elements, `.82rem` (13.1px) on 1,038, `.74rem` (11.8px) on 355, `.72rem` (11.5px) on 230, `.68rem` (10.9px) on 112 and `.65rem` (10.4px) on 145, counted across the 38 Tier-1 routes. The clearest consequence is `.fg-handle-finishes__grid span { font-size: .74rem }` (11.84px) inside a grid that drops to `repeat(3, minmax(0,1fr))` at `<=560px`, giving 114.5px cells, so 'Traditional Monkey Tail Handle' wraps to three lines. The same pattern applies to `.fg-upvc-colours__grid span` (RAL codes). This is a legibility/comfort judgement rather than a measurable defect: no standard sets a minimum body font size, there is no overflow or clipping, and cards within each grid row do share a common height and baseline (the 205px and 221px measurements are row 1 versus row 2, not siblings in one row).
- **Recommendation:** Drop the colour and handle grids to `repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr))` at `<=430px` so cells are ~175px and two-word finish names stop wrapping to three lines. If a size floor is also wanted, add a single `@media (max-width: 560px)` override raising the five shared label selectors (`.fg-heritage-door-colours__grid span, .fg-upvc-colours__grid span, .fg-blind-colours__grid span, .fg-alu-colours__grid span, .fg-handle-finishes__grid span`) to `.8rem` rather than editing declarations individually. Do NOT add `align-content: start` — grid already stretches siblings to a shared row height and the cards in each row are already aligned.
- **Why:** Six stocked door layouts is the whole point of that section, and five of them are currently unreadable to a screen reader on a page that sells bespoke configuration.
- **Affected:** `/heritage-aluminium-doors/` only. `src/js/main.js:4458-4682` (notably 4472 and 4506); `template-parts/sections/heritage-aluminium-doors.php:235-253`.
- **Evidence:** `src/js/main.js:4506` `slide.setAttribute('aria-hidden', absOffset < 0.5 ? 'false' : 'true');`; `4472` `carousel.setAttribute('tabindex', '0');`. Markup at `heritage-aluminium-doors.php:235` has no role/aria-label. Contrast with `live/colour-options.html`: `<ul class="fg-colour-rail__track" data-fg-colour-rail-viewport tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="uPVC colours. Scroll or swipe sideways.">`.
- **Verification:** The measurements are exact but the finding's headline mechanism is refuted by its own data and by the screenshot, and the fix it proposes addresses a defect that does not exist. What holds: I summed probe-mobile.json fontSizes across all 38 routes and got 12.5px x872, 13.1px x1038, 13.8px x377, 11.8px x355, 11.5px x230, 10.9px x112, 10.4px x145 — every figure matches to the unit. The CSS is as quoted: `.fg-heritage-door-colours__grid span,.fg-upvc-colours__grid span,.fg-blind-colours__grid span,.fg-alu-colours__grid span,.fg-handle-finishes__grid span{color:var(--color-muted);font-size:.74rem;line-height:1.3}` with no media override anywhere in main.css, and I confirmed by brace-scanning that the 3-column drop is inside `@media(max-width: 560px)`. Cell width 114.5px is arithmetically consistent (gap is `clamp(.7rem,1.4vw,1.1rem)` = 11.2px at 390px; 3x114.53 + 2x11.2 = 366 = the 390px container less its 24px padding). 'Traditional Monkey Tail Handle' does wrap to three lines — visible in scratchpad/mfold/cas-handles.png. What is REFUTED: 'the cards in a row end up 205px and 221px tall because the label lengths differ, breaking the row baseline.' The finding's own measurement reads 205/205/205 then 221/221/221 — that is row 1 versus row 2, and every card WITHIN a row is identical. The screenshot confirms it: all three card borders in row 1 terminate at the same y, all three in row 2 likewise, because CSS grid stretches items to the row height by default. There is no broken baseline. Consequently the recommendation's third clause, 'Add `align-content: start` to the grid items so cards in a row share a baseline', fixes a non-problem and is also the wrong property for the stated goal. Type should be Creative, not Objective: no standard sets a minimum body font size, the probe measured no overflow and no clipping here, and the screenshot shows the grid reading as a tidy, legible spec board rather than a defect. The residual real observation is a consistency one — a shared label rule with zero mobile handling — plus the genuine 3-line wrap in 114.5px cells, which the 2-column drop at <=430px would address on its own.

#### [139] /tilt-turn-windows/ spends nearly as long on finishes as on its argument, and never shows the sash turned in

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 58% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The bespoke middle is sharp and correct — everything comes off the direction of travel — but it measures 3,768px against 3,551px of finishes (glass band 800 + colours 1,533 + handles 1,218), so the page spends nearly as long on swatches as on its argument. The argument is illustrated by four Liniar studio renders plus a room hero. Two of those four (`Tilt-turn-ventilation-1.jpeg`, `-2`) do show a sash open in the TILT position with the scissor stay visible, so the tilt is answered; the other two (`Tilt-turn-keep-1`, `-2`) are keep close-ups, and NOTHING on the page shows the sash TURNED fully in — the position the page opens by describing. PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md:118-128 already records both halves: the missing photograph is "the largest gap on any window route", and the four renders are on the page precisely because they are the only assets that show the product working.
- **Recommendation:** Do not add a technical drawing of the tilt — the two ventilation renders already answer it. The unanswered position is the turn. Either wait for the photograph PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md:126-128 asks for ("a sash turned fully in, again from inside, ideally with somebody reaching the outside face of the glass"), or, if that is not coming soon, put one two-state section drawing of the TURN alone to the owner. Separately, and independently of any imagery, the 800px "Specification choices" preamble (`fg-product-gallery-band`) is the cheapest cut available and would put the argument clearly ahead of the swatches.
- **Why:** The skip link is the single accessibility affordance every keyboard and screen-magnifier user reaches first, on every one of 712 pages, and it is the site's only mechanism for bypassing a mega-menu header. A sighted keyboard user (RSI, tremor, temporary injury — a much larger group than screen-reader users) gets a focus ring that vanishes into the header and has no idea where focus is. This is a clean WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) failure and a 2.4.7 Focus Visible failure, and it is roughly a one-line fix.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages (skip link emitted from header.php:24, header from template-parts/layout/site-header.php:10).
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:174-187 (`z-index: 20`, `:focus` changes transform only); main.scss:194 (`.site-header` z-index 50, sticky); main.scss:22596 (mobile z-index 1000). Live verification on https://fensterglazing.com/: skip link focused, matchesFocus true, rect [16,-6,131,46], header rect [0,0,1280,73], `document.elementFromPoint(centre)` → `IMG.site-brand__logo`.
- **Verification:** The arithmetic reproduces exactly and the photo gap is real and already documented, but the central visual claim is wrong.

Confirmed by live measurement at 375x812: the bespoke middle is 874 + 796 + 803 + 1,295 = 3,768px, and the finishes are fg-product-gallery-band 800 + fg-upvc-colours 1,533 + fg-handle-finishes--five 1,218 = 3,551px. Body image inventory is exactly as stated: tilt-turn-room-hero-1920w.webp plus Tilt-turn-ventilation-1.jpeg, -2, Tilt-turn-keep-1.jpeg and -2, and nothing else of the window (the rest are 16 colour swatches and 5 handle cut-outs). PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md:118-122 is quoted accurately: "TILT AND TURN — WE OWN NO PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE OPENING. New gap, 2026-08-12, and it is the largest on any window route." The SVG-capability claims check out too: fg-rp-svg exists in window-door-repairs.php:240 and AI.md:564 records the AutoCAD register with dashed hidden line for concealed hardware.

But 'there is no photograph of a sash tilted or turned in' and 'illustrated by four hardware close-ups' misdescribe the assets. I rendered all four jpegs: Tilt-turn-ventilation-1 and -2 are cutaway renders of a sash IN THE TILT POSITION, open at the head with the scissor stay and hinge visible — they show the sash open, which is precisely the question the finding says goes unanswered. Only Tilt-turn-keep-1 and -2 are pure hardware close-ups (keeps). The TURN position is genuinely unillustrated; the tilt is not.
