PHOTO-CHECKLIST itself says the same thing from the other side: "The page was rebuilt around four Liniar studio renders of the mechanism BECAUSE THEY ARE THE ONLY ASSETS THAT SHOW THE PRODUCT DOING ITS JOB" — i.e. the current treatment is the recorded, deliberate response to the gap, and the checklist's own remedy is to take the photograph, not to draw one.

#### [138] The door-handle grid costs 1,499px of mobile scroll on the four routes that carry it

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 45% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `fg-handle-finishes--doors` renders eight handles at a measured 1,499px on mobile on /composite-doors/, /upvc-doors/, /aluminium-doors/ and /french-doors/. On composite it is the second-largest section on the page (fg-product-faq is 1,589px). `/handle-options/` exists as the site-wide handle hub and the section already ends with "See the full handle specification →". Two other routes carry different, smaller handle families that are NOT this section and must not be folded into it: /tilt-turn-windows/ (`--five`, 1,218px, greenteQ) and /patio-doors/ (`--five --patio`, 1,098px, Mila ProLinea), which AI.md:810 and AI.md:843 rule are separate families.
- **Recommendation:** Before proposing a layout change, note that main.scss:37140-37145 already records the reason for the current mobile treatment: "Eight over three would leave a row of two. Two keeps the rows even and the long backplate readable on a phone." The grid is already 2-up at 375px, not stacked. If the scroll cost is worth attacking, attack the parts that carry no such reason — the 276px section head and the ~200px of note/link furniture around a 1,014px grid — rather than shrinking the cut-outs to a 140px rail, which trades away the readability that comment protects. Any change applies to four routes, not five, and must not touch the tilt-turn or patio families.
- **Why:** This is the single largest accessibility defect on the site and it sits on the money path. "Get an instant price", "Instant Quote" and the header phone number are the three highest-intent controls on a 712-page lead-generation site, and all three are below the legal AA threshold for anyone with reduced contrast sensitivity — which in a Milton Keynes home-improvement audience (older homeowners) is a large share of the buyers. The fix is a two-hex-code change with no layout consequence.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages. `.button` 3,512 occurrences / 712 pages; `.eyebrow` 6,041 occurrences / 712 pages; `.site-header__phone` 712 occurrences / 712 pages; `.text-link` 82 / 70 pages. In the desktop probe, 562 of the 834 sampled low-contrast entries (67%) are this exact colour pair, on 38 of 38 routes.
- **Evidence:** src/scss/main.scss:47 (`--color-accent: #2eac66`), :48 (`--color-accent-dark: #20824c`), :1503 `.button`, :1449 `.eyebrow`, :1517 `.text-link`, :1426 `.site-header__phone`. Pixel-sampled shots/desktop/home--fold.png: button fill rgb(46,172,102), glyph rgb(255,255,255) → 2.91:1; header phone rgb(46,172,102) on rgb(254,254,254) → 2.91:1. Computed: #20824c on white = 4.82:1, #2eac66 on #061d24 = 5.99:1. probe-desktop.json lowContrast, 562/834 entries.
- **Verification:** The core measurement is right, the scope is wrong in both directions, and the recommendation argues against a reason already written in the stylesheet.

Confirmed by live measurement at 375x812: `fg-handle-finishes--doors` = 1,499px on /composite-doors/ (8 handles, images 194px tall, head 276px, grid 1,014px), and 1,499px on /upvc-doors/ and /aluminium-doors/. On composite it is second-largest — but the finding's own evidence line ('composite's largest sections are fg-cd3-colour 1,394 and handles 1,499') is wrong: fg-product-faq is 1,589px, so the FAQ is largest and handles second. Both sections do end with 'See the full handle specification' pointing at the hub.

Scope error 1: /tilt-turn-windows/ and /patio-doors/ do NOT carry `fg-handle-finishes--doors`. Their classes are `fg-handle-finishes--five` (1,218px, greenteQ tilt-and-turn family) and `fg-handle-finishes--five fg-handle-finishes--patio` (1,098px, Mila ProLinea family). AI.md:810 and AI.md:843 rule explicitly that these are separate families and must not be merged, and that the long-plate door grid must never render on /patio-doors/. Calling them 'the five-finish variant' of the door grid is the exact conflation the docs forbid.

Scope error 2: it misses /french-doors/, which DOES render `fg-handle-finishes--doors` (confirmed in the live section list; french-doors was added back to door_handles.slugs on 2026-08-07 per AI.md:843). So `--doors` is four routes: composite, upvc, aluminium and french doors.

Recommendation error: it is not 'a stacked grid'. The mobile layout is already 2-up — computed gridTemplateColumns is '169.898px 169.906px' at 375px — and main.scss:37140-37145 records why: "Eight over three would leave a row of two. Two keeps the rows even and THE LONG BACKPLATE READABLE ON A PHONE." A 140px rail would trade away the readability that comment was written to protect.


### J. Architecture and maintainability

#### [40] The sitemap's exclusion of commercial-glazing-northamptonshire is silently overridden, and commercial-glazing-milton-keynes is excluded yet linked from every commercial page

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** `fenster_maybe_render_generated_sitemap()` lists `commercial-glazing-milton-keynes` and `commercial-glazing-northamptonshire` in `$excluded_slugs` (inc/generated-pages.php:1974-1975). That array is only consulted in the first loop, over `data/pages.json` (:1990). The commercial-county loop at :2033-2044 then walks `fenster_commercial_county_pages()` and echoes every county unconditionally — and Northamptonshire IS a county profile (:844), so it is re-added. Verified: https://fensterglazing.com/commercial-glazing-northamptonshire/ is present in the 712-URL sitemap. The exclusion is dead code that reads as an active decision. Milton Keynes is not a county profile, so its exclusion does hold — but generated-page.php:2059-2063 explicitly adds `commercial-glazing-milton-keynes` to the related-links band of every commercial route, and the page returns 200 with a self-referencing canonical and no noindex. So one route is excluded-but-linked-and-indexable, and its neighbour is excluded-but-published.
- **Recommendation:** Decide per route and make one mechanism enforce it. If Milton Keynes should not be in the sitemap, remove it from the `$add_related_routes([...])` call at generated-page.php:2062 and add it to `fenster_slug_is_noindex()` (inc/generated-pages.php:1755) so a single function decides indexability; if it should be indexed, delete it from `$excluded_slugs`. Either way, move the `$excluded_slugs` and gone/redirect/noindex test out of the first loop into a small `fenster_sitemap_should_list(string $slug): bool` called by all four loops at :1990, :2020, :2033 and :2047, so an exclusion cannot be bypassed by whichever loop emits the route.
- **Why:** Four independent emit loops each apply a different subset of the filters, so a slug's presence in the sitemap depends on which loop reaches it first. That is invisible to review and it has already produced one exclusion that does nothing and one that contradicts the internal link graph.
- **Affected:** inc/generated-pages.php:1968-2059 (four emit loops, filters applied in one); template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:2059-2063
- **Evidence:** inc/generated-pages.php:1975 excludes commercial-glazing-northamptonshire; it is nonetheless line 644 of urls.txt. `curl -I https://fensterglazing.com/commercial-glazing-milton-keynes/` returns 200 with `<link rel="canonical" href="https://fensterglazing.com/commercial-glazing-milton-keynes/">` and no robots noindex, while being absent from the sitemap and linked at generated-page.php:2062.
- **Verification:** Every element reproduced. `template-parts/components/product-pulse.php:60` is exactly `<section class="fg-product-pulse fg-product-pulse--usps" aria-label="<?php echo esc_attr($pulse_title . ' key specifications'); ?>">`, and the section already carries `<p class="eyebrow">Key specifications</p>` at :63 and an `<h2>` at :64, so the recommended `aria-labelledby` swap is available exactly as described. generated-page.php:3535-3537 sets the two sentence titles (`'Sheerline Prestige, in four figures.'` and `'Liniar EnergyPlus, in four figures.'`), with the surrounding comment at :3528-3534 confirming they were added on 2026-08-12 specifically to stop the pulse title repeating the H1 — the fix that caused this.

Both affected routes verified. scratchpad/live/tilt-turn-windows.html renders `aria-label="Liniar EnergyPlus, in four figures. key specifications"`. I curled the second route, which is not in the Tier-1 set, and https://fensterglazing.com/aluminium-flush-windows/ renders `aria-label="Sheerline Prestige, in four figures. key specifications"` live. Grepping the pulse aria-label across all 40 live pages returns 13 routes, matching the claimed scope for the redundant-label half; the other 11 are noun phrases and read correctly.

No ruling anywhere sanctions this — AI.md and STYLE.md rule on the sentence titles themselves and on the strip's content, never on its aria-label.

#### [35] A product slug lives in at least 20 slug-keyed registries across 8 files, and their key sets already disagree by 13 to 67 entries with no guard anywhere

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 95% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** M · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** On the routes still running the generic journey the product name appears as the H1, again as the `fg-product-pulse` H2, and a third time as the `fg-product-why` H2 — the last because generated-page.php:4079 prints `$journey_why_heading`, which :1278 defaults to `$title`. The code already knows this is wrong: :174 records that `/aluminium-doors/` 'printed "Aluminium Doors" as an H2 twice under an H1 already saying it' and was converted to a bespoke middle for that reason, and the gate at :4031 now excludes eleven named bespoke routes from `fg-product-why` — but the five routes not on that list still do exactly what aluminium-doors was fixed for. The pulse repeat is acknowledged at :3524-3534 as 'a site-wide structural smell ... flagged rather than fixed', with the code itself noting 'Two of twenty-three is not the fix, and the site-wide one is still open'. This is already logged twice in the project docs and still live: ACTION-PLAN.md:144 describes the exact triple ('H1 plus two more identical H2s (key specs + product info)') and AUDIT.md:369 describes the pulse repeat, both as open items.
- **Recommendation:** Give `fg-product-why` a heading that is not the route title — override `$journey_why_heading` (generated-page.php:1278) per route rather than defaulting to `$title`. The section already contains three-to-five H3 benefit cards, so the H2 should name the argument ('Why a French door rather than a single', 'Where integral blinds earn their place'), matching the pattern /aluminium-doors/ and /flush-casement-windows/ adopted when they went bespoke. Separately, apply the pulse-title treatment at :3536-3538 to the remaining routes rather than leaving it at two of twenty-three. Close ACTION-PLAN.md:144 and AUDIT.md:369 in the same commit, since both describe this and both still read as open.
- **Why:** AI.md, HANDOVER.md and the in-code comments are the only thing keeping these in step, and they only work if the next session reads all of them. A rename or a new product is currently a 20-file job with no way to know you missed one until a page prints a contradiction — which is what happened to the tilt-and-turn chamber count (six vs four, product-hub-data.php:622-633) and to the flush-casement U-value (0.95 vs 1.2, :571-576).
- **Affected:** inc/site-data.php, inc/generated-pages.php, inc/product-hub-data.php, inc/legend-assistant.php, inc/case-studies-data.php, inc/blog-posts.php, template-parts/sections/generated-page.php, template-parts/sections/location-service.php
- **Evidence:** Computed key-set sizes for 15 of the registries: 13/21/21/21/23/25/26/26/26/27/27/27/67. product-hub-data.php:596-599 comment: the two glazing arrays "are separate arrays and nothing joins them". product-hub-data.php:622-633 records the six-vs-four chamber contradiction that shipped live.
- **Verification:** The defect reproduces exactly and the route lists are right, but one supporting claim is false. Confirmed: `grep -l fg-product-why live/*.html` returns exactly the 5 named routes — aluminium-bifold-doors, aluminium-windows, french-doors, integral-blinds, patio-doors — and no others. Confirmed the mechanism: `generated-page.php:4079` prints `$journey_why_heading`, which `:1278` defaults to `$title` for anything that is not /about/ or commercial, so the H2 is the route title verbatim. Confirmed the gate at :4031, which excludes exactly eleven named routes. Confirmed the admission at :174 ('printed "Aluminium Doors" as an H2 twice under an H1 already saying it') and the pulse comment at :3524-3534, which literally says 'Two of twenty-three is not the fix, and the site-wide one is still open' — so this is a flagged-open item, not an owner ruling. Confirmed the pulse-title overrides at :3536-3538 and that /tilt-turn-windows/ now renders 'Liniar EnergyPlus, in four figures.' as its pulse H2. Confirmed the 6 double-repeat routes and the roof-lanterns near-repeat from probe-desktop.json headings. What is wrong: 'the second, deeper repeat is not mentioned anywhere' is false — ACTION-PLAN.md:144 records precisely the triple ('product pages render "uPVC Doors" as H1 plus two more identical H2s (key specs + product info)') and marks it 'also flagged in the old audit §6.11, still live'; AUDIT.md:369 records the pulse repeat separately. That makes this a known, twice-logged, unfixed item rather than a new discovery, which is worth saying because the recommendation should be reconciled with what those docs already propose (AUDIT.md:369 suggests demoting the strip heading to a styled `<p>`).

#### [39] 18 variables in generated-page.php are written and never read, including a 16-colour palette and the entire $journey_* label set

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 93% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Problem:** I parsed every assignment in template-parts/sections/generated-page.php and counted reads across all 76 PHP files in the theme. 18 variables have zero reads anywhere: `$journey_options`, `$journey_option_eyebrow`, `$journey_option_heading`, `$journey_heading`, `$journey_steps`, `$journey_type_label`, `$journey_gallery_eyebrow`, `$journey_gallery_heading`, `$journey_trust_heading`, `$journey_trust_copy`, `$designer_sections`, `$scroll_story_sections`, `$is_bifold`, `$composite_door_gallery`, `$composite_palette`, `$product_hub_support_image`, `$window_handle_intro`, `$upvc_pick`. The biggest chain is `$upvc_colour_routes` (:1212) -> `$is_upvc_colour_product` (:1224) -> `$product_colours` (:1225-1262, sixteen uPVC entries plus a six-entry aluminium override) -> `$journey_options` (:1308, overridden again at :1330 and :1339) -> nothing, plus the pet-flap overrides at :1325-1326. That is roughly 95 lines. It is not merely dead, it is misleadingly authoritative: the dead `$product_colours` uPVC list disagrees with the live `colour_options.materials.upvc` array (site-data.php:3208) — it names "Steel Blue" where the live data says "Blue", omits "Gale Grey Finesse (Anthracite Smooth)" entirely, and adds a "Custom RAL" entry the uPVC range does not offer. Anyone grepping for the uPVC palette hits the wrong one first because it is in the template.
- **Recommendation:** Delete lines 1212-1262 (`$upvc_colour_routes`, `$is_upvc_colour_product`, `$product_colours` and the aluminium override), the ten dead `$journey_*` assignments at :1264-1308 and their overrides at :1311-1347 that touch only dead names, `$designer_sections` (:127-130), `$scroll_story_sections` (:131-137) and `$is_bifold` (:150). Keep the live journey strings — `$journey_intro_heading`, `$journey_intro_copy`, `$journey_why_*`, `$journey_faq_*` and `$journey_order_*` are all read. Re-run the write-only scan after the edit to confirm nothing else fell out.
- **Why:** generated-page.php is 5,376 lines and the brief for every session is "read the routing logic". Ninety-five lines of authoritative-looking colour and label data that reaches no output is a direct tax on every future reader, and it has already drifted away from the live colour source, so a session that copies it will publish wrong swatch names.
- **Affected:** template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:127-137, :150, :1212-1262, :1264-1308, :1311-1347 (~95 lines, 18 variables)
- **Evidence:** Read/write analysis over all theme PHP: `$journey_options` 3 writes 0 reads; `$product_colours` read once, only into `$journey_options`. `$journey_options` does not appear in any get_template_part args or any template-parts file. `$product_colours` uPVC entries (generated-page.php:1227-1242) vs colour_options.materials.upvc (17 entries incl. Smooth White) differ on Steel Blue/Blue, Gale Grey Finesse and Custom RAL.
- **Verification:** Reproduced exactly, and it is slightly worse than described. The `fg-areas-page__hero` block in scratchpad/live/areas-we-cover.html renders `<a class="button button--light" href="https://fensterglazing.com/online-quote/">Get an instant price</a>` followed by `<a class="button" href="https://fensterglazing.com/contact/">Ask about your postcode</a>` — the secondary style first, the green primary on the contact link. STYLE.md:265 is the correct line and reads exactly as quoted, including the dark-panel exception.

The dark-panel exception does not apply, and I checked rather than assumed: main.scss:5575-5581 sets `background: transparent` on `.fg-areas-page__hero`, :5594-5596 sets the H1 to `var(--color-steel)` (dark ink), :5601-5604 sets body copy to `--color-muted`, and :5608-5615 puts a `rgba(255,255,255,0.84)` white card beside it. The page canvas underneath is `--fg-page-gradient` (main.scss:64-68), whose base layer is `linear-gradient(135deg, #eef5f4, #ffffff 44%, #e8f1f0)` — a near-white light gradient. So this is a light panel and `.button--light` is the wrong modifier by the letter of the rule.

The extra severity: `.button--light` is `border-color: #ffffff; background: #ffffff` (main.scss:1530-1534). A pure-white button with a pure-white border sits on a #eef5f4-to-#ffffff canvas, so the site's highest-value CTA is not merely demoted, it is close to edgeless. The secondary `/contact/` collision is also real — the same page labels `/contact/` both `Ask about your postcode` and `Contact Fenster`. And the finding is right that no screenshot exists: `ls shots/desktop/ | grep -i areas` returns nothing, so this was never visually reviewed.

#### [36] The shared enquiry form renders five structural shapes; the residential split is deliberate, but the same textarea carries two labels and the compact variant drops the fieldset grouping

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 85% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** L · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php` renders five structurally different forms: default gated (19 Tier-1 routes), default with the gate suppressed by `lock_project_type` (roof-lanterns, heritage-aluminium-doors, flat-rooflights), `show_company` commercial (extra Company field, phone/postcode rows rearranged, :238-272), `compact` (flat grid, no gate, no fieldsets — 8 Tier-1 routes plus the ~238-URL town matrix and all articles), and consultation. The variant split is NOT arbitrary: SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md section 9 and AI.md:163 record pre-scoped compact forms on bespoke routes as the intended design. Two real defects remain inside it. (1) The same field is labelled `Project details` in the compact branch (:159) and `Tell us about your project` in the default branch (:278). (2) The default branch groups fields in three `fieldset.fg-enquiry-form__step` elements with legends (:227/:248/:275); the compact branch has none, so a screen-reader user gets a different programmatic structure for the same conversion event depending on the route. Separately, `$project_options` is computed at :40-41 and never used in any branch, so the bespoke arrays passed by location-service.php:1388 and :1473 are dead.
- **Recommendation:** Unify the textarea label on one string (`Project details` reads better and is already the shorter of the two) and add the three `fieldset`/`legend` groupings to the compact branch so the programmatic structure is identical across routes. Do not merge the compact and gated variants without an owner ruling — the compact form is documented as deliberate. Either wire `$project_options` into a real select or delete it and the two dead arrays in location-service.php.
- **Why:** On a proxy-cache MISS this is ~16ms and 10MB of the origin's work for every page, and the site has 712 URLs so misses are routine after a deploy. It also caps how much the theme can ever add per request. The 222KB of unreachable records is pure waste that also pollutes `$route_exists()` (see the matrix-routes finding) — those dead slugs are exactly what makes internal-link existence checks unreliable.
- **Affected:** inc/generated-pages.php:12-48; data/pages.json (4.3MB, 274 records); every uncached front-end request
- **Evidence:** data/pages.json = 4,514,266 bytes, 274 pages. Benchmarked locally: file_get_contents 2.12ms, json_decode 13.86ms, +10.00MB, peak 18.31MB. Field weights measured: sections 1.91MB, seo 0.70MB, images 0.50MB, links 0.29MB. 32 never-rendered records = 222KB.
- **Verification:** Every line citation is exact and every count reproduces. enquiry-form.php:139 is the compact branch, :159 is `Project details`, :192-193 the lock/gate condition, :194 the audience fieldset, :227/:248/:275 the three `fg-enquiry-form__step` fieldsets, :278 `Tell us about your project`. The caller citations are exact to the argument line (generated-page.php:5354-5355, casement-windows-v2.php:725-726, location-service.php:1387 and 1472, generated-article.php:256, roof-lanterns.php:323). Counting live HTML: 19 routes render the audience gate, 8 render `fg-enquiry-form__compact-grid`, 30 routes carry a form in total — all three numbers land exactly on the finding's claims. `/casement-windows/` compact vs `/flush-casement-windows/` gated is real; `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` is compact with `project_type` hard-set to `Double glazing in Milton Keynes`.

What is wrong is the framing. 'On no discernible rule' and the implication that nothing rules on it do not survive the docs. SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md section 9 states the sash form 'is pre-scoped to sliding sash windows. It does not ask the customer to identify the product category again' and that mobile deliberately uses 'the compact form presentation'. AI.md:163 rules on the gate directly and records that `lock_project_type` routes 'render no gate at all and are already fixed to Commercial glazing' as correct behaviour. PROGRESS.md:5110 records casement getting 'a casement-specific shared enquiry form' in an owner-reviewed rebuild. The discernible rule is: bespoke or pre-scoped routes take the compact locked form, generic shared-template routes take the gated one. So 'cannot accept a business enquiry' is describing the deliberate purpose of pre-scoping, not a silent fault.

The count is also four variants only if you ignore `show_company`, which moves the phone field, adds Company and adds a separate postcode row (:238-247, :255-272) — that is a fifth structural shape, on the commercial routes.

One thing the finding missed and I confirmed: `$project_options` is built at enquiry-form.php:40-41 and never referenced again anywhere in the file. location-service.php:1388-1393 and 1473-1478 pass a bespoke six-item array to a variable that is dead in all three branches.

What survives as objective: the same textarea has two labels, and the compact branch drops the fieldset/legend grouping so the form's programmatic structure changes between routes.

#### [134] /casement-windows/ is the only route on the site where the reviews land after the enquiry form

- **Severity:** MEDIUM · **Impact:** Medium · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 72% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** `/casement-windows/` renders its own tail via `casement-windows-v2.php` and the review showcase is the last content section on the page — after `fg-enquiry`, which the template opens at line 708 while the `review-showcase` template part is called at line 733. Of the 16 live routes that carry both sections, this is the only one in that order; the other 15 place the reviews between the quote tool and the form. Separately `fg-cas-proof` — the mosaic captioned "Every photograph is a Fenster installation" — measures 501px on mobile, five figures at 288x216 in an overflow-x:auto rail (scrollWidth 1,477 against a 351px client width). That makes it the smallest BODY section on a 21,752px page (the hero at 368px and the pulse strip at 313px are smaller still), against an FAQ of 1,722px and a case-study strip of 1,760px.
- **Recommendation:** Move the `fenster_review_cards()` block in `casement-windows-v2.php` from line 733 to sit immediately before `#fenster-enquiry` at line 708, matching the other fifteen routes. Do NOT resize `fg-cas-proof` as part of the same change: the mobile scroll-snap rail is the site's documented pattern for this component (PROGRESS.md:5114, shared with sliding-sash and heritage, verified on a 390 at PROGRESS.md:3201), so growing it to a 2-up stacked grid is a preference to put to the owner separately, not a defect to fix.
- **Why:** Small, but `sameAs` is the main lever the site has for connecting itself to the third-party profiles the authority programme depends on, and one wrong entry in a five-item array is a quarter of the signal.
- **Affected:** All 712 pages (LocalBusiness node)
- **Evidence:** inc/generated-pages.php:2315-2321; identical `sameAs` array parsed from the JSON-LD on every one of the 712 crawled pages.

Scanning all 41 live HTML files, 16 carry both sections and /casement-windows/ is the ONLY one where fg-review-showcase precedes... sorry, FOLLOWS fg-enquiry; the other 15 (not 14) put reviews first. HANDOVER.md:1011 is quoted correctly and does not govern the tail below the quote tool, so this is not owner-ruled.

Two things are wrong. (1) 'making it the smallest section on a 21,752px page' is false: fg-hero is 368px and fg-product-pulse is 313px, both smaller than fg-cas-proof's 501px. It is the smallest BODY section, not the smallest section. (2) The recommendation to replace the 216px rail with a ~1,000-1,200px stacked grid argues against a deliberate, documented site-wide pattern: PROGRESS.md:5114 records the casement Real homes mosaic as 'a desktop mosaic that becomes a scroll-snap rail under 860px', the same pattern sliding-sash and heritage use, and PROGRESS.md:3201 records it being verified as a swipe row on a true 390. I measured the rail: .fg-cas-mosaic has overflow-x:auto, scrollWidth 1477 against clientWidth 351, 5 figures at 288x216. So the mosaic half is a preference against an established convention, not a defect.

#### [45] Imported title tags are inconsistent sitewide: 71 en-dash, 20 with no brand token, 14 over the SERP limit across 274 pages

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 96% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Titles for generated pages come from `data/pages.json` `seo.title_tag` via `fenster_generated_document_title()` (inc/generated-pages.php:2117-2128), i.e. they are inherited from the old-site scrape rather than authored. Across all 274 imported entries: 183 use a pipe, 71 use an en dash, 20 carry no separator and no brand token, and 14 exceed the ~62-character SERP display limit (worst: `commercial-glazing-leeds` at 138 chars, `commercial-glazing-manchester` at 107, `commercial-glazing-london-2` at 99). In the 38-route probe sample this surfaces as `/meet-the-team/` and `/what-is-a-door-lintel/` on en dashes, `/secondary-glazing/` with no brand token, and lengths of 67, 71 and 84. AUDIT.md:273 already records this as an open normalisation item.
- **Recommendation:** Do the AUDIT.md:273 pass on `seo.title_tag` in data/pages.json: normalise all 71 en dashes to pipes and append ` | Fenster Glazing` to the 20 with no brand token — that part is mechanical and genuinely low risk. Handle over-length titles case by case and EXCLUDE `/what-is-a-door-lintel/` from any head-phrase change: it holds position ~3 on 542k impressions and AI.md:627 forbids displacing a ranking head phrase. For that page, trim only the tail ('Understanding Door Lintels: Importance and Key Functions | Fenster Glazing') and measure before/after in GSC. Prioritise the four commercial city/county titles over 99 characters, which have no rankings to protect.
- **Why:** functions.php:27-28 shows the project already knows load order is load-bearing and documents it there. This is the same hazard undocumented, and it sits on the ad-attribution path, which is how Google Ads conversions are matched back to leads — a silent break here loses attribution rather than throwing.
- **Affected:** inc/ad-attribution.php:192-196; inc/website-tracking.php:129-142; functions.php:34-35 (load order)
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn fenster_ad_attribution_request_allowed` returns three hits: two `permission_callback` registrations (inc/ad-attribution.php:195, inc/website-tracking.php:132) and one definition (inc/website-tracking.php:136). functions.php lists website-tracking.php at index 34 and ad-attribution.php at 35, with no guard.
- **Verification:** Every number reproduces exactly from probe-desktop.json (35 pipe, 2 en dash, 1 no separator; titleLen 84 / 71 / 67). Three corrections. (1) SCOPE: 'four routes' is a 38-route-sample artefact. These titles are emitted by `fenster_generated_document_title()` at inc/generated-pages.php:2117-2128 from `$page['seo']['title_tag']`, which comes from the imported `data/pages.json` scrape. Across all 274 imported pages the real counts are 183 pipe, 71 en dash, 20 with no separator, and 14 titles over 62 characters — including a 138-character one on `commercial-glazing-leeds`. (2) ALREADY LOGGED: AUDIT.md:273 already records this verbatim — 'Imported titles are inconsistent in pattern (– Fenster Glazing vs | Fenster Glazing vs none). Worth a one-pass normalisation of seo.title_tag/meta_description across pages.json for the ~60 pages that matter most.' (3) RISK IS NOT LOW ON ONE ROUTE: `/what-is-a-door-lintel/` is the single biggest traffic source on the site — SEO-AUDIT.md:219 records 3,360 clicks (35% of everything) at position ~3, SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md:79 records 3,010 clicks / 542k impressions. AI.md:627 is explicit that the head phrase is the query and displacing it costs traffic. The separator swap is Low risk; retitling that page is not, and the finding's own suggested replacement ('What Is a Door Lintel? | Fenster Glazing') drops 'Understanding' and 'Importance and Key Functions' from a title ranking at position 3. Minor: the STYLE.md:250 support does not apply — that rule bans em dashes, and every offender here is an en dash. Minor: 'affected: 4 routes' then lists five.

#### [37] 22 routes give one destination two or more CTA labels on the same page, including `/online-quote/` labelled both `Get an instant price` and `Get an instant quote`

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Medium · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** L · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** Same-page label collisions on a single destination, where no contextual difference justifies the split. `/aluminium-bifold-doors/` gives `#fenster-enquiry` five labels on one page; french-doors, integral-blinds and patio-doors give four. `/casement-windows/` labels `#fenster-product-quote` both `Instant pricing` and `Get an instant price`. `/home/` and `/double-glazing-milton-keynes/` label `/online-quote/` both `Get an instant price` and `Get an instant quote` — TONEOFVOICE.md:147 names `Get an instant price` as the plain form. Both price guides label `#fenster-instant-pricing` both `Price your own job` and `Try it on your job`. 22 of 40 Tier-1 routes carry at least one such collision. The site-wide variety on `#fenster-enquiry` (10 labels) is largely contextual copy and is a judgement call, not a defect.
- **Recommendation:** Fix only the same-page collisions where the two labels describe the identical action. Retire `Get an instant quote` in favour of `Get an instant price` on home and double-glazing-milton-keynes; pick one of `Instant pricing` / `Get an instant price` for `#fenster-product-quote` per page; pick one of `Price your own job` / `Try it on your job` for `#fenster-instant-pricing` on both price guides. Leave contextual enquiry labels (`Ask about handles`, `Ask about glass options`, `Request a repair`) alone — they state the next action, which is what STYLE.md:263 asks for. Note that tracking already captures destinations as well as labels (AI.md:202), so this is a vocabulary problem, not a measurement one.
- **Why:** Every one of the 712 pages downloads and parses the composite-door page's CSS, the obscured-glass page's CSS and the aluminium-windows scroll story's CSS. At 111KB gzip that is the single heaviest render-blocking resource on the site, and 73% of it can never match anything on the page being viewed.
- **Affected:** src/scss/main.scss (42,407 lines, no partials); assets/css/main.css (698,156 bytes, 111KB gzip); inc/assets.php:20-25; all 712 pages
- **Evidence:** Mapped 570 `fg-` base blocks in assets/css/main.css against every .php file: 427 single-template (436KB), 77 zero-template (64KB); conservative pass counting only blocks whose name appears in no PHP or JS at all gives 64 blocks / 491 rules / 53.2KB. `grep -c '^@use\|^@import' src/scss/main.scss` = 0.
- **Verification:** The headline count is right and the evidence line overstates it. Re-extracting every `<a class="button…">` inside `<main>` across all 40 live pages, `#fenster-enquiry` resolves to 12 raw strings — but three of those are artefacts of the responsive hero CTA, which renders `<span class="fg-hero-cta__full">Start your design consultation</span><span class="fg-hero-cta__short">Design consultation</span>` inside one anchor. Merging those, it is exactly the 10 labels the title claims. The per-page collisions reproduce: `/aluminium-bifold-doors/` genuinely gives one anchor five labels (Start your design consultation, Start your project, Start a product enquiry, Ask about this product, Start your enquiry); french-doors, integral-blinds and patio-doors give four each; `/casement-windows/` labels `#fenster-product-quote` both `Instant pricing` and `Get an instant price`; home and double-glazing-milton-keynes both label `/online-quote/` `Get an instant price` and `Get an instant quote`; both price guides label `#fenster-instant-pricing` `Price your own job` and `Try it on your job`. All confirmed. STYLE.md:263 is the correct line for 'Buttons state the next action' (the finding cited :264).

Two corrections. Scope: 22 routes carry a genuine in-page collision, not 25. My run flagged 24, and two of those (3d-visualiser, online-quote) collide only on the WindowCAD external link's `Open in new tab` / `Open quote tool` pair, which is a hidden/visible label pattern rather than two competing CTAs.

Rationale: 'any click tracking keyed on label text fragments a single conversion into five buckets, which makes the funnel unmeasurable' is not supported. AI.md:202 records that consent-safe journey detail 'may include page time, scroll milestones, CTA labels/destinations' — destinations are captured alongside labels, so `#fenster-enquiry` remains one measurable bucket.

Type: the site-wide variety is a defensible copy choice. Putting `Ask about handles` beside handle content and `Ask about glass options` beside glass content is contextual CTA writing, not a defect, and no doc forbids it. What is objectively wrong is the same-page collision where nothing contextual distinguishes the two labels — most clearly `/online-quote/` reading `Get an instant price` and `Get an instant quote` on one page, when TONEOFVOICE.md:147 already names `Get an instant price` as the canonical form.

#### [38] The `/casement-windows/` early return silently drops the links band and the order-process rail, and `/roof-lanterns/` loses both the same way

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 90% · **Type:** Objective · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** generated-page.php:3550-3561 closes `</article>` and returns for `casement-windows` before the shared tail runs, so `/casement-windows/` never reaches the order-process rail (gated at :5050) or the related-links band (gated at :5361). `/roof-lanterns/` returns earlier in the same file and loses both for the same reason. Neither route is named in either gate and neither omission is recorded in AI.md, STYLE.md or PROGRESS.md — unlike `/sliding-sash-windows/`, `/composite-doors/`, `/aluminium-sliding-doors/` and the repairs route, which are explicitly excluded from the rail at :5050, and sliding-sash and composite-doors which are explicitly excluded from the links band at :5361. The section order on casement (quote, enquiry, reviews) is NOT a defect: PROGRESS.md's 2026-07-27 'Casement Windows Page Recomposed' entry records it as the owner-approved composition.
- **Recommendation:** Add the `fg-links-band` block to `template-parts/sections/casement-windows-v2.php` and `template-parts/sections/roof-lanterns.php` (or move the two early returns after :5361), so both routes rejoin the internal-linking mesh AI.md:43 calls the priority fix for high-impression pages. Then put the order-rail omission to the owner as a question rather than a fix: three sibling routes are deliberately excluded from it at :5050, so casement and roof lanterns may belong in that list — they are just not in it. Leave the section order alone.
- **Why:** Every visitor downloads, parses and executes controllers that can never find their element. It is also a live trap: a session that later adds `data-fg-product-intel` markup will silently activate a tab controller nobody has tested in weeks, and the dead attributes make it impossible to tell by grep which behaviours are real.
- **Affected:** src/js/main.js (33 orphan selectors of 213; two blocks totalling ~210 lines); inc/assets.php:165-198, :278-316, :334-375; template-parts/sections/generated-page.php:3309, :4056
- **Evidence:** inc/assets.php:180 `return [];` under a docblock reading "This map is empty and the traveller therefore renders nowhere." Deployed asset check: `data-scroll-video`, `data-fg-product-video-final`, `data-fg-product-video-start`, `fg-product-traveller-float` all present in assets/js/main.js, assets/css/main.css and the live main.js/main.css; `data-scroll-video` appears in zero PHP files and zero of the 38 live pages.
- **Verification:** The code citations are exact. generated-page.php:3560 is `<?php return; ?>` immediately after `</article>` at :3559, inside the `$slug === 'casement-windows'` branch opened at :3550 — so the shared tail is unreachable. :5361 is exactly `<?php if (! empty($related_links) && $slug !== 'sliding-sash-windows' && ! $is_composite_doors) : ?>`. casement-windows-v2.php:668 (FAQ), :689 (cs-strip), :708 (enquiry) are exact, with the review-showcase include at :733, after the enquiry. AI.md:43, :62, :239 and :215-224 all read exactly as quoted. My own section-order scan reproduces the canonical tail ORDER > QUOTE > REVIEWS > (CASES) > ENQ > LINKS on exactly 11 routes, and casement-windows as QUOTE > CASES > ENQ > REVIEWS with no `fg-order-process` and no `fg-links-band`.

Three corrections.

(1) Reviews-after-enquiry on casement is an owner-approved composition, not a defect. PROGRESS.md, '2026-07-27 - Casement Windows Page Recomposed' (the pass that followed the owner rejecting the previous version), records the approved structure verbatim: 'Six body sections: intro, opening styles, inside the frame, glass/locking/hardware, colour, nearby styles. Then quote tool, enquiry, reviews and FAQs.' Reviews after the enquiry form is the recorded intent. That also removes the quote-hoisted-above-FAQ complaint, which is the same documented ordering.

(2) The order rail is NOT missing by accident from sliding-sash, composite-doors or repairs. generated-page.php:5050 gates it explicitly: `if ($slug !== 'sliding-sash-windows' && ! $is_composite_doors && $slug !== 'aluminium-sliding-doors' && ! $is_repairs)`. Three of the five 'affected' routes are deliberate exclusions. Only casement-windows and roof-lanterns lose it as a side effect of an early return.

(3) AI.md:239 is misread. 'There is one process rail and one set of steps' governs which markup and which step set (it replaced six step sets across three templates); it does not say every route must render one. Casement is not 'silently exempt from it'.

What survives: `/casement-windows/` and `/roof-lanterns/` render no `fg-links-band` and no order rail purely because the early return skips the shared tail, with no code gate and no doc ruling for either — unlike sliding-sash and composite-doors, which are named in both gates.

#### [42] The review showcase is absent from both price guides and all three specification hubs, with no ruling behind it

- **Severity:** LOW · **Impact:** Low · **Risk of change:** Low · **Confidence:** 70% · **Type:** Creative · **Effort:** S · **Verdict:** REVISED
- **Problem:** The review showcase renders on 30 of 40 Tier-1 routes and is absent from 10. The absences include both price guides (`/composite-door-prices/`, `/window-door-prices-milton-keynes/`) and all three specification hubs (`/colour-options/`, `/handle-options/`, `/obscured-glass/`), plus `/commercial-glazing/`, `/areas-we-cover/`, `/fensa-approved-installers/`, `/case-studies/` and `/what-is-a-door-lintel/`. AI.md:215-224 governs sourcing, attribution, link targets and the aggregateRating ban but contains no per-route gate, and no other doc records a decision, so these look like omissions rather than choices — though nothing is broken by them.
- **Recommendation:** Put the two price guides to the owner as a question first, since this is a conversion judgement rather than a fault: a price page is where credibility is decided and it currently carries no customer evidence. If approved, add the shared `review-showcase` component before the closing CTA on `/composite-door-prices/` and `/window-door-prices-milton-keynes/`. Note that AI.md:224 expects the context string to be a town or product name, which a multi-product price guide does not have — pass the product for the composite guide and accept generic cards on the MK guide, or leave it. Do not add it to the three specification hubs without asking: they are mid-decision reference pages reached from a product page that already showed the reviews.
- **Why:** An unauthenticated POST creates a CRM lead in the business's AdminBase instance. Even without malice it is a spam surface on the highest-value data path the site has, and the fail-open shape is the opposite of the pattern the same codebase already got right for the conversions feed after being bitten once.
- **Affected:** inc/adminbase.php:185-231 and :287-360; REST route fenster/v1/windowcad registered at :178
- **Evidence:** inc/adminbase.php:195-208 — the 401 branch is nested inside `if ($secret !== '')`, so an empty secret bypasses it. inc/adminbase.php:30 — `fenster_adminbase_config_value()` returns the `$default` of `''`. Contrast inc/google-ads-conversions.php:86-92, which returns a 503 when neither token nor basic auth is configured, under a comment about failing closed.
- **Verification:** The facts hold; the classification does not. My own section-index scan across all 40 live pages returns the review showcase absent from exactly the 10 routes listed — areas-we-cover, case-studies, colour-options, commercial-glazing, composite-door-prices, fensa-approved-installers, handle-options, obscured-glass, what-is-a-door-lintel, window-door-prices-milton-keynes. I read AI.md:215-224 in full: it covers the Places API source, the server-side key, the curated fallback, Google's attribution requirement, the review-link target, the aggregateRating ban and the `fenster_review_cards()` context string. There is no per-route gate in it, and grepping AI.md, STYLE.md and PROGRESS.md for a review gating decision on hubs or price pages returns nothing. So the finding is right that no ruling explains the absences.

One number is off: the showcase renders on 30 of 40 routes, not 28 (10 absent of 40).

The type is wrong. This is not a measurable usability, technical, accessibility or consistency defect — nothing is broken, mislabelled, inaccessible or contradictory. It is an argument that social proof would convert better on price and specification pages, which is a marketing judgement where reasonable people disagree. Note the counter-case the finding does not engage with: the three specification hubs are reference pages a visitor arrives at mid-decision from a product page that already carried the reviews, and the site already has a documented aversion to adding sections to hubs (AI.md:695 rules the colour hub must show the whole range rather than adding interaction). The price guides are the stronger half of the argument. Also worth flagging as risk: AI.md:224 says the context string should be 'the town or product name', and a price guide covering multiple products has no single product name to pass, so the cards would fall back to generic proof.

## Appendix A — Findings killed by verification

**Do not re-raise these.** Each was proposed by an auditor and then refuted, or found to
be a deliberate owner decision already recorded in the project docs. This list exists so a
future session does not spend its budget rediscovering them.

- **[34] 14 product routes ship ~1.3KB of hero markup per page that CSS unconditionally hides** — `ALREADY_RULED`. Every mechanical claim reproduces, but the decision it calls a defect is documented twice as deliberate, so the High/Objective framing does not survive. PROGRESS.md:3186 (entry dated 2026-07-29): '**`.fg-hero--compact` hides `.fg-hero__intro` by design**, so the lead paragraph and the three reassurance points were moved into their own block below the hero rather than left marked up and never shown.' PROGRESS.md:3887 (2026-07-22): 'the product-journey hero hides `.fg-hero__panel` on every route, so a new `fg-hero--composite` modifier opts composite back in.' COMPOSITE-DOOR-REDESIGN.md:200: '`fg-hero--composite` exists purely to opt this route back into the hero card, which `.fg-hero--compact` hides everywhere else. Do not remove the modifier without moving the price anchor somewhere equally prominent.' So 'the component built to solve that is present and switched off' is the intended compact-hero design — a full-bleed photo with eyebrow, H1 and CTA pair — and /composite-doors/ is the sanctioned opt-back-in, not evidence of an oversight. Two secondary claims are also wrong: the hidden H2 is `display:none`, so it is removed from the accessibility tree and is not an outline defect for screen-reader users (the probe reports it because the probe walks the DOM, not the a11y tree); and STYLE.md:329's 'lead paragraph that does the selling' describes the composite/heritage/roof-lantern reference heroes, which is exactly the pattern PROGRESS.md:3184-3186 records moving away from on the shared route. What genuinely survives is a Low-impact hygiene item, and PROGRESS.md:3186's own phrasing ('rather than left marked up and never shown') endorses it: the markup is still emitted. I measured it at 1,122 bytes of `<aside>` on 12 routes and 973 on integral-blinds and window-and-door-repairs, plus 250-358 bytes of hidden `<p class="fg-hero__intro">`, on 14 routes. roof-lanterns carries the class but renders neither, as the finding correctly notes.
- **[64] The moment of maximum engagement is spent on a confirmation panel that offers nothing next** — `ALREADY_RULED`. The observed facts are all accurate, but the composition it calls a defect is a documented owner ruling. HOMEPAGE.md:179-187 enumerates exactly this list in exactly this order: "The theatre contains five homeowner-facing product groups: 1. Windows 2. Doors 3. Roof Lanterns 4. Integral Blinds 5. Other Services", and gives the rationale on the next line ("Other Services groups replacement glass, glazing repairs, cat and dog flaps, porches and smaller upgrades into one route card. Commercial Glazing is intentionally excluded."). HOMEPAGE.md:529 adds "Do not restore Commercial Glazing as a homepage product theatre item", proving the five-item set is actively curated rather than accidental. The theatre is explicitly framed as homeowner-facing product GROUPS, not as a mirror of the menu taxonomy, so the level-mixing the finding objects to is the intended design. The finding's primary recommendation ("reduce the theatre to the three real hubs") directly contradicts this. I verified every underlying fact and they hold: home-experience.php:48-54 defines the five routes as described; site-data.php primary_nav_fallback has three mega columns with Windows 9 / Doors 9 / Other Services 8 items; Roof Lanterns and Integral Blinds are both items inside the Other Services column; the homepage <main> exposes 20 unique internal targets of which the only product-level ones are /roof-lanterns/ and /integral-blinds/; mobile cards render at home-experience.php:243. The secondary suggestion (add a row of best-selling product links) is not itself ruled on, but the finding's core premise is.
- **[107] "Hundreds of customer reviews" sits on the same 527 pages as the checkable "Rated by 136 customers"** — `ALREADY_RULED`. The measurements are all exactly right, but the conclusion is not. PROGRESS.md:4470, under the dated heading '## 2026-07-06 - Reviews Copy And Privacy Policy Cleanup', records: 'Replaced hardcoded review-count claims such as `200+ five-star reviews`, `Google 130 reviews` and `Trustpilot 226 reviews` with stable wording around hundreds of customer reviews across Google and Trustpilot.' So this wording is a deliberate, dated decision taken specifically to stop hardcoded counts going stale, and the finding's recommendation would revert it. It also refutes the finding's premise on the numbers: the site's own record puts Trustpilot at 226, which with the current 136 Google reviews is roughly 362. 'Hundreds' is therefore literally true, not rounding in Fenster's favour, and the badge copy directly beneath it already scopes the claim to both platforms ('Feedback across Google and Trustpilot'). Replacing it with '136 Google reviews' as recommended would understate the real total by about two thirds. The finding was honest that it could not verify Trustpilot, and I could not either (I re-fetched uk.trustpilot.com/review/fensterglazing.com with a browser User-Agent and got HTTP 403; the scratchpad's earlier tp.html is a 991-byte 403 body, so the prior attempt failed the same way) — but the answer was in the project's own changelog rather than on Trustpilot. One residual point does survive and is worth putting to the owner, though it is not the one the finding argued: in shots/desktop/home--fold.png the 'Hundreds of customer reviews' card is the one carrying the Google logo, while the Trustpilot logo sits on the adjacent 'Rated Excellent' card. It is the logo pairing, not the word 'hundreds', that could read as attributing hundreds of reviews to Google alone.
- **[135] No Article or datePublished markup, and no date at all, on the 31 imported guides that carry most of the traffic** — `ALREADY_RULED`. The absence of the EnergyPlus banner on /patio-doors/ is an explicit owner instruction, written into the docblock of the function that renders it. inc/product-hub-data.php:534-538: "Owner instruction, 2026-07-27: Thermlock on every aluminium product including roof lanterns but not slide and fold; EnergyPlus on every Liniar product EXCEPT PATIO DOORS." The banner is gated on the `$energyplus_routes` array at inc/product-hub-data.php:549-557 (casement, flush-casement, bow-bay, french-casement, tilt-turn, upvc-doors, french-doors) and patio-doors is simply not in it.

The finding's stated mechanism is also refuted. It claims the missing `glazing_u_values` entry 'is the mechanical reason the banner is absent'. It is not — the two arrays are unrelated. /french-doors/ has NO `glazing_u_values` entry either and still renders a full fg-tech-banner (confirmed in the live HTML section list and by the fact that french-doors is in `$energyplus_routes`); it just renders with no glazing figures. So the recommendation 'add a patio-doors entry to glazing_u_values so the EnergyPlus banner renders' would not render the banner at all.

The `glazing_u_values` absence is separately and deliberately recorded too, at inc/site-data.php:600-602: "Not listed, and each for a reason. uPVC doors and patio doors are awaiting fabricator figures."

One fragment survives and is not ruled anywhere: "Liniar-style" does appear twice in source — inc/product-hub-data.php:263 ('Liniar-style uPVC sliding patio door profile') and inc/site-data.php:2110 ('Liniar-style multi-chambered uPVC frames') — and I found no ruling on it in AI.md, HANDOVER.md, STYLE.md, TONEOFVOICE.md, PROGRESS.md or LIVECHANGES.md. That hedge is worth raising on its own, but it does not rescue a finding whose headline, mechanism and primary recommendation are all ruled or wrong.
- **[136] 341 of 712 title tags exceed 60 characters, and the ones that matter are the case studies and the /blog/ hub cards** — `ALREADY_RULED`. The order is a documented, dated, deliberate restructure recorded in the template's own header. upvc-doors-v2.php:11-21: "RESTRUCTURED 2026-08-12, and the restructure is the point of this file... The order now runs: what it is, how it opens, what it looks like, what else you choose, what it is made of, what gets settled at survey. Nothing is said twice, and each section answers the question a customer asks next." `fg-upd-detail` ('The threshold and the lock.', line 355) is 'what gets settled at survey' and is deliberately last of the six. AI.md:501 states the same sequence from the other end: "Four sections: what 'made to the opening' means, the randomiser, the three ways the system opens, and the three things settled at survey."

The tech-banner placement the finding treats as an obstacle is also deliberate and explained: upvc-doors-v2.php:39-45, "THE TECH BANNER IS DEFERRED INTO THIS FILE rather than rendering in its usual slot... It now sits after the choosing and before the survey detail, which is where 'what am I actually getting' belongs." The deferral is implemented at generated-page.php:3577 (`$defer_tech_banner`). Moving `fg-upd-detail` above the colour section would strand that banner.

The AI.md quote at line 506 is accurate but is about the page saying the security position plainly, not about where it sits.

Measurements are very close but slightly off: fg-upd-detail's real top on the live page at 375x812 is 8,863px, not 8,785 — the finding summed section heights and dropped the 76px sticky header. Same 76px offset on the /aluminium-doors/ comparison: its security band `fg-alu-door-band` ('Held at several points, not just at the lock.') starts at 4,030px, not 3,953. Every individual section height it quotes is exact.
- **[137] Alt text on /colour-options/ is bare colour names with no product context** — `ALREADY_RULED`. Both halves are recorded owner decisions.

The missing price route is an explicit owner instruction, with the reason written at the gate. generated-page.php:932-939: "Integral blinds cannot be priced consumer-side: a blind unit is a sealed unit specification made to the host window or door, and the tool prices windows and doors. Sending someone to it from here promises a number they cannot get, so the route offers a CONSULTATION INSTEAD. Owner instruction, 2026-08-04. Add a slug here rather than deleting the buttons, so the two hero variants and the hero card stay in step." `$no_instant_price_routes = ['integral-blinds', 'window-and-door-repairs']`. HANDOVER.md repeats it in the Integral Blinds Page section: "Instant pricing is off on this route via $offers_instant_price... the button promised a number nobody could get. Both hero variants and the hero card are gated on the same list." So the second hero button being a consultation rather than 'Instant pricing' is the designed fallback, not a wasted slot, and the finding's suggested fix — link to a price guide — is the exact promise the owner removed.

The standalone colour grid is also deliberate, and it exists so this route does NOT look different. HANDOVER.md, Integral Blinds Page: "The slat colours lay out on the page, via template-parts/components/blind-colour-grid.php, sharing the .fg-upvc-colours / .fg-alu-colours styles so this route does not look like a different kind of page. Because the grid is inline, the route renders no colour card at all in Specification choices." Folding it into the visualiser would reintroduce the colour card it replaces.

The measurements are correct (visualiser 1,433px, fg-blind-colours 926px, no fg-product-quote-embed, hero CTAs #fenster-enquiry and /book-a-consultation/), and both blocks do list the same nine names and codes. But 'repeats itself' overstates: the standalone grid carries copy the visualiser does not — the BY012 'two sided' code, the bespoke-RAL note, the frame-versus-blind distinction, and the 'Compare colours across every material' link to /colour-options/ — and it explicitly cross-references the visualiser ('Tilt it one way in the visualiser above to see each face').
- **[143] The shared parallax controller ignores prefers-reduced-motion — 2,588 elements on 528 pages** — `ALREADY_RULED`. The underlying gap is real and already tracked, and both proposed remedies are explicitly ruled against in AI.md. (1) The image inventory in the finding is wrong: the page carries FIVE images, not three. In document order inside <main>: hw-hero-steel-look-2048w.webp (Sheerline hero), sheerline-heritage-windows.jpg ('Dark heritage aluminium windows along a traditional terrace'), sheerline-heritage-window-closeup.jpg ('Close view of slim dark glazing bars…', under the heading 'A stepped sash, and the bars in the right places'), hw-install-stone-gable-1200w.webp (ours), heritage-door-brick-1200w.webp. So the claims that the page shows nothing dark and illustrates no bar layout are both contradicted by the live markup — AI.md:429 calls the closeup 'the one real bar photograph'. (2) 'Give the one install a second wider composition from the same shoot' cannot be done and is not a no-new-job fix: AI.md:435 is titled 'ONE INSTALL OF OURS, AND ONE PHOTOGRAPH OF IT', and AI.md:436 records that the close crop of the same frame was published and pulled on the owner's instruction ('the finishing isnt actually great so just have the zoomed out version') from the page AND the pool. AI.md:435 also instructs 'do not draw attention to it being the only one'. (3) 'Bring the two heritage-door studies onto the page as adjacent proof' is directly refused: AI.md:426 — 'The two heritage DOOR studies still do not count either: those jobs had no windows in them.' (4) The remaining true gap — no owned steel-replacement install — is already PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md:98-103, which calls a steel before-and-after 'the single most valuable shot on this list', which is what the finding itself concedes.
- **[44] Three of the four handle-grid headings hardcode their item count as an English word while the fourth derives it** — `REFUTED`. The section indices reproduce exactly (tech banner at index 2 on eight routes — the finding says nine but lists and I count eight — index 5/18 on casement-windows, 8/17 on upvc-doors). But the entire rationale is false. I extracted and word-counted the sections preceding the banner: 788 words on `/casement-windows/` and 753 on `/upvc-doors/`, not 'several thousand'. More decisively, the manufacturer credibility beat is NOT delayed on either route. On `/casement-windows/` the hero (section 0) already says 'Fenster specifies Liniar uPVC profiles' and section 2 — the exact index the finding wants the banner moved to — is `fg-cas-overture`, which carries the badge '70mm Liniar EnergyPlus'; section 4 `fg-cas-energy` carries another 'EnergyPlus' block. On `/upvc-doors/` the hero opens 'The same Liniar system makes a single front or back door...'. So on both routes the reader is told whose system it is in the first screen, and on casement at index 2. The banner is a deeper technical elaboration arriving after the system has been named, which is a coherent reading order, not an artefact. There is nothing to investigate and nothing to record in AI.md.
- **[46] The WordPress template hierarchy is entirely unreachable and front-page.php still points at a superseded homepage** — `REFUTED`. The measured field order is exactly right (28 routes name,phone,email,location; /commercial-glazing/ name,company,email,phone,location; /book-a-consultation/ the third variant). But the diagnosis is disproven by the source. The order is NOT an arbitrary transposition and is NOT fixable in one line. enquiry-form.php lays the fields out in two-column `fg-enquiry-form__row` grids inside named fieldsets. Fieldset 'Your contact details' (:229-245) renders exactly two cells: `[name][phone]` normally, `[name][company]` when `show_company` is set. Fieldset 'How should we reply?' (:250-266) renders exactly two cells: `[email][postcode]` normally, `[email][phone]` when `show_company` is set — the phone field is the SAME input element, switched by ternary on type/name/autocomplete/pattern (:257-264). Postcode then drops to its own full-width label at :267-272. So inserting `company` necessarily displaces phone into the next row's slot and postcode out of it — the transposition IS required by adding a field, which is precisely what the finding says it is not. The recommended sequence (name, company, phone, email, postcode) would put three fields into a grid I verified is `grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr))` in main.css, leaving phone stranded alone on a second line. Calling this evidence 'the commercial branch was written rather than derived' is backwards: it is one shared component with ternaries, not a separate branch.
- **[47] The router's early-return dispatch is a 1,030-line linear if-chain in which order is the only rule and nothing states it** — `REFUTED`. The rendered output is exactly as described — 15 routes in the sample carry the span pair, and 2 have identical full/short strings ('Send us the sizes' on /double-glazing-replacement/, 'Request a repair' on /window-and-door-repairs/); 13 genuinely shorten. But the premise is wrong three ways. (1) NO MAINTENANCE BURDEN: the short label is not a hand-kept per-route string. generated-page.php:3267 is a single three-branch ternary (`$is_repairs ? 'Request a repair' : ($is_replacement_bespoke ? 'Send us the sizes' : 'Design consultation')`), mirroring the five-branch `$cta_label` at :887. There are two expressions, not fourteen strings, so 'two of fourteen routes have already collapsed them' misdescribes the mechanism. (2) THE IDENTICAL VALUES ARE THE DOCUMENTED FIX, NOT THE DRIFT: the comment at :3259-3266 records that replacement glazing said 'Send us the sizes' on desktop and 'Design consultation' on mobile until 2026-08-10, and HANDOVER.md:872-874 states the rule — 'The hero CTA is overridden in two places. $cta_label and the separate fg-hero-cta__short string for narrow screens. Override one and the phone quietly says something else.' Making them agree is the required behaviour. (3) NOTHING NEEDS SHORTENING: I read the mobile fold screenshot at 1170px. 'Send us the sizes' sits on one line, comfortably inside a green button roughly half the viewport wide, beside 'Instant pricing'. The finding's own recommendation — invent a distinct shorter mobile string — would re-introduce exactly the desktop/mobile divergence the comment and HANDOVER warn against, for no gain. The finding itself concedes 'the current output is correct'.
- **[158] WordPress block-library CSS (112 KB) is render-blocking on every page and not one block class is used anywhere** — `REFUTED`. The stepped enquiry form does not exist. `grep -rn 'enquiry-step' --include='*.php' --include='*.scss' --include='*.html'` across the whole theme returns nothing outside src/js/main.js and the compiled assets/js/main.js — no PHP template emits `data-fg-enquiry-step`, `data-fg-enquiry-progress`, `data-fg-enquiry-step-controls`, `data-fg-enquiry-prev` or `data-fg-enquiry-next`, and there is no matching SCSS. `grep -l data-fg-enquiry-step live/*.html` returns 0 of 40, while `grep -l fg-enquiry-form live/*.html` returns 30 — so every rendered enquiry form has zero step elements. Since `const steps = [...form.querySelectorAll('[data-fg-enquiry-step]')]` (main.js:2414) is always empty, `isSteppedForm()` (:2441) is always false, `progress` (:2415) is null so `progressText` (:2417) is null, the `if (progressText)` guard at :2515 never fires, and `showStepForInvalidField()` returns at :2559 on its first line. The described experience — hearing nothing on a step change, being jumped backwards silently — cannot happen to any visitor. The docs confirm it is intentional dead scaffolding: HANDOVER.md:1116 "All fields are visible in one form flow; the old stepped/wizard presentation has been removed", HANDOVER.md:1118 "Some old stepped-form CSS/JS selectors may still exist as inactive scaffolding, but the shared PHP component does not currently render the stepped data attributes or step controls", PROGRESS.md:4869 "Removed the stepped/wizard markup from the shared enquiry form so all fields are visible at once." The finding's own mechanism claim is wrong independently of that: it says the stepped mode is "viewport-dependent via isSteppedForm()", but main.js:2441 is `const isSteppedForm = () => steps.length > 1` — a step-count test with no matchMedia and no viewport term. The one incidental sub-claim that holds (a grep for aria-live in the theme finds elements, none of them an enquiry progress text — I count 11 in template-parts, not the 12 claimed) holds only because the element does not exist. There is a real but different observation buried here — roughly 180 lines of unreachable stepped-form JS still ship in the 139 KB bundle — but that is not the reported finding.
- **[230] The Legend assistant covers the bottom of the mobile fold and sits above the open navigation** — `REFUTED`. The premise fails at the call sites. The finding is right that both `fg-wipe__tag` spans carry `aria-hidden="true"` and that `$sr_label` defaults to 'Reveal the second photograph over the first' — but that default is never used. All three call sites already pass a descriptive `sr_label` naming both sides: `template-parts/sections/flush-casement-windows-v2.php:242` 'Reveal the standard casement over the flush one'; `template-parts/sections/replacement-glazing-v2.php:153` 'Drag to reveal the misted unit over the replaced one'; `template-parts/sections/aluminium-flush-windows-v2.php:146` 'Reveal the standard outer frame over the flush one'. I confirmed all three in served HTML: live/flush-casement-windows.html has `<label class="fg-cas-sr" for="fg-wipe-1">Reveal the standard casement over the flush one`, live/double-glazing-replacement.html has the misted/replaced one, and `curl https://fensterglazing.com/aluminium-flush-windows/` returns the aluminium one. So a screen-reader user IS told what the two sides are — the exact thing the finding says does not reach assistive tech. The recommendation ('pass `sr_label` as e.g. "Reveal Standard over Flush" from both call sites') is already implemented, and better worded than the suggestion. The scope is also wrong: three routes, not two. The only residue is an unused default string in the component, which is not a defect on any live page.

## Appendix B — Strengths recorded by the audit

- **The page-canvas gradient is a genuinely well-engineered system, not a decoration** (design-system) — `--fg-page-gradient` composes three radial layers plus a linear base, and every one of its parameters is exposed as its own token — position (x/y), size and alpha for each of the green, blue and wash layers, 13 tokens in total. It is painted once on `body` with `background-attachment: fixed`, exactly as STYLE.md's site-wide background rule requires, so the canvas is continuous rather than restarted per section. This is the most sophisticated thing in the stylesheet and it is the reason the site reads as one surface rather than stacked bands. STYLE.md even documents the failure mode (a route wrapper repainting it, causing visible seams) and names the pages still to check, which is unusually mature engineering hygiene. Protect this: it should be the model for how the rest of the tokens are structured.
- **The SCSS records design intent and rejected alternatives in prose, not just what the code does** (design-system) — There are 511 comment blocks and they explain reasoning rather than restating the CSS. Examples: "The chapter number is a marker, not a headline: large, hairline, quiet" above `.fg-cas-num`; "Three foils are effectively white and would read as a gap in the wall"; "The gap under the buttons was 123px at 390, built from four separate…"; "On a phone the panel stopped being a backdrop and became an overlay the…". Several record what was tried and why it failed. In a 42,407-line single-file stylesheet maintained by rotating agents, this is the single thing preventing the codebase from being unreadable, and it is far better than most professional design systems manage. Any cleanup work must preserve these comments when it moves the rules they annotate.
- **Accessibility and progressive-enhancement scaffolding is consistently present** (design-system) — 116 `focus-visible` rules mean keyboard focus is styled deliberately across components rather than left to the browser default or, worse, removed. 27 `prefers-reduced-motion` blocks mean the substantial motion work on this site degrades properly. And `overflow-x: clip` is paired with four `@supports not (overflow: clip)` fallbacks to `hidden` on `html`, `body`, and the header/main/footer wrappers — a careful, modern detail that most sites get wrong. This restraint is also measurable in outcome: 38 of 38 desktop routes have zero horizontal overflow despite 42,000 lines of bespoke per-page CSS, which is real discipline.
- **The base `.button` is correctly specified** (design-system) — `.button` uses `inline-flex` with both axes centred, an explicit `min-height: 46px` that clears the 44px tap-target minimum, symmetric padding, a 6px radius consistent with the ≤8px card family, and a border matching its background so outline and solid variants share identical geometry. That last detail is what stops secondary variants from jumping by 2px against primaries, and it is a thing many mature systems get wrong. The component's problem is the fifteen overrides layered on top of it, not the base — so the fix is subtraction, which is low risk.
- **Header and footer are byte-identical on all 40 pages** (cross-page-consistency) — On a 712-URL site with roughly 20 distinct page templates, several early returns and at least six bespoke middles, the two components every visitor sees on every page have not drifted by a single byte. That is the hardest kind of consistency to hold and it is held perfectly. It means the primary navigation, the Instant Quote / Free Consultation CTA pair, the phone number and the whole footer link mesh are guaranteed identical regardless of which template rendered the page. Do not let any route-specific header or footer variant in.
- **The enquiry form's field contract is genuinely shared and correctly wired everywhere** (cross-page-consistency) — Despite four different layout variants, the underlying field schema does not vary: 28 of 30 form-bearing routes emit exactly `name, phone, email, location, message, attachments[], privacy` plus the honeypot, every visible field is programmatically labelled, the required flags match on every route, and every input renders at 16px so iOS never zooms on focus. The two exceptions are both intentional (commercial adds `company`; the consultation form drops attachments and adds day/time). Whatever is wrong with the four layout variants, the data contract behind them is sound and safe to unify against.
- **The key-specification strip derives its U-value treatment from data rather than a hand-kept route list** (cross-page-consistency) — The component computes the lowest achievable figure from `glazing_u_values` and decides whether to star it by asking whether a second figure exists, rather than consulting a list of "routes that have been converted". The file explains that it used to be gated on a `single_u_value_routes` list and that the list "could only drift out of step with the data", so it was deleted. That is precisely the right instinct on a codebase where the same name lives in six or seven registries, and it means adding a route to `glazing_u_values` is the only edit ever needed. Every shared component on this site should be built this way.
- **Eleven product routes share a genuinely canonical tail, exactly in order** (cross-page-consistency) — FAQ → order rail → quote embed → reviews → case studies → enquiry → links band renders in that precise sequence on flush-casement-windows, tilt-turn-windows, aluminium-windows, heritage-windows, upvc-doors, french-doors, patio-doors, aluminium-doors, aluminium-bifold-doors, integral-blinds and secondary-glazing. Given how much bespoke work has gone into the middles of these pages, holding eleven tails identical is a real achievement and gives a clear, defensible target to pull the four deviant routes back to.
- **Head-tag hygiene is complete across every probed route** (cross-page-consistency) — All 38 probed routes carry a canonical URL, a meta description, an og:image, a robots directive and `lang="en-GB"`. There are no missing canonicals and no missing descriptions anywhere in the sample — on a code-generated 712-URL site with no SEO plugin doing the work, that is not the default outcome.
- **Every gate carries a dated owner ruling and the reason it exists** (architecture) — This is the most valuable asset in the codebase and it is not typical of any theme I have read. Almost every conditional records who decided it, when, and — crucially — what went wrong before. generated-page.php:190-206 explains why replacement glazing drops three tail sections, naming the A+ rating that could not be true of a sealed unit; :229-243 explains that the tilt-and-turn case-study strip "was live and wrong until this build" and names the three studies it wrongly showed; product-hub-data.php:571-587 records the 0.95-over-1.2 U-value contradiction the owner reported on 2026-07-29 and why a route with no confirmed figure now gets none. Several of my findings were only provable because the code told me where to look. Protect this absolutely: it is the reason a 5,376-line template with 20 registries has not collapsed.
- **Output escaping and REST authorisation are handled with real discipline, and past mistakes were fixed structurally** (architecture) — I scanned every `echo`/`print` of a variable across all 76 PHP files. The 97 candidates resolve almost entirely to literal ternaries; the handful of genuine raw echoes are locally constructed markup and carry explicit `phpcs:ignore WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput` annotations, so they were decisions rather than oversights. Scraped `pages.json` content is escaped everywhere it is rendered, and where limited HTML is permitted it goes through `wp_kses` with an explicit tag allowlist. The public form carries a nonce. Most impressive: `fenster_google_ads_feed_is_authorized()` fails closed and the comment above it documents the exact `hash_equals('','')` bug that once let an unset password authorise the whole feed — the fix was to restructure the predicate, not to patch the symptom.
- **Data lookups fall back to the canonical set rather than to nothing** (architecture) — The order-process rail is the model. generated-page.php:1398-1438 reads `order_process.steps`, mutates one or three sentences for the routes outside the FENSA/CPA schemes, and if the data key is missing sets `$product_order_steps = null` with the comment "Fall back to the canonical set rather than to nothing. A missing data key must not silently empty the rail." That instinct — degrade to the shared correct thing rather than to an empty section — is the right one and appears throughout. It is worth noting because the one place the codebase does the opposite (the all-studies fallback in `fenster_case_studies_for_product()`) is the source of the second finding above: falling back to something wrong is worse than falling back to nothing, and the rest of the theme already knows the difference.
- **Memoisation and cache headers are correct where it counts, including one genuinely subtle carve-out** (architecture) — `fenster_generated_pages_payload()`, `fenster_generated_pages_index()`, `fenster_get_generated_page()` and `fenster_image_dimensions()` all use static caches correctly, including negative caching via `array_key_exists` so a null result is not recomputed. `fenster_send_public_cache_headers()` (inc/generated-pages.php:1812-1840) declines to set shared-cache headers when the request carries an ad click identifier, because the response embeds an attribution reference derived from that click and a path-keyed proxy would hand it to the next visitor — and the comment even names the hook priority (`template_redirect` -10 vs 0) that would otherwise undo `fenster_record_ad_click()`'s no-cache headers. That is a correctness bug most codebases ship. I also confirmed the consent gate is purely additive client-side (inc/consent.php strips trackers server-side unconditionally), so the HTML genuinely does not vary by consent cookie and the shared cache is safe.
- **$route_title() derives matrix names instead of restating them** (architecture) — generated-page.php:1949-1990 is the right answer to the registry problem, arrived at under pressure and written down. When the 2026-08-12 rename left eight stale `pages.json` records making /patio-doors/ link to "Patio Doors Northampton" under an H1 reading "uPVC Sliding Doors", the fix was not to correct the eight records — the comment says explicitly that would have "left the same trap armed for the next rename" — but to derive the label from `fenster_location_matrix_products()` so changing one array moves everything. That is exactly the pattern the twenty other registries need, already implemented in this codebase, with the reasoning preserved. Any consolidation work should start by copying this function's approach rather than inventing one.
