- **The /online-quote/ rebuild is the best-designed conversion page on the site and it answers the awkward question head on** (cro-conversion) — It does the three things the product pages do not. It puts the live tool 711px down on mobile, just below the fold. It proves the tool is live rather than asserting it — a "LIVE" badge and an animated ghost hand that stops the moment the visitor touches the frame. And it discloses the details wall three times, including an FAQ that opens with "Do I have to give my details to see the price? Yes." The six-screen walkthrough uses real screenshots of the actual tool in the actual order. This is the pattern every other quote surface should copy, and the template even records why it exists.
- **The sticky mobile "Call us" pill** (cro-conversion) — An accent-coloured, 46px-minimum, always-visible call action pinned in a fixed header on every mobile page. For a trade where the phone is the likeliest closing channel, having a permanent one-tap call is the correct default, and it is executed properly — real minimum tap height, focus-visible outline, and the desktop number swapped for it rather than shown alongside.
- **The composite-doors quote block is the only one on the site that gives before it asks — protect it and copy it** (cro-conversion) — It is the single product page that puts a real fitted figure (£2,000, with the full specification) next to the tool, offers the price guide as an alternative to opening the tool at all, and leads its hero with `Get an instant price` plus `Call 01908 429200` rather than a mislabelled consultation button. Every other product page is a worse version of this one. It is also the only page whose FAQ answers the price question directly.
- **The enquiry form is engineered far better than most agency work** (cro-conversion) — AJAX submission with in-place feedback and scroll-position restore, per-field trimmed validation for phone, email and postcode with real custom messages, a `form_validation_error` event that names the offending field, a honeypot, multi-file upload up to 8MB, and a full set of attribution fields (journey, visitor, consent state, gclid, opaque marketing ref) that survive a consent change. The probe found every visible field correctly labelled on all 30 form routes and 16px font on every input.
- **The consultation booking flow is short, honest and correctly scoped** (cro-conversion) — Three clear steps with a real calendar that excludes bank holidays and weekends, a working noscript fallback, back buttons at every stage, and the line "Your preferred time is a request. We will confirm your appointment directly" — which refuses to imply a confirmed booking the business cannot honour. At 6,210px on mobile it is by far the shortest conversion page on the site, which is exactly right for its job.
- **The three hub pages are the best decision-support IA on the site and should not be touched except to reorder** (ux-ia) — Each hub answers the question a visitor actually has rather than listing SKUs. /windows-milton-keynes/ gives nine cards each carrying a plain-English 'fit' line — 'The everyday all-rounder', 'Sits level with the frame', 'A shape, not a style', 'An opening, not a style' — which pre-empts the two most common confusions (bay/bow and French casement are not systems). /other-services/ is better still: its decision panel is organised by symptom, not product — 'The glass has failed', 'The room is cold or loud', 'There is no wall left' — which is exactly how a homeowner arrives at the problem. The supplier badge on each card (Liniar, Sheerline, Roseview) does honest disambiguation work at card level.
- **The three navigation registries are in exact agreement — no orphans, no mismatches, in either direction** (ux-ia) — Given the project's recorded 'a name lives in 6-7 registries' problem, this is the one place the discipline held. Cross-checking every product slug in `product_hub_groups` (26) against every `home_url()` target in `primary_nav_fallback` (48 distinct URLs) against the 712-URL sitemap produced zero hub products missing from the nav, zero nav product items missing from a hub, and zero hub product slugs missing a live page. Column-to-hub mapping is exact: nav Windows column 9 items = hub windows 9 products; Doors 9 = 9; Other Services 8 = 8. Only ordering differs (roofline and the bow-bay/french-casement pair).
- **The matrix pages roll up properly and carry a real, well-built related-links band** (ux-ia) — Despite the reachability problems reported above, the template itself is right. /casement-windows-bletchley/ carries 31 main-content links: the parent product page, the town hub /double-glazing-bletchley/, all three hubs, two genuinely relevant case studies, and a 24-link 'Products, services and nearby areas' band rendered as image cards with photo-backed labels rather than a naked link list. The pages are not thin doorway pages — 8,965px tall, one H1, an enquiry form, town-specific housing-stock copy and an FAQ. The design is sound; only the link-eligibility gate is broken.
- **The header CTA pair and the mega-menu CTA cards are a genuinely well-judged conversion IA** (ux-ia) — The header carries two clearly differentiated actions rather than one generic 'Contact' — 'Instant Quote' (green) and 'Free Consultation' (dark) — and the Products mega menu repeats them as explanatory cards that say what each one actually is ('Price windows and doors through the online quote tool.' vs 'An expert comes to you, goes through the options and prices the job. The visit costs nothing.'). The variant colour is declared per CTA rather than inferred from order, with an in-code note explaining why. /online-quote/ has 83 in-links and /book-a-consultation/ 22 across the crawl, so the pattern is being used consistently across the site, not just in the header.
- **The case-study and commercial-project indexes link their full sets, with no truncation** (ux-ia) — /case-studies/ links all 13 residential studies and /commercial-projects/ links all 9 commercial projects plus the four sector pages that have real proof behind them (healthcare, student accommodation, hospitality, care homes) — the four sectors AI.md says were chosen because genuine completed work exists in them. Individual product pages then link only the studies that are actually relevant to them (e.g. /roof-lanterns/ → the Sheerline roof lantern and the roof-lantern-and-heritage-doors studies). This is the one content cluster on the site with no orphans and no truncation defect.
- **The whole of /about/, and the accreditations section in particular** (copy) — It is the only page on the site where every claim is anchored. It names the fitters (Johnnie and Tom), the month (August 2025), the town (Northampton), the products (S1 roof lantern, black steel-look heritage doors) and then says "This is the actual job." The badge section does the hardest thing on the site — it states the guarantee's limits in the body of the page rather than in a footnote, and it says why. The showroom paragraph uses handling verbs rather than admiring ones, exactly as the voice document prescribes. Nothing here should be touched, and every weak page on the site has a fix available by copying its method.
- **/commercial-glazing-leeds/ — the rewritten county page, and the model for the other three** (copy) — It does in its first paragraph what the other three county pages never do: names a real building, its scale and its completion date. Then it volunteers the awkward answer before the customer asks for it, in a heading that is itself a customer truth. It is written entirely in the first person, in sentence case, with a plain H1. It is the proof that the commercial rebuild standard works, and it is the reference text for Manchester, Birmingham and Essex.
- **The "Start here" diagnostic on /other-services/** (copy) — It solves the hardest copy problem on the site — a page of unrelated small services — by reframing it as three questions the customer can answer about their own house, each with a real specification attached (new sealed units and argon fill; 1.8 W/m²K and full RAL; lanterns up to 3.2 x 6m with solar control glass). The heading is a genuine customer truth that also lowers the perceived cost of enquiring, and the paragraph under it protects the customer from being oversold by us. The FAQ below it is the best short technical writing on the site.
- **The /window-and-door-repairs/ hero and diagnostic, including its one aside** (copy) — The lead states the customer's situation in their own words, promises three specific things in order, and volunteers the sentence most installers avoid. The four reasons below it are all facts rather than adjectives — "Two of them, with decades each behind them, and a van carrying the parts that fail most often" is worth more than any number of trust badges. The symptom list is written the way a customer would describe the fault, not the way a fitter would name it, and it lands the site's best deadpan aside.
- **The /handle-options/ section headings** (copy) — Nine headings, every one of which describes what the object physically does in five words or fewer, with no adjective anywhere. They are the purest example on the site of TONEOFVOICE's "physical, sensory verbs" principle, and they prove that the heading rule produces better copy when it is followed than when it is decorated. They are also the strongest argument against the 525 matrix H1s: this page shows the same writer can name a thing without appending a campaign line to it.
- **The "Local knowledge" block on the matrix pages — the only section that earns their indexation** (copy) — Buried three-quarters of the way down /casement-windows-bletchley/ is the only copy on that page that could not be pasted onto any other route. It knows the building stock, draws a practical consequence from it, and closes with a genuine customer warning that costs us nothing to give and immediately separates us from a doorstep salesman. If the matrix is going to keep 525 routes, this block is the argument for it and everything above it is the argument against.
- **The shared order-process rail** (copy) — Fifteen routes carry it and it does not read as template on any of them, because every step contains a fact rather than a promise. It names what the survey is not, which is the awkward-thing-first principle working correctly; it keeps the owner's clearing-up commitment in plain words; and it resolves the site's biggest credibility risk — the gap between an online figure and a doorstep figure — in one sentence. It is the benchmark for what a shared section should look like, and the counter-example to the 525-route filler sentences.
- **The commercial sector-page opening headings** (copy) — Three headings that understand the buyer's actual anxiety rather than the product's features, written in the register AI.md sets for the commercial set — declarative, sober, no asides — while still sounding like Fenster. Each one names the constraint the specifier is actually managing, which is a stronger opening than any capability list. COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-2026-08-12 §3 identified these as the part of the commercial set worth keeping through the rebuild, and it is right.
- **Zero duplicate or missing titles and meta descriptions across all 712 URLs** (seo) — On a 712-URL site that is 74% programmatically generated, uniqueness at this level is rare and it is the foundation the launch's measured +33% CTR was built on. Every page has a title, a description, and a canonical; nothing is templated into collision; not one description exceeds 160 characters. The failure modes I went looking for — the matrix colliding with itself, the county pages colliding, the price guides colliding — do not occur.
- **Canonicalisation is airtight against every duplicate-URL vector I could construct** (seo) — Non-trailing-slash, http, www, mixed case and index.php all 301 to the single correct HTTPS trailing-slash form. Double and triple trailing slashes and a leading double slash return 200 but emit the correct clean canonical, so they cannot generate duplicates. Query strings do not alter the canonical. Invented sub-paths under a real page (/composite-doors/foo/) return a hard 404, not a soft one. Every canonical across 712 pages is absolute and self-referencing.
- **Every FAQPage block matches its visible content exactly, and there is no risky markup anywhere** (seo) — Across all 712 pages, 36 emit FAQPage and every single question name and answer text is present verbatim in the rendered page — 0 mismatches. All JSON-LD on all 712 pages parses without error. There is no aggregateRating and no Review anywhere, exactly as the owner ruling and AI.md require, and the LocalBusiness node is fully populated (geo, opening hours, areaServed, hasOfferCatalog, foundingDate, currenciesAccepted) and consistent site-wide. This is the part of the site most audits find broken and it is clean.
- **The noindex debris policy is real, consistent and enforced in both places** (seo) — AI.md:272 states that debris must be handled in fenster_gone_slugs(), fenster_redirect_target() and fenster_slug_is_noindex() rather than by sitemap omission alone — and unusually, the code actually does it. All twelve ad landers and utility shells return 200 with robots noindex,follow AND are absent from the sitemap; the category/, tag/, author/ and blog/page/ archive prefixes are handled by rule rather than by list; retired duplicate town slugs 301 rather than 404. That is the correct belt-and-braces behaviour and it is applied without a single exception I could find.
- **Alt text on the product pages is among the best I have audited on a trade site** (seo) — Not one image in <main> across 712 pages is missing an alt attribute. On the product pages the text is specific, product-named and genuinely descriptive — "Friction stay along the cill of a white uPVC side hung casement, the sash swung open on the arm", "Kenrick Excalibur multi-point window lock, showing the die-cast gearbox, the square spindle drive", "Distinction Rustic Renown RR03 composite door, Rustic Renown collection". Filenames match (cas-stay-open.webp, rustic-renown-rr03-300w.webp); decorative images correctly carry alt="". This is doing real work for image search and for screen readers and it should not be touched.
- **Zero missing alt text across 712 pages, and the alt text is genuinely descriptive** (accessibility) — Every <img> in the entire production corpus carries an alt attribute, and the 522 distinct alt strings contain no filenames, no "image of", no dimension codes and no generic placeholders. They describe the thing that matters — "A conventional door hinge standing proud of the frame, beside the InvisiHinge set flush into the edge of an anthracite aluminium door" — rather than the object class. Decorative overlays and avatars correctly carry alt="". Not one link is an image-only link without an accessible name. This is the single hardest accessibility discipline to maintain at 712 pages and it has been held perfectly.
- **Heading structure is perfect on every page — one H1, zero level jumps, 712 for 712** (accessibility) — I re-derived the outline independently of the probe, parsing headings inside <main> on all 712 pages rather than the 38 the probe covered. Every page has exactly one H1 and not a single skipped heading level anywhere on the site. lang and the skip link are present on all 712. For a code-driven theme where headings are assembled from data files across dozens of section templates, this is very unusual and it is the backbone of screen-reader navigation. Protect it: any new section template must take its heading level from context rather than hardcoding one.
- **The cookie consent modal is a native <dialog> with showModal() — and I verified the trap works live** (accessibility) — Rather than hand-rolling an overlay, inc/consent.php uses a real <dialog> opened with showModal(), which gives focus containment, top-layer rendering, inertness of the page behind and Escape handling from the platform rather than from code that can drift. aria-labelledby/aria-describedby are re-pointed when the panel switches between the overview and the customise view, focus is moved into the customise panel on switch, and the close button is correctly hidden while a choice is mandatory so the modal always offers a way out through its own buttons.
- **The duplicate "Aluminium Heritage" menu problem was solved properly, in both renderers, with the reasoning written down** (accessibility) — The brief flagged this as a screen-reader risk and it is already handled. Each mega-menu column is a <section aria-labelledby="fg-mega-column-N"> named from its own heading link, and the mobile drawer repeats the treatment with its own id counter naming the section from the accordion button. So the two identically-labelled "Aluminium Heritage" links are disambiguated by their column name when a screen reader lists links out of context. The ids come from a counter rather than the label specifically to avoid duplicate ids, and a source comment explains why the shortened labels depend on this and instructs the next developer to change both renderers together.
- **The compare-wipe component is a model implementation of an invisible control** (accessibility) — It uses a real <input type="range"> stretched invisibly over the photograph, so keyboard operation, touch handling and value announcement all come from the platform instead of being reimplemented — and because the input itself can carry no visible focus, the stage wears the focus ring instead via :has(). The source comments state the reasoning, including why there is deliberately no reduced-motion branch (it only moves while a person is actively dragging it). This is the pattern the obscured-glass and blind visualisers should be copying, and it is already written and shipped.
- **Form markup is correct throughout: implicit labels, real autocomplete tokens, 16px inputs, honeypot properly hidden from AT** (accessibility) — Every field in the shared enquiry form is wrapped in its own <label> (no fragile for/id pairing to break), carries the right HTML autocomplete token (name, tel, email, postal-code, organization), and renders at 16px on mobile so iOS does not zoom on focus. required is native and each required field also shows a visible "Required" marker. The spam honeypot is done exactly right — a wrapper with aria-hidden="true" containing an input with tabindex="-1" — so a screen-reader user can neither hear it nor tab into it and get their enquiry silently binned, which is the usual way honeypots break accessibility.
- **prefers-reduced-motion is honoured almost everywhere, by both stylesheet and script** (accessibility) — Lenis smooth scrolling is not even instantiated under reduced motion. The door wall, the blind visualiser, the scrub videos, the page gradient, the reveal observer, the review carousel and the Legend sprite animations all check it, and several re-check on the media query's change event so a mid-session preference switch is respected rather than latched. The parallax controller called out in the findings is a genuine outlier in an otherwise consistently motion-aware codebase, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than a symptom of a wider gap.
- **The quote iframe deferral is the best-executed lazy-loading on the site** (performance) — The instant-quote embed is the site's primary conversion mechanism and also its heaviest third-party dependency. It is rendered with `data-quote-iframe-src` and no `src` at all, so the browser cannot request it early, and the wrapper carries an explicit policy per route: `data-quote-autoload="near"` on product pages (load when approaching the viewport) and `"idle"` on /online-quote/ where it is the point of the page, with a `[data-load-quote]` button as the manual path. It also carries `data-lenis-prevent` so smooth scroll releases the pointer inside it. This is the pattern the rest of the site's images should be following, and AI.md:37 correctly instructs future work not to undo it.
- **Every image is dimensionally constrained by CSS, so CLS is zero even where width/height attributes are missing** (performance) — The probe reports large `images.noDims` counts — 59 of 69 on /colour-options/, 44 of 65 on /flush-casement-windows/ — which looks like a textbook layout-shift defect. It is not. main.css carries 160 `aspect-ratio` declarations and 218 `object-fit` rules, and every image sits inside a container that reserves its box. I checked the worst page in a live browser: on /colour-options/, cumulative layout shift was 0, there were zero layout-shift entries at all, and of 69 images not one lacked both a dimension attribute and an aspect-ratio/height constraint. The missing attributes are cosmetic, not a defect. This is a genuinely well-built layout system and it must not be 'fixed' by someone reading the probe number in isolation.
- **The homepage hero video gate is real, not aspirational — verified in code, not in the docs** (performance) — 9.36 MB is enough to ruin a mobile first impression, and the theme genuinely keeps it off the initial payload. The `<video>` is emitted with `preload="none"` and a `<source data-src>` carrying no `src`, so the markup alone cannot trigger a fetch. The controller then branches on four independent signals — viewport <=860px, `connection.saveData`, `effectiveType` in slow-2g/2g/3g, and `prefers-reduced-motion` — and on desktop still waits for the `load` event plus `requestIdleCallback` with a 1,800 ms timeout. The poster is separately preloaded with `fetchpriority="high"` so the mobile first paint is a 175 KB image. The mobile fold screenshot confirms the poster is what a phone actually shows. The only flaw is the scope of the interaction listener, reported separately.
- **Brotli is on across the board and the compression ratios are good** (performance) — Every text asset I tested is served with `content-encoding: br` at what looks like q=11, and the transport layer is doing everything it can. This matters because it means the byte problems found in this audit are genuinely payload problems, not delivery problems — no amount of further compression tuning will help, and nobody should waste time looking there. HTTP/2 and `vary: Accept-Encoding` are both correct too.
- **Lazy loading is applied broadly and correctly, and the first image in a gallery is deliberately eager** (performance) — 204 `loading="lazy"` sites across the theme's PHP, and the live HTML shows the discipline holding at scale. Where it matters the code is nuanced rather than blanket — generated-page.php:3624 emits `loading="<?php echo $index === 0 ? 'eager' : 'lazy'; ?>"` so the first card in a family grid is not lazy-loaded into a layout the visitor is already looking at. The reason page weights still look bad is not lazy loading; it is that the individual files are 10-100x larger than the slots they fill. Worth stating explicitly so the fix is aimed at file size, not at the loading strategy.
- **The all-intra scrub video encoding is a genuinely expert decision, correctly documented** (performance) — `fenster_product_scrub_videos()` in inc/assets.php encodes the scroll-scrub videos as all-intra H.264 — every frame a keyframe — because a scroll scrub seeks on nearly every frame and a normal GOP forces a decode from the previous keyframe. The comment records the actual measurement that motivated it (prestige-slider had one keyframe in 101 frames, so every seek decoded from frame zero), notes that all-intra costs about 5x the file size, and explains why that trade is correct. It also lists the mobile source first because a browser takes the first matching `<source>`, and rejects VP9/WebM specifically because it is less reliably hardware-decoded. This is the right technique, measured, and written down — and it is the encoder I would reach for to fix the aluminium-windows frame story.
- **HTML documents carry correct, deliberate cache headers with stale-while-revalidate** (performance) — Every page returns a short browser TTL, a longer shared TTL, and a day of stale-while-revalidate so a cache miss never blocks a visitor on a PHP render. It measurably works. This also makes the total absence of the equivalent headers on static assets look like an oversight in one config block rather than a policy, which is encouraging for how quickly that can be fixed.
- **Images carry width and height via a central helper that reads the real file** (performance) — `fenster_image_attr_string()` and `fenster_image_dimensions()` resolve a theme URL back to its path on disk, call `getimagesize()`, memoise the result in a static cache, and inject the true width and height plus `decoding="async"` unless the caller has overridden them. That is the right architecture: one place to change, dimensions that cannot drift from the file, and no per-request cost after the first call. It is also exactly the right place to add `srcset` — the recommendation in this audit is to extend this function, not to replace it.
- **/composite-doors/ is the best product page on the site and the template the others should be judged against** (product-experience) — It is the shortest of the major pages (14,809px mobile against casement's 21,752) and the densest. It runs a clean progression — six collections and why the slab separates them, a browsable wall of over 300 real door faces, a layered cutaway of what is inside the slab, the £5,000 break-in guarantee with all three lock components named, colour shown on a real door rather than as a chip, eight handles, then price. It is the only page that answers "how much" with a checked figure (£2,000 inc VAT for a 900x2100 Distinction Esteem) and a link to the guide. It has one enquiry CTA label rather than four. It hides the mobile quote iframe and shows a single "Price my composite door" action. And its FAQ volunteers the awkward answer — "Why is there no U-value shown for composite doors?" — instead of inventing one.
- **The key-specification odometer is exceptional engineering that most sites would get wrong** (product-experience) — The strip animates its figures as a real counter: single-unit steps so every numeral between the start and the value is actually on screen, per-wheel keyframes rather than a transition so a static digit does not creep, geometric timing so it decelerates, capped at 900-1800ms with a 150ms stagger, direction reversed for U-values because lower is better, and the markup restored byte-for-byte afterwards. Crucially the true value is placed in a screen-reader-only span for the whole run and the wheels are hidden from the accessibility tree, so no intermediate reading is ever announced, and the whole thing is gated on `prefers-reduced-motion` and `Element.prototype.animate`.
- **The integral blind visualiser is the right kind of interactive and the only one of its class on the site** (product-experience) — "Work the blind before you order it." — a real Notan magnetic unit drawn straight on, two magnets you drag, one that tilts the slats and one that raises them, in any of the nine colours. It teaches the product's one non-obvious behaviour by letting you do it, and unlike the two home-built configurators the owner removed on sight it never pretends to quote. It also states plainly that it demonstrates the magnetic system specifically, so it cannot imply magnetic is the only control offered.
- **The replacement-glazing before/after pair carries its own control** (product-experience) — The wipe on /double-glazing-replacement/ is one window five minutes apart, and it was chosen over a more dramatic pair because the panes either side of the failed one are clear in both frames — so a viewer does not have to take the difference on trust. Getting the two frames to register took a 1.05 degree rotation and a 22% scale correction solved off the centre pane's four edges, verified on the frame rather than the whole image. That is the most rigorous piece of image work on the site and it is in service of the one thing that page has to prove.
- **/window-and-door-repairs/ is structured around the visitor's actual question rather than the product** (product-experience) — It opens on why to have us do it, then goes straight to diagnosis — the mechanism, the hinges, the handle, each mapped to an inline AutoCAD-register schematic with concealed hardware on dashed hidden line — then the parts wall, then the honest verdict section that says when a repair is not the right answer, then the process. It carries exactly one price ("from £96 including VAT") tied to a physical thing rather than an average, claims no guarantee it does not have, and invents no callout window or same-day service. 49% of the page is about the job, the highest ratio after composite.
- **The uPVC door randomiser solves the configurator problem without competing with the quote tool** (product-experience) — It shuffles a finish, a glass and a handle, names what it landed on and hands over to WindowCAD for a price. The door image changes only by finish because that is the only dimension a real render exists for; the handle and glass are shown as their own product photographs beside the door rather than composited onto it, and the caption says which is which. It never repeats a finish twice in a row, and the spec text moves with the picture rather than before it. That restraint is why it survived where two home-built configurators did not.
- **The specification discipline across the range is genuinely rare** (product-experience) — Component figures are never restated as Fenster performance figures — Kenrick's Excalibur data on casement, Sheerline's Classic data on heritage, Liniar's PAS 24 on uPVC doors are all attributed and the footnotes saying so are protected from deletion. "PAS 24 capable" keeps Kenrick's word. Heritage prints A rated not A+ because A+ describes a sash we do not sell. Tilt and turn holds Liniar's own 1.3/0.93 instead of being reconciled to casement's 0.95. Composite prints no U-value and says why. Any competitor would have published the best number in every range.
- **The compare-wipe is the best interaction on the site** (motion-interaction) — It does the whole job with one native `<input type="range">` stretched across the stage and a single CSS custom property. Keyboard operation, touch behaviour, the announced value and the focus ring all come from the platform. `--fg-wipe` has a CSS default of 50%, so with JavaScript off the box is still a working half-and-half comparison rather than a dead widget. Nothing is measured and nothing listens on the window, so there is no scroll or resize path to get wrong and it is correct at any width. The controller is five lines. It was generalised from `flush-sash-wipe.php` to serve a second route without any change to the markup, CSS or JS — only the argument names.
- **Scroll containers are labelled as regions in the markup, and the doubled track is hidden from assistive tech** (motion-interaction) — Both `[data-fg-door-wall]` and `[data-fg-colour-rail-viewport]` ship `tabindex="0" role="region"` plus an aria-label that names the content and states the gesture, in the HTML rather than added by JS. The door wall's duplicated half — the trick that makes the loop seamless — carries `aria-hidden="true"` on every clone and `display: none` under reduced motion, so a screen reader reads 33 doors once and a reduced-motion visitor is not paying for a second copy at all. That is more care than most production sites take with an infinite marquee.
- **The homepage theatre's inactive scenes are visibility:hidden, not just transparent** (motion-interaction) — `setActiveScene` writes `aria-hidden="true"` onto the four inactive `<article>` elements, each of which contains a real product link. That combination is the single most common ARIA violation in scroll-driven galleries — a focusable element inside an aria-hidden subtree. It is avoided here because the CSS uses `opacity: 0; visibility: hidden; pointer-events: none` with a delayed `visibility` transition, so the links are genuinely out of the tab order the whole time they are hidden. Somebody thought about this.
- **Motion is restrained where it is easy to be indulgent** (motion-interaction) — 42,407 lines of SCSS contain nine `@keyframes` total and 167 `transition` declarations. Almost all motion is scroll-linked or interaction-linked rather than time-linked, which is why it reads as responsive rather than busy. There are 25 separate `prefers-reduced-motion` checks in the JavaScript — the door-wall drift, the page gradient, the chapter stack, the lock arrival, the pulse drum, the review auto-advance, the Legend sprite loop, the theatre easing and the mobile carousel scroll behaviour all honour it. Only the shared parallax was missed.
- **The repairs diagnostic is progressive enhancement done properly, with the traps documented in place** (motion-interaction) — The interactive shell ships `hidden` and is revealed by the controller, while the plain symptom-to-part list is server-rendered and hidden by the same controller — so with JavaScript off you get real content and indexable symptom language rather than dead buttons. The two traps that cost review rounds are fixed and commented at the point of the fix: the explicit `[hidden] { display: none !important }` guards that beat class rules setting `display`, and the use of `setAttribute`/`removeAttribute` rather than `el.hidden` because `hidden` is an HTMLElement IDL property that SVGElement does not inherit. Both comments will stop the next person reintroducing the bug. A JSON parse failure also leaves the fallback showing rather than a broken widget.
- **Legend's drawer has correct non-modal dialog semantics and a live transcript** (motion-interaction) — `role="dialog"` with `aria-labelledby`, a transcript marked `role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions"`, `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` on the launcher, Escape to close, and focus returned to the launcher on close. It deliberately does not claim `aria-modal`, which is right for a drawer that does not block the page. The typing indicator carries a `.screen-reader-text` label. For a bolted-on chat widget this is better wired than most first-party ones.
- **Carousel dots elsewhere on the site are indicators, not controls** (motion-interaction) — The mobile theatre dots are explicitly `pointer-events: none` and sit beside real prev/next buttons, and the composite-collections dots are `<span>` elements rather than buttons. That is the correct call for an 8px pip: report position, do not pretend to be a target. It is why the 6px sash dots stand out as the one place the pattern slipped rather than as a systemic problem.
- **Zero horizontal overflow on all 38 routes at a real 390px** (mobile) — STYLE.md:351 names horizontal body scroll as a shipping blocker, and the site clears it completely — not on a 500px floor but at genuine CDP-emulated 390px with dsf=3, across pages carrying 127 images, 250 resources, embedded iframes, colour grids, comparison tables, scroll-snap rails and a 31,310px location page. On a codebase this large with this many bespoke sections that is a real discipline result, and the `overflow-x: clip` guards on `.site-header, .site-main, .site-footer` show it was engineered rather than lucky. Protect it: every recommendation above should be re-verified against this number.
- **Forms are textbook mobile — 16px inputs, single column, fully labelled** (mobile) — 630 of 631 visible form fields render at exactly 16px, which is the threshold below which iOS Safari force-zooms on focus; there is not a single sub-16px text input anywhere on the site. Every form measured is single-column at 390px (zero fields sharing a row), inputs are 332px wide and 52-53px tall, textareas 128-155px, and 100% of visible fields are programmatically labelled across all 38 routes. STYLE.md:278-279 asks for exactly this and the implementation is complete, not partial. The only sub-16px field anywhere is the 12.5px privacy consent checkbox label, which is a legitimately secondary control.
- **The mobile navigation is genuinely designed rather than collapsed** (mobile) — Six top-level rows at 56px tall and full 362-364px width, in a 768px panel that needs no internal scroll (scrollHeight === clientHeight), with zero sub-44px targets among them. The two commercial actions are promoted to coloured full-width buttons (Instant Quote in accent green, Free Consultation in steel), Products and Commercial carry visible + accordion affordances while leaf items carry arrows, and both the Call pill and a Close button stay reachable in the header while the panel is open. This is the clearest example on the site of a mobile surface that was drawn on purpose.
- **Both hero folds put the value proposition and both primary actions on screen without scrolling** (mobile) — On the homepage at 390x844 a visitor sees the 77px header with a Call pill, the eyebrow, a three-line H1 at 36px, a four-line proposition paragraph and both CTAs ("Get an instant price" and "Explore our products") as full-width buttons — all inside the first viewport with room to spare. The product template is even denser and still fits: hero image 302px, H1 overlaid, a two-button action bar, and a four-tile Key Specifications card (U-value, colour choice, energy rating, security) all land within 733px of the 844px viewport. Getting a product image, a name, two actions and four hard numbers above the fold on a phone is a strong result and should be the constraint any redesign works within.
- **Layout stability at mobile is close to perfect** (mobile) — CLS measured on cold, throttled 390px loads ranges from 0 to 0.04, and the only shift source recorded on any route is the consent dialog opening (`DIALOG.fg-cookie-consent`). On a site where 45 of 65 images on a product page carry no width/height attribute, that stability has to be coming from CSS aspect-ratio and sized containers — which is the right way to do it. Content does not jump under the reader's thumb, which is the failure mode phone users notice most.
- **Vertical rhythm is genuinely tuned down for mobile** (mobile) — Section padding is not inherited from desktop — measured on /casement-windows/, the same seven sections render `padding: 40px 0` at 390px versus `63px 0` at 1440px, a deliberate 37% reduction, and the location-page sections use 48px at mobile. Combined with the mobile nav and the sash template, this shows the team does adjust for mobile when it looks at a component; the findings above are gaps in coverage, not an absence of intent.
- **Review-card truncation is deliberate and correctly signposted** (mobile) — Review paragraphs render with clientHeight 140 against scrollHeight up to 489 — which looks like a clipping bug until you read the CSS. It is `-webkit-line-clamp: 6` with `overflow: hidden`, so the browser adds an ellipsis, and each card carries an explicit `.fg-review-showcase__read` link ("Read on Google") beneath. The cards sit in a 268px scroll-snap rail inside a 358px container, so the next card peeks and the horizontal scroll is discoverable. This is the correct pattern and I flag it explicitly because an automated clipped-text detector will keep reporting it as a defect.
- **The consent modal fits the mobile viewport at both stages without internal scrolling** (mobile) — At a real 390x844 the first-stage dialog measures 374x503 — 59.6% of the viewport height, confirming the ads audit's 501-of-812 figure — and the expanded Customise view measures 781px, 92.5% of the viewport, with scrollHeight exactly equal to clientHeight, meaning the full three-button decision (Use necessary only / Save choices / Accept all), both category switches and the policy link all fit on one screen with no nested scroll. Action buttons are 335x50, and the switch rows are wrapped in 72px-min-height `<label>` cards so the whole card is the hit area rather than the 52x30 switch. Fitting a three-category consent UI into 844px without a scroll trap is not easy and it has been done properly.
- **Every one of the 712 sitemap URLs resolves 200 in a single hop** (technical-qa) — Zero 404s, zero redirects and zero soft-404s across a 712-page generated matrix is genuinely rare. It means the routing layer and the sitemap are in exact agreement, and no crawl budget is wasted. This is the property most large template-generated sites fail.
- **Link and asset integrity across the fetched pages is near-perfect** (technical-qa) — 1,171 of 1,173 unique link and asset URLs return 200. The only genuine internal issue is the logo space-encoding (reported separately); the two external failures are a Google local-reviews URL and Trustpilot returning 403 to non-browser agents. Nothing is silently broken.
- **404 handling and the documented 301s are both correct** (technical-qa) — Nonsense URLs and nonsense town/product combinations all return a true 404 — no soft-404 masking, which is what generated-page routers usually get wrong. The 404 page is genuinely useful rather than a dead end, and is correctly noindex,follow with no canonical.
- **The enquiry form is properly progressive and its endpoints are correctly gated** (technical-qa) — The form posts to admin-post.php with a real server handler, so it works with JavaScript disabled, and enhances to AJAX with inline feedback when JS is available. Every error state has its own written notice with the correct role (status for success, alert for failures), phone and postcode carry both pattern and title, and the nonce is genuinely enforced rather than decorative.
- **Zero unnamed links or buttons, and clean document-level head hygiene** (technical-qa) — Every icon-only and image-only link carries a real aria-label or meaningful img alt — including the trust badges and the brand link. Combined with consistent lang, viewport and charset, and no unsafe target=_blank, this is a well-disciplined baseline that most sites of this size fail on at least one count.
- **Rendering is stable across viewports: no overflow, no console errors, one H1 everywhere** (technical-qa) — Zero horizontal overflow at 1440, tablet and mobile widths on a site with 42k lines of SCSS and heavy bespoke layout work is a strong signal of layout discipline. Zero console errors means no silently failing feature is hiding behind a working-looking page.
- **Zero duplicate titles and zero duplicate meta descriptions across 712 pages** (hostile-competitor) — At 712 URLs with 576 of them generated from templates, unique titles and descriptions on every single page is genuinely rare — most programmatic sites this size have hundreds of collisions. The theme owning SEO output and suppressing Yoast/Rank Math (AI.md:29) is what makes this hold. Whatever happens to the location pages in a consolidation, this generator discipline must survive it.
- **Seventeen named staff with real photographs, real roles and specific biographies** (hostile-competitor) — Almost every competitor in this market uses stock photography or no faces at all. Fenster shows David Foord, Kerry Lince, Johnnie Greenwell with 20 years in the trade, and names the fitters in the case studies ('Johnnie and Tom fitted it'). This is the single hardest thing for a rival to copy and the strongest E-E-A-T signal on the site. It is also the honest answer to '50+ yrs of combined experience' — the real version is better than the aggregate.
- **The review showcase reads the real Google rating, count and reviews from the Places API rather than hardcoding them** (hostile-competitor) — inc/google-reviews.php fetches rating, userRatingCount and the latest reviews with a six-hour transient, keeps the API key server-side, falls back to curated reviews rather than breaking, and renders each reviewer's own name, photo and link as Google's terms require. The count on the page today (136) genuinely is the live count. Most sites at this level paste a number into a template and let it rot — this one cannot.
- **Accreditation copy that states the limits of its own badges** (hostile-competitor) — /about/ introduces the accreditations with 'Any installer can print a logo, so here is what each of ours covers, including the limits most keep in the small print', then explains what FENSA registration actually does. That is a genuinely differentiated posture in a category built on badge theatre, and it is the frame that makes the missing FENSA number (finding 15) so fixable — the argument is already made, only the checkable number is absent.
- **Product copy written to a real editorial standard, with specifications a buyer can actually use** (hostile-competitor) — The casement, colour, handle and glass sections name RAL codes for all 16 foils, distinguish Georgian bars inside the unit from astragal bars bonded to the face, give whole-window U-values for triple and double (0.95 vs 1.2 W/m²K), and answer 'how many colours are there?' with 'Sixteen foils, plus smooth white as the unfoiled profile'. It also declines to overclaim: 'Liniar publish a wider foil catalogue, but availability, lead time and cost depend on the exact profile and the fabricator, so we confirm before you order.' This is better than anything a 20-year incumbent is likely to have, and it is the asset the location pages should have been built from.
- **Clean rendering fundamentals across all three breakpoints** (hostile-competitor) — Zero horizontal overflow on every route at desktop, mobile and tablet; zero console errors; exactly one H1 per page on all 712; every visible form field correctly label-wired (labelled:true) and set to 16px on mobile so iOS does not auto-zoom on focus. These are the things that quietly break on most WordPress sites at this scale, and none of them is broken here.
- **Case studies that name the street, the product, the finish and the date** (hostile-competitor) — 'Six secondary glazing units in a listed Winslow home, five horizontal sliders and one lift-out, fitted inside the original windows in white aluminium' and 'Agate grey flush casement windows (RAL 7038) … with trickle vents in the frame heads' are the level of specificity that survives a sceptical read. The 13 that exist are strong; the problem is only that there are 13 and a button that pretends there are more.
- **Internal link integrity is effectively perfect** (customer-journeys) — 654 of 655 unique internal URLs referenced across 58 pages return 200 on a direct GET, and the single exception is one anchor pointing at a working 301. On a 712-URL site built from six or seven separate registries that do not cross-check each other, that is an unusual result and it means no journey I ran ever hit a 404. It should be protected with a scheduled crawl before any route rename, because AI.md already records that a rename here is never a one-file job.
- **The repairs diagnostics component is the best conversion asset on the site** (customer-journeys) — Twelve plain-English symptoms — "The handle is broken or loose", "It has dropped, or catches on the frame", "The glass is misted or broken" — each resolve to a named part, a real studio photograph of that part, a plain sentence on what it is and a second on how it is fixed, with the part highlighted on a to-scale technical drawing. It lets a customer who has no vocabulary describe their problem and get a real answer without phoning, and the misted symptom correctly hands off to /double-glazing-replacement/ with its own labelled link. It is the only place on the site where the visitor's actual words are the entry point rather than a product name.
- **The repairs page answers the price question first, without breaking the no-prices rule** (customer-journeys) — AI.md forbids any repair price table and permits exactly one figure. The page opens its FAQ with "How much does a window or door repair cost?" as the first `<details>`, and it is the only one rendered with the `open` attribute, so the £96 answer and its "depends on which part" framing are visible without a click. That is the hardest constraint on the site handled with real care — the question is answered before it is asked and the rule is still kept.
- **The /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ mobile fold does the whole job in one screen** (customer-journeys) — At 390x844 the visitor gets the H1, one sentence naming every product and the survey promise, two unambiguous CTAs ("Get an instant price", "Ask Fenster to quote"), and then immediately Google, Trustpilot, FENSA and CPA marks with a "Why you can trust Fenster Glazing" link. That is orientation, action and proof before any scroll on the site's highest-impression organic page. It is the pattern the product pages should be copying.
- **/online-quote/ de-risks the tool before the visitor commits to it** (customer-journeys) — "Six screens, and this is all of them", followed by the six named steps, then "Worth having to hand" and "What actually happens next", removes the single biggest reason people abandon an embedded quote configurator — not knowing how long it will take or what it will ask for. Pairing that with "Your details come before the number, and nothing is ordered" is honest about the one thing visitors fear and still gets them to start.
- **A phone number is one tap away on pages 37 viewports long** (customer-journeys) — The header is `position: fixed` at ≤860px and carries a 46px-tall green "Call us" pill next to the menu toggle at every scroll position. On /double-glazing-milton-keynes/, which is 31,310px tall on mobile, and on the 20,000px product pages, that is the difference between a reachable business and a scroll to the footer. It should survive any future header simplification.
- **/contact/ leads with the visitor's intent rather than the company's structure** (customer-journeys) — The H1 is "How do you want to start?" and the four options underneath are labelled by what the visitor wants — Instant quote, Consultation, Call, Email, Showroom — each with a sentence explaining who it suits, followed by "Not every enquiry starts in the same place" splitting home projects from commercial from price-first. It is the only page on the site that routes by intent instead of by product, and it is why journeys 8 and 10 both recover quickly once a visitor reaches it.

## Appendix D — Coverage notes from each audit

**design-system** — Inspected: the full `:root` token block (src/scss/main.scss:41-79) and the two other `:root` blocks (:14054 commercial tag tokens, :22587 mobile header height); the compiled production `live/main.css` (694,634 bytes) for every font-size, border-radius, box-shadow, padding, gap, clamp, transition, hex and rgba value; all 38 routes in probe-desktop.json (headings, fontSizes histograms, smallTargets, maxFontSize); the 40 live HTML files; the theme's PHP/JS for class emission; STYLE.md in full, plus targeted checks of AI.md and HANDOVER.md for owner rulings on the links band, enquiry heading sizes and the casement exception; desktop screenshots for /upvc-doors/ (enquiry section) and the mobile screenshot for /what-is-a-door-lintel/.

Could not check, and why:
- **probe-mobile.json and probe-tablet.json do not exist.** Only probe-desktop.json is present in the scratchpad, so every rendered measurement I report is at 1440px. Mobile claims (e.g. that the global 48px h2 is unresponsive) are derived from CSS analysis — I confirmed no bare `h2` font-size override exists inside any media query in the shipped CSS — plus one mobile screenshot, not from rendered measurement across routes. Mobile deserves its own probe pass.
- **The probe's `sections[]` array is unusable for spacing.** It captured only the top-level `<article>` wrapper, one per route, all reporting `padTop: "0px"` / `padBottom: "0px"`. The brief asked me to measure section padding distribution from `sections[].padTop/padBottom`; that data does not exist, so the entire spacing finding is derived from the compiled CSS instead and is stated as such. Real rendered section-padding distribution remains unmeasured.
- **smallTargets is capped at 30 per route**, and product pages reported 37–41, so absence of a small target on those pages is not evidence. I relied on CSS computation plus the one probe-confirmed 43px case on /3d-visualiser/, and explicitly did not report `.fg-product-quote-embed__actions .button` as a tap-target breach because it computes to ~45px.

Checks I ran that failed and had to be redone (per the ground-truth rule, reporting these so the numbers are trustworthy):
- My first namespace-usage count used an unquoted `--include=*.php`, which zsh globbed, returning 0 for every namespace. Every zero was false. Redone with quoted globs.
- My first "unstyled classes" pass reported 1,050 classes; the regex character class `[a-z0-9-]` excluded `_`, so every BEM `__element` looked unstyled. That number was an artifact and is not reported.
- My "the correct H2 clamp is used exactly once" reading came from `grep -c`, which counts lines — and the minified CSS is nearly one line. It is actually used 26 times. Corrected before reporting.
- I verified `fg-team-person--<name>` and `fg-cd3-layer-` are built by PHP string concatenation and excluded 47 such dynamic prefixes from the dead-code count, which is why I report 271 rather than the raw 309.

Not assessed (outside this dimension or not substantiable from available artefacts): actual contrast ratios (the probe's lowContrast detector is documented as unreliable over gradients and dark overlays, and this site is built on both — I made no contrast claims); third-party asset weight (probe ran consent-declined); tablet breakpoint behaviour; and the ~672 routes outside the 38-route sample, which means dead-code figures are a floor for the sampled set rather than a site-wide total.

**cross-page-consistency** — WHAT I INSPECTED. All 40 live HTML files in scratchpad/live/ (the brief said 38; two extra — areas-we-cover and window-door-prices-milton-keynes — are present as HTML but absent from the probe and from all screenshot sets). I extracted and compared, per route: the full `<section>` class sequence inside `<main>`, hero internals (eyebrow / H1 / lead / CTA labels+variants+order / image and list counts), the key-specification strip (presence, aria-label, H2), every `<a class="button">` grouped by href to detect label collisions, form field order and labels and submit labels, and byte-level MD5 of the header and footer slices. From probe-desktop.json I used `headings` (complete, not truncated), `forms`, `schemaTypes` and `head`. I read the relevant source: generated-page.php (hero block ~3240-3300, pulse dispatch 3521-3538, product-why gate 4031, enquiry block 5340-5375), product-pulse.php, enquiry-form.php, casement-windows-v2.php, roof-lanterns.php, heritage-aluminium-doors.php, and main.scss around the hero, eyebrow and CTA rules. I read STYLE.md's Reference Pages, tone and CTA sections and AI.md's Order Process Rule, Product Data Rule, Product Quote Embed Rule and Review Showcase Rule before reporting, and dropped several candidate findings that turned out to be owner rulings (links band gated off sash/composite at generated-page.php:5361; no pulse on secondary-glazing and repairs; no aggregateRating; the hero secondary CTA varying between "Instant pricing"/"Call"/"Book a consultation" is correct logic driven by whether a quote collection exists). I measured contrast myself with ImageMagick pixel sampling plus the WCAG luminance formula rather than trusting the probe's lowContrast array, per the brief's warning. I looked directly at desktop fold screenshots for casement-windows, composite-doors and roof-lanterns, and mobile folds for casement-windows and home. I verified one claim against the live site by curl (/composite-doors-wolverton/) rather than inferring the town matrix from one Tier-1 sample.

ONE THING I DELIBERATELY DID NOT REPORT. 14 of 38 mobile `--fold.png` shots do not match the top 600px of the corresponding full-page shot (deltas 0.03-0.61 in mean luminance; roof-lanterns 0.61, sliding-sash-windows 0.53, aluminium-bifold-doors 0.43). That initially looked like a scroll-jump bug. The 14 affected routes correlate almost exactly with the routes that have scroll-driven or pinned sections (casement-windows-v2, upvc-doors-v2, sash, roof-lanterns, heritage, flush, aluminium-bifold, composite), and full-page capture works by resizing the viewport to the document height, which necessarily renders scroll-driven sections in a different state. That explains the mismatch as a capture artefact, so per the brief's rule that a verification failure is not evidence until the check itself is proven sound, I did not raise it as a defect. It is still worth one manual mobile load of /sliding-sash-windows/ and /roof-lanterns/ to rule out a genuine restore-scroll problem.

**architecture** — Read in full or in substantial chunks: functions.php, inc/assets.php (430 lines, all), inc/template-tags.php (270, all), inc/generated-pages.php (routing, redirects, gone slugs, noindex, sitemap, matrix, county profiles, page cache — roughly 1,200 of 2,530 lines), template-parts/sections/generated-page.php (all flag computation :1-450, the sash/composite data blocks :450-1200, journey + related-links construction :1200-2100, the full early-return dispatch :2100-3140, the article/enquiry/case-study tail :5200-5376, plus sampled render bands), inc/product-hub-data.php:540-797, inc/case-studies-data.php:1683-1740, inc/adminbase.php:12-360, inc/website-tracking.php:129-170, inc/google-ads-conversions.php:63-140, inc/legend-assistant.php:130-155, inc/consent.php:20-120, header/footer/front-page/page/index/single.php, package.json and scripts/.
