WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. The Trustpilot review count: uk.trustpilot.com returns HTTP 403 to any fetch, so "Hundreds of customer reviews" is filed as INVESTIGATE at 72% rather than as a confirmed overclaim. I did not read all ~270 blog and guide bodies word by word — those were pattern-swept for banned vocabulary, punctuation, Americanisms, truncated sentences, Title Case headings and self-referential copy, and only pages that surfaced hits were then read in full, so a bland guide page with no flagged pattern could have escaped. I judged the 525-route matrix family from three routes read fully (Bletchley, Furzton, Luton) plus reading the generating template, on the basis that all 525 come from one file. Rendered-appearance claims are backed by screenshots I actually opened (home--fold, patio-doors); everything else is text and source.

**seo** — WHAT I INSPECTED. All 712 sitemap URLs, fetched live and stored in scratchpad/all/ — not just the 38 Tier-1 pages. For every one I extracted title, meta description, canonical, robots, og/twitter tags, H1 set, <main> word count and every JSON-LD block (parsed, not regexed). I built a distinct-source internal link graph over the full corpus by exact href match, which is what produced the orphan count (75), the matrix inbound histogram (407/525 at exactly one source) and the price-guide and county link counts. I diffed live metadata against the imported Yoast records in wp-content/themes/fenster/data/pages.json to identify the 44 pages still on old-site copy. I read SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md, SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md, HIGH-INTENT-SEARCH-PLAN.md and the relevant parts of SEO-AUDIT.md, AI.md, HANDOVER.md and BLOG-CALENDAR.md before writing anything, and I checked candidate findings against them; several plausible-looking issues are owner rulings and are not reported (no aggregateRating, the 2-level breadcrumb on flat URLs, price guides existing at all, the informational library's international audience). I verified canonicalisation, redirects and 404 behaviour with live curl, and confirmed the noindex set live rather than from code. Word-level difflib on matrix pairs established that MK Tier-1 town pages carry ~13% genuinely unique local copy (real Wolverton railway-terrace and conservation-area content) while MK suburb pages differ from each other by only ~7% — the matrix is templated but it is not empty, which is why I recommend testing before pruning.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. (1) Actual index coverage. I have no Search Console access, so I cannot confirm which of the 712 URLs Google has indexed, whether the price guides are excluded or merely unranked, or whether the duplicate /design-your-windows-and-doors/ has been canonicalised away by Google of its own accord. Every indexation statement here is inferred from crawlability and internal links, not observed. (2) Live SERP appearance. No uule-encoded SERP checks were run in this pass; the CTR reasoning rests on the July checks in HIGH-INTENT-SEARCH-PLAN.md §4, which are three weeks old. (3) Current GSC numbers. All click, impression and position figures I quote are from SEO-LEAD-AUDIT-2026-08-05.md and SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026.md, i.e. up to 3 August, not measured by me. (4) Backlinks and external authority — entirely out of scope of the data available. (5) One important caveat on code citations: the local theme is AHEAD of production. /commercial-replacement-glazing/ and /industrial-and-logistics-glazing/ exist in inc/generated-pages.php and 404 live, and the fenster_gsc_seo_overrides() entries for commercial-glazing and commercial-windows-and-doors ("Commercial Glazing Contractors | Our Own Fitters") are not on the live site, which still serves the older strings. That is the commercial overhaul in flight, dated 2026-08-12, not a defect — and it means SEO-AUDIT-AUG-2026 §5 code item 2 (commercial hub snippet pass) is DONE in code and pending deploy, which I would otherwise have reported as still open. Every finding above was verified against the LIVE response before being written; code line numbers are given as root cause only where the live behaviour confirms them. (6) I did not attempt to price the risk of consolidating the informational clusters, which is why that one is INVESTIGATE rather than REMOVE — those pages carry a third of the site's clicks and a bad 301 there costs more than the split does.

**accessibility** — Inspected: all three probe JSONs (headings, headingJumps, lowContrast, smallTargets, forms, landmarks, emptyLinks, focusStyles, images) plus harness.py itself to understand what each field actually measures; the full 712-page live HTML corpus in scratchpad/all (not just the 38 Tier-1 pages), scripted for heading outline, alt coverage, accessible names, aria reference integrity, tabindex, iframe titles, duplicate ids, aria-hidden-with-focusables and multiple landmarks; src/scss/main.scss (42k lines) for focus, reduced-motion, target size and contrast; src/js/main.js (8.2k lines) read component-by-component for the mega menu, mobile drawer, door wall, colour rail, obscured-glass slider, blind visualiser, lightbox, review carousel, product theatre, tabs, consultation booking, enquiry form and Legend chat; inc/consent.php in full; inc/template-tags.php nav renderers; AI.md and STYLE.md for owner rulings. Screenshots read at desktop and pixel-sampled for contrast.

Probe claims I disproved and deliberately did NOT report. (1) emptyLinks — 24 on the homepage at desktop, 0 in the static HTML. The probe uses a.innerText, which returns '' for display:none elements, so it is counting the hidden mobile drawer on desktop and the hidden desktop nav list on mobile. Not a defect. (2) lowContrast entries at ratio 1.0–1.2 over gradient overlays — .fg-cd3-door__label, .fg-ph-tile__label, .fg-cas-anatomy__name, .fg-cas-display — are false positives; bgOf() cannot see linear-gradient(transparent, rgba(1,20,26,0.86)) and falls back to a light ancestor. I computed the real composite for the composite-door labels at roughly 7.9:1. Every entry whose bg is the string "rgb(255,255,255)" without spaces is the probe's hardcoded fallback, meaning the DOM walk reached the root — those are unverified, not findings. (3) focusStyles reports outline:none on all 38 routes, but it uses programmatic .focus(), and :focus-visible does not match under programmatic focus in an unfocused document — I confirmed exactly this in the live browser (activeElement === skipLink while matches(':focus') === false). The field is meaningless; I checked focus styling in the CSS instead. (4) smallTargets — most of the 1,227 entries are inline text links, exempt from SC 2.5.8; the 18×18 consent checkbox and the 20px-tall footer buttons pass on the spacing exception once the geometry is worked, so I left them out rather than pad the count. (5) aria-hidden="true" on the homepage product-theatre articles looked like the classic focusable-inside-aria-hidden bug until I checked the CSS — the inactive panels are visibility:hidden (main.scss:20342-20352), so their links are already out of the tab order. Correct, not a defect.

Not covered. No assistive technology was available (no VoiceOver/NVDA), so screen-reader announcement claims are derived from ARIA name-computation rules and markup, not heard. The browser automation in this environment proved unreliable — javascript_tool was evaluating against a different tab and viewport than the visible pane (it returned a 375px-wide /casement-windows/ context while the pane showed a 1280px homepage), so I used it only where results were internally self-consistent and corroborated by source, and I explicitly flagged the one finding (door wall) reported from source alone. No testing at 200%/400% zoom, Windows High Contrast, or with colour-blindness simulation — the last is worth a separate pass given how much status information the site carries in the accent green. The 674 non-Tier-1 pages were analysed as static HTML only; their rendered contrast, tap targets and JS behaviour are inferred from the shared templates they demonstrably use.

**performance** — WHAT I INSPECTED. All 38 routes in probe-desktop.json and probe-mobile.json (perf, images, iframes, head fields) plus the 40 saved live HTML files and the compiled main.css/main.js. Theme source: inc/assets.php (all 430 lines), inc/consent.php (all 822), template-parts/sections/home-experience.php, src/js/main.js (structure plus the hero-video, Lenis, aw-story and blind-visualiser blocks read in full), package.json build scripts. Docs: AI.md, HANDOVER.md, PROGRESS.md, LIVECHANGES.md and STYLE.md searched for rulings on critical CSS, async stylesheets, srcset, the hero video, the Legend sprite, the aluminium-windows frame story and image versioning before reporting anything as a defect.

WHAT I MEASURED MYSELF rather than taking from the probe. (1) CSS coverage: parsed main.css into 5,959 rules accounting for 99.2% of its bytes, matched every rule's classes against every page's class set, and ran a sensitivity test allowing runtime is-*/has-* classes (moves 88.5% to 88.0%). (2) srcset waste: resolved every images.oversized entry to a file on disk and re-encoded it to 2x its measured display width with ImageMagick, rather than modelling a ratio. (3) Live browser on fensterglazing.com: renderBlockingStatus for all four blocking resources, font resource-timing (which proved the double download), the 144.9 ms Clarity CSS injection, block-library parse (5.7 ms) and jQuery eval (8.7 ms), CLS via buffered PerformanceObserver, and live consent state. (4) curl: raw/gzip/brotli for every shared asset and third-party tag, full response headers, and cache-busted TTFB sweeps. (5) esbuild/brotli on extracted source regions to size the blind visualiser and Lenis inside the bundle.

WHAT I CORRECTED RATHER THAN REPORTED. Three checks failed and turned out to be my error or the probe's, and are deliberately not in the findings. (a) I saw a second unversioned 97.7 KB main.css download in the live network log and nearly reported it as a cache-key bug — it was my own earlier fetch() in the same tab. (b) probe images.broken flags 6 routes; in the browser the only zero-natural-width element is a lightbox <figure> placeholder <img> with src=null, which issues no request. Benign. (c) probe images.noDims looks like a CLS defect on 20+ routes; measured CLS is 0 and no image lacks a dimensional constraint — listed as a strength, not a fault. I also ignored probe images.lazy = 0 on every route, because the probe rewrites loading=lazy to eager before measuring; lazy counts came from the saved HTML instead.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. (1) Real-user Core Web Vitals: no CrUX or RUM access, so LCP/INP figures are lab measurements on a wired Mac; where I scale to mobile I say so and give the assumed 3-5x CPU factor. (2) LCP element identification: largest-contentful-paint returned no buffered entries through the browser tool, so LCP attribution on /contact/ and the homepage is inferred from resource weight, eagerness and fold screenshots, not directly observed. (3) The 674 routes outside the 38-route sample — commercial, county, blog and case-study detail templates — are unmeasured; the 204 KB of CSS matching nothing in the sample is partly theirs and I have not called it dead. (4) Third-party weight under full consent is measured by fetching gtm.js/fbevents.js/clarity directly, not by tracing a fully consented page load with all GTM child tags fired, so ~885 KB raw is a floor. (5) No Lighthouse run and no throttled trace. (6) I made no changes to any file in the repo — every write went to the scratchpad.

**product-experience** — WHAT I INSPECTED. All fifteen routes: live HTML (fetched Tier-1 copies), full-page desktop screenshots at 1440 (read as multi-column contact sheets for casement, composite, patio, aluminium-doors, integral-blinds, bifold), mobile full-page captures, probe-desktop.json and probe-mobile.json, and — most importantly — LIVE per-section measurement of every one of the fifteen pages at 375x812 via the browser, because the probe only records the article wrapper as a single section. Those live numbers (page height plus every section height) are the basis for every length, ratio and ordering claim here. I also read AI.md end to end for the rules touching these routes, HANDOVER.md's casement and integral-blinds sections, TONEOFVOICE.md, PHOTO-CHECKLIST.md, SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md, and the relevant parts of inc/site-data.php, inc/case-studies-data.php, template-parts/sections/generated-page.php and src/scss/main.scss.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT REPORT. Three probe/capture artefacts that look like defects and are not. (1) `images.lazy` reads 0 on every route in both probes; the live HTML actually carries `loading="lazy"` on 18-111 images per page, so the probe field is wrong and I did not report a lazy-loading problem. (2) The mobile full-page screenshots for six routes (bifold, upvc-doors, aluminium-windows, heritage, tilt-turn, flush, aluminium-doors) are blank below roughly 40% of the page — 26-28 of 40 sampled bands are pure white — while the desktop captures of the same routes are complete. That is a capture failure, not a rendering one, so no claim here rests on the lower part of a mobile screenshot. (3) A mobile screenshot of the casement spec strip showed "1.21 W/m²K" and "1 options"; that is the odometer mid-run, not wrong data, and I have listed it as a strength instead.

I also checked and dropped several candidate findings that turned out to be owner rulings or non-issues: the missing colour panel, order rail and related-links band on /sliding-sash-windows/ (all documented decisions in SASH-PAGE-REDESIGN.md sections 7 and 10); the gated case-study strips on aluminium-windows, tilt-turn, heritage and replacement glazing (correct, and the gating reason is recorded); the absence of a configurator on product pages (removed twice on sight); the absence of aggregateRating schema; and a suspected "compact mobile enquiry form" used on only three routes — the 304px difference turned out to be copy length, not a variant, so there is nothing to propagate.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. Whether the WindowCAD iframe renders usable content at 542 logical px on a phone — it is third-party and rendered blank in every capture I have, on desktop as well as mobile, so I framed that finding around the structural duplication rather than asserting the tool is broken. I could not verify the patio-doors system provenance (hence an INVESTIGATE rather than a CHANGE), nor whether Roseview's 1.2 W/m²K is publishable as the sash route figure. Third-party weight is absent from every performance number because the probe ran with consent at necessary-only, so the payload figures I quote are the best case, not the typical one. I did not audit the ~260 town matrix routes that read the same arrays, though several findings (the 14-options colour count, the Ultra slim tile, the 72mm frame tile, the aluminium-doors and bifold image pools) propagate to them.

**motion-interaction** — Read `src/js/main.js` end to end (8,234 lines) and enumerated every interactive controller, cross-referencing `src/scss/main.scss` (42,407 lines), the compiled `assets/css/main.css` and `assets/js/main.js`, and the shipped `lenis@1.3.23` source in node_modules. Read the motion-relevant sections of AI.md, STYLE.md and HANDOVER.md before reporting each finding, and dropped several candidates on the strength of owner rulings recorded there (the coverflow being retained alongside the rail per AI.md:733; the case-study strip gating; the removed configurators; the hub showing all products at once rather than behind a coverflow). Verified controller liveness with a scripted sweep of every `querySelector(All)` token in main.js against all theme PHP and all 38 fetched live pages, then hand-checked the runtime-generated false positives (consultation calendar days, Legend typing indicator) before reporting anything as dead. Parsed the compiled CSS with a brace-matching walker to establish parallax consumers and reduced-motion coverage rather than grepping. Measured asset weights on disk and confirmed the aluminium-windows frame sequence is live with `curl -I`. Used probe-mobile.json for tap targets and page heights, and drove the live site in a browser for structural checks. One near-miss worth recording: an early grep appeared to show `.fg-wipe__range:focus-visible)` shipping with a stray parenthesis, i.e. a broken focus ring on an invisible slider. Re-checking the live `main.css` showed the selector is intact (`.fg-wipe__stage:has(.fg-wipe__range:focus-visible)`) and my regex had matched a substring — the CSS is correct and it is listed as a strength instead. Three things I could not settle. (1) I measured, repeatedly and on four routes, that `element.focus()` on a control far below the fold does not scroll the page — but the control test proved this is a harness artefact: `document.visibilityState` was `"hidden"` and `document.hasFocus()` was `false` in the automation, and Chrome will not scroll the visual viewport in that state, while an inner scroll container in the same test scrolled correctly (1461px). I am therefore NOT reporting a focus-scroll defect; it needs a human at a real keyboard to confirm or clear, and it is the single highest-value thing to check next. (2) rAF is throttled in this harness (nick.md records the same), so I did not attempt to measure animation smoothness, Lenis settle time or scroll-linked timing empirically — the lerp/settle figures are derived from the Lenis source, not measured. (3) The mobile quote touch-lock and the obscured-glass divider both need a real phone; HANDOVER already flags the divider as never having been tested with a thumb, and I flag the touch-lock the same way rather than guessing. I did not audit the enquiry-form submit/success path, the consultation booking calendar, or the cookie-consent modal's interaction design in depth — the first two are form UX rather than motion, and the third belongs to another dimension, though I note in passing that the live modal dims and blurs the whole page on first paint, which reads as blocking against HANDOVER's claim that it "does not block", and its body text says "Analytics and marketing cookies are already on", which contradicts the consent-first ruling in AI.md/HANDOVER dated 2026-08-11.

**mobile** — WHAT I INSPECTED. All 38 Tier-1 routes in probe-mobile.json (genuine CDP 390x844 dsf=3, not a window-size floor) for pageHeight, overflowPx/culprits, smallTargets, fontSizes, headings, forms, images, iframes, lowContrast and perf. I read 20 mobile screenshots directly, including the homepage and all six top product folds; because the harness takes its `--fold.png` after a full-page `captureBeyondViewport` capture, several fold shots were left mid-page (e.g. casement-windows--fold.png shows content ~7,000px down), so I re-derived true folds by cropping the top 1170x2532 device px out of the full-page PNGs — scratchpad/mfold/*-top.png. I ran six independent live measurement passes against fensterglazing.com at 390x844 to verify things the probe could not: section-by-section block outlines at 390 vs 1440, grid column resolution, clipped-text detection, cold-cache throttled perf with LCP and CLS via PerformanceObserver, the consent dialog at both stages, the open mobile nav, and the Legend assistant's box and pointer-events. I read STYLE.md (mobile section, type scale, CTA rules) and AI.md before reporting, and cross-checked the SCSS source for the h2 clamp and the online-quote copy string.

PROBE ARTEFACTS I CAUGHT AND DID NOT REPORT. (1) `images.lazy` is 0 on all 38 routes, but the harness sets `img[loading=lazy].loading='eager'` before the probe runs; the live HTML has 23/36 lazy images on the homepage and 51/65 on casement, so lazy-loading is present and working. (2) The full-page casement screenshot appears to clip the colour-swatch labels ("Golden Oa", "Chartwell Green" cut off) and shows a large blank region where 11 swatches should be — a live DOM check returned `overflow: visible` with scrollHeight === clientHeight on every one of the 17 swatch items, so that was a scroll-reveal caught mid-animation by the capture, not a clipping bug. (3) The probe's `lowContrast` over-reports over gradients and translucent overlays (e.g. `rgba(255,255,255,0.86)` on `rgba(255,255,255,0.055)` at ratio 1.0, 78 instances) — I discarded all composited-background candidates and reported only the two pairs I recomputed from hex tokens. (4) Disabled calendar days and Google/Trustpilot brand-mark colours were excluded from the contrast finding. (5) The 10.7MB image figure on /meet-the-team/ in probe-mobile.json is the post-scroll, forced-eager total, not an initial load; I re-measured initial payload separately and reported that number instead.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. The WindowCAD configurator's internal behaviour at 390px is cross-origin and would not finish loading in headless within 12s on the throttled profile — hence that finding is filed as INVESTIGATE at 65% confidence and needs a real-device test. I did not establish the exact trigger conditions for the Legend prompt bubble: it is visible in the harness sweep screenshots on four routes but rendered `visibility:hidden` in my own instrumented runs (a prior-session `is-chat-acknowledged` state was set), so the obstruction is confirmed by screenshot while the trigger logic is not. Third-party weight (Clarity, GTM, Meta) is absent from every perf number because both the sweep and my runs used necessary-only consent — all LCP and byte figures are the consent-declined best case and will be worse in production. I audited the 38 Tier-1 routes only; the remaining 674 sitemap URLs (town pages, blog, case studies) were not swept at mobile, though the h2 clamp, font double-download, badge weight, header button height and footer target findings are site-wide by construction. No files in the repo were modified.

**technical-qa** — WHAT I INSPECTED. Link integrity (the headline check) was done exhaustively, not sampled: I extracted every href, src, data-src, poster and srcset candidate from all 40 fetched pages, normalised relative/protocol-relative/anchor forms, dropped tel:/mailto:/javascript:/data:, deduped to 1,173 unique URLs and curl-checked every one with -L and a plain UA (a spoofed Chrome UA does get WAF-blocked, as warned). I then separately status-checked all 712 sitemap URLs — the full set, not a sample — and separately fetched all 712 again to diff in-page `href="#..."` against emitted ` id="..."` and to count `<main>` elements. Also covered: probe consoleErrors/images.broken/overflowPx across all three viewport files; duplicate IDs by grep+count over the 40 pages and over all 712 for main-content; accessible names computed independently for every <a> and <button>; the enquiry form read end-to-end in inc/enquiries.php and template-parts/components/enquiry-form.php including the upload handler; live POST against admin-ajax.php; response headers, http→https, www→apex, the four documented 301s, four nonsense-URL 404 shapes and the uploads directory; the quote iframe endpoint (200, embeddable, no X-Frame-Options/CSP from the vendor, title attributes present, loading=lazy).

TWO PROBE FIELDS ARE FALSE POSITIVES — do not report them as defects. (1) `images.broken` shows `[""]` on 6 desktop/mobile routes and 2 tablet routes. There is no empty or missing src anywhere in the static HTML of those pages. The cause is the gallery lightbox, which `document.body.appendChild`s `<img alt="">` with no src attribute at all (src/js/main.js ~6955) and does `removeAttribute('src')` on close. An img with no src attribute issues no request (unlike `src=""`, which would re-fetch the page URL), and it sits inside a `hidden` dialog. The 6 flagged routes match exactly the 6 pages containing `data-fg-gallery-lightbox` — aluminium-bifold-doors, casement-windows, double-glazing-replacement, flush-casement-windows, sliding-sash-windows, tilt-turn-windows. There are zero genuinely broken images site-wide. (2) `emptyLinks` (24 on the homepage) counts links with empty textContent regardless of aria-label or img alt; recomputing accessible names properly gives 0 truly unnamed links on the homepage and 0 across all 40 pages. I also initially flagged 23 composite-doors colour swatches as unnamed and disproved it myself — they carry `<span>Anthracite Grey</span>` labels; that was my own regex over-stripping aria-hidden content, not a site defect.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. I did not execute JavaScript — no headless browser was available to me, so console errors, the lightbox, the door/colour selectors and the AJAX submit path are assessed from source plus the lead auditor's probe rather than observed at runtime; the probe's own caveat that its hook only captures errors after injection therefore stands unresolved. probe-tablet.json covers only 8 of 38 routes, so tablet overflow is materially less well covered than desktop and mobile. I could not test an actual form submission end-to-end (that would create a real enquiry post and send mail to the office, i.e. a side effect on a production system), so the validation-failure and data-loss behaviour in finding 8 is derived from reading the code path, not from a live failed submit — hence its lower confidence. I could not demonstrate an actually-exposed uploaded file (finding 10) because no upload URL is discoverable and directory listing returns 403; that finding is code-derived and marked INVESTIGATE. Third-party weight is absent from all perf numbers because the probe ran with consent pre-seeded to necessary-only, so Clarity, GTM and Meta never loaded — my jQuery finding is measured directly by curl and is independent of that, but any total-page-weight figure should be treated as the consent-declined best case. Finally, I did not re-derive the srcset coverage gap or the type-scale ceiling; those belong to other dimensions.

**hostile-competitor** — What I inspected: all 712 URLs as extracted text (scratchpad/alltxt/) and raw HTML (scratchpad/all/); the 38 Tier-1 live HTML captures; probe-desktop/mobile/tablet JSON; seo_all.json for all 712 head tags (note: its `text` field is truncated to exactly 400 chars on every entry, so I re-ran every absence claim against the full-text corpus — the finance/lead-time/company-number results are from alltxt, not seo_all); mobile and desktop screenshots for home, online-quote, meet-the-team, sash-window-prices; the theme source under wp-content/themes/fenster (inc/consent.php, inc/google-reviews.php, inc/site-data.php, template-parts/sections/location-service.php and online-quote.php); AI.md, TONEOFVOICE.md and STYLE.md for owner rulings. I also drove a live browser against production to verify consent state, resource timings, DOM measurements and the dead "Show more" button, and ran ~120 curl HEAD requests for real content-lengths.

Probe claims I discarded rather than reported, having checked them: the probe's `images.lazy: 0` is wrong (live/tilt-turn-windows.html contains 41 `loading="lazy"` attributes on 55 images); `images.broken: [""]` on six routes does not correspond to any `src=""` in the static HTML and is most likely a transient JS-inserted state, so I left it out; the 13.3px form inputs on /book-a-consultation/ are desktop-only and are 16px on mobile, so the iOS auto-zoom defect does not exist and I dropped it; most of the 72 low-contrast candidates on /patio-doors/ are gradient/overlay artefacts, so I reported only the two flat-colour pairs I recomputed by hand. I also dropped a candidate "16 vs 17 colours" contradiction after counting the DOM: 16 foil swatches plus one Smooth White cell reconciles with the FAQ's "sixteen foils, plus smooth white".

What I could not check: Trustpilot's actual review count and score — uk.trustpilot.com returns 403 to every request path including its own JSON API, so the "Rated Excellent" badge on 712 pages is unverified either way and I have flagged only the missing count, not the claim. I did not fetch Crown Windows' or Gallaghers' sites, so their 72 case studies and 4.9/173 are taken from the brief. I have no CrUX field data, no Search Console impressions/CTR, and no conversion data, so all revenue rankings are reasoned from funnel position rather than measured. I did not complete an end-to-end quote through the WindowCAD iframe, so I cannot say whether it prices internal foil colour correctly — that is the one open question behind finding 4. I also observed that production served the opt-in consent copy at 08:20 GMT (the live/ captures) and the opt-out copy from 09:34 GMT onward on cache MISSes; I have reported only the currently verified state and flagged the repo/production divergence, but somebody should establish whether a deploy was rolled back today.

**customer-journeys** — WHAT I DID. I read AI.md in full plus the relevant sections of PROGRESS.md, STYLE.md references, ACTION-PLAN.md, BLOG-CALENDAR.md, COMPOSITE-DOOR-REDESIGN.md and TONEOFVOICE.md before reporting anything, and I dropped several candidate findings that turned out to be owner rulings (the single £96 repair price, no aggregateRating, no U-value on composite doors, price guides existing, the case-study strip gated off replacement glazing, the commercial step set being unreachable). I worked from the 38 pre-fetched Tier-1 pages plus 20 more I curl-fetched myself (the seven price guides, the commercial product/projects pages, the condensation and replacement articles, /blog/, /careers/, /french-casement-windows/, /slide-fold-doors/, /aluminium-sliding-doors/), the desktop and mobile screenshots, both probe files, the compiled main.css and main.js, and the theme PHP.

JOURNEY SCORES, mobile-first. 1. Replacement windows, no idea of type — 7/10: /double-glazing-milton-keynes/ or /windows-milton-keynes/ → hub grid → product page. Three taps to a product, good fold, but the product page opens with no explanation (finding 1), the comparison panel does not compare (finding 12), and there is no way back to the range from four of the routes (finding 5). Biggest fix: restore the hero explanation. 2. Aluminium bifold — 6/10: /aluminium-bifold-doors/ → scroll ~17,000px → quote embed headed with a different product name, or the form at the foot. No price guide link despite /bifold-door-cost/ existing. Biggest fix: link the matching price guide and fix the embed heading. 3. Composite front door — 6/10: strong page, "See example prices" present, but headed with a supplier name, no consultation route, no lead time, no business/homeowner switch, and no exit to any other door. Biggest fix: add the doors-hub link and the consultation CTA. 4. Broken window / repair — 7/10: the destination is excellent, the route to it is not — four taps behind "Products → Other Services", mislabelled in the footer, and its qualifying sentence is CSS-hidden. Biggest fix: promote Repairs to a top-level nav item. 5. Roughly what does this cost — 5/10: seven good price guides that 19 of 20 product pages do not link to, absent from nav and footer. Biggest fix: cross-link the exact-match guide from each product page. 6. Compare uPVC and aluminium — 5/10: one decision panel, on the hub only, whose third row compares different attributes; no product page links back to it. Biggest fix: align the rows and link the panel from the product pages. 7. Is Fenster trustworthy — 6/10: the content is strong but the page's only proof CTA goes to a Google search page, there is no Trustpilot link in the hero, and the page is not in the nav. Biggest fix: trust-page.php:21. 8. Request a quote — 6/10: three competing routes (tool, form, consultation), six required fields including mandatory free text at the foot of a 20-screen page, and a success state that promises nothing. Biggest fix: reduce required fields and tell the visitor what happens next. 9. Misted unit, no vocabulary — 4/10, the weakest: the article that catches the search never uses the words, there is no site search, and the answer is link 11 of 12 in a band whose heading is untrue. Biggest fix: a signpost box at the top of /deal-with-condensation/. 10. Contractor pricing commercial — 6/10: the enquiry path is clear and the projects list is real, but the county-page dump undermines credibility, the pre-qualification marks are footer-only, and the form will not take a .zip. Biggest fix: accept .zip and name Constructionline/SSIP on the hub.

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. I never submitted a form, so error-state rendering, the AJAX success panel in situ and attachment upload behaviour are read from source, not observed. I could not drive the WindowCAD iframe, so the claim that six routes share two collections is proven from the URL parameters, not from what the tool actually shows on screen — verify inside the tool before acting on that half of finding 6. The Legend assistant's answers were not exercised. The 674 routes outside my 58-page sample (town matrix pages, county commercial pages, most blog articles) were checked only for HTTP status. Consent was pre-seeded to necessary-only, so nothing I saw reflects a visitor who accepted cookies. Two probe artifacts to be aware of: `.fg-home-quote-station` carries `content-visibility: auto`, which makes the quote block render blank in full-page screenshots and return empty `innerText` in the probe — I confirmed the block is present and correct and did not report it as a defect; and my first parallel link sweep returned a 301 for /obscured-glass/ that did not reproduce on three subsequent serial checks, so I report the redirect in the opposite direction only.
